unlocked, as AMS-TeX loads no LaTeX.pool there). amsppt1.tex:105-135 then redefines `\enddocument` from amsppt.sty's
state, or keeps an older version calling `\runaway@` (gone since amsppt 2.0) when `\add@missing` is undefined, as it was
in both Perl and Rust (4 undefined-macro errors; KPE #642).

**Rust** (batch 66d, amsppt_sty.rs): the binding clears `\abstract:locked`, and defines amsppt.sty's environment-end
tracker `\add@missing`/`\envir@end` (:107-111; `\envir@end` a sentinel for :126's `\enddocument␣`; the binding's environments close themselves, so none fires), the
address count (:330-331), `\ifmonograph@` (:441) and `\thetranslator@` (:506), and its captions
`\topcaption`/`\botcaption#1#2\endcaption` (:820-836: the label in `\smc`, `.\enspace`, the text; a paragraph, as the
inserts are no-ops here; q-alg9505010, q-alg9507011). Witnesses alg-geom9505028, alg-geom9606011,
2310.08131, q-alg9505010, q-alg9507011. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch66d::{amsppt1_abstract_shim_is_kept, amsppt_captions_are_paragraphs}`; repros
`amstex/{amsppt1_abstract_braced, amsppt_botcaption}`.

### 572. `{filecontents}` ends at its `\end{…}` anywhere in a line, as LaTeX's does

latex.ltx:19047-19066 reads each line as `##1\E##2\E##3\relax`: the text before `\end{<currenvir>}` is written as the
file's last line ("Writing text … before \end{…} as last line"), the text after it ignored ("Ignoring text … after
\end{…}"). The port matched the whole trimmed line (fancyvrb's rule, the former `capture_raw_lines_until`, now removed), so
`\end{tikzpicture}\end{filecontents*}` or `\end{filecontents}{b.tex}` captured the rest of the document (Fatal
`Document:Malformed`; Perl's unanchored regex, latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:4274/4292, ends there too).

**Rust** (batch 66d, `cache_filecontents`): the capture ends at the marker anywhere in a line, with LaTeX's two warnings;
a prefix of spaces only is neither written nor warned about (LaTeX writes it as a blank last line, with the warning,
latex.ltx:19055-19058, its spaces being of category other). Witnesses 1909.03404, 2311.02007,
2503.03764. Guard `perfect_kernel_batch66d::filecontents_ends_mid_line`; repro `macro-state/filecontents_end_midline`.

### 573. A driver with `\begin{document}` vetoes the preamble it inputs whatever their scores

Perl's main-file pick (Pack.pm:180-182) removes every `\input` argument from the candidates; the port honoured a veto
only when the vetoer scored at least the vetee's score (a 2-line `\input{main}` wrapper beside the real main.tex,
2307.13586). A driver that `\input{preamble}`s its `\documentclass` file scores lower than the preamble, so the preamble
was converted alone (Fatal `Document:Malformed`: 1402.3465, 2503.12837, 1505.07539, hep-th0609123).

**Rust** (batch 66d, main_tex.rs `find_main_tex` and its cortex_worker.rs copy): a vetoer with a `\begin{document}` line
vetoes unconditionally, as Perl; one without keeps the score gate. Guards
`main_tex::tests::{driver_vetoes_the_preamble_it_inputs, wrapper_without_begin_document_keeps_its_main}`.

### 574. The kernel's `\shorttitle`/`\shortauthor` aliases yield to the document's `\newcommand`

sect05.rs predefines `\shorttitle`→`\@shorttitle` and `\shortauthor`→`\@shortauthor` (Rust-only, for templates that read
them before `\author`, 2406.14142); latex.ltx has neither. A document's `\newcommand{\shorttitle}{…}` was refused as a
redefinition, and `\title[\shorttitle]{…}` then set `\@shorttitle` to the alias of itself (Fatal `Timeout:Recursion`:
1105.4905, 0909.2464; pdflatex and Perl 0).

**Rust** (batch 66d): the two aliases are kernel stubs (`DefinitionOrigin::Stub`), which `\newcommand` treats as
undefined, as the AAAI `\equalcontrib` stubs. Guard `perfect_kernel_batch66d::shorttitle_is_the_documents_own`; repro
`sectioning-frontmatter/shorttitle_newcommand_by_document`.

### 575. AMS-TeX's `\tag` recovers where TeX errs

AMS-TeX's `\tag` takes its text to the display's `$$` (`\def\tag#1$$`, amstex.tex:597-605) or, in a row, opens the
row's tag cell without an argument (`\def\tag{\global\tag@true…&&}` in `\align`, :633-635; `\def\tag{&}` in `\gather`,
:797). Perl's `\let\tag\eqno` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #643) errs on these shapes too, in its own way. Measured with pdftex
(TL 2025, `\input amstex`, `\input amsppt.sty`, `\document`; each shape followed by a paragraph and `\enddocument`):

| shape (in `$$\align … \endalign$$`) | pdftex | ours |
|---|---|---|
| `a&=b\tag 1\displaybreak c&=d` | 4 errors ("Extra alignment tab has been changed to \cr" twice, "Misplaced \crcr", "Misplaced \noalign": the measuring pass's tag cell is `\eat@{##}`, :655); tag "(1c)" | 0 errors, tag "(1)" on its row |
| `a&=b\tag 4\par\\ c&=d` | 8 errors, from "Paragraph ended before \align was complete" (`\csname align \endcsname#1\endalign`, :667/:687, not `\long`); the alignment is lost | 0 errors: the `\par` ends the tag cell |
| `a&=b\tag{3\par}\\ c&=d` | 9 errors (the same, and "Too many }'s") | 0 errors: the `\par` stays in the tag's text, `(3)` |
| `a&={b\tag 2} c\\ e&=f` | 100 errors ("Argument of \maketag@@@@ has an extra }" and "Paragraph ended before \maketag@@@@" twice each, 47 "Missing \cr inserted", 46 "Misplaced \cr", …), Fatal, no PDF | 0 errors: the `}` ends the tag cell, `(2)` |
| `a&=b\tag{5\\ c&=d` | 3 errors ("Paragraph ended before \align was complete", "Missing $ inserted", "Display math should end with $$"; "Forbidden control sequence found while scanning use of \align" when the `\outer` `\enddocument` follows the display); the alignment is lost | 1 error ("Missing } inserted before the row's end in \tag"); see below |
| `{\it … $$\align a&=b\tag{5\\ c&=d\endalign$$ …}` | 3 errors, as the row above; the alignment is lost | 1 error, as the row above; the `{\it` group and its text after the display kept |
| `\vbox{… $$\align a&=b\tag{5\\ c&=d\endalign$$ …}` | 4 errors (the same three, then "You can't use `\end' in internal vertical mode"), then Emergency stop; Fatal, no PDF | 1 error, as the row above; the `\vbox` and its text kept |
| `a&=b\tag{{3\par}5\\ c&=d` | 9 errors, as `\tag{3\par}\\` | 1 error, as `\tag{5\\`; the tag is "(35)" |
| `a&=b\tag{{5\\ 6}\par c&=d` | 7 errors (as `\tag 4\par\\`, less "Invalid use of \\"); the alignment is lost | 3 errors: "Missing } inserted …" twice, then "Missing { inserted" at the second row's `&`; the `}` after the row's end closes the next row's cell-template `{` (`$\displaystyle{##}$`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #908, 69c), and the `&` meeting the count −1 gets its `{` (tex.web §1127 `align_error`, 70b), so both rows are kept, "(5)" on the first (before 69c: 3, that `}` closing the display, the alignment lost; 69c: 2, the `&` taken for the cell end with no v-part) |
| `a&=b\\ c&=d\tag{5 e` and `\enddocument`, no `\endalign` | 3 errors ("Forbidden control sequence found while scanning use of \align" at the `\outer` `\enddocument`, amsppt.sty:1091; "Missing $ inserted", "Display math should end with $$"); the alignment is lost | 1 error ("Missing } inserted …"); the document ends; the open row's last cells are dropped, with or without a tag (RED `amstex/amstex_align_unclosed_at_enddocument`) |

On rows 1-3 and 5-10 TeX's errors are not `\tag`'s: they come from `\align` reading its body as a non-`\long` argument
and from the measuring pass. On row 4 they are the tag cell's own: its template reads the cell as `\maketag@##\maketag@`
(amstex.tex:678, :700), and `\maketag@@@@#1\maketag@` (:604) meets the `}` closing the group opened before the tag
("Argument of \maketag@@@@ has an extra }", then its runaway). Content comes first, so the row tag keeps the author's text
and errs only where the tag's text cannot end.

**Rust** (batch 66e, amstex.rs `amstex_tag`): in a row (an AMS-TeX alignment's, or a LaTeX equation row's when the
AmSTeX pool is loaded, which no `\tag#1$$` governs either) a `\par` outside the tag's own groups, or a `}` closing a
group opened before the tag (an enclosing group's `}` too), ends the tag cell with the text read so far and no error; it
is never read into the tag. A `\par` inside a group of the tag stays in its text if that group closes before the row's
end (`\tag{3\par}\\`, `\tag{{3\par}5…`). A row's or environment's end (`\\`, a token meaning `\cr`, `\endalign`, a
display end, `$$`, the document's end `\enddocument` or `\bye`) read while a group of the tag is open stops the scan at once (`\tag{5\\ c&=d\endalign$$`): TeX's
`\cr` inside a cell's braces is "Missing } inserted" (tex.web §1126-1127), so the tag raises it once per open group
(TeX does so at depth 1 and 2 only: at depth 3 or more `align_error`, tex.web:21562-21563, finds `abs(align_state)>2`
and reports "Misplaced \cr", dropping the `\cr`), or TeX's runaway error ("Paragraph ended before \tag was complete") when a `\par` was read in a group still open there;
it keeps the text up to the earlier of that `\par` and that end, closes its groups, and the input is read again from
there (`close_runaway_row_tag`, which retracts the kept braces from the alignment ledger). The file's end raises "File
ended while scanning use of \tag" with the same recovery. A `$` opening inline math inside a row's tag cell or a group
of the tag is paired with the `$` closing it, which is never the start of `$$` (`\tag{$a$$b$}\\`, `\tag $a$$b$\\`:
two inline maths, as in TeX's restricted horizontal mode, tex.web §1138); only the `$$` form's own level matches `$$` as
tokens (`\def\tag#1$$`). The document's end (`\enddocument`, amsppt.sty:1091, and `\bye`, both `\outer` in TeX) is never
read into a tag: in a row it is a row end as above; in the `$$` form it is TeX's "Forbidden control sequence found while
scanning use of \tag" and the call is dropped (tex.web §336-339). The next row, the alignment, an enclosing group, every later
paragraph and `\enddocument` are kept. Trade-off of this fail-safe rule: a row tag whose braces hold an inner
alignment's row end (`\tag{$\matrix a\\b\endmatrix$}\\`, which TeX sets, the inner `\halign` resetting `align_state`)
stops at that `\\`; no braced tag holding a row end, a `\par` or `matrix` occurs in a scan of 10,000 arXiv source zips
(9204-9608, about 1,000 braced tags). The `$$` form keeps TeX's errors (tex.web §395-396). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch66e::{amstex_row_tag_ends_at_every_row_ender,
amstex_row_tag_cell_ends_at_par_and_extra_brace, amstex_row_tag_open_group_stops_at_the_row_end,
amstex_tag_in_latex_equation_row_ends_at_extra_brace, amstex_tag_stops_at_the_document_end,
amstex_tag_inline_maths_are_not_a_display_end}`; repros `amstex/amstex_row_tag_runaway_group`,
`amstex/amstex_row_tag_open_group_in_enclosing_group`.

### 576. `\begin{document}` opens the `.aux` under the job's name, as latex.ltx's `\document` does (Perl: none)

latex.ltx's `\document` (:9491-9494) does `\if@filesw \immediate\openout\@mainaux\jobname.aux
\immediate\write\@mainaux{\relax}\fi`, so the `.aux` exists from then on. Perl's `\begin{document}` opens none; its only
open is `latex_base`'s `\openout\@mainaux\jobname.aux` (latex_base.pool.ltxml:722), run when LaTeX.pool loads. Without
a preload that is at `\documentclass` (TeX.pool.ltxml:33-39), after `\jobname` is installed (Core.pm:152), and the
in-memory `.aux` (TeX_FileIO.pool.ltxml:120-126) is found by a later `\input` (Package.pm:2104). With the format
preloaded (a preload such as `ar5iv.sty`, as on arXiv) it runs when the state is initialized (Core.pm:143), before
`\jobname`, so the stream is not under the job's name. Ours (latex_base.rs:743) ran at that early point too, or, under a
dump, at the dump's build, whose `output_file:*` streams the dump does not keep. A class or package `\enddocument` that does `\input
\jobname.aux` under `\if@filesw` (jpsj3.cls:90-96, bio.cls, lamuphys.sty:1240-1247, caosp.sty:916) then met
`Error:missing_file:<jobname>.aux`. Ours opens it in `\begin{document}`'s after-digest (latex_constructs/sect02.rs) in
latex.ltx's place, so the `\input` reads the in-memory `.aux` (its `\relax` and whatever the document wrote). `\nofiles`
stays Perl's no-op (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3773, sect11.rs), so `\if@filesw` stays true. Witnesses 2605.24927,
2605.04825, 2605.28673, 2605.20125, cond-mat9607109, astro-ph9805185 (each 1 error → 0, text unchanged). Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch66f::jobname_aux_exists_after_begin_document`; repro `loader/jobname_aux_exists_after_begin_document`.

### 577. nicematrix `[opacity=…]` fills are flattened against a white page

nicematrix.sty:5605-5616 (`\__nicematrix_color_opacity:w`) reads a `\CodeBefore` color command's optional argument as
keys: `opacity=` sets the PDF fill opacity (`\pgfsetfillopacity`) over whatever lies beneath. Our cell and row fills are
plain CSS background colors, so `opacity=o` is rendered as the color mixed with white at `o` — what the PDF shows on a
white page and the same on a white HTML page, but not over a colored or dark background. Perl has no nicematrix binding.
Witness 2605.25123 (`\columncolor[opacity=0.2]{blue}{3}`, "Unrecognized color model" Error before). Code
latexml_contrib/src/nicematrix_sty.rs (`nice_color`); guard `perfect_kernel_batch66f::nicematrix_color_opacity_key`.

### 578. `\hypertarget` in math: an empty anchor, its text after the mode test

hyperref.sty:4805-4811 (nesting off, its default :323) sets the destination and then `#2` in every mode
(`\hyper@@anchor{#1}{\relax}#2`); Perl (hyperref.sty.ltxml:258-266) digests `#2` as the anchor's own text in every mode.
In text ours keeps Perl's shape (the anchor holds its text, `anchor_own_text`). In math, where an `ltx:anchor` holds no
math, the anchor is empty and `#2` follows it in place, so a brace-less call takes one token there and a formula opened
by it stays whole (`\hypertarget{e1}` before `\left( \frac{n}{p}\right)`: 2606.15438's `\left(` read as the anchor's
text was closed at that argument's end, its `\right)` "Extra"). `#2` comes after the conditional: hyperref's own `#2`
sits before its `\fi`, so a brace-less `\hypertarget{e2}\frac{n}{p}` has `\frac` read `\fi` as its numerator
(pdflatex `\showbox`: the destination, an empty-over-n fraction, then p); ours renders n over p. A `\relax` before
`\ifmmode` (amstex.tex:72's `\RIfM@`) keeps a row-initial call in `align`/`aligned`/`array` on the math branch, where
TeX is still expanding in search of `\omit` before the cell's math begins. Open: the math anchor's `xml:id` is generated,
not the target's name, so a `\hyperlink` to it dangles, and the anchor parses as an operand (RED
`package-bindings/hypertarget_math_anchor_keeps_its_id`). Code hyperref_sty.rs `\hypertarget`/`\lx@hypertarget`; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch66f::hypertarget_braceless_in_math`.

### 579. The article/report/book bindings define `\fnum@figure`/`\fnum@table` as the tag LaTeXML composes (Perl: undefined)

article.cls:457/469 (report, book alike) define `\fnum@figure`/`\fnum@table`; Perl defines neither and composes the
tag in `\lx@@fnum@@` (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:1041-1056), which an undefined `\fnum@<type>` falls back to. Code that
takes their current body then found nothing: babel's ini caption templates (babel.sty:2959-2965
`\gdef\fnum@table{…{\[fnum@table]}…}`, for a language loaded on demand such as Lithuanian) captured the undefined token
itself, and the new `\fnum@table` called itself at the first caption (2605.29738: Fatal IfLimit; Perl loops too, KPE
#654). Ours defines each as `\lx@@fnum@@{figure}`/`{table}` in the article, report and book bindings, where LaTeX's
classes define them, and every caption's tag is the one composed before; a class or package `\def`/`\renewcommand` of
them works as in LaTeX. Residual: letter.cls, without floats, defines neither, but has no binding, and the OmniBus it
falls back to loads the article binding; so a letter-based class's `\newcommand` of them (newlfm.cls:1006/1012), which
LaTeX accepts, is ignored with an Info `Ignoring redefinition`, and its captions keep the composed tag. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch66h::babel_ini_caption_template_needs_fnum`.

### 580. The algorithm2e binding loads no float package (Perl: float)

algorithm2e.sty loads no float package: its float is its own `\@float{algocf}` (algorithm2e.sty:2487-2488). Perl's
binding requires float (algorithm2e.sty.ltxml:37), and so did ours, which put float's binding where TeX has none. Beside
floatrow (floatrow.sty:34 marks float loaded and carries its interface) that replaced floatrow's `\float@end` with
float_sty.rs's no-op whichever came first — after floatrow, float's binding redefined it; before, floatrow's
`\newcommand`s were refused — and every restyled float's box stayed open (`\endgroup` errors; 1811.04370, 2007.08784,
1609.05867, 1910.09976, 1807.05059: five of the nine floatrow papers of the run-347 `\endgroup` drill-down; the other
four load float themselves after floatrow, which floatrow.sty:34 makes a no-op in LaTeX, KPE #668, open). The binding's
float frames and top caption are float_sty.rs's Rust helpers (`add_float_frames`, `reposition_caption_top`), which need
no load. A document using float's commands (`\restylefloat`, `\newfloat`) with algorithm2e and without
`\usepackage{float}` now finds them undefined, as in LaTeX. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch66m::algorithm2e_beside_floatrow_keeps_floatrows_end`.

### 581. `\lstinline` is robust (Perl: expandable)

listings.sty:1941 `\newcommand\lstinline[1][]{…}` is `\@protected@testopt`: under `\@unexpandable@protect` it stays
unexpanded. Perl's `\lstinline` (listings.sty.ltxml:54) is an expandable macro, and ours was too: its expansion opens
the inline listing's group (listings_sty.rs `\lx@lstinline` `bgroup()`, as Perl's `$STATE->getStomach->bgroup`), so in
our engine an `\edef`/`\xdef` that should keep it ran it. ifthen's `\ifthenelse{\equal{\lstinline|N|}{}}` evaluates
its test in an `\xdef` (ifthen.sty:101-110), and the group it opened met the `\endgroup` after it (ours: 1406.5453
729 errors, 1605.05104 89; Perl's run of the repro gives 0, its recovery not traced). Ours defines it `protected`. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch66m::lstinline_robust_in_ifthen_equal`.

### 582. IEEEtran's convenience `\keywords` yields to the document's (Perl: locked)

IEEEtran.cls (1.8b) defines no `\keywords`; the binding's (`\keywords{…}` or `\keywords … \endkeywords` as the
keywords block, Perl IEEEtran.cls.ltxml:398-403) is a convenience Perl locks, so a document's
`\newcommand{\keywords}{M-estimators, …}` was refused and `\keywords` in `{IEEEkeywords}` opened a second keywords
block whose end met the environment's `\endgroup` (KPE #664; 2006.10005, 2008.05854, 2011.04315). Ours defines it with
the `Fallback` origin (#408, `is_definable_latex`), unlocked: the document's definition wins, and without one the
convenience works as before. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch66m::{ieeetran_document_keywords_macro_wins,
ieeetran_keywords_fallback_still_works}`.

### 584. A bare `\endX` ends only an environment's frame (Perl: any frame of the same mode)

Perl's bare `\endX` (Package.pm:1970-1975) pops the top frame if it binds the environment's mode. Ours ends the mode only
when the top frame is an environment's — a bare `\X`'s (`lx@env@bare@end`), a `\begin{X}`'s (`lx@env@begin@end`) or one a
group's end handed back (`lx@env@ended@by@group`); any environment's, since amsmath ends a `\equation*` display with
`\endequation` (tcolorbox `ams equation*`, 2211.17024). A frame no environment opened (a box's) is left alone with one
Warning, as LaTeX's list-ending `\endX` does no group work. Witnesses 2301.00752, 2602.19492 (IEEE Open Journal keywords
boxes; the body was read into the box). KPE #674; guard `perfect_kernel_batch66t::bare_end_without_its_begin_keeps_the_box`.

### 586. A list's frame is ended by the group around it (Perl: an Error, the rest swallowed)

`\list`/`\@trivlist` open no TeX group (latex.ltx), so the `\lx@list` mode frame they open (OD #180) is LaTeXML's alone.
Ours marks it a bare environment's frame, ended by `\endlx@list`: a `}` or `\endgroup` meeting it ends the list first
(stomach.rs `close_environment_frame`, an Info) and then its own group. Perl's frame has no such mark: `\end{X}`'s
`\endgroup` meets it ("Attempt to close a group that switched to mode internal_vertical") and the rest of the document
goes into the last item. `\endlx@list`, not `\endlist`: a group's end does not undo `\list`'s global `\@listdepth` step.
Witnesses astro-ph9806019 (iopconf `\references`), 0902.3464 (jT `resume`), 2106.10067 (INFORMS `\Trivlist`); KPE #676;
guards `perfect_kernel_batch66x`.

### 587. A MetaPost figure gets the fonts dvips would download (Perl: the figure fails to convert)

MetaPost's default PostScript (`prologues:=0`) is not self-contained: its text is `(S) cmmi10 9.96265 fshow`, the fonts
are named by their TeX names and listed only in `%*Font:` header comments, which dvips reads to download them when it
includes the figure (`finclude.pro` supplies `fshow`) — so arXiv's PDF shows them. Ghostscript alone stops at
`/undefined in cmmi10`; Perl's ImageMagick path and ours reported `Error:imageprocessing:failed_to_convert` and left the
figure out (about two thirds of the run-349 image-conversion Error papers; 40/40 sampled were MetaPost). Before converting,
ours does what dvips does (`latexml_post/src/postscript_fonts.rs`, called from `graphics.rs` `convert_image`): a copy of
the figure gets, before its `%%EndProlog`, each listed font's Type1 program (TeX Live's `pdftex.map` entry, the `.pfb`
through kpathsea, inlined as PFA), its TeX name bound to the font, and MetaPost's own `prologues:=1` `fshow`; the copy is
converted and removed. Fonts whose map entry re-encodes (`ptmr8r`) or is missing are not supplied — the figure fails as
before. Witnesses gr-qc0001079 (`foliation.ps`), math0102124 (38 figures), cs0005010 (34): each E → 0; guard
`postscript_fonts::tests::metapost_figure_gets_the_fonts_dvips_would_download`.

### 588. Under the ar5iv preload, `\url`/`\href` are hyperref's when nothing defined them (Perl: undefined)

arXiv's build loads hyperref into every paper (a 00README `nohypertex` opts out; 2101.07380's PDF says "LaTeX with
hyperref" though its source never loads it), so a paper that uses `\url` or `\href` with neither url.sty nor hyperref
loaded builds there; pdflatex alone, Perl and we stopped at "Undefined control sequence" (812 `\url` + 473 `\href`
papers live in run 349, ~80% of a 40-paper sample loading neither package). Provide-only (user ruling 2026-10-14): the
ar5iv preload (`latexml_contrib/src/ar5iv_sty.rs`) queues `\lx@arxiv@provide@hyper@urls` at `\begin{document}`, which
defines whichever of the two is still undefined as hyperref's (`hyperref_sty.rs` `define_hyper_urls`, shared with the
hyperref binding), with url.sty's default `\UrlFont`/`\UrlLeft`/`\UrlRight` where missing. A paper that loads either
package, or defines the command itself in its preamble or in an `\AtBeginDocument` hook, keeps its own; nothing is
supplied without the ar5iv preload, and hyperref is not loaded for every paper (the rejected option). The supplied `\url`
is locked as the hyperref binding's is (OD #500), so a `\renewcommand\url` in the document body is ignored with an Info.
hyperref loads url.sty, so url.sty is then loaded provide-only too (67q): its `\path`, `\urlstyle`, `\urldef` and `\Url`
for the names still undefined. An elsarticle-num `.bbl` defines `\path` only when `\href` is undefined, and its
`{\path{doi:…}}` entries were undefined once `\href` was supplied (2605.07373, 2605.08166, 2605.12003). Witnesses
cond-mat0407333, cs0409028, hep-th0411273, 1001.4826 (`\doi` → `\href`); guards `perfect_kernel_batch67a`.

### 589. Paul Taylor's `diagrams`: a diagram is a math array of its objects and arrows (Perl: `<ERROR>{diagram}</ERROR>`)

diagrams.tex/.sty (v3.97, www.PaulTaylor.EU/diagrams; not in TeX Live, in arXiv's tree: `\diagramstyle` 467, `\newarrow`
441, `\rTo` 362 papers undefined in run 349) had only Perl's ar5iv-bindings `diagrams.tex.ltxml`, which discards every
`{diagram}` body and puts `<ltx:ERROR>{diagram}</ltx:ERROR>` in its place; `\newarrow` and the arrow commands were
undefined. Ours (latexml_contrib/src/diagrams_tex.rs, modelled on amscd's `{CD}`) keeps the diagram, its surface taken
from the package manual (manual.tex v3.97) and checked against the 100 witness papers' use:
`\begin{diagram}[opts]`/`\diagram … \enddiagram` is an `XMArray` (`name=diagram`, `datameaning=commutative-diagram`)
whose cells are the objects and arrows (`&`, and `\\` as the package's `\cr`, diagrams.tex:729/739: no `[dim]`, a row
may begin with a bracket, math0109209, math0403203); outside maths it is a `$$` display (plain TeX's `\input diagrams`
too, math0105166), in restricted horizontal mode (a `c` cell, an LR box: math0010298, math0109209) or with `[inline]` an
inline formula, with `[LaTeXeqno]` a numbered `equation` (manual FAQ "Display options", "Options"). An arrow
`\<dir><Name>` (r l u d ru rd lu ld) reads what the source's reader reads: inside a diagram (`\CD@PB`, diagrams.tex:290-299)
`[opts]`, a span `(x,y)`, the labels `^ _ < > ~`, a `.` and a positional `{f}{g}`; outside one (`\switch@arg`, :301-306)
only `^ _ [ . ~` and `{`, so `$X\rTo (0,1)$` keeps its pair as pdflatex prints it (a diagonal shorthand used in text,
`\nNE` = `\ruTo(2,3)`, prints its span `(2,3)`, where TeX prints the default span as well, `(2, 2)(2, 3)`). The label sides are the manual's ("Labels": above=left,
below=right on verticals, the reverse on negative-gradient diagonals); a positional `{g}` after `^f` is the lower label,
after a lower label it ends the arrow (`\positional@`, :578). A horizontal or diagonal arrow is a stretchy `ARROW` with
its labels as scripts (amscd's `\lx@amscd@stack`, plus the role `ARROW` on a superscript-only stack so `$A \rTo^f B$`
parses as a relation), a vertical one has its labels beside it (amscd's `\lx@amscd@adjacent`). An arrow and
`\diagram` test the mode when digested, not when expanded (the source's arrows begin with `\relax`), so one at an
alignment cell's start, met by the look-ahead for `\omit` before the cell's maths begins, is in that cell's maths
(`&\rTo` in `align*`, math0404431).
`\newarrow{Name}{tail}{filler}{middle}{filler}{head}` (diagrams.tex:449, local definitions, ignored with a Warning in
maths) draws each direction with the Unicode arrow of its components (`|--->` ↦, `C--->` ↪, `>--->` ↣, `----{>>}` ↠,
`===={=>}` ⇒, `<--->` ↔, `.....` ⋯/⋮, `33333` ≡, …; an unknown component the plain arrow, no component nothing,
math0310311); the source's predefined arrows and synonyms (section (24): `\rInto`, `\hLine`, `\NW`, …) are defined, a
synonym under its own name. `\pile` is a one-column array. `\diagramstyle[opts]` or `\diagramstyle{opts}` (one argument
when no `[` follows, :282-285; math0403203) and the package options set the drawing; their `amstex` (manual "Options",
`\cds@amstex`) loads the amscd binding for `{CD}` (math0104206, math0403203). That is a substitution: the source's
`\cds@amstex` (diagrams.tex:627-628) makes `\CD` mean `\diagram[amstex]` and `@` active throughout the document, so
`@>>>`, `@VVV` are read by the diagrams code; ours are amscd's, the same syntax, and `@` keeps its catcode outside `{CD}`. `\newarrowhead/tail/middle/
filler`, `\newdiagramgrid` and `\HonV`/`\VonH`/`\HmeetV` draw nothing (layout).

Recoveries and losses, each against what TeX does:
- **A horizontal arrow in text** (`Text \rTo\ word`): TeX's `! Commutative Diagram: "$" inserted before horizontal
  map.` (`\CD@nB` → `\CD@E`), then its inserted `$` runs on to the paragraph's end. Ours raises that Error and sets the
  arrow alone as a `$…$` formula, so the text after it stays text. After an earlier map TeX's wording is `between
  vertical map and horizontal map` (`\CD@YF` holds the previous map's name); ours always says `before`.
- **A vertical arrow outside a diagram**, in maths or text (`$A \dTo B$`, `A \dTo{} B`): TeX's `! Commutative Diagram:
  vertical map ignored outside diagram.` (`\CD@pB` sets `\CD@ZD` to `\CD@LK`, diagrams.tex:488; the message :497-498),
  with no `$` test, and the arrow is dropped. Ours raises that one Error and keeps the arrow, the author's content flagged
  by the Error, as for a horizontal one (main-session ruling 2026-10-14, content first); in text it is set as a `$…$`
  formula without a further Error.
- **A diagonal arrow outside a diagram** (`A \ruTo{} B`): TeX raises nothing (diagonals go through `\Vector@Map`/`\CD@HK`,
  not `\CD@nB`) and prints junk such as `(2, 2)`. Ours raises nothing and draws the arrow, in text as a `$…$` formula.
- **A `\pile` in text** (`A \pile{\rTo^a\\ \lTo_b} B end.`): its cells are set in text mode, so each arrow is the
  horizontal-arrow Error (2) and the paragraph's rest goes into the formula (`tex="$\rTo^{a}$\\ $\lTo_{b}$B end. …"`);
  TeX's `"$" inserted between horizontal map and pile`, and its maths runs on too. No content is lost on either side.
  Residual.
- **Inside a diagram, an `(x,y)` or `[opts]` after a label** (`\rdTo^f(1,2)`) is not read (the `!any_label` test in
  `read_arrow_labels`); the source's `\CD@PB` loop (:290-299) reads them in any position. No witness; residual.
- **A text arrow's `[…]` that is no option list** (`$f\colon X\rTo [0,1]$`; the test: it begins with a letter) and a
  `(…)` in a diagram that is no span (`\rTo (B & C)`) stay in the formula; TeX reads them as options (warning "\relax
  inserted before `[0'") and as a span.
- **The pullback corners** `\SEpbk`, `\SWpbk`, `\NEpbk`, `\NWpbk` (diagrams.tex:1314-1331 `\make@pbk`) are a visible mark
  (⌟ ⌞ ⌝ ⌜ at the cell's corner) that we do not emit; the witnesses type them mid-expression (math0203179:674/848/1052
  `X\times_Z\SEpbk Y`, math0306018:825/1572), where an inline token would disturb the parse. Open; the proposal (a class
  on the cell, the corner drawn by CSS) waits for the end-of-goal CSS review.
- **Not implemented**: the `eqno=` option (its equation number is dropped), `\diagraminline`, the dotted-shaft `.` after
  an arrow (read, but the arrow drawn solid), `\diagram[amstex]` inside one diagram (the `@` commands of `\CD@O`),
  `\puncture`, `\lessthan`/`\greaterthan`, `\commdiag`, the `\HorizontalMap`/`\VerticalMap` family; the positional-label
  message ("labels as positional arguments are obsolete") is not given.
- **The `tex` attribute** is a reconstruction: a plain-TeX `\diagram … \enddiagram` reverts as `\begin{diagram} …
  \end{diagram}` (the shared matrix code's form); `\nNE`-style shorthands revert to `\ruTo` without the span, an
  arrow's options are dropped, and labels revert in the canonical syntax (`\uTo^m_n` as `\uTo<{m}>{n}`).
- **A `\\` inside braces in a cell** (`{A \\ A'} & \rTo & C`) splits the row silently; TeX's `! Missing } inserted`.

**Why**: content — every commutative diagram of these papers was lost. Witnesses math0001049, math-ph0001006,
math0003019, math-ph0007001, math0010298, math0012073, math0102115, math0104065, math0104175, math0104206, math0105166,
math0109209, math0203179, math0306018, math0310311, math0403203, math0404431, cs0204036; repros
`package-bindings/diagrams_*`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch67d`.

### 590. pict2e keeps the `\@tempdimd` of its pre-2020 versions and its graph-code layer (Perl: raw pict2e, TL 2025)

pict2e before v0.4b (2020/09/30, "use of fewer system dimension registers", pict2e.dtx:3317-3318) allocated
`\@tempdimd`; TeX Live's own ellipse.sty:95 and longfbox.sty:107, which load pict2e, still use it, so TL 2025 pdflatex
fails on both ("Undefined control sequence", 101 errors on a one-ellipse document; 0 with `\newdimen\@tempdimd`). Our
pict2e binding (`latexml_package/src/package/pict2e_sty.rs`) allocates it when undefined, loads trig as pict2e.sty:123
does in its mode > 0 branch (`\CalculateSin`/`\UseCos`), and binds the graph-code layer ellipse.sty drives directly
(pict2e.sty:164-217: `\pIIe@add@nums`, `\pIIe@add@CP`, `\pIIe@addtoGraph` with the pdftex operator names) onto the
native path, so an ellipse's Bézier arcs are drawn; a path ended by `\pIIe@fillGraph` (`\fillpath`, `\ellipse*`,
`\polygon*`) is one filled, unstroked `ltx:line` (`\lx@pic@polyline`'s mode `2`, as `\circle*` fills). Witness 2109.06028 (`\lfbox` around every hexdigest: run 349 Error
with 643 errors, then Fatal at the same-error cap once other errors no longer interleaved); run 349 had 23 papers with
undefined `\CalculateSin`/`\UseCos` and 18 with undefined `\pIIe@addtoGraph`. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch67g::pict2e_ellipse_has_its_old_registers_and_trig`.

### 591. A math-alignment row its author tagged is kept even when its cells are empty (Perl: dropped with its tag)

pdflatex prints a tag on its own row: amsmath's `\notag \\ \tag{29}`, and Scientific Word's eqnarray
`… \nonumber \\ && \TCItag{27}`, which SW uses for every wrapped numbered equation. Perl drops these rows together with
their tags, in three places (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #682). Here, a row whose `EQUATIONROW_TAGS` were set by
`\lx@equation@settag` counts as tagged: `tags` together with the `reset` from its retract
(`Template::has_explicit_tags`, `latexml_core/src/alignment/template.rs`). Such a row is never pruned as empty
(`normalize_prune_rows`), and its element carries the internal `_tagged` attribute (`TAGGED_ROW_ATTRIBUTE`, stripped
at finalization). eqnarray's `rearrange_eqnarray` treats a tagged empty row as it already treated a numbered labelled
one (#54, 63j): in a multi-column eqnarray it joins the unnumbered equation above, which then carries the tag, or stands
alone when that equation has a number; in an eqnarray using a single column (nlin0106009's (27), whose formula sits in
the third column only) it stands as its own equation holding the tag, as in align and gather. amsmath's `rearrange_ams_align`/`rearrange_ams_gather` (`empty_row_keeps_number`) keep it as an equation
holding only its tags, which is where pdflatex prints it. An auto-numbered empty row still goes, as in Perl: the
trailing `\\` of an eqnarray or align (pdflatex prints an empty numbered line in both, an accident of the markup),
and an inner `\\ \\`. Witness nlin0106009: its 11 tag-only rows (27), (32b-d), (34d), (37), (46b-d), (53a-b) were lost
once 67j made `\TCItag` amsmath's `\tag`. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch67j::{ams_tag_only_row_keeps_number,
tcilatex_tcitag_tags_eqnarray_rows, trailing_row_without_tag_is_still_pruned}`. RED residuals: `\TCItag` in
`eqnarray*` or after `\nonumber` on its row prints a number pdflatex does not (tcilatex 5.0 `\@@eqncr` prints
`\@taggnum` only under `\if@eqnsw`; repro alignment/tcitag_in_unnumbered_row_prints_nothing); amsmath `\tag{z}\notag`
on one row loses the tag, as in Perl (repro alignment/ams_tag_then_notag_keeps_tag).

### 592. A binding standing in for a class or package takes the algorithm packages from the paper's copy of that file

The algorithm packages differ between copies of one class or package, by version and by the paper's own edits: every
ICML style as distributed loads `algorithm` and `algorithmic` (icml2016.sty:70-71 … icml2025.sty:95-96), and papers
that use algpseudocode comment `algorithmic` out of their copy (icml2024.sty:94 "removed due to conflict with
algpseudocode", 2402.05403), since loading it first bails algorithmicx (algorithmicx.sty.ltxml:9-12, Perl alike) and
leaves `\State`/`\For` undefined; WileyNJD-v2.cls:3331 and WileyNJDv5.cls:6820 load `algorithm, algorithmicx,
algpseudocode` (one copy `algorithm2e`, 2002.02812); bmvc2k.cls `algorithm` with `algorithmic` or with `algpseudocode`
by year; pnas-new.cls:110-111 `algorithm` and `algpseudocode[noend]`; edited copies of neurips_2023.sty (2402.18905)
and siamltex.cls (2210.03478) load them where the distributed files load none. Perl has no binding for the classes and
scans the paper's copy from OmniBus (Package.pm:2776-2813), so for them this is Perl's own behaviour. For icml20xx.sty
it is beyond Perl (as pdflatex): Perl's `FindFile_aux` tries the versioned-name fallback binding before a raw copy it
is not interpreting (Package.pm:2135-2138; the glued suffix `[vV]?[-_.\d]+`, :2180, maps icml2017 to icml.sty.ltxml),
which loads the distributed pair whatever the copy says (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #684). Our bindings
stand in for them (icml_support_sty.rs `load_icml_style` for icml2016-2025, icml2019_sty.rs after its raw read, icml_sty.rs
when it answers a versioned fallback such as `icml2026` or `./icml2018`; wileynjd_cls.rs, bmvc2k_cls.rs, pnas_new_cls.rs,
siamltex_cls.rs, neurips_sty.rs), and loaded either the distributed ICML pair or no algorithm package at all. Now each
calls `shipped_class::require_shipped_algorithm_packages`: the dependency scan (`require_dependencies_only`,
content.rs) of the file being loaded (the load's `\@currname`, or the request a versioned fallback answers,
`fallback_request`), kept to `ALGORITHM_PACKAGES`, so the copy's choice, order and options win; without a copy, the
ICML binding keeps the distributed pair and the others load none (as OmniBus has nothing to scan).
Perl's icml_support.sty.ltxml, reached by name from icml.sty.ltxml for `\usepackage{icml}`, still loads the pair; Perl's
neurips.sty.ltxml loads none, and a shipped neurips.sty copy now adds its algorithm packages (beyond Perl, as
pdflatex). The scan's comment pattern also drops a comment on a last line without its newline (Perl's `s/%[^\n]*\n//gs` keeps it), which a
`{filecontents}` copy has. Run 349: `\State` 560, `\For` 470, `{algorithm}` 544 papers. Witnesses 1706.03643,
1706.04918, 1706.04933, 1706.04964, 2002.06473, 2106.05074 (icml); 1810.03033, 1810.12033, 2106.06046, 2402.13183,
2506.07013 (Wiley); 2210.06270, 2210.01640 (bmvc2k); 2402.10236 (pnas-new). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch67l::{icml_style_copy_decides_the_algorithm_packages, icml_style_without_a_copy_keeps_the_distributed_pair,
wileynjd_class_copy_loads_its_algorithm_packages, wileynjd_class_copy_with_algorithm2e,
bmvc2k_class_copy_loads_its_algorithm_packages, icml_versioned_fallback_follows_the_copy,
neurips_copy_loads_its_algorithm_packages}`.

### 593. In maths an old font command switches the math alphabet to the group's end, as latex.ltx's `\@fontswitch` (Perl: the alphabet takes the next token)

latex.ltx's `\DeclareOldFontCommand#1#2#3` is `\DeclareRobustCommand#1{\@fontswitch{#2}{#3}}` (14309-14311), and
`\@fontswitch` (14312-14321) in maths lets `\math@bgroup` to `\relax` before `#2\relax`: the alphabet `\mathrm\relax`
reads the `\relax` as its argument and selects its math group to the end of the enclosing group, so `{\rm LP-HF}` is
`LP-HF` upright. Article/book/report/letter's `\cal` and `\mit` are `\@fontswitch\relax\mathcal` / `\mathnormal`.
Perl's `\@fontswitch` (`\ifmmode #2\relax\else #1 \fi`, latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:5200) and `\DeclareOldFontCommand`
(a closure returning the bare `#3`, :5315-5320) run the alphabet with its own grouping, so it reads the next token
(KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #685). We follow latex.ltx: `\@fontswitch` is `\ifmmode\lx@math@alphabet@switch{}{#2}\else#1\fi`
(sect13.rs), and an old font command's maths branch is `\lx@math@alphabet@switch{<its name>}{#3}`. The switch merges the
font an alphabet's binding carries (`font => {…}` on the constructor or primitive, kept on the definition as
`Definition::declared_font`: `\mathrm`, `\mathbf`, `\mathcal`, `\mathbb`, every `\DeclareMathAlphabet`'d one) into the
current font, as the native `\rm`/`\bf` primitives do in maths (plain_constructs.rs), and reverts as the old command's
name (`{\rm LP-HF}`; through `\@fontswitch` directly, as the alphabet: `{\mathcal H}`). The name travels as a character
string, so an `\edef` in maths cannot expand the command into itself. In TeX the `\relax`'d `\math@bgroup` makes
any alphabet `#2` expands to a switch, so the switch looks through parameterless macros with a token body and
`\protect` (a robust command's `\protect\X␣`) up to 16 deep (`math_alphabet_font`): `\newcommand\Bbbx{\mathbb}`
`\DeclareOldFontCommand{\bbx}{\normalfont}{\Bbbx}` makes `{\bbx RZ}` a blackboard R and Z, as pdflatex sets them
(`\U/msb/m/n/10`). A `#2` that reaches no font-carrying alphabet that way — a macro with an argument, a closure-bodied
macro, a body that begins with anything else (`\def\Bbbx{\relax\mathbb}`) — is TeX's `#2\relax`, which is
latex.ltx's behaviour when `#2` is not an alphabet and a residual when it is one reached otherwise. The text branch is latex.ltx's `#1` (Perl's `#1 ` set a space after `{\cal x}`'s `\relax`). It shows when a
raw-loaded class or package re-declares the old font commands: under the ar5iv rawclasses lever 511 outputs had an
empty `\math..{}` (ptptex 306, jpsj2 98, paper 71, artikel1 12) and about 8 papers new errors; under the bound article
classes `\rm` is the native switch and was already right. Witnesses jpsj2 cond-mat0510381, 0711.1066, 1004.2823;
ptptex gr-qc0605108, 0804.3840, 1101.1147, hep-th0507073; paper math0405417. Repro
fonts-nfss/old_font_command_switches_math_alphabet; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch67r::{old_font_command_switches_the_math_alphabet,
old_font_command_switches_package_and_declared_alphabets, old_font_command_alphabet_through_a_macro}` (repro
fonts-nfss/old_font_command_alphabet_through_a_macro).

Residual (deferred): through `\@fontswitch` directly the box reverts as the alphabet, so a multi-token group's `tex=`
does not round-trip: `{\cal AB}` reverts as `{\mathcal AB}`, which TeX reads as `\mathcal{A}B` (base: `{\mathcal{}AB}`,
with the content wrong too). There is no standard switch form of `\mathcal`, and `\@fontswitch\relax\mathcal` round-trips
only under `\makeatletter`. The only direct `\@fontswitch` users in TeX Live's standard classes are article.cls:497-498
`\cal`/`\mit` (and the book/report/letter copies), which the kernel binds natively (reverting as `\cal`); a sound
round-trip would revert as `\cal`/`\mit` when `#2` is `\mathcal`/`\mathnormal` and that command's current robust body is
exactly `\@fontswitch\relax<alphabet>`.

### 596. amsthm's `{proof}` is kept against a class or package that copies it (Perl: the file's environment replaces it)

amsthm_sty.rs locks `\proof` and `\endproof` against the class and package files (`:locked@files`, state.rs
`name_carries_lock`), as the kernel's `\endabstract` (sect05.rs) and `\minipage` (sect12.rs) are, but only against a
COPY of amsthm's interface (`\proof:locked@copies`, state.rs `files_lock_holds`): a redefinition whose first parameter
is an optional argument with a non-empty default (`takes_optional_first`) — amsthm.sty:431's own
`{proof}[1][\proofname]`, which smfart.cls:1194, smfbook.cls:1281, ijmart.cls:336 or thuthesis.cls:4052
(`[1][\thu@proof@name]`) re-implement over a `\trivlist`. A robust copy (`\DeclareRobustCommand\proof[1][\proofname]`)
is judged by its inner `\proof␣`, as `owns_calls` judges a robust binding (its own meaning is the parameterless
`\protect\proof␣`); an ltcmd copy (`\RenewDocumentEnvironment{proof}{O{\proofname}}`) is not read as one and goes
through (no TeX Live file defines the proof either way). Perl locks nothing there (amsthm.sty.ltxml:146-192,
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #690). A copy's `\renewenvironment{proof}` is skipped (`\renewenvironment` reads `lock_holds_against`,
sect08.rs), its `\newenvironment` after a clearing `\let\proof\relax` is refused and the binding put back
(`install_definition`, `let_i`; guard `perfect_kernel_batch67s::package_redefined_proof_keeps_the_binding`), and the
proof stays `<ltx:proof>`, titled from the optional argument or else the refused copy's own default
(`record_redefined_default`, `\proof:redefined@default`, recorded only under this lock; it is never empty, an empty
default not being a copy), so the class's language and name still title it (smfart.cls:1288 "Démonstration",
thuthesis's `\thu@proof@name`); with no copy refused, `\proofname`. A redefinition with a head of its own — no optional argument, or an empty default
(fascicules.sty:142 "Démonstration:", NotesTeX.sty:124, beautybook.cls:1211, thmbox.sty:214 `[1][]` with `\proofname\
#1`, a raw `\def\proof{…}`) — goes through with the head text and end mark it wrote; the end half `\endproof` follows
its begin half (locked while `\proof` is still the binding's). The lock keeps the binding only while its proof is in
force: once the document (or a definition the lock let through) has replaced or undefined `\proof`, it lapses and later
definitions go through as in LaTeX (amsart, the document's `\let\proof\undefined\let\endproof\undefined`, then a
package's `\newenvironment{proof}[1][Nachweis]`: pdflatex "Nachweis."; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch67ps::proof_lock_lapses_once_the_document_undefines_it`). 0705.0545 (the same `\let`, then the
author's nccthm.sty:173 `\newcommand*{\proof}[1][]`) goes through on the copy rule alone, its default being empty
(`perfect_kernel_batch67ps::proof_lock_passes_an_empty_default`). It is not set by a borrow (`require_package_borrowed`, theorem.sty's and
ntheorem.sty's bindings: LaTeX has no amsthm proof there, so a class's `\def\proof` after `\RequirePackage{theorem}`
stays its own), nor by the real load that follows a borrow when a file or the document has already put its own proof in
place (amsthm.sty:431's `\newenvironment{proof}` fails over it in LaTeX; the binding then leaves `\proof`/`\endproof`
alone, with an `Info:ignore`). The document's own `\newenvironment{proof}`/`\renewenvironment{proof}` is honoured, as in
LaTeX and Perl (an author `{proof}` in paper.cls papers), and so is a class's redefinition made from an
`\AtBeginDocument` hook, which runs with the document's origin (rawclasses study R7): GT.cls:1469-1470 `\let\proof
\relax` at class level, then its copy `\newenvironment{proof}[1][\proofname]` inside `\AtBeginDocument` (:1488-1494),
so 2503.05183 keeps the class's trivlist (as on a03442572a), a residual of this rule. apxproof builds on the binding's
proof: its parameterless wrappers (apxproof.sty:393-417 `\def \proof`, sending a `theoremrep`'s proof to the appendix,
read back as `\begin{axp@oldproof}`) are not copies and go through, so apxproof_sty.rs needs no lift of the lock
(witness 2502.18805, whose 53 proofs otherwise stayed in the body). Residuals of a kept copy: its head layout, font,
case and punctuation do not carry (smfart's ` — ` after the head, ijmart's slanted head, isamms's small caps;
theoretics.cls:418's `\MakeTextUppercase{#1}`, so 1609.05867's "PROOF SKETCH." is "Proof Sketch."), and its end mark is
the binding's ∎ (theoretics's red `\blacksquare` `\qedsymbol`; a copy that prints no QED gets one). The lock covers the
names `\proof`/`\endproof` only: a file's `\newtheorem{proof}` after amsthm still defines the `\begin{proof}` that
`\begin` looks up first and makes a `<theorem>`. Under the raw-class lever 86 papers had lost every proof (smfart 72,
ijmart 11, smfbook 3; witnesses 1711.11547, 1902.02049, 2108.12000); without the lever the copies in papers' own classes
keep their proofs (jloganal.cls 1202.3460, theoretics.cls 1609.05867, gtart_h.cls math0003189, gtart.cls math0203159,
math0302254, math0412216, smfart.cls 2309.14926; not GT.cls 2503.05183, the `\AtBeginDocument` residual above). Repros
package-bindings/{amsthm_proof_kept_against_a_class_renewenvironment, amsthm_proof_lock_lets_a_hardcoded_head_through,
amsthm_proof_copy_titled_by_its_default, amsthm_proof_lock_lapses_after_the_document_undefines_it,
amsthm_proof_lock_passes_an_empty_default, amsthm_proof_lock_holds_against_a_robust_copy,
theorem_borrowed_proof_yields_to_a_class_def}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch67s::{class_renewed_proof_keeps_the_binding,
package_redefined_proof_keeps_the_binding, document_renewed_proof_is_honoured, apxproof_wraps_the_locked_proof}`,
`perfect_kernel_batch67ps::*`.

### 597. Under sn-jnl, program.sty's programbox `\(`…`\)` stays inline maths

The older sn-jnl.cls copies load program (sn-jnl.cls:311 of 1812.02207's copy, :621 of 1911.08756's; 106 of 148
sampled copies), and sn_jnl_cls.rs's scan of the class now loads it, for the `\gt`/`\lt`/`\union` its papers use
(138 run-353 papers). program.sty:175-176 also redefines `\(` as `\begin{programbox}` (a `\textwidth` minipage around
a `{program}`, :165-173), which the papers of these copies write as inline maths; pdflatex sets them in the line
(2112.05038 on 413 lines: "For a domain Y ⊂ Rn, there exists…"), where the raw emulation made each an `ltx_minipage`
inline-block holding a one-item `ltx_trivlist` list (1331 in 2112.05038). sn_jnl_cls.rs puts the kernel's `\(`/`\)`
(`\lx@begin@inline@math`, sect07.rs) back after the class's loads when program loaded; program's other definitions,
the active `;` included, stay. Program loaded under another class, or by the document's own later
`\usepackage{program}` (the test sits in the class binding, right after its scan), keeps the programbox. The faithful
alternative was to drop the two lines (every `\(…\)` an inline-block). Approved by the main session 2026-10-15: the
class, not the author, loads program; the authors write inline maths; content and semantics first. Perl's scan loads
no program (no binding), so its `\(` is the kernel's and `\gt` is undefined. Repro class-bindings/snjnl_class_copy_loads_program; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch67u::snjnl_class_copy_loads_program`.

### 598. kluwer's overprinted symbols are their Unicode characters (Perl: no kluwer binding; the class draws them)

kluwer.cls:162-176 composes `\lsim`/`\gsim` from a raised `<`/`>` over a `\sim`, `\nequiv` from `\not\equiv`, and the
double-struck `\dC`, `\dP`, `\dN`, `\dR`, `\dZ`, `\dQ` from overprinted letters and rules (`\dR` is `I\!\!R`, a box of
two letters). kluwer_cls.rs defines each as the symbol it draws, as the astronomy bindings set `\la`/`\ga`
(aa_support_sty.rs): ≲ ≳ ≢ and ℂ ℙ ℕ ℝ ℤ ℚ, with their meanings (`less-than-or-similar-to`, `reals`, `integers`…).
The faithful port made two letters and a kern of `\dZ` in the formula, which neither reads nor parses as one symbol;
the PDF shows one glyph. Approved by the main session 2026-10-15 (round-1 open question). Papers: `\gsim`/`\lsim` 14/13
(astro-ph0309194, astro-ph0510296, astro-ph0401471), `\dZ`/`\dR`… (math0308074, math0212055, astro-ph0410557).
Repro class-bindings/kluwer_class_commands; guard `perfect_kernel_batch67y::kluwer_class_commands_are_defined`.

egpubl.cls:1000-1008 (v4.0, 2609.32222's copy) `\copyrightTextTitPag{<text>}` stores the copyright line its title

(`\lx@add@copyright`, a `<ltx:date role="copyright">`), where the copyright of every other binding goes; the

given to it twice. Its running-page copy (`\copyrightTextRunPag`) stays page furniture. Approved by the main session
