### 603. A `\section` opening Wiley NJD's `{boxtext}` is the box's head (Perl: no Wiley binding)

WileyNJD-v2.cls:466-475 (`\BX`, an `\fbox` round a `\vbox`), WileyASNA-v1.cls:267-271 and WileyNJD-v1.cls:281-285 (an
`{mdframed}`) frame the body of `{boxtext}`; wileynjd_cls.rs frames it as framed.sty's `{framed}` (a
`<ltx:logical-block framed="rectangle">`; framed.sty is the binding's vehicle for the frame, no version loads it), and
rebinds `\section` inside it: a `\section` or `\section*` in the box is the box's head, a bold line inside the frame
(`\lx@wiley@boxhead`), as the PDF shows it ("BOX TITLE" in the box; 1811.09505, 2012.13740). A section in the frame
cannot end at the box's end: it took the framing attributes and every later paragraph, acknowledgement and biography
of the document. The class itself has `\let\section=\boxhead` commented out at :467. Only `\section` is rebound: the
390 witness papers put 10 `\section`s in a `{boxtext}` and no other level (a `\subsection` there is still a framed
subsection that runs past the box). WileyNJDv5.cls:592-608 frames the arguments of `{boxtext}[1]` and
`{boxwithhead}[2]` (boites' `{breakbox}`, :6244), the body following the box; the binding frames them the same way.
Repros class-bindings/wileynjd_v2_class_commands, wileynjdv5_box_environments, wileyasna_funding_in_text; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch67w::wileynjd_v2_class_commands`, `::wileynjdv5_box_environments`, `::wileyasna_funding_in_text`.
Approved by the main session 2026-10-15 (round-1 open question).

### 604. oup-authoring-template's `\figalttext` alt text is kept as the image's description (the class drops it)

The newer oup-authoring-template.cls copies define `\figalttext[short]{long}`, a figure's alternative text for
accessibility, as `\newcommand\figalttext[2][]{\relax}` (2602.07066's copy :1935): pdflatex prints nothing, and a
faithful binding would drop it. The alt text is author content written for accessibility (about 1,000 words in
2608.22901), which HTML can carry where PDF does not, so the binding gives it acmart's `\Description` treatment (#83):
the shared float_description.rs mechanism (`define_float_description`, `float_description_tokens`; `\lx@acm@description`)
makes the short text the lone image's `description` (`@alt`) and the long one a hidden note in the caption that the
image's `aria-describedby` names, a plain long text alone the `description`, and on a float of several images both on
the float, with acmart's Warning naming `\figalttext`. Defined only where the paper's copy defines it (TL 2025's copy,
of 2022, has none), so a paper whose copy does not can define its own. Ruling: main session 2026-10-15 ("author content
for accessibility — keep it on the figure image's description, as acmart's `\Description` does"). Witnesses 2608.22901,
2608.14294, 2609.06413 (their words come back: 13,753 → 12,706 → 13,752 for 2608.22901, base → 67z → 67z r2). Perl has
no oup-authoring-template binding; it raw-loads the class and drops the text. Repro
class-bindings/oup_v2602/oup_figalttext_is_the_images_description; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch67z::oup_figalttext_is_the_images_description`.

### 605. The dependency scan skips a package the document marked loaded (`\ver@<name>.<ext>`; Perl: records only)

A binding's dependency scan (`content.rs::require_dependencies_filtered`, Perl `maybeRequireDependencies`,
Package.pm:2776-2810) stands in for the scanned file's own `\usepackage`/`\RequirePackage`/`\LoadClass` lines, and LaTeX
skips such a line when `\ver@<name>.<ext>` is defined and not `\relax` (latex.ltx:18750 `\@onefilewithoptions` →
`\@ifl@aded`, :18397-18402). The scan now does the same for a candidate our own records (`_loaded`/`_raw_loaded`) say
is not loaded, with `Info:dependencies:<file> Skipping dependency <file>: it is marked loaded`
(`marked_loaded_unrecorded`). The marker may come from the document, from a class or package read raw (memoir's
`\EmulatedPackage`, imakeidx.sty:61 `ver@makeidx.sty`, xcolor.sty:315 `ver@color.sty`) or from a binding (biblatex's);
LaTeX skips the line for each alike. Perl tests only its records (Package.pm:2328-2330), so it would load the package — the
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #780 gap, latent there. Witness 2201.11056: sn-jnl-setup.sty suppresses sn-jnl.cls:311's
`\usepackage{program}` through `\AddToHook{class/sn-jnl/before}`, which our scan loaded (active `|`, pgf broken,
`oom`). Scan-only by ruling (main session 2026-10-16): `\usepackage`/`\RequirePackage` keep the records-only test (user
ruling 2026-10-14, no general loader `\ver@` rule — floatrow_sty.rs records float/rotfloat loaded rather than setting
their markers, ams_support_sty.rs reads amsart.cls's own `\ver@amsthm.sty`, subcaption_sty.rs describes a document's
`\@namedef{ver@subfig.sty}`). Repro loader/scan_skips_document_marked_loaded_package; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch68f::scan_skips_a_package_the_document_marked_loaded`.

### 607. breqn's displays are equations and equation groups; breqn.sty is not read raw (Perl: no breqn binding)

breqn.sty (TL 2025 v0.98l) typesets each display by measuring and re-breaking boxes (:441-1700) and loads flexisym.sty,
which replaces the math characters' mathcodes by macros (flexisym.sty:178-400): read raw, the formulas would lose their
symbols' meaning, and the breaks are the renderer's to make. The binding (latexml_contrib/src/breqn_sty.rs) keeps the
structure: `{dmath}`/`{dmath*}` are `{equation}`/`{equation*}` with their keys (:383-436; `label` a `\label` with the
pending `labelprefix`, `number` a `\tag`, the layout keys ignored), `{dgroup}` the subequation group amsmath's
`{subequations}` makes, its options the breqn keys (:1793, a `label` the group's, :1808): numbered equations are
(2a), (2b) and the group's own number is not printed, a group of `{dmath*}` prints its number (2) once, as breqn prints
the group number only when its equations are unnumbered (:1861, :1880; the HTML checked against pdflatex), `{dgroup*}`
an unnumbered `ltx:equationgroup` of its equations (:1778-1783), `{dsuspend}` text of the group (:2027-2041),
`{dseries}`/`{dseries*}` one `ltx:equation`, numbered or not, holding the series' in-line formulas and the text between
them (:1724-1748), and the display parameters with breqn's types and values (:179-198: registers, `\eqindent` the
macro `C`). breqn.sty:47-48's amsmath and graphicx are loaded as it loads them. Divergences: no automatic line
breaking; the punctuation breqn's `\end{dmath}` moves into the display (`\check@punct@or@qed`, :654-659) stays after
it; blank `{dsuspend}` lines join the group's text paragraph. The stub's `missing_file` notice stays, saying so.
Witnesses 0903.2087, 1008.1366, 1107.4667, 1111.2451, 1201.6197, 1606.07330, 1706.02708, 1811.11912, 2008.13194,
1805.03313, 2607.02409 (labelled `{dgroup}`s). Repros package-bindings/{breqn_display_environments,
breqn_group_label_and_parameters}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch68b::{breqn_display_environments,
breqn_group_label_and_parameters}`.

### 608. hyperref's index page numbers and url's `\Url@FormatString` are text (no PDF page anchors, no url math)

hyperref.sty:8019-8068 `\hyperpage{95}` (makeindex's encap under `hyperindex`) parses ranges and lists as hyperref does
but sets each page number as text: `\HyInd@pagelink` (:8062) links it to the PDF page anchor `page.95`, which an XML
document has none of, so the link would dangle. url.sty:127-133 `\Url@FormatString` sets `\Url@String` in math with the
url font so that it may break at the `\Url…Breaks` characters; here, as the binding's `\url`, it is the url font's text
(the JOSS/pandoc template's `\href@Urllike`, 1902.08702). Witnesses 0712.1142, 1011.1558, 1902.08702. Perl defines
neither (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #750, #752). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch68b::{hyperref_internals_called_by_papers,
url_format_string_and_tilde}`.

### 613. llncs's `\switcht@albion` restores this binding's English names, not the class's

llncs.cls:79-117 `\switcht@albion` sets the class's English names, which the class also sets at load (:117): "Abstract.",
"Fig.", "{\bf Keywords:}", "Acknowledgments.", "Table of Contents". This binding keeps its own names (article's
"Abstract", "Figure", "Contents"; its `\keywordname` `\textbf{Keywords}`, to which `\keywords` adds the colon, and
`\ackname` "Acknowledgements"), and llncs_cls.rs's `\switcht@albion` restores those, captured at the end of the class's
load (`\edef` of the current meanings), so a paper or package that calls it (pscproc2.sty:5: 0905.3107, 0908.0239,
1006.0809) or patches it (the Springer template's `\edef\switcht@albion{\relax\unexpanded\expandafter{…}}`:
1812.03939, 1812.03953) changes nothing it had not, and no name gets a second colon or period from the binding's own
punctuation. `\switcht@deutsch`/`\switcht@francais` give the class's German and French names (:121-197) in the same
forms (`\keywordname` without the colon, `\abstractname`/`\ackname` without the run-in period). Taking the class's
names at load would be a separate change to every llncs paper's headings (not made). Repro
class-bindings/llncs_class_internals; guard `perfect_kernel_batch68a::llncs_class_internals`.

### 614. llncs's `\@spothm` alias counter is emulated, not aliascnt's; the paper's copy picks the version

`\@spothm{env}[base]{caption}{capfont}{bodyfont}` (the class's shared-counter branch of `\spnewtheorem`, and its
`\spn@wtheorem` under `envcountsame`) differs between the shipped copies (18 versions, v2.2 to v2.26, in 1,250 arXiv
llncs papers): v2.2-v2.14 `\@namedef{the#1}{\@nameuse{the#2}}` and `\@spthm{#2}` (the env steps `base`,
hyperref's type: an envcountsame lemma autorefs as "Theorem 2"); v2.16-v2.23 `\newaliascnt{#1}{#2}` and `\@spthm{#1}`
(the env steps its own alias of `base`'s counter: the same number, its own type, "Lemma 2"); v2.24-v2.26 (TL 2025) also
`\if@envcntsect\@addtoreset{#1}{section}\fi`, which resets `base` by the section through the alias. That reset matters
where `base` is not `theorem` (already reset under `envcountsect`): `\spnewtheorem{hyp}{Hypothesis}…` with
`\@spothm{conj2}[hyp]…` prints "Hypothesis 1, Conj 2" in each section in v2.26 and "Hypothesis 3, Conj 4" in section 2
in v2.20 (pdflatex with each copy). llncs_cls.rs reads the paper's copy of llncs.cls (`shipped_class_text`, its
`\@spothm` body: `\newaliascnt`, `\@addtoreset`) and defines that version's `\@spothm`; without a copy, v2.26's.
Divergence: the v2.16+ copies load aliascnt.sty, this binding does not (`\@ifpackageloaded{aliascnt}` is false; main
session ruling 2026-10-16). Its `\lx@llncs@newaliascnt` is aliascnt's `\newaliascnt` (aliascnt.sty v1.5): `\c@`, `\the`,
`\theH`, `\p@` let to `base`'s, `\AC@cnt@` and `\cl@` defined as aliascnt.sty :54-57 defines them (so a paper
loading aliascnt itself can `\aliascntresetthe` the class's alias), the alias recorded for the numbering and hyperref (`register_counter_alias`, shared with
aliascnt_sty.rs) — without aliascnt's `\@addtoreset`/`\@removefromreset` patch, which maps a `within` alias to its root.
A `\newcounter` of the alias after `\let\c@<env>\relax` (2303.08726) drops the alias, as LaTeX's fresh `\c@<env>` does
(`new_counter`). All 27 shared-counter declarations of 19 sampled envcountsect papers use `[theorem]`. Repros
class-bindings/llncs_theorem_numbering_envcountsame_envcountsect, llncs_spothm_section_reset{,_v220_copy},
llncs_autoref_envcountsame{,_v214_copy}, llncs_alias_newcounter; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch68g::{llncs_numbering_envcountsame_envcountsect, llncs_spothm_section_reset,
llncs_spothm_section_reset_v220_copy, llncs_autoref_envcountsame, llncs_autoref_envcountsame_v214_copy,
llncs_alias_newcounter}`. Witnesses 2202.10090, 2601.04573 (`\@spothm`), 2412.05162 (`\let\c@case\relax` before
`\spnewtheorem{case}[theorem]`), 2303.08726 (`\newcounter{case}` of the alias), 1612.00484.

### 615. llncs: a paper's `\newtheorem{x}{X}[section]` prints "X 1.1", not the PDF's "X 11"

llncs.cls:1058 `\edef\@thmcountersep{}` (`.` only under `envcountsect`, :1140) is the separator kernel `\newtheorem`'s
`\@xnthm` puts between the section and the theorem number (latex.ltx `\@thmcountersep`), so outside `envcountsect`
pdflatex prints a paper's own `\newtheorem{x}{X}[section]` (or `\spnewtheorem{x}{X}[section]{…}{…}`) as "X 11" for
section 1's first. This binding keeps the kernel's `.`: "X 1.1", as Perl prints it. Main session ruling 2026-10-16:
semantics over the PDF — "11" cannot be told from the eleventh, and a `\ref` to it reads as one. 5 of 374 sampled llncs
papers with a main file are affected (68g round 1). Minimal trigger: `\documentclass{llncs}`
`\newtheorem{x}{X}[section]` `\section{A}\begin{x}a\end{x}` — pdflatex "X 11 a", both engines "X 1.1".

### 616. An ORCID iD given as its orcid.org address is the iD (Perl: the contact holds the text as written)

The kernel's `\lx@add@orcid` (base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_fields.rs) makes the iD a link, `https://orcid.org/<iD>` (html_feedback #6571).
An author who writes the address instead of the iD (`\orcidauthor{https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6534-6641}{…}`,
2104.12510; `http://`, `www.`, a bare `orcid.org/…`, a trailing `/`) got `https://orcid.org/https://orcid.org/…`. The
address's iD is taken (`\lx@orcid@id`, `orcid_id`), for every class whose `\orcid`-like setter routes there (acmart,
svmult, ceurart, cas, revtex, egpubl, pasj00, mrm's three-argument `\author`), and for the two inline links that build
the address themselves: mrm's `\orcid` (mrm_cls.rs) and apa7's `\addORCIDlink` (apa7_cls.rs; apa7.cls:322-326 builds
`https://orcid.org/#2`, so pdflatex shows and links the doubled address). An argument holding a macro, or text that
is no orcid.org address (2106.08963's swapped `{Andrew S. Nencka}`), is kept as written. orcidlink.sty's
`\orcidlink{https://…}` stays doubled, as orcidlink.sty builds `https://orcid.org/#1` (the kernel `\lx@orcidlink` is
its link, without the normaliser). Perl's `\lx@add@orcid` (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:659-660) puts the text in the
contact with no link, so it has no doubled address to fix. Repros sectioning-frontmatter/{orcid_given_as_url_is_the_id,
orcid_inline_link_takes_the_id}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch68h::{orcid_given_as_url_is_the_id,
orcid_inline_link_takes_the_id}`.

### 617. caption formats the kernel's float captions through `\lx@format@caption@@`; a line-breaking separator is the text's first break

caption.sty replaces latex.ltx's `\@makecaption` (caption.sty:206; caption3.sty:1661-1715 `\caption@@@make`): the label
is the label format applied to the type's name and number, then the label separator, the fonts and the text format
caption's options set. The kernel's float caption (`\@caption@@@`, sect09.rs) and longtable's (longtable_sty.rs) now
format through `\lx@format@caption@@{type}{text}`, which is `\lx@format@title@@` until caption_sty.rs takes it
(`caption_format_tokens`): with no caption setting for the type and a non-empty text, the class's title format is
used unchanged (`\format@title@<type>`); otherwise, in a group, `name=` defines `\<type>name`, `labelformat=` the
type's `\fnum@<type>` (`original`/`default` keep the class's), `labelsep=` the title format's separator (an empty
text has none, caption3.sty:1680-1683, empty as `\caption@ifempty` tests it, :1713-1748: nothing left once spaces, a
leading `\ignorespaces` and `\label{…}`/`\index{…}`/`\glossary{…}` are taken away), `font=`/`labelfont=`/`textfont=`
add `\caption@font@<name>` to `\fnum@font@<type>` and `\format@title@font@<type>` (caption v1's size options replace
`font=`, caption.sty:124-129), `textformat=` wraps the text (`empty` keeps its `\label`s). `figurename=`/`tablename=`
are also added to the current language's `\captions<language>`, as newfloat's `\newfloat@setname` does
(caption3.sty:1344-1345, newfloat.sty:179-188), so babel keeps them. The package options are passed to
`\captionsetup` as written (caption.sty:171-172; `\ProcessOptions` reads the option list as latex.ltx:18557's
`\protected@edef`, content.rs), so a robust command in a value (`figurename=\textsc{Fig}`) stands, and the caption v1
keywords are matched against the option as written (caption3.sty:374-399 hands the list on by `\@expandtwoargs`,
another `\protected@edef`), so the robust command's body does not run at package load; subcaption's the same.
subfig reads the key expanded, as subfig.sty:125 and :217 `\edef` the list (a robust command whose body is undefined
then errors, as in pdflatex), and passes the value as written, where subfig.sty's `\edef` would expand it. A name
of `\protect` and a robust command is the tag's name (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #194). The separator is the `ltx:tag`'s `close` attribute, text only: a separator caption declares as
breaking the line (`\caption@LabelSeparatorWithNewline`, caption3.sty:769, :782, `newline`) is put as the caption
text's first `\\` (`<ltx:break/>`) and the tag gets none. Not carried: sub-captions keep their packages' formats
(subcaption_sty.rs, subfig_sty.rs; the general keys do not reach them, nor the `[sub]`/`[subfloat]` separator);
`\captionsetup[longtable]{…}` (caption's `longtable` type, caption.sty:1167) is not read for longtable's captions,
which take the `table` settings ("Table 1." where pdflatex prints "Table 1 LT one." for `labelsep=space`);
`\caption*` takes its fonts and text format since 78l (`\lx@format@scaption@@`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1063); `\caption{{}}` counts as empty
(the kernel's label hoist, sect09.rs `\@hack@caption@`'s delimited read, strips the group; pdflatex "Figure 1:");
the relative sizes `smaller`/`larger`, the spacing fonts and `hypersetup` are no fonts here, and the layout keys
(`format`, `justification`, margins, `singlelinecheck`) stay stored and unread. Perl's binding reads none of the keys
(KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #795). Witnesses 1306.0788 (`labelsep=space`), 2002.05188 (`labelsep=period`), 1810.00606
(`labelformat=empty`), math0609211 (caption v1's `it`). Repros captions-floats/{caption_keys_set_the_label_and_separator,
caption_option_values_unexpanded, caption_names_survive_babel, caption_empty_text_ignores_label,
caption_option_key_is_read_unexpanded, protected_robust_name_is_a_name_noun}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch68h::{caption_keys_set_the_label_and_separator, caption_option_values_unexpanded,
caption_names_survive_babel, caption_empty_text_ignores_label, caption_v1_size_option_is_the_caption_font,
caption_option_key_is_read_unexpanded, protected_robust_name_is_a_name_noun}`.

### 619. rotating's `\rotdriver{<driver>}` loads no driver file

rotating.sty:64 `\def\rotdriver#1{\makeatletter\input{#1.def}\makeatother}` inputs a graphics driver; 42 arXiv papers
call `\rotdriver{dvips}` (0704.0929, 0704.1238, 0802.2495; `{dvitops}`, `{textures}`). Under the latex + dvips the
papers were written for, dvips.def is already the driver and the call changes nothing; under pdflatex it replaces
pdftex.def's image rules with dvips's, and the paper's PDF and PNG images are lost (TL 2025 probe: `example-image` then
needs an `.eps`). LaTeXML's graphics have no driver files (graphics.sty's driver options select none, graphics_sty.rs),
so rotating_sty.rs reads the driver name and loads nothing: the images stay. Perl's binding lacks the command
(KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #803). Repro package-bindings/rotating_rotdriver; guard `perfect_kernel_batch68i::rotating_rotdriver`.

### 620. tocbibind names the bibliography after the class's sectioning and writes its heading as `\<unit>*{\tocbibname}`

tocbibind.sty:115-123 sets `\tocbibname` to `\bibname` when the class defines it, else `\refname`. LaTeXML defines a
`\bibname` for every class (sect11.rs) and natbib's binding a `\refname` (natbib_sty.rs), so the test would pick
"Bibliography" in an article; tocbibind_sty.rs tells the class's name by its sectioning instead, as the standard
classes pair them: `\bibname` with chapters (book, report: pdflatex "Bibliography", also under natbib), else `\refname`
(article "References"). The heading `\t@cb@bchapsec`/`\t@cb@bsection` (:133-152) is a conditional, which the
bibliography constructor cannot read as a heading (`begin_bibliography_clean` reads `\bibsection` as `\<unit>*{<title>}`),
so at the document's start the binding writes the heading those conditionals select in that form —
`\chapter*{\tocbibname}`, `\section*{\tocbibname}` (the unit `\tocotherhead` names as of `\begin{document}`; the
real `\t@cb@bchapsec` reads `\@tocextra` when the bibliography is set, so a later `\tocotherhead` does not reach the
bibliography's heading), unstarred under `numbib` — where tocbibind sets `\bibsection` (:154-159, :184-198).
`\tocfile{<title>}{<ext>}` (:263-271) is a TOC of `<ext>` titled `<title>`; after `\tocsection` (:313-315) in a class
without chapters it follows a numbered `\<unit>{<title>}` instead, untitled (pdflatex "1 List of Algorithms", then "2
Intro"). Residual: the bibliography's number — under `numbib`, or under `\tocsection` for a class without chapters
(pdflatex "3 Literature") — is not modelled: the constructor strips the heading's star and numbers no bibliography, so
it stays "Literature". The chaptered witnesses (1605.05950 book, 2204.09786 scrbook) are unaffected: a class with
chapters ignores `\tocsection`. Repro package-bindings/tocbibind_names_and_tocfile; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch68i::{tocbibind_names_and_tocfile, tocbibind_book_bibliography_is_bibname}`.

### 623. svmult's `\greeksym{<letter>}` is the Greek letter the Symbol font has at that letter

svmult.cls :987 `\newcommand{\greeksym}[1]{\usefont{U}{psy}{m}{n}#1}` sets its argument in the Symbol font, whose
encoding (Adobe Symbol) puts the Greek alphabet on the ASCII letters: `\greeksym{D}` prints Δ, `\greeksym{m}` μ
(1111.1183's `\newcommand{\uDelta}{\mbox{\greeksym{D}}}`, 0903.0562). LaTeXML's fonts carry no Symbol-encoding map, so
the faithful definition writes the ASCII letter in a `symbol` font — "D" — losing the letter the PDF shows.
svmult_cls.rs maps a single ASCII letter to its Symbol-encoding Greek letter, upright (`symbol_font_greek`: a α … z ζ,
A Α … Z Ζ, with j ϕ, J ϑ, v ϖ, V ς as the encoding has them); any other argument keeps the faithful `\usefont` form.
Repro class-bindings/svmult_aas/svmult_class_commands; guard `perfect_kernel_batch68k::svmult_class_commands`.

### 624. amsppt's author list is one creator a name; the addresses after a block naming several pair with its names in order or are shared

**Background.** amsppt.sty:322-326 `\author … \endauthor` sets one centred box, so a paper names its authors in one
list (`Nobuo Hara and Kei-ichi Watanabe`, math0002054; `S.Yu.Orevkov, V.M.Kharlamov`, math0002213); a second
`\author` replaces the box, while amsguide.tex:547 has each author tagged separately, followed by the address(es)
associated with that author. The addresses are apart from the names: `\address` numbers each in `\addresscount@`
(:330-335), `\curraddr` joins the current one, `\email`/`\urladdr` pair with it under the same number (:336-370,
amsppt.doc:852), and `\enddocument@text` prints them, in order, after the paper (:1106-1116); an `\email` before any
`\address` (`email0`) is never printed. `\affil` is one box under the names (:327-329).

**Perl behavior.** amsppt.sty.ltxml:57 `\lx@add@author{#1}`: one creator holding the list, every address and email on
it (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #819); ours flagged it `frontmatter:merged_creators` (247 class-less run-353 papers with no other
error).

**Rust behavior.** amsppt_sty.rs parses each block as a per-author class's `\author` is (amsart's,
ams_support_sty.rs): `\lx@add@authors@append`, one creator a name, split only where the line reads as names, a
list-wide brace group unwrapped; every block's names are kept (the PDF shows the last block's only). A block naming one
person is followed by that person's contacts, attached to the last creator as before. The contacts after a block
naming several are that block's (main-session ruling 2026-10-16): when the block is followed by as many addresses as
it names people, the i-th address and what pairs with it (`\curraddr`, `\email`, `\urladdr`) are the block's i-th
person's (`label=author:N`); otherwise they stay together, in order, on the shared creator below the authors (#159), as
the PDF prints them (math0002213's three addresses for two names). The count is the block's own, known once its
contacts are read, so each label is `\lx@amsppt@paired{<block>}{<n>}`, read when the frontmatter is digested
(`digested_author_count`); the `\affil` box and an `\email` before any `\address` are the block's shared contacts
(`label=addresses:block`). The separators between the creators are synthesized from their order, amsart's `,\ ` and
`\ and\ ` (the flush's `before`), not the ones written: the kernel's splitter drops each name's separator
(`split_author_line`) and its flush sets every later creator's `before`, so `Roger Temam$^{1, 2}$ \& Shouhong
Wang$^1$` (chao-dyn9304004) reads "… and …" and `A and B and C` "A, B and C". A byline's "by" before the names
(`\author by Arkadiusz P\l{}oski \endauthor`, alg-geom9305006), which TeX prints and the kernel's splitter drops, is
the first creator's `before` ("by "; a later block's first creator's is the flush's separator).

**Why.** Content and semantic markup: one creator per person as every class binding gives, and no address given to a
person amsppt does not tie it to. Residuals (the kernel's cautious name split, shared with amsart): a names line with
`\footnotemark` in it (`Huai-Dong Cao \footnotemark and Lei Ni\footnotemark`, math0211283, math0301047, math0304096,
math0405036), `,\␣\&\␣` separators (math0408166, math0410384) and a `\footnotetext` inside the list (0711.1928 and six
more by the same authors) stay one creator, flagged. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch68r::{amsppt_author_list_is_one_creator_a_name,
amsppt_extra_address_is_shared, amsppt_author_blocks_pair_their_addresses, amsppt_author_byline_is_kept}`.

### 629. A refused printing `\title` called inside the document's `{titlepage}` prints there (Perl: no visible title)

When a class, style or the document `\def`s a `\title` that typesets its argument where it stands instead of storing
it — cernart.cls:217 `\def\title#1{\vskip1em\begin{center}\normalsize\bf#1\end{center}\vskip1.5em}`, asp2006.sty:157,
pdproc.sty:61, gr-qc9404034.tex:96 `\def\title#1{\begin{center}{\large #1}\end{center}}` — the lock refuses the
definition (state.rs, `\lx@dropped@title`, `\title:redefined`) and the kernel's `\title` keeps the title for the
frontmatter. Outside a titlepage that is the PDF's output: the frontmatter's title is placed first, where those
setters print. Inside `{titlepage}` pdflatex prints the title on the cover, and the HTML shows the cover in place of
the document's `<ltx:title>` (LaTeXML-structure-xhtml.xsl:374-375, Perl's :358-359), so Perl and the base showed no
title at all (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #828). Now the `{titlepage}` the document lays out (not a `\maketitle` deposit's,
which builds no `ltx:titlepage`) sets `lx_titlepage_cover`, and a `\title` called in it runs the class's own refused
`\title` at the call, its output kept on the cover (sect05.rs `titlepage_class_call`, `titlepage_class_run`, Info
`frontmatter:titlepage`), then the kernel's part (the structured title stays: metadata, hidden by the XSLT rule),
whose vocabulary is defined (`dropped_class_setter`). Whatever else the class's `\title` does: a run that typesets
nothing (a frontmatter setter, dp_delphi.cls `\def\title#1{\xdef\@title{\@title \par #1}}`, hep-ex0404013) shows
nothing at its call and is undone — its assignments rolled back (`AssignmentJournalGuard::rollback`), its diagnostics
held and discarded — so it keeps its value only through the kernel's `\title`, as outside a titlepage; one that stores
and prints (`\def\title#1{\gdef\@title{#1}\centerline{#1}}`, review probe p2; cernphprep.cls:285, the CERN preprint
header and title of the ALICE/COMPASS papers 1205.3963, 1205.5121, 1503.00681, 2112.00610) keeps what it printed and
stored, as in pdflatex (round 1 ran only a `\title` that stores nothing, `class_command_stores`, and showed 0 titles there). A class
`\title` that calls a saved kernel `\title` hands the title to the frontmatter once (`\lx@titlepage@kernel` skips the
kernel's part); when no assignment journal can open, a `\title` that may store is not run. The print is the class's
typesetting of an argument the kernel's copy also digests, so the kernel's copy owns the argument's side effects:
`\thanks`, `\footnote`, `\label` and `\index` are `\@gobble`d and `\footnotemark` is `\relax` during the print
(`COVER_PRINT_GOBBLED`, the list of the `\maketitle` deposits and of `replay_class_setter`) — before, a `\label` in the
title argument labelled `<ltx:document>` (a `\ref` rendered the title text, pdflatex "See .") and a `\thanks` made a
second `ltx:pubnote` (probe p5). The bindings' own `\title[]{}` (revtex4_support — `\documentstyle{revtex}`,
gr-qc9404034 —, ams_support, iopart_support, mn2e_support) take the same rule (`\lx@titlepage@class@call`). Only
`\title`: the XSLT hides no other field beside a titlepage, so a refused printing `\author`/`\address` there
(gr-qc9404034.tex:97-98, cernart.cls:220) is not run — the frontmatter's `ltx:creator` is its one displayed copy. The
title-ink dedup never searches a document with a titlepage (#146).

The print stays only on a cover that stays one. It is built between two empty Rust-only marker elements
(`\lx@cover@title@begin`/`@end`, reverting as nothing; `ltx:_CoverTitleBegin_Capture_`/`ltx:_CoverTitleEnd_Capture_`,
`base_utilities/frontmatter/field_ink.rs` `COVER_TITLE_BEGIN`/`COVER_TITLE_END`): `_Capture_`-suffixed, so the model admits them anywhere
and no paragraph opens or closes for them, and the paragraph trims reach past them (document.rs
`is_empty_capture_mark`; the frontmatter position mark too) as if they were not there. One helper,
`drop_cover_title_ink(scope)`, removes everything between each pair in document order — elements and bare text alike
(`\def\title#1{#1}` in the cover's open paragraph, probe p9) — with the marks and the wrappers left empty; an unmatched
mark goes alone. It is called wherever a `{titlepage}` stops standing in for the document's `<ltx:title>`, which the
HTML then displays: `\unwind@titlepage` (`\begin{titlepage}\title{X}\maketitle\end{titlepage}`, probe p13: 2 visible
titles in round 1), `demote_stranded_titlepage` (a titlepage after body content, #257), and at `\end{document}`
`settle_cover_title_ink` (`\lx@finalize@document`), by the XSLT's own test: while the document has a top-level
`ltx:titlepage` (its title hidden) the marks are removed and the print kept, wherever the cover's typesetting put it
(hep-th0010274's `\vbox{\center\LARGE{#1}}` print set beside an emptied cover); without one (a titlepage nested in a
section or box, every cover unwound or demoted) the print goes.
A stray mark never reaches the output (the core finalize drops an empty `_Capture_` element). Witnesses 0904.2708
(cernart), gr-qc9404034: 0 → 1 visible title, 0 errors either side. Repros sectioning-frontmatter/
{titlepage_refused_title_prints_on_the_cover, titlepage_unwound_cover_drops_the_class_title_print,
titlepage_demoted_cover_drops_the_class_title_text, titlepage_class_title_print_gobbles_label_and_thanks,
titlepage_storing_class_title_prints_on_the_cover}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch68t::{titlepage_refused_title_prints_on_the_cover,
refused_title_outside_titlepage_is_the_frontmatter_title, refused_storing_title_in_titlepage_prints_nothing,
binding_title_in_titlepage_runs_the_refused_printing_title, stranded_titlepage_drops_the_class_title_print,
titlepage_unwound_cover_drops_the_class_title_print, titlepage_demoted_cover_drops_the_class_title_text,
titlepage_class_title_print_gobbles_label_and_thanks, titlepage_storing_class_title_prints_on_the_cover,
titlepage_class_title_calling_the_kernel_title_adds_it_once}` (HTML: one visible title).

### 634. A raw class's keywords reach the frontmatter: the `\keywords` its abstract defines for its body, and a `{keywords}` that only typesets a label (Perl: undefined, or the class's run-in heading)

**Perl behavior**: the kernel's `{abstract}` is locked (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1130-1142: `\begin{abstract}` is
`\lx@begin@abstract`, `\abstract` locked), so under raw class loading a class's own abstract code never runs, and a
`\keywords` the class defines only there is undefined — wiley-article.cls:446-489 (`\NewEnviron{wiley@abstract}
{\newcommand{\keywords}[1]{…}…}`, `\renewcommand{\abstract}{\wiley@abstract}`; nbdt-article.cls:430-473 the same),
astlb.cls:91-205 (the abstract's body collected into `\abstract@toks`, `\endabstract` calling `\maketitle`, whose
`\@maketitle` typesets it inside `{pazhabstract}`, the only place `\def\keywords##1` is made; pazhastl, pazhb, pazhb_eng,
pazha2, astrobul the same), mtt.cls:176-181 (its own `\renewenvironment{abstract}[1][ru]{…\def\keywords##1…}`). A class
`{keywords}` whose begin code only typesets a label (paper.cls:621-627 `\def\keywords{\small\paragraph*{\keywordname:}}`)
is the class's run-in heading; OmniBus (OmniBus.cls.ltxml:126-156), used when the class is not read raw, makes any
`{keywords}` the keywords.
**Rust behavior**: K11 (frontmatter_stores.rs) serves the table's keywords setters (`STORE_SETTERS`: `keywords`,
`keyword`, `kword`, `kwd`, `terms`) in these two shapes too, each found by a check on what the class defined, never a
name pattern. (1) The kernel abstract's body begins with `\lx@abstract@class@setters` (base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_fields.rs
`\lx@begin@abstract`), which walks the refused class abstract — `\lx@dropped@abstract`/`\lx@dropped@endabstract`
(state.rs; a refused `\renewenvironment` now keeps its begin and end code there too, sect08.rs) — and the commands it
hands control to (`\begin{X}` as `\X`, environ's `\csname env@X@process\endcsname`, a refused command as its
`\lx@dropped@` record, the kernel `\maketitle` as the class's `\@maketitle`, which it deposits), at most 512 definitions
a raw file or the document made, for a one-argument definition of a table setter (`\def\keywords#1{`,
`\newcommand{\keywords}[1]{`) whose body uses its argument — one that only warns or drops it (beilstein.cls:854,
fbithesis.cls:272) is not a setter of it, and is defined there as the class's own (its warning, as in pdflatex). Each
found is defined there, for the abstract's body only, as its frontmatter API (`\lx@add@keywords{#1}`), named by the
class's label ahead of the argument where its code shows one (`label_before_argument`, the label rule below:
astlb.cls:200 `\medskip Key words:~~\emph{##1}` "Key words:", pazhastl.cls:191 "Keywords:"; wiley-article.cls:449's
`\allcaps[…]{keywords}` and mtt.cls:181's `\item…\mtt@keywords` are not that shape and keep the default name), made
as the class makes it: a `\def` replaces the document's own `\keywords` inside the abstract (pdflatex prints the
class's there), a `\newcommand` leaves it. In an abstract kept in place as a supplement's (after the body began,
OXIDIZED_DESIGN #154) the keywords stay in place with it (mtt papers' English and Ukrainian abstracts at the end, whose
keywords otherwise replaced the paper's Russian ones and were then dropped as a supplement's: 1310.0585, 1310.0589,
1212.3890), typeset by the class's own definition when it only typesets its label and argument
(`typesets_label_and_argument`), else as a paragraph of the class's label where its code shows one and the keywords —
mtt.cls:181's `\item` belongs to the class's own abstract list, which the kernel's abstract is not, and its label
`\mtt@keywords` is chosen by the abstract's language, so those keywords have no label in place: never the English
default name where pdflatex prints "Ключовi слова:" (1310.0585, 1310.0589, 1212.3890). Known limitation: the main
frontmatter `<keywords>` of such a class carries the default name, as its language-selected label cannot be read
without running class code (pdflatex "Ключевые слова:" on 1310.0585's Russian abstract). Outside the abstract `\keywords`
stays undefined, as in pdflatex. (2) After a raw class loads (`reroute_keywords_environments`), a table setter it defined as an environment —
no parameters, an `\end<name>` beside it, not a binding's — whose begin code typesets only a label
(`label_only_begin_code`: layout that typesets nothing — font, size and paragraph declarations, `\fontsize`, `\vspace`,
`\addvspace`, glue settings as `\rightskip5.5pc`, a class macro made of them as pasa.cls:56 `\keywordfont` — around one
run of label material: text, a sectioning heading's argument, a `\textbf`-like command, a group of them, a class macro
that is text such as `\keywordname`) becomes `\lx@class@keywords{<name>}`: inside `\begin{<name>}` the frontmatter's
keywords read up to `\end{<name>}` (`\lx@begin@keywords[name={<label>}]`), as mn2e_support_sty.rs does; called as a
command, `\keywords{…}` is `\lx@add@keywords[name={<label>}]{…}` when that group ends the keywords — `\par`, a blank
line or an `\end…` follows it (`braced_group_ends_the_keywords`); any other `\keywords` (`\keywords {alpha}, beta,
gamma`, a bare `\keywords text`), whose extent only the class's layout knows, runs the class's own begin code
(`\lx@class@keywords@<name>`). `\end<name>` is chosen by `\@currenvir` the same way: the end of the frontmatter's
keywords in the environment, else the class's own end code (`\lx@class@keywords@end@<name>`; paper.cls:622
`\par\bigskip` after a bare `\keywords alpha \endkeywords`). The label is the keywords' name, made of its TEXT only
(`LabelText`): its characters and text macros, a source space, a horizontal skip or a kern between two pieces (a class
macro's too: `\quad`) one space, an explicit `\ `/`~` one space, a trailing space dropped — never a font or layout
command, which would print as a command name in the name and, out of the label's group, set the keywords text in the
label's font (emsprocart.cls:668-670 `\vspace{2pt}\small{\noindent\bfseries{\keywordname.}\vspace{\z@}}` "Keywords.",
1202.4161, 1006.0632, 1610.08545; ieice.cls:952-954 "key words:", 2002.00666, 1604.03276, 2509.21881; 1604.03313's
lni.cls:157-158 "Keywords:"; paper.cls "Keywords:", biometrika.cls:526 "Some key words:"). The keywords text is the document's, in no class font
(pdflatex sets ieice's in the class's ungrouped `\itshape`). Converted, in the versions read (TeX Live 2025 where it ships
the class, else the papers' copies): paper.cls:621-627 (TL), pasa, biometrika, irmaems, ieice, the emsprocart copies of
1202.4161/1006.0632/1610.08545/0803.2841/1203.6509, the lni copies of 1604.03313/1810.05361/2108.00996/2110.01641. A begin
code doing anything else stays the class's: a flag its title page reads (tADR2e.cls:450 `\global\keywordstrue`; TeX
Live 2025's lni.cls:561-565 `\global\keywordstrue…\def\and`, and the lni copies of 2403.01613, 2402.18227), a box it
fills (ar-1col's `\global\setbox\@kwdbox\vbox\bgroup`, iau, biom), a list (fundam, basi, cpc-hepnp), a conditional
(the emsprocart copies of 0803.2060 and math0612455, icmart's, `\if@twocolumn\section*{\keywordname}`), an optional
argument (vmsta). A document's own `{keywords}`, defined after the class, replaces the rerouted one.
Limitations: the braced command form is taken only before `\par`, a blank line or `\end…`; a `\keywords{a}` followed by
`\section`, `\maketitle` or `\begin{…}` runs the class's run-in code, as before (a lost conversion, not a fidelity loss).
The setter walk ignores conditionals: a class abstract written as beilstein.cls:850-855
(`\ifthenelse{…}{\newcommand{\keywords}[1]{…#1}}{\newcommand{\keywords}[1]{\ClassWarning…}}`) would have its keywords
typeset where pdflatex warns and drops them (the setter that uses `#1` is preferred); no abstract reaches that today.
**Why**: the keywords are the author's content and the frontmatter carries them as such (user ruling 2026-09-18 on raw
classes' title-page stores, `feedback_frontmatter_api_for_raw_classes`); the undefined `\keywords` was the only error of
373 papers of run 353, of which 330 now convert error-free (wiley-article 214, nbdt-article 40, astlb 26, the pazh
family and astrobul 38, mtt/mttr 3, renamed wiley-article copies 9); paper.cls's keywords were the R9 classification
loss of the rawclasses lever (150 of 160 paper-class losses).
Witnesses 1706.00599, 1712.05593, 1712.05708, 1801.08881, 1809.03406, 1202.2889, astro-ph0306137, 1507.06302,
2103.05801, 1310.0585; under the lever 0707.1307, 0712.4042, 1004.5246; shipped raw classes 1801.03506 (pasa),
2412.19242 (biometrika). Not served (listed in SYNC_STATUS): a parameterless `\keywords` run-in heading inside an
abstract (hsrbericht.cls:348; a document's own `\renewenvironment{abstract}{…\providecommand\keywords{\par…}}`, the
"article" row: 1403.4689, 2405.19523), a locked `\abstract` patched twice (cup-pan.cls:134-147 `\preto` then `\appto`:
the refused-definition record keeps the last patch; 2008.06930, 2004.14479), pazh's `\englishkeywords`. Repros sectioning-frontmatter/class_keywords/*;
guards `perfect_kernel_batch68n` (22: round 2 added `group_label_*` (6),
`braced_first_group_that_does_not_end_the_keywords_runs_the_classs_code`, `bare_endkeywords_is_the_classs_end_code`,
`abstract_setter_that_only_warns_is_the_classs_own`; round 3 `group_label_pieces_parted_by_quad_and_kern`,
`supplement_abstract_keywords_without_a_readable_label_have_none`).

### 637. `\unvbox` splices a vbox's list only into a vertical box's own list, between two boundary marks

tex.web §1110 puts an `\unvbox`ed box's list into whatever vertical list is current. tex_box.rs `vlist_of` does so where
the list is a vertical box's own (`VBoxContents`: `\vbox`, `\vtop`, `\parbox`, a `p` column's cell; the frame its
mode was bound in carries `lx@vbox@list`, base_utilities/boxes_lists.rs `predigest_list_in_mode`), where LaTeXML sets a box's
hboxes as lines (`_CaptureBlock_`) — the peel loops of KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #840 and the accumulating
`\setbox\b=\vbox{\unvbox\b …}` idiom. Everywhere else the box goes back whole, as Perl's: on the main vertical list,
in a float's, a footnote's or a minipage's body, inside an environment that sets its own mode within the `\vbox`
(`\vbox{\begin{center}…\unvbox\B…\end{center}}`, itemize alike, though in TeX that is still the vbox's list),
in `\vadjust`/`\insert` material, and in math. Spliced on the main list its hboxes ran together into one paragraph
(`\setbox0\vbox{\hbox{C1}\hbox{C2}}\unvbox0 After.` gave `<p>C1C2After.</p>`; pdflatex three lines), since an `\hbox`
in vertical mode is a line of its own only in a captured block (box family root R6; the shape of case 8-9 of
boxes-groups/box_primitives_unpack awaits a ruling). The box's end closed what its contents had opened in the XML — the
paragraph it finished (§1086 `end_graf`), the `ltx:p` a minipage or `\parbox` opened, a `\noindent` paragraph's
`ltx:para` — and a spliced list has no end: the list goes back between a pair of boundary marks
(`\lx@splice@begin`, `\lx@splice@end`, Rust-only constructors), and when absorbed the begin mark records the element it
starts in (by the internal `_lx_splice` attribute, a value that no rename or removal leaves dangling) and the end mark
closes back to that element whatever was opened since — only while it is open under the same name, only if what lies
between may auto-close, and not at all without its begin mark (`\vsplit`). The marks are no node in TeX: the
list-tail primitives see through them (stomach.rs `is_list_tail_transparent`) and they revert as nothing; a list of
nothing but marks goes back empty. Without them the material after the splice ran into the open element: "Para
two.More.", and `\setbox\B\vbox{\begin{minipage}{3cm}MiniA\end{minipage}}\vbox{\unvbox\B AfterA}` set MiniA and AfterA
side by side where pdflatex sets two lines (68q round 1, whose line-only `\par` mark the pair replaces). Perl's
t/digestion/box golden nests the two `\unvbox`ed boxes of `\vbox{\unvbox\myboxA\unvbox\myboxB}` as blocks;
latexml_oxide/tests/digestion/box.xml now has the four lines in the one framed box, as pdflatex sets them, and
tests/alignment/arraycr_halign.xml's `\vcenter{\vbox{\unvbox0}}` reverts with one `\vbox` fewer (`tex=` attribute only).
A box's attachment goes with the box: floatrow's caption spliced into its `\vtop` (floatrow.sty:393) is
`vattach="top"` (guard `perfect_kernel_batch58::floatrow_floatbox_steps_its_counter_once`). floatrow's caption panel is
opened when the `\vtop`'s captured block is placed, after the marks were absorbed, so a `\floatfoot` set after the
caption in that `\vtop` is a child of the caption's `<figure>`, where it had been a `logical-block` beside it; the text
order is the PDF's (Body / Table 1: Cap / A foot note), accepted by the main session (guards
`perfect_kernel_batch58::{floatrow_floatfoot_keeps_its_text, floatrow_subcaption_stays_in_its_panel}`). A
`\paragraph` heading set in the box no longer takes the text after the splice into its section: it closes at the end
mark. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch68q::{unvbox_lastbox_peel_loop, unvbox_splice_closes_what_its_list_opened}`,
`box_primitives::{lastbox, unpack}`, `box_test`.

### 641. The undefined-token error stub installs past a lock (Perl: refused, the token loops to TooManyErrors)

The Stomach's recovery from an undefined control sequence defines it as `<ltx:ERROR/>` and re-reads it (Perl
State.pm:532-554 `generateErrorStub`, Stomach.pm:234-238 `invokeToken_undefined`). Perl installs the stub through
`installDefinition`, which refuses a locked name (State.pm:502-517), so a locked binding a `\let` has cleared stays
undefined and the retry raises the same Error until TooManyErrors (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #841).

**Rust** (68u): the stub is the engine's recovery, not a source redefinition, so `generate_error_stub` (and the
undefined-environment stub, `install_undefined_error_constructor`) install it with the state unlocked
(state.rs `past_the_lock`): one Error per name and its `<ltx:ERROR/>`, as pdflatex gives one "Undefined control
sequence" per use, and the text after it is typeset. The lock itself is unchanged, so a later redefinition is still
judged by it. The stub of a name that carries a lock is installed at LOCAL scope (state.rs `stub_scope`; round 3), every
other name's globally as Perl's (State.pm:553): such a name is undefined only because a `\let` cleared its binding, and
the stub ends where that clearing ends — `{\let\cite\undefined X\cite{a}} Y\cite{b}` typesets the second citation,
as pdflatex does, and `\begingroup\let\section\nonexist\section{A}\endgroup\section{B}` keeps the section B; a
top-level clearing keeps the stub for the rest of the document (one Error per name). A discarded diagnostics hold
undoes such a stub only while it still stands (`remove_error_stub`). Witnesses (the rawclasses lever, study
agent_reports/2026-10-15_rc_rawcls_regressions.md R4): 2006.07968 (apa6, the document's `\let\cite\parencite` with
`\parencite` undefined: 507 Errors and Fatal → 1, as pdflatex), 1509.06375 (pittetd.cls:313
`\AtBeginDocument{\let\maketitle\HyOrg@maketitle}` before 67q's `\HyOrg@maketitle`), 2311.14793, 2501.10505, 2510.26876
(eulerpx.sty:130-132 `\let\mathscr=\undefined` then a `\DeclareMathAlphabet\mathscr` the kernel's lock refuses: 511
Errors and Fatal → 1; 2203.12624 the same, then a separate `multlined` root). Repro
macro-state/locked_name_let_to_undefined_stub_loop; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch68u::{a_locked_name_let_to_an_undefined_one_errs_once, a_locked_maketitle_let_to_an_undefined_one_errs_once,
a_locked_name_cleared_in_a_group_is_back_after_it}`.

### 642. `\|` is a protected macro over the double-bar atom, as LaTeX's `\|` is (Perl: the atom itself)

LaTeX defines `\|` with `\DeclareMathDelimiter{\|}` (fontmath.ltx:467), which `\set@mathdelimiter` (latex.ltx:13641-13645)
makes `\protected\xdef\|{\delimiter"026B30D }`: one expansion step gives the body. beilstein.cls:264 (copied from
bpchem.sty), in an `\AtBeginDocument` hook, relies on it: `\expandafter\DeclareRobustCommand\expandafter\|\expandafter
{\|}`. Perl's `\|` is the unexpandable math atom (math_common.pool.ltxml:84 `DefMathI('\|', …)`), so that line defines
`\|` as itself and its first use loops (`Fatal:Timeout:Recursion`; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #842).

**Rust** (68u): the atom (VERTBAR `∥`, name `||`) is the internal `\lx@math@Vert`, whose `alias` keeps the reversion
`\|`, and `\|` is a protected macro expanding to it — the shape of `\{` over `\lx@math@lbrace` (math_common.rs).
`\Vert` is still `\let` to `\|`; `\left\|`, `\bigl\|` and an infix `\|` reach the same atom (`tex_math::DELIMITER_MAP`
names the internal too), so their XML is unchanged; `\meaning\|` is `\protected macro:->\lx@math@Vert ` where pdflatex
prints `\protected macro:->\delimiter "026B30D `. Witness 2604.06890 (beilstein, the rawclasses lever: 7k words → 0
under the raw class, now 0 errors and its text). Repro
expansion-primitives/robust_double_bar_over_its_expansion_beilstein; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch68u::{a_robust_double_bar_over_its_expansion_typesets_it, double_bar_is_a_protected_macro_over_the_atom}`.

### 643. A raw class's frontmatter setter is the frontmatter's by its name: a store only its title page reads, a setter with side definitions, a redefined `\date`, a keywords environment collecting its body (Perl: lost)

Under the rawclasses lever a TeX Live class without a binding is read raw; the kernel's locked `\maketitle` refuses
the class's, so a store only its title page reads reaches no output. K11 (#634 and the entries it cites) rerouted a
table setter (`STORE_SETTERS`) only when its body was a pure store into its OWN `\@name`. Perl reaches none of these
(an unknown class is OmniBus there, whose table maps the names; read raw, the stores are lost).

**Rust** (68u r2, `frontmatter_stores.rs`): (a) a table setter whose body is a pure store of its argument into one
`\@X` of another name is rerouted when the **reader scan** (`ClassReaders`) finds `\@X` read by the class's
title-page code and nothing else: the scan covers every macro a raw file defined (`DefinitionOrigin::File`: the class
and what it loaded, surveyed once as the class ends), reads each body's control sequences (a `\def`-family, `\let`,
`\g@addto@macro` or `\renewcommand`-family target is a write; `\@ifundefined{X}`, `\@nameuse{X}`, `\csname X\endcsname`
read `\X`), and takes as title-page code the refused `\maketitle` (`\lx@dropped@maketitle`) and `\@maketitle` and,
to a fixpoint, every macro only they call. apa6.cls:760 `\affiliation` → `\@affil` and :779 `\authornote` → `\@acks`
(read by its `\maketitle` and the `\check@author` it calls, :786-795; `authornote` joins the table as apa7's binding
maps it, a note of role `authornote`); uiucthesis.cls:97 `\department` → `\@dept` (its replayed title page then read
the department as empty, as it reads every captured store; since 68x r2 the line rule of #662 keeps it in its line). A store another macro reads stays raw — letter.cls:155
`\address` → `\fromaddress` (`\opening`), afthesis.cls:535 `\addr@ss` (its vita) — as does a kernel-owned one
(`\@date`). (b) A setter's body may make side definitions beside its store (`\def`-family, `\let`,
`\renewcommand`-family, in `\begingroup`; a store inside a group counts only when global); anything else — a
`\RequirePackage` (apa6.cls:780 `\journal`), a flag (tADR2e.cls:450), typesetting — keeps it the class's. (c) The kernel
`\date` is not locked; a raw file's redefinition storing `\@date` among side definitions keeps them and hands the
date to the frontmatter as the kernel's `\date` does (tufte-common.def:608-614, `\thedate`). (d) A `{keywords}` whose
begin code is environ.sty's `\Collect@Body\X`, `\X` storing the collected body in one macro only the title page
reads, is the frontmatter's keywords (cclayout.sty:71-73, read at :889-898), beside #634's label-only shape. Witnesses
1710.08171, 1705.02935 (apa6), 2003.11668 (apa.cls:443), 2603.01440 (tufte-handout), 1905.07821 (cc). Repros
sectioning-frontmatter/{raw_class_setter_store_read_only_by_title_page_apa6, maketitle_replay_gate_ifundefined_branch_apa6,
raw_class_date_with_side_definitions_tufte, raw_class_collected_keywords_env_cc}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch68u::{a_raw_class_store_only_its_title_page_reads_is_the_frontmatter,
an_apa6_journal_mode_affiliation_is_the_authors, a_raw_class_store_another_macro_reads_stays_the_classs,
a_raw_class_date_with_side_definitions_sets_the_date,
a_raw_class_keywords_environment_collecting_its_body_sets_the_keywords}`,
`perfect_kernel_batch61::uiucthesis_title_page_is_replayed`.

### 644. beilstein.cls, lni.cls, apa6.cls and apa.cls author blocks are bindings over the raw class (Perl: no binding)

Both classes build their author block in accumulators only their `\maketitle` reads, through an `\author` the
kernel's (or authblk's) lock refuses: beilstein.cls:586-737 (`\author[marks]{name}`, `\author*[marks]{name}{e-mail}`,
`\affiliation{…}` numbered in order and given to the author just named), lni.cls:384-464 (authblk's code copied:
`\author[marks]{name}{e-mail}{ORCID}`, `\affil[mark]{…}`). Read raw, a starred beilstein author was a creator named `*`
and every affiliation, e-mail and ORCID was lost; OmniBus (and Perl) guess `\affiliation`/`\affil` only.

**Rust** (68u r2, latexml_contrib `beilstein_cls.rs`, `lni_cls.rs`): each binding loads its class raw and defines the
author interface over the frontmatter API — beilstein: each author a creator carrying its marks and the numbers of
the affiliations after it (handed on at the next `\author` or `\maketitle`), the e-mail a contact, each affiliation a
contact labelled by its number; lni: authblk's binding's `\author`/`\affil` (`authblk_sty::define_author_and_affil`)
restored after the class's copy, the e-mail and ORCID the author's contacts. Witnesses 2203.09951, 2604.06890,
2011.08032, 2506.23338, 2108.11247 (beilstein), 2608.21389 (lni). Repros
class-bindings/{beilstein_author_affiliation_numbers, lni_author_email_orcid_affil}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch68u::{beilstein_authors_carry_their_numbered_affiliations,
lni_authors_carry_email_orcid_and_affiliation}`.

Round 3 (latexml_contrib `apa6_cls.rs`, `apa_cls.rs`): apa6.cls:745-777 (apa.cls:427-459 the same lines) store the
numbered forms' names in `\@authorOne` … `\@authorSix` and affiliations in `\@affilOne` … `\@affilSix`, read only by
the refused `\maketitle`, whose every layout (man :1143-1214; jou/doc `\put@two@authaffil` :1344-1365 at :1378-1414)
sets name n over affiliation n. At `\maketitle` (`\lx@maketitle@begin`) the binding makes, slot by slot, the slot's
names (split as the kernel's `\author`, appended: `\lx@add@authors@list`) carrying affiliation n
(`annotate=new`); once `\@authorTwo` is defined the numbered names supersede what `\author`/`\affiliation` said, as
on the class's title page (the kernel's creators cleared, the one-author `\@affil` emptied so K11 does not give it to
every author). Without numbered names K11's own harvest of `\@affil` (a numbered affiliation form's first one) stands.
The `mask` option (apa6.cls:126) hides the numbered names as the class does. A class only named like the family (the
prefix fallback's apa6e.cls, a paper's renamed copy) is read as itself (`requested_shipped_class`). A class a
binding reads raw is a raw class to K11: `input_definitions` (latexml_core/src/binding/content.rs) fires the reroutes
(`\lx@class@loaded@raw`) at the end of the class load for the class the binding read, after the binding's own
definitions, which `store_setters::mark_bound` keeps the binding's (68x: one rule for every binding that reads its
class raw, replacing 68u r3's explicit calls in these four; without it a binding's raw class lost K11's reroutes —
lni.cls `\subtitle` a bold paragraph instead of `<subtitle>`; apa6's `\shorttitle`, `\affiliation`, `\authornote`,
`\keywords`; guard `perfect_kernel_batch68x::a_class_a_binding_reads_raw_reroutes_its_stores`).
Witnesses 2102.04789, 1710.04173, 1811.01821, 2011.06172, 1401.2054, 1402.6720, 1605.09288, 1609.04156 (71 papers use
the numbered forms). Repro class-bindings/apa6_numbered_author_affiliation_forms; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch68u::{apa6_numbered_authors_carry_the_affiliation_of_their_number,
apa_numbered_authors_supersede_the_one_author_forms, apa6_one_author_line_with_numbered_affiliations_carries_the_first,
beilstein_author_with_marks_and_email_options}` (beilstein.cls:627 `\author[marks][e-mail]{name}`).

### 645. `\try@load@fontshape` reads the family's .fd, `\DeclareFontShape` records the shape, and `\f@encoding` names the encoding `\fontencoding` selected

Perl makes `\try@load@fontshape` empty (latex_bootstrap.pool.ltxml:62) and `\DeclareFontShape` a no-op
(latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2690), and `\fontencoding{U}` falls back to OT1 for want of a `U` fontmap. amsart's test
for amsfonts (amsart.cls:377-391 `\begingroup\fontencoding{U}\fontfamily{msa}\try@load@fontshape\endgroup`
`\@ifundefined{U/msa/m/n}{\ClassError…}{\RequirePackage{amsfonts}}`) therefore failed in every raw class that copies it,
the class skipped amsfonts, and its `\edef\@dh{\noexpand\mathhexbox{\hexnumber@\symAMSb}67}` met an undefined
`\symAMSb` (197 papers, run 353-365: nyjm.cls 2401.06615, cedram.cls 2105.03188, myart.cls 1506.02470, fcaa-var). Ours:
`\try@load@fontshape` is latex.ltx:10605-10620 (an unknown `\<enc>+<family>` is remembered and `<enc><family>.fd` is
input, lowercased, else as written; locked as Perl's, latex_bootstrap.rs), `\DeclareFontShape` is latex.ltx:10279-10305
(arguments under `\nfss@catcodes`, `\<enc>/<family>/<series>/<shape>` defined; sect08.rs), and `\f@encoding` names the
encoding `\fontencoding` was given (latex.ltx:10490): `\lx@fontencoding` of an encoding without a map still merges OT1
into the font, which decodes through it as before, and keeps the name beside it (`lx@fontencoding@unmapped`,
tex_fonts.rs), which `\f@encoding` (sect08.rs) reports while the font's encoding is still OT1 — a later switch to a
mapped encoding clears it. The `U` encoding itself has no map, only the per-family `U_msa`/`U_msb` (u_fontmap.rs), so a
math symbol of a U symbol font of any other family stays undecoded (U+FFFD, and one Warning per symbol font: #27) — unless it is a kernel or AMS
name declared at its fontmath.ltx/amssymb slot (#910): giving `U` OT1's map decoded shuffle.sty's `\shuffle` ("001)
as Δ (2306.04672) and stmaryrd's `\boxslash` ("1C) as an italic ø. Left out: the
unknown-family error of `\DeclareFontShape`, its `\series@maybe@drop@one@m` (latex.ltx:10288, the shape is recorded
under the series as written, not with a redundant `m` dropped — sect08.rs `\DeclareFontShape@`) and the note that goes
with it, `\@font@info` and the "No file" typeout (none is in the dumpless base). KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #845. Repros
fonts-nfss/{amsfonts_try_load_fontshape, u_symbol_font_without_map}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch68v::{batch68v_try_load_fontshape_finds_amsfonts, batch68v_u_symbol_font_without_a_map_stays_undecoded}`.

### 646. empheq's `left`/`right` material is kept, and `overload` gives the AMS environments the option

Perl's empheq binding (empheq.sty.ltxml) reads `\begin{empheq}[<options>]{<env>}`'s options and drops them, defines
none of `\DeclareLeftDelimiter`'s commands, and has no `overload`: `\usepackage[overload]{empheq}`
`\begin{align}[left={F(x)=\empheqlbrace}]` typeset the option list as math in the first cell and `\empheqlbrace` was
undefined (229 papers; 1410.0933, 1906.02657, 2210.09120, 2201.03303, 2207.01386). Ours (empheq_sty.rs): the options
are empheq's keys (empheq.sty:785-838) — `left` opens the environment's first cell, `right` closes its last, the boxes
are styling and dropped; `overload`/`overload2` redefine equation, gather, align, flalign, multline, alignat and their
starred forms as empheq.sty:961-1066 does, an optional `[…]` (after alignat's count), each keeping its lock; and
`\empheq<delim>`/`\empheqbig<delim>` for the sixteen delimiters of empheq.sty:868-883 are the delimiter grown to the
display (`\left\lbrace\right.`, the phantom and kerns presentational). A constructor environment (`\begin{equation}`)
keeps its own end, so takes no `right`. Timing: empheq.sty:961 makes the `overload` redefinitions `\AtBeginDocument`;
ours makes them when the package loads (empheq_sty.rs), so an AMS environment a preamble package redefines after
empheq loads keeps that package's definition, where LaTeX's overload would replace it at `\begin{document}`.
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #846. Repros package-bindings/{empheq_overload_left, empheq_lbrace_empty_fence}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch68v::{batch68v_empheq_overload_left_and_right, batch68v_empheq_lbrace_empty_fence_known_gap}` (the
second pins the math parser's 7 warnings on the empty fence `\left\{\right.` opening a cell, a known gap — math parsing
is a separate stream, SYNC_STATUS 68v).

### 647. A command a class's environment defines for its body is made where it is called, when the kernel's environment runs instead

`\begin{X}` runs the kernel's `\begin{X}` constructor when one is defined (sect01.rs; Perl's `\begin` the same), and
the kernel's abstract collects its body for the frontmatter; a raw class's own `\X` — or the one the lock refused,
`\lx@dropped@X` — never runs, nor anything it defines for the environment's body. bmcart.cls:712-717
`\def\@figure[#1]{…\def\csentence##1{{\mathversion{bold}\bfseries ##1}}…}` (a caption's bold lead sentence; 100
papers: 2305.08284, 1611.01327, 1909.07026) and :1505-1510 `\def\abstract@fmt[#1]{…\def\parttitle##1{\vskip3\p@
\noindent{\bfseries ##1:}}…}` (a structured abstract's run-in headings; 78 papers: 2007.07886, 1907.07303, 2106.01700)
were undefined. Ours: when an undefined control sequence is about to become `<ltx:ERROR/>` (the two call sites of the
kernel autoload, `kernel_autoload::try_refused_environment_definition`), the open environments are searched innermost
first — the kernel's abstract, which is no environment frame, first inside its body (`lx_in_kernel_abstract`, set by
`\lx@abstract@class@setters`) — but only code that never ran: an environment's `\lx@dropped@X` (refused by the lock) and
its `\X` when a `\begin{X}` constructor shadows it, never an environment its own `\X` began
(`\newenvironment{myenv}{\ifshowfoo\def\foo{…}\fi}{}` leaves `\foo` undefined in its body, as in pdflatex) — through
each and the commands it hands control to (frontmatter_stores.rs `handed_to`), only definitions a raw file or the
document made, at most 64 per environment, for a `\def`/`\gdef`/`\edef`/`\xdef` of exactly that name outside any
`\if…\fi` (whether the body makes it depends on a test not run here) whose text reads none of the outer call's
arguments; it is made where the call stands (in the call's group) and the call retried. Only a command that would otherwise be an Error is ever
defined this way. Perl leaves them undefined (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #851). Repro
class-bindings/bmcart/{bmcart_environment_body_commands, environment_code_ran_not_searched}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch68v::{batch68v_bmcart_environment_body_commands, batch68v_an_environment_whose_code_ran_is_not_searched}`. A frontmatter field's text is set by the class
where its setter put it, so while one is digested (`digest_frontmatter_item`, base_utilities/frontmatter/queue_digest.rs, marks the field:
`lx_frontmatter_item`) the class's own setter of that field is searched first (`\lx@dropped@author` for a creator):
vmsta.cls:278-283 `\csdef{name@m}{…\def\fnm##1{##1}…}`, which its `\@@author` applies to each author (69 papers:
1508.02842, 1411.4499, 1601.01109; the full title page's `\name@m@front` sets `\@fnm~\@snm`, "Yuliya Mishura", where
the identity gives "YuliyaMishura", and the initials glue on: 1508.02842's creator reads "Yu.YuliyaMishura", where
67int15 had "Yu.<ERROR>YuliyaMishura"). The kernel's own author markup for a refused `\author` (OmniBus's `\inits`,
`\snm`, … : #444) is defined before and stands. Repro class-bindings/vmsta/vmsta_name_parts; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch68v::batch68v_vmsta_author_name_parts`.

### 648. A refused class setter's replay keeps what it defines locally, as the setter would where it is called

The replay of a raw class's frontmatter setter that the kernel's lock refused (`replay_class_setter`, sect05.rs;
OXIDIZED_DESIGN #482) ran the class's body inside the replay's group, so its local definitions ended with it — in TeX
the class's `\author` runs at the call, in no group of its own. MastersDoctoralThesis.cls:218
`\DeclareDocumentCommand{\author}{m}{\newcommand{\authorname}{#1}\renewcommand{\@author}{#1}}` left `\authorname`
undefined where the document prints it ("I, \authorname, declare…"; 86 papers: 2603.21941, 2312.06150, 2011.02318,
DoctoralThesis and HKUThesis copies), and revtex4.cls's `\@author@def` `\@booleanfalse\collaboration@sw` (a `\let`)
left the switch undefined for its `\affiliation`'s `\move@AU` (79 papers: qm2008_abs.cls 0805.2253, snp.cls 0806.0481,
jasatex.cls 0805.4759). Now the body runs in a group of its own inside the replay's (the scaffolding — the inert
frontmatter, the gobbled notes — stays outside it), `\lx@replay@capture` takes at its end the meanings first made in
that group, bound nowhere outside it (state.rs `top_frame_new_meanings`), and a clean, balanced replay assigns them
again, locally, where the call stands, before the kernel's stores and the stores the body defines are put back (so
those stay as before). Only what the setter creates — a getter, a switch: its changes to what was defined already
stay in the replay (pos.sty's `\seq_put_right:Nn` on the class's author seq, which the deposited title page would
print a second time; `perfect_kernel_batch56::class_maketitle_replay_that_errors_is_dropped`). Meanings only; none of
an erring or unbalanced replay. Perl never runs a refused definition (State.pm:502-517;
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #852). Under the revtex4 copies the class's `\affiliation` now runs past the switch; the witnesses
lose only the ERROR, their creators intact (0805.2253 "Takeshi Osada"/"Grzegorz Wilk", 0806.0481, 0805.4759). Repros
class-bindings/{mastersdoctoralthesis/mdt_authorname, revtex4_copy/rtcopy_collaboration_switch}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch68v::{batch68v_replayed_author_keeps_authorname, batch68v_replayed_author_keeps_collaboration_switch}`.

### 653. A heading inside `{thebibliography}` splits it into bibliographies titled by the headings

pdflatex prints a `\section*`/`\subsection*` (or a beamer frame) inside the bibliography's list, the entries after it
the list's, numbered on. The schema has no heading inside `ltx:biblist`, so each heading after which entries follow
becomes the title of a bibliography of its own (the unit that held it absorbed, `absorb_bibliography_heading`), the
entries numbered through the list (`[1]`, `[2]`, `[3]` across them) — Perl errs on every entry (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
#855). The environment's own bibliography, left holding nothing but its heading, is removed when that heading is the
author's (`\begin{thebibliography}{99}\section*{References}`: pdflatex prints "References" twice, here once) or is
empty (`prune_interrupted_bibliography`); with another heading (a "References" over topical `\section*`s,
hep-th0109182) it stays, an empty bibliography over the groups, as the PDF heads them. Its labels move to the next
one. Only the author's `{thebibliography}` is split (`lx_bibliography_author_env`): not a bibliography a `\bibitem`
opened in another environment (a list's, a minipage's). A heading inside a group in the list (`{\small\subsection*{…}}`)
is not split either: the group's end restores the bibliography state and the entries after it err as before (Perl's
error, no regression). A continuation is entered by `\lx@bibitem`, so it undoes the entry redirection its setup armed
as `\restoring@bibitem` would (an entry's `\\` and paragraphs stay its own, hep-th0109182 [17]); one whose heading the
unit before it did not give (a `\paragraph` and text between entries) drops its own `\refname` title and TOC entry
(`drop_own_bibliography_heading`), the list going on as pdflatex prints it. Ids are the one bibliography's: a
continuation of a bibliography interrupted before its first entry (nothing digested in it — no entry, no text,
read back through the box lists to its `\thebibliography`, `holds_nothing_yet`; an entry the recovery opened empty for
a blank line or the heading's own `\par` is none, nor a whatsit that makes no box, the kernel's `alignmentSkippable`
ones — a `\label{refs}` before the heading, whose label moves on with the others — and `@bibitem` not stepped) takes that one's number (`begin_bibliography_clean`,
`lx_bibliography_reuse_number`), so its entries are `bib.bibN`, and the pruned one's freed id `bib` is the survivor's
(Perl fixes ids at digestion, latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3877-3883; the duplicate it meets while built is renamed as
Document.pm:1447-1456 recordID does, `biba`, and freed as :1460 unRecordID); a later separate bibliography is `biba`.
Where the empty one stays (topical groups), the first group keeps that `biba` with entries `bib.bibN`, and the next
group's `biba` is renamed `bibaa`. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch68w::heading_inside_thebibliography_*`.

### 654. sn-jnl without its `pdflatex` option keeps hyperref's `\href`

sn-jnl.cls:1462-1467 (`\breakurldefns`, run when the `pdflatex` option is absent) loads breakurl and makes
`\let\href\burlalt`: `\href{a}{b}` then shows `a` and links `b` (breakurl.sty:50-51 `\hyper@linkurl{\Hurl{#1}}{#2}`),
the reverse of hyperref's `\href{url}{text}`. The authors write hyperref's order (10 of 12 sampled sn-jnl papers
without the option: 2405.04967 lost 63 links to `href="mp-66"`-style targets, 2207.12959, 2603.09685), for which the
class's PDF shows the URL linked to the text. sn_jnl_cls.rs loads breakurl and does not make the `\let` (main-session
ruling 2026-10-16 by the user's priority order: author content, then semantic links, then PDF fidelity). The template's
own swapped order (`\href{here.}{https://…/Datasets_-_RMSC/…}`, 2401.05832) is then hyperref's reading of it: the URL is
the link text, its `_` a script error (2 Errors), as pdflatex errs with the `pdflatex` option. Repros
class-bindings/sn_jnl_href_keeps_hyperref_order (guard
`perfect_kernel_batch68w::sn_jnl_href_keeps_hyperref_order_without_pdflatex`), class-bindings/sn_jnl_href_swapped_order
(RED).

### 655. apacite's `\cite` is parenthetical, with or without notes, in its classic citation mode

apacite's default citation mode (`apaciteclassic`, apacite.sty:76-83, executed at :181-182) defines a `\cite` whose
parentheses (`\def\@BBOP{\BBOP}`, :258-267, inside `\if@APAC@classic@cite`) do not depend on what follows: `\cite{k}`
prints "(Smith, 2001)". The binding delegates its citations to natbib's emulation, whose `\cite{k}` is textual in author-year mode
(natbib.sty:694-701); apacite's `\cite` asks for natbib's parenthetical form by name
(natbib_sty.rs `\lx@natbib@cite@parenthetical`), keeping the `ltx_citemacro_cite` class of the macro the author wrote.
Its notes go on as read (`apacite_delegate`, `natbib_invocation`): a lone `[note]` is the post-note (apacite's
`\@cite<>[note]`, :313-327), a `<pre>` alone the pre-note. `\citeA` stays textual, `\citeNP` unparenthesised, as
apacite defines them. The other modes are declared as apacite.sty:85-110 declares them: under `natbibapa` (:995-1037;
the `[natbibapa]{apacite}` of WileyASNA-v1.cls:2120, the Wiley NJD classes, apa7.cls's natbib choice and sn-jnl.cls's
`sn-apa`) and `nocitation` apacite defines no `\cite`, so natbib's own stays (textual without notes, "A Smith (2001)"
as pdflatex prints it; witnesses 2307.11525, 2406.19732); under `natbibemu` `\cite` is `\citep` when a `[` follows and
`\citet` otherwise (:883-892). Perl ships no apacite binding (apacite_sty.rs header). Witnesses
2002.00730, 2005.00039, 2303.06091, 1901.06889. Repros package-bindings/{apacite_notes_as_read, apacite_citation_modes,
apacite_natbibemu_cite}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch68w::{apacite_notes_absent_stay_absent,
apacite_natbibapa_keeps_natbibs_cite, apacite_natbibemu_cite_is_citet_or_citep}`.


### 659. aguplus.cls is a binding over the raw class: the AGUTeX title page as the AAS binding's, natbib for its copy (Perl: no binding)

Perl has no aguplus binding (OmniBus: `\authoraddr`, `\lefthead`, `\slugcomment` undefined). Under the rawclasses
lever the class was read raw and its title page was its own typesetting: `\author`/`\affil` build the `\@title` box
(aguplus.cls:227-238), which `\xmaketitle` sets at the first `\section` (:192, :225), so the affiliations were body
paragraphs (and the refused `\author`'s replay set the box over the kernel's `\@title` text, a "Missing number" warning
per author); `\authoraddr` (agupp.sty:154-158) gathers `\authaddr@list`, printed only by the class's own end of the
references (agupp.sty:271-306), which the kernel's bibliography replaces, so every address was lost; and the class's
copy of natbib 7.0 (aguplus.cls:861-1173) printed a bold "?" for every `\citet`/`\citep` (no `\bibcite` under the
kernel's bibliography; 1010.3998: 75). Ours (latexml_contrib aguplus_cls.rs): the class read raw (it reads the
AGUTeX package its option names, :47-71), natbib's binding loaded with `square` (:864 `\NAT@open{[}`), the refused
`\title`/`\author` not replayed, and the AGUTeX title-page commands — which AGUTeX shares with AASTeX, from which it
derives — given the AAS binding's frontmatter forms (aas_support_sty.rs, Perl aas_support.sty.ltxml:121-134):
`\affil` the affiliation of the authors before it without one, `\altaffilmark`/`\altaffiltext`, `\received`,
`\revised`, `\accepted`, `\slugcomment` (and `\date`, :245). `\authoraddr` is gathered as the class gathers it and
handed on where the authors are queued — at `\maketitle`, else ahead of the frontmatter fallback at the first section,
else at the end — each address placed with the author it spells, else the only author, else the block
(`\lx@add@contact@placed`), as the class prints them together. Running heads and journal ids stay the class's
(page furniture). Witnesses 1107.5305, 1203.5042, physics9702009, 1010.3998 (104 → 1 warnings, the "?" gone, each
address on its author), 0811.3118. Repros class-bindings/aguplus/{aguplus_author_block_and_citations,
aguplus_altaffil_and_spelled_addresses}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch68x::{aguplus_authors_carry_affiliations_and_addresses,
aguplus_altaffiliations_and_addresses_go_to_their_authors}`.

### 660. cjs-rcs-article.cls is a binding over the raw class: its environ-collected abstracts and keywords are the frontmatter (Perl: no binding)

Perl has no binding (OmniBus). Read raw, cjs-rcs-article.cls:379-386 makes `{englishabstract}`, `{frenchabstract}` and
`{keywords}` with environ.sty's `\NewEnviron`, each `\global\let`-ing its `\BODY` into a store (`\CJS@englishabstract`,
…) only its `\maketitle` reads (:414-480: each abstract under `\selectlanguage{<language>}\paragraph{\abstractname}`,
the keywords as an enumitem inline list joined by "; ", :387-393), so both abstracts and the keywords were lost
(2608.13762). Ours (latexml_contrib cjs_rcs_article_cls.rs): the environments keep the class's environ form
(`\RenewEnviron`), the body handed to the frontmatter as its tokens — each abstract an `ltx:abstract` with its
`xml:lang` and the heading babel gives it in that language (`\captions<language>`'s `\abstractname`: "Résumé"), not
clearing the other (`\lx@add@frontmatter`, not `\lx@add@abstract`), the keywords `\lx@add@keywords` named as the class
names them, their `\item`s joined by "; " as the class's list joins them (in a group: the document's lists keep their
`\item`). Not a K11 (frontmatter_stores.rs) reroute: the abstracts are no table names, and the keywords' items need the
list the title page wraps them in. `{classification}` (:394-404) has the same shape; no witness uses it. Repro
class-bindings/cjs_rcs_article_abstracts_keywords; guard `perfect_kernel_batch68x::cjs_rcs_abstracts_and_keywords_are_frontmatter`.

### 661. smfart.cls and projlib-author.sty are bindings over the raw files: the other-language abstract and the author-block lines are the frontmatter (Perl: no binding)

Perl has neither binding. smfart.cls:568-583 `{altabstract}` scans its body into `\@altabstract` (:506-521
`{@genabstract}`), set in a box under "\altabstractname (\emph{\@alttitle})" only by `\@setaltabstract`, which the
class's `\maketitle` runs; projlib-author.sty:98-139 provides `\institute`/`\address`/`\curraddr`/`\email`, each adding
a line under the author it follows to the `cmd/@author/after` hook, run only where `\@maketitle` prints `\@author`. The

address (2609.02711, colorart.cls + ProjLib) were lost. Ours: smfart_cls.rs reads the class raw and makes
`{altabstract}` the frontmatter's second abstract as the kernel's `{abstract}` is made (read to `\lx@end@abstract`, not

(a name is an attribute: its math and ligatures would be raw TeX); an abstract of the same name in another
`xml:lang` is another element, not a replacement (base_utilities/frontmatter/queue_digest.rs `frontmatter_clear_same_name`, #154: the kernel
names the document's abstract "Abstract" too, before the class's captions are set);
projlib_author_sty.rs reads the package raw and, for each of the four it provided (one defined before it stays, as

`perfect_kernel_batch68x::{smfart_altabstract_is_a_second_abstract, projlib_author_lines_are_the_authors_contacts}`.

### 662. K11 hands a class default to the frontmatter only when the class's title page or page styles print it, and leaves a store the title page prints in one line with a value the frontmatter does not carry (Perl: no reroute)

K11 (frontmatter_stores.rs) reroutes a raw class's title-page stores — under the rawclasses lever and, since 68x, for
the class a binding reads raw. A store the document never set kept the class's default, which the kernel's
`\maketitle` handed to the frontmatter (`\lx@store@defaults`; lion-msc.cls:200 `\gdef\@affiliation{Huygens-Kamerlingh
Onnes Laboratory, …}`, which pdflatex prints). A default is now handed only when the class prints the store
(`ClassReaders::printed`: every macro a raw file defined that the title-page roots — `\@maketitle` of any origin, a
binding's too: titling_sty.rs's reads lion-msc's `\posttitle` — or its page styles (`\ps@…`, `\@oddhead`, …: gGAF2e's
`\ps@plain` prints its `\@jname` default, 2304.14584, 2512.18461) reach; `read_by_the_title_page`): tlp.cls:697-728's
placeholders `\@volume` "1 (1)", `\@journal` "TLP 1 (1): 1–000, January 20XX. © 20XX Cambridge University Press DOI:
10.1017/S147106840100xxxx", read only by the running head that its `\@j@urnal` switch (:760-764) does not even print
without `prodtf`, became pubnotes in 1209.2617 once the tlp binding's raw read went through K11 (68x r1). And a store
the title page prints in one line with a value of the class's that the frontmatter does not carry — another
parameterless macro a raw file defined, not a rerouted store nor a kernel field, in the innermost group around the
store's read (`ClassReaders::store_lines`; a written store, ptptex.cls:110 `\gdef\@abst{}`, is no read) — is
not rerouted: it is part of the class's line. tlp.cls:627 `{\it submitted \@submitted; revised \@revised; accepted
\@accepted}` (`\submitted` is no table setter) printed "submitted 30 November 2010; revised ; accepted" with the
other two in `<date>`s; now the line is whole, as pdflatex prints it, and the dates stay in it. So too uiucthesis.cls:177
`for the degree of \@degree\ in \@dept\\` (`\@degree` from `\phdthesis`, :81): `\department` — #643's rule (a)
affiliation — stays in the line "for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy in Food Science", as pdflatex prints it, and
