the author has no affiliation (guard `perfect_kernel_batch61::uiucthesis_title_page_is_replayed`). One rule for both
paths: under the lever a raw class's defaults and lines are read the same way. Why not "only stores the document
set": the lever path's lion-msc default (pinned by `class_census::k11_class_default_store`) and gGAF2e's journal name
are printed by pdflatex. `printed` does not see a head built through a binding or a token register: a class-level
`\fancyhead[L]{\@journal}` (fancyhdr's binding builds the head) leaves the class's journal default no pubnote, which pdflatex prints in the head
(review 68x r2 probe ka; accepted residual), and sig-alternate.cls:1640's DOI placeholder "10.1145/1235", read through a
token register into its `\copyrightetc` box (:1653-1663), is no longer a pubnote (1710.01977) — correct there only
because the document disables the box (clickbait17-notebook.tex:57 `\def\@copyrightspace{\relax}`), not by the rule.
68x's binding-read K11 also gives apa7 its `\shorttitle` as `<toctitle>` (2609.00670, 2609.02899, 2609.12869,
2609.19448). Repro class-bindings/tlp/tlp_placeholders_and_date_line (a tlp.cls with the class's shapes: the paper
ships it); guard `perfect_kernel_batch68x::tlp_placeholders_stay_and_its_date_line_is_whole`.

RULED refinement (user ruling 2026-10-22, 79a): only printed text is a value, decided by expansion, and `\par` and `\\`
end the line. The line is the store's innermost group cut at the line breaks around the store (`ends_a_line`: `\par` —
a blank line in the code is one —, `\endgraf`, `\\`, `\newline`, `\break`, `\linebreak`, `\cr`, and the primitive
`\vskip`, which in horizontal mode ends the paragraph), and a macro in it is a value only when its expansion prints text
(`prints_as_a_value`, `prints_text`, read in TeX terms down to 6 macros deep): a character or math does; a font, size or
shape switch (a definition that carries a font, `Definition::declared_font`, and LaTeX's declarations by name,
frontmatter_stores.rs `LAYOUT`), spacing (`\hskip`/`\vskip`/`\kern` and a register with their glue, `\vspace{…}`,
`\quad`, `\hfill`, …), a rule (`\hrule`/`\vrule` with their `height`/`width`/`depth`, `\rule[…]{…}{…}`), `\relax`,
`\protect`, a line break with its `*`/`[<skip>]`, and nothing do not; anything else counts as printing. So
`{\@addrfont\@address\par}` with `\def\@addrfont{\itshape}` (review 68x r2 probe ka; the shape of bgteubner,
umich-thesis, philosophersimprint), a title page in one `\vbox{…\@jinfo\par\@author\par \@address\par}` (probe kb) and
`{\@jinfo\\[2pt]\@addrfont\@address}` with `\@addrfont` a font setter's store holding `\small\itshape` (paper.cls:109-111's
shape: 1406.5776, 2105.09416, 2107.05207, the cost of the narrowing rejected in 68x) give `\address` to the frontmatter;
`{\@jinfo, \@address\par}`, tlp.cls:627 and uiucthesis.cls:177 keep their lines.

The other values of the line are judged twice (79a r2, review rev79a Q1): as the class leaves them, when it is loaded
(`reroute_raw_class_stores`: a store in one line with printed text is not rerouted), and with the document's, when
`\maketitle` prints the title page (`ClassReaders::store_lines` records them, `lx_store_line_values_<name>`;
`harvest_stores` → `prints_in_a_line_with_a_value`): a store not handed on there stays un-nulled in the deposit
(`\lx@captured@stores`), which prints the class's line whole. A store the class leaves empty, `\gdef\@submitted{}` for a
setter no table names, prints the document's `\submitted{1 May 2026}`, so `{\itshape submitted \@submitted; e-mail
\@email\par}` keeps the e-mail in the class's line, as pdflatex prints it (r1 handed it on and left "submitted 1 May
2026; e-mail"). A store handed on as it is set (`\lx@store@hand`) waits for `\maketitle` when its line has such values
(`lx_store_deferred_<name>`), and is handed on there when they print nothing (`{\itshape \@issueinfo; DOI \@doi\par}`
without `\issueinfo`: the DOI pubnote). No static shortcut decides it: zzfmc's `\@addrfont`, an `\addressfont` setter's
store, holds `\small\itshape` and is no value. A store a running head prints is in no line of the title page
(`running_head_arguments`: the arguments of `\markboth`/`\markright`/`\@mkboth`, fancyhdr's and scrlayer-scrpage's head
and foot commands, page furniture LaTeXML drops): preprint.cls's `\maketitle` `\ihead{\@shortauthor:~\@shorttitle}`
keeps 2512.04983's `<toctitle>` (judged at `\maketitle` with the document's `\shortauthor`, the head's line had kept
it the class's). So are titleps's `\sethead`/`\setfoot` (with their `*` and three optional arguments) and the body of a
head or foot macro a definition there sets — `\def`/`\gdef`/`\edef`/`\xdef`/`\renewcommand` of `\@oddhead`,
`\@evenhead`, `\@oddfoot`, `\@evenfoot` (`head_definition_body`; 79a r3, review rev79a2 finding 1: a class
`\@maketitle`'s `{\def\@oddhead{\@shortauthor: \@shorttitle\hfil}}`, ptptex.cls's `\maketitle` head, made `\shorttitle`
the class's and lost "Short T"), for the glued rule too (`\gdef\@evenhead{Vol.\@volume\hfil}` glues `\@volume` to no
title-page text). A store waits for `\maketitle` only for a value that is a placeholder the document can fill
(`may_become_a_value`, 79a r3, review rev79a2 finding 5): undefined, `\relax` (LaTeX's undefined), or a parameterless
macro expanding to nothing — not the line's code, a macro with parameters (`\@setfontsize`, `\@ifundefined`), a
primitive, a register or a font macro: USG.cls:1590 `\smash{\@journalfont\@journal}` deferred 2605.00042's `\journal`
for `\@journalfont` and put its pubnote after the volume.

A store glued to the class's printed text is part of a value the frontmatter does not carry, and its line stays the
class's (79a r2, review rev79a finding 1, Q2; `glued_to_class_text`): the character token right before or after the
occurrence is a letter or a digit, or a `.`, `/` or `-` inside a word, with no space, glue or line break between —
piparticle-final.cls:272 `\if\@doi\relax\else{DOI: 10.4279/PIP.\@doi}\fi` (r1 handed `\@doi` on, so the pubnote read
"020001", a DOI that does not exist, and "10.4279/PIP." was lost: 1002.3829, 1012.4507, 1503.03445, 1503.07722,
1510.06950), ar-1col.cls:335 `https://doi.org/\@doi\endgraf` (1903.12215, 2004.12182, 2603.20393), rsos/rspa's
`\@jname.royalsocietypublishing.org` (2005.14200, 2602.20067: "rsos" was a journal pubnote and the header read
".royalsocietypublishing.org"). Not glued: a sentence's full stop (`\enspace\@ACMCCS.}`, CSML.cls's shape), a label's `:`
or a bracket (`doi:\@doi`, lms, jfp1; `(\@pubyear`, mnras, new_tlp), the dimension of a skip, kern, penalty or register
(`\hskip.5em\@kword`, jps-cp.cls; `\vskip 4ex\@subtitle`, jurabook.cls; `in_a_dimension`), an operand of `\if`, `\ifx`
or `\ifcat` (`\if!\@subtitle`, lipics-v2021, llncs), and `\href`'s first argument, a link's target
(`\href{mailto:\@email}`, modernposter). kluwer.cls:888 `Accepted\@accepted` is glued, but K11 hands no store there:
`\accepted@` (:898) stores " in final form: #1", not its argument alone, so kluwer's date line is the class's either way.

Accepted residuals (SYNC rows): a store printed outside any group is never in a class's line (the group bound kept from
68x); a store kept the class's at class load is not judged again at `\maketitle`; a line whose other value the document
leaves empty hands the store on and leaves the class's text around it ("; DOI"); a page style the class defines but never
selects (`\ps@jhead`) still counts as printed, so zzfmb's `\@journal` default is a pubnote pdflatex does not print.
A/B: SYNC 79a. Repros class-bindings/title_page_typesetting/{address_after_a_font_macro,
address_in_a_vbox_with_a_class_line, address_after_a_line_break, value_in_the_line_stays_the_class_line,
doi_glued_to_class_text, store_in_a_line_with_a_document_value, short_title_in_a_running_head,
short_title_in_a_head_definition, store_beside_a_font_macro_keeps_its_order}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch79a::{
address_after_a_font_macro_is_the_frontmatters, address_after_a_class_line_ended_by_par_is_the_frontmatters,
address_after_a_class_line_ended_by_a_line_break_is_the_frontmatters, a_store_in_one_line_with_class_text_stays_the_class_line,
a_store_glued_to_class_text_stays_the_class_line, a_store_in_one_line_with_a_document_value_stays_the_class_line,
a_store_in_a_running_head_is_the_frontmatters, a_store_in_a_head_definition_is_the_frontmatters,
a_store_beside_a_font_macro_keeps_its_order}`.

### 663. emulateapj's deluxetable keeps the rows between `\tablehead` and `\startdata` as heading rows, which TeX prints only in the continuation head or not at all (Perl: rows outside the table)

emulateapj.cls:1324 `\startdata` is `\kill\caption{…}\endhead\hline\endfoot`: the rows since `\tablehead` ended with
`\\` are the longtable's continuation head (`\endhead`), which TeX prints at the top of every page but the first
(`\endfirsthead` is the `\tablehead`'s own rows, :1329-1345), and the line `\startdata` ends — a second head line
written without `\\` — is `\kill`ed: measured, printed on no page (an article `{longtable}` `AAA \\ \endfirsthead FULL
\\ PART \kill\caption{Cap}\endhead` with 120 rows prints FULL on pages 2-3, PART on none). Such rows — 1605.03270
Table 1 `\tablehead{…}\\ \colhead{} & \colhead{Name} & \colhead{(mag)} & …` (killed), 2002.02307, 1509.01261's
`\multicolumn` row — are kept here, heading rows under the head (emulateapj_cls.rs `\lx@eapj@head@extend`): the HTML
has one page and the rows are the author's text (the column units "Name (mag) (mag) (pc)"; ruling KEEP, 68y r2).
Empty rows (the `\\` after the head) and the rules between them, which carry no content, are dropped, and the head's
own rule is set under the last kept row, above the first data row, where TeX's first page has it. Perl's binding
(deluxetable.sty.ltxml:35-43) leaves these rows outside the alignment (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #874). Why not TeX's first
page: the author's column units would be lost. Repro class-bindings/emulateapj_startdata_ends_head; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch68y::emulateapj_startdata_ends_the_head`.

### 664. emulateapj's `\tablecaption` given after `\tablehead` is kept, after the tabular, unnumbered (TeX: stored for the next table; Perl: before the tabular)

emulateapj.cls:1294 `\tablecaption` stores the caption (`\gdef\@tablecaption`) for the `\caption` the head sets (:1325,
:1333); one written after `\tablehead`, inside the longtable, stores it after the head has been set up, so TeX's first
page prints the caption the store held before — the previous table's, or none — and the new one goes to the next table
(68y review probe e3 `\tablehead{…}` `\tablecaption{CaptionInData\label{tcd}}` `\startdata`). Here the head prints the
store as TeX does (#740), and the caption given in the data is stored and also kept for this table's end (emulateapj_cls.rs
`\lx@eapj@labels`, deluxetable_sty.rs `\lx@deluxe@late`, with the notes and labels), unnumbered — the table has its
number — after the tabular, so the row it was written in stays empty; the next table's repeat of it drops its
`\label` (#740). When the store was empty the head printed the
number alone ("TABLE 1", no text), so the first caption given in the data is the table's numbered caption there, as
before (1104.2619: `\tablehead{…}\tablecaption{GOODS AGN sample…}`). Why kept: the author's caption is content, and
a table may be the last. Why after the tabular: the data is open from `\tablehead` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #874), so a
caption set there would be a row. Perl's binding (AASTeX's table, deluxetable.sty.ltxml:35-43, `\tablecaption` the
float's `\caption`) opens the data at `\startdata`, so it set the caption before the tabular. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch68y::emulateapj_startdata_ends_the_head` (Table 3: "Cap two" at its head, "Late cap" after its
tabular) and `perfect_kernel_batch73a::emulateapj_stored_caption_repeats` (the empty store), repro
class-bindings/emulateapj_startdata_ends_head.

### 677. A bibliography begun inside `{quote}`, `{quotation}` or `{verse}` closes the quote and is the document's bibliography (TeX: the heading and list set in the quote's margins; Perl: errors, the bibliography left in the quote)

article.cls:565-584 `thebibliography` is `\section*{\refname}` and a `\list` (book.cls, report.cls alike); begun inside
a quote — the AAAI template's `\begin{quote}\begin{small}\bibliography{…}\end{small}\end{quote}` — TeX sets the heading
and the entries in the quote's `\list` margins (article.cls:389-408), indented and in the quote's font. The LaTeXML
schema allows neither the unit the bibliography stands as (`BACKMATTER_ELEMENT`, `ltx:section`) nor `ltx:bibliography`
in `ltx:quote` (LaTeXML-block.rnc `quote_model`), and the quote does not auto-close: Perl and Rust before 69a erred
twice (`<ltx:section>` / `<ltx:bibliography> isn't allowed in <ltx:quote>`) and left the bibliography inside the quote,
out of the back matter. Here (latex_constructs/mod.rs `close_list_containers_before_backmatter`, called by
`adjust_backmatter_element`, and `Document::close_quotes_blocking`, shared with #678) the quotes that block it, from the
innermost, are closed first — only when that alone (with the auto-closing elements between) makes the bibliography's
place reachable: a quote in a list item stays open and errs as before; the walk passes a box's capture (a bibliography
in a `minipage` is placed outside the box), closing a quote inside the box but none outside it — and each one left
empty is dropped. The environment's end acts on the quote it opened (sect06.rs `quote_environment`): found closed, it closes no
other quote (one around it stays open) but only the `ltx:p` the text after the bibliography is in, as `\endlist` ends
the paragraph, so that text and the text after the environment are two paragraphs' text. The font changes inside the quote (`\small`) are digested into the
entries and stay. What differs from the PDF: the indentation (the quote's margins) — the bibliography is the
document's, with its entries and citation links. User ruling 2026-10-16 (CLOSE the container). Witnesses 2203.09193
1904.12066 1610.09996 2109.09861 2403.09260 1609.06434 (AAAI), astro-ph0410583 (quote), 1504.06728 (verse); repros
index-bib/{bibliography_in_quote, bibliography_in_verse_after_text, bibliography_in_quote_tail_paragraph,
bibliography_in_quote_in_quotation, bibliography_in_quote_in_minipage}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch69a::{bibliography_in_a_quote_closes_the_quote, bibliography_in_a_verse_keeps_the_text_around_it,
bibliography_in_a_quote_keeps_the_tail_paragraph, bibliography_in_a_nested_quote_keeps_the_outer_quote,
bibliography_in_a_quote_in_a_minipage_closes_the_quote}`. Not covered: amsrefs `{bibdiv}` in a quote (not placed by
`adjust_backmatter_element`; errs as before).

### 678. A display sectioning unit inside `{quote}`, `{quotation}` or `{verse}` closes the quote and is the document's own unit; a run-in `\paragraph` stays in the quote (TeX: the heading set in the quote's margins; Perl: error, the unit nested in the quote)

LaTeX's quote environments are its unlabelled list, `\list{}{…}\item\relax` (article.cls:389-408): a margin, no
structure. A `\section*{}` in a `{quotation}` (0712.1985's title page wraps its abstract in one), a whole paper inside
one, a `\chapter` in one in a report: TeX typesets the units inside the margins. `ltx:quote` cannot hold a sectioning
unit and does not auto-close, so Perl and Rust before 69a erred (`<ltx:section> isn't allowed in <ltx:quote>`).

Display units (`\part` to `\subsubsection`, starred or not; `is_quote_closing_unit`) arriving in a quote close it
(`find_insertion_point_qsym` → `Document::close_quotes_blocking`, the same close as a bibliography's, #677): the quotes
in the way are closed only when that alone makes the unit's place reachable (a quote in a list item stays open and errs
as before; one in a `minipage` is closed and the unit is placed as in a `minipage` without a quote), each one left empty
is dropped, and the unit is a real one — its number, id, labels and table-of-contents entry, its back matter after it.
The environment's end finds its quote closed and closes only the paragraph text of its tail (#677). Main-session ruling
2026-10-17 (an unlabelled list follows the item bridge's margin-list exemption, #189; it replaces the 2026-10-16
inline-sectional-block ruling for display units, whose block left a whole paper's sections and bibliography inside one
paragraph).

The run-in units `\paragraph` and `\subparagraph` (`\@startsection` with a negative after-skip, article.cls:314-321) do
not close the quote: pdflatex sets the heading and everything after it up to the environment's end inside the quote's
margins (algorithm cases, LLM prompts, proof steps: 2607.27159, 2505.18677, 2305.11603, 1809.03802, 2208.14587), so
they open an `ltx:inline-sectional-block` in the quote (`AUTO_OPEN_BRIDGES`; the quote's model takes `Misc.class`),
the quote's end closes it, and the text after the environment stays outside. A later display unit in the same quote
still closes the quote — the inline block, whose model would hold a section, is not its place (`holds_in_quote_block`;
2110.03376, 1905.08876). Main-session ruling 2026-10-17 (round 3).

Where the PDF differs: the indentation of a display unit and what follows it in the quote; and a quote inside a
theorem or a proof — the walk closes the quote and then the theorem or proof around it (they auto-close) to reach the
unit's place, so the heading, its text and the rest of the theorem or proof leave it and the text after the environment
joins the unit's last paragraph ("Proof tail.∎After.", review probes d_thm, d_proof3 with `\subsection`), where TeX
keeps them all in the theorem or proof; 67int17b kept the structure with one error (a heading directly in a proof
already merges so, review probe d_proof2). SYNC_STATUS 69a residual; RED repro
sectioning-frontmatter/subsection_in_quote_in_proof. Not for a labelled list item or a float, which open an
`ltx:inline-sectional-block` for every unit (#189). Repros sectioning-frontmatter/{section_in_quotation,
whole_paper_in_quotation, chapter_in_quotation, paragraph_in_quote, section_after_paragraph_in_quote,
paragraph_in_quote_in_theorem}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch69a::{section_in_a_quotation_closes_it,
whole_paper_in_a_quotation_has_its_sections, chapter_in_a_quotation_is_a_chapter, paragraph_in_a_quote_stays_in_it,
section_after_a_paragraph_in_a_quote_closes_it, paragraph_in_a_quote_in_a_theorem_stays_in_it}`.

### 679. An `&` in a glossary entry's stored fields is the character, not an alignment tab (TeX: an error only where the field is typeset; Perl: an error at the definition)

glossaries.sty stores an entry's fields (`\newacronym{cisa}{CISA}{Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency}`,
2602.09131) and typesets them only where the entry is used — `\gls{cisa}`'s long form, the `\printglossary` list — so
an entry never used makes no error in pdflatex. The binding digests every field into the entry's
`<ltx:glossarydefinition>` phrases at `\begin{document}` (the deferred queue, #293), where the `&` was a stray
alignment tab (`Error:unexpected:&`, Perl the same: KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #892). Those phrases are stored data, so the
`&` is read as the character there (glossaries_sty.rs `\lx@glossaries@newentry`, `&` let to `\&` as in an index entry,
sect11.rs `\@index`), in the family of the 2026-10-10 ruling on stored metadata (a binding's stored, never-typeset
argument reads `&` literally). A use still typesets the field from its macros, so `\gls{cisa}` with a raw `&` errs as
pdflatex does, and the printed glossary shows the `&` (pdflatex would err there). Repro
package-bindings/glossaries_untypeset_ampersand; guard `perfect_kernel_batch69a::glossary_entry_ampersand_is_stored_text`.

### 689. A theorem, a proof or a table of contents inside a container that holds no Para.class opens an `ltx:inline-logical-block` there (Perl: "isn't allowed" Error, element inserted anyway)

`{quote}` (`quote_model = Block.model`, widened by #271 with para/logical-block/sectional-block only), a `\footnote`'s
`ltx:note` (`tags?, Flow.model`), a `{wrapfigure}`'s `ltx:figure`, an `ltx:text` and an `ltx:td` (`Inline.model`)
have no Para.class, so `ltx:theorem`, `ltx:proof` and `ltx:TOC` cannot go there; pdflatex sets them inside the
container's box (a theorem in a quote is indented with it, one in a footnote is in the footnote). Perl's Document.pm
`find_insertion_point` (no autoOpen route, no auto-close to a holder) errors "<ltx:theorem> isn't allowed in
<ltx:quote>" and inserts it anyway, schema-invalid. Here the last auto-open bridge of `find_insertion_point_qsym`
(document.rs `AUTO_OPEN_BRIDGES`) opens an `ltx:inline-logical-block` (Misc.class, `Para.model`,
LaTeXML-para.rnc:77-90) — the wrapper `\marginpar` already gives its note body (sect09.rs `\lx@marginpar`) — after
closing the auto-closable elements around the point up to the outermost whose parent holds the block (the `ltx:p` a
`\trivlist` ends, latex.ltx `\@trivlist`'s `\par`); a container that cannot auto-close keeps it inside. The schema is
unchanged and #271 stays as it is (main-session ruling P1, 2026-10-17). Like the other bridges it applies only after
every direct, auto-open and auto-close route is exhausted, so a theorem in a section, a list item or a minipage is
unaffected, and the text that follows in the same container continues inside the block (it auto-closes with the
container). Why not widen the quote model with Para.class: every container would need it (note, figure, text, td).
Excluded: the frontmatter containers `ltx:abstract`, `ltx:acknowledgements`, `ltx:keywords`, `ltx:classification` and
`ltx:creator`, and anything inside one (document.rs `outside_frontmatter_container`) — a theorem or a TOC in an
abstract is a frontmatter question (what the abstract's model should hold, whether the block belongs in the
frontmatter at all) that the pending frontmatter study decides, so there the Perl/base "isn't allowed" Error stands
(main-session ruling 2026-10-17; guard `perfect_kernel_batch69c::theorem_in_abstract_is_not_bridged`).
Witnesses 2406.11811 2103.03402 0806.0214 2602.15784 2301.10544 1410.7242 (theorem in a quote), 1412.2039 math0603642
(TOC in a quote), 2507.09788 2307.10959 2308.06338 2410.15097 0804.3724 math0612590 (theorem in a footnote), 1310.0491
(an ltx:text). Repros block-model/para_level_in_{quote,note_wrapfigure}_opens_inline_logical_block; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch69c::{para_level_block_in_quote_opens_an_inline_logical_block,
para_level_block_in_note_and_wrapfigure_opens_an_inline_logical_block}`.

### 701. A graphics rule keeps its converter command unexpanded, and a TeX source given as a graphic is sized by its asked width, height or scale alone (graphics.sty: `\edef`, graphicx's full `\Gin@req@sizes`)

graphics.sty:150-154 `\DeclareGraphicsRule` `\edef`s `\Gin@rule@<ext>`, expanding `<command>`; here it is kept
`\unexpanded` (graphics_sty.rs): no converter runs, and the expansion would reach macros only a driver defines
(`\OutputFile`). graphicx's `\includegraphics` follows a rule as `\Gin@setfile` does (graphics.sty:254-301;
graphicx_sty.rs `\lx@Gin@include`, `\lx@Gin@setfile`) when its type is one a package includes itself — a
`\Ginclude@<type>` that is not a driver's (pdftex.def, dvips.def, xetex.def, dvipdfmx.def, luatex.def, dvisvgm.def
types: eps, pdf, png, jpg, …) — and the rule names no command: gincltex.sty:43 `.tex`, figlatex.sty:120 `.pdftex_t`.
The type's reader (`\Gread@<type>`) sets the bounding box when the rule reads the file's own extension, and the
requested size is graphicx.sty:140-187's in part: `width`, `height` (`totalheight` as height), else `scale` of the
bounding box; `keepaspectratio`, `angle`, `trim`, `viewport` and the `*` clip are not applied to it. Only the file's
own extension is matched, on the name expanded (tikzscale.sty:183 passes `{\tikzscale@fileName}`), with no
`\Gin@rule@*` and no extension appended from `\Gin@extensions`; a file the graphics search path and `\input` do not
find goes to the image constructor as before. svg's `\includeinkscape` (svg_sty.rs)
sizes its overlay by the overlay's own `\svgwidth`/`\svgscale` interface, where svg.sty:1355-1370 patches `\picture`
to set `\unitlength` (the same width; `scale` scales the picture; a `height` alone is not applied). Why: the author's figure, which went to the
image converter and was lost (1604.05572, 2511.17298, 2305.04329, 2408.06999, 2305.16841, 2402.04829, 2310.03515;
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #921). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch70a::{gincltex_tex_graphic_is_read_as_tex,
includeinkscape_inputs_the_overlay, standalone_loads_gincltex}`.

### 702. pgfsys-latexml.def answers gnuplot-lua-tikz's driver table as pgfsys-tex4ht.def (`html`)

gnuplot-lua-tikz-common.tex:17-32 (gnuplot's lua terminal style, which papers ship beside their plots) keys its output
mode by the pgf driver file and stops with an `\errmessage` for a driver its table lacks. pgfsys_latexml_def.rs defines
`\gnuplot@select@driver@pgfsys-latexml.def` as `html`, the mode of pgfsys-tex4ht.def, the other driver that writes SVG
for the web: a plot's image file is `\pgfimage` (`\gploadimage`, :88-90), an inline raw image gnuplot's own "not
implemented" warning (:79-83), never the `pdf`/`ps` modes' PDF/PostScript image operators (:50-77). The table's own
`\def`s leave the entry alone. Witness 2501.11366. Guard `perfect_kernel_batch70a::gnuplot_lua_tikz_driver_mode`.

### 707. Every alignment cell's frame is a braced template's `{…}`: a cell's stray `}` closes it, whatever the template (TeX: per template — latex.ltx's tabular braces, array.sty's `\begingroup`, a bare `\halign`'s none)

**TeX**: a cell's `}` that closes one group more than the cell opened meets what the template put around the cell.
latex.ltx's tabular template (`\@tabclassz`, latex.ltx:16666) wraps the cell in `{…}`, so the `}` closes that brace and
the column end then meets `align_state` −1 (tex.web §1127 `align_error`, "Missing { inserted"); array.sty's
(`\d@llarbegin` = `\begingroup`) gives "Extra }, or forgotten \endgroup" (§1069), the `}` deleted; a bare `\halign{#…}`
meets the alignment group itself, "Missing \cr inserted" (§1132), and the row ends there.

**Perl**: the `}` pops the cell's group (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #923).

**Rust** (70b): the cell frame carries the template-brace mark of KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #908 (alignment.rs `start_column`),
so for every alignment the cell's `}` closes the template's `{` and the frame stays; the column end then gets its `{`
from `align_error` and `end_column` closes it. One shape, the latex.ltx tabular's, for all templates: the error count
matches each case's pdflatex count in the measured shapes (`{a & b} \\` 2, `a & b} \\` 1, with and without array.sty),
the message is latex.ltx's, every cell kept; the bare-`\halign` row break of §1132 is not reproduced. Why: the frame
holds the column's bookkeeping (`alignmentStartColumn`), and popping it lost the first cell to a spanning second
(`<td colspan="2">b</td>`), the content loss Perl shows. Guard `perfect_kernel_batch70b::tabular_stray_brace_keeps_its_cells`.

### 715. A printed `\@title` or `\@author` is the field's ink by its tokens' provenance, lifted where the frontmatter is placed (Perl: the structured copy and the print both shown)

Frontmatter model M3, stage S1 (field provenance only; user rulings 2026-10-17, design study
agent_reports/2026-10-16_frontmatter_design_study.md §6; the title-print study's rule R3, its stage 3; main-session
ruling 2026-10-17: out-of-band provenance, not in-band mark tokens). Perl takes the frontmatter from the setter call
(`\lx@add@title` at latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1059-1063, `\lx@add@authors` at :1076-1079) and renders the header from
that copy; a document that also typesets the stores itself — no `\maketitle`, `{\Large\bf \@title\par}` (lrec's
`\maketitleabstract`: 2402.14614, 1603.09631), 1605.00182's own `\centerline{\Large\bf{\noindent\@title}}`, puthesis's
`\LARGE \@title` (1503.06457) — shows the title (and the author line) twice, in Perl as here before (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
#935); the title copy went only by the text-matching dedup (#146), the author's not at all.

**Provenance, out of band.** `Token` (latexml_core token.rs) has a `prov: u16` field (`0` = none) in what was the
struct's padding: `Token` stays 8 bytes (`token_size_invariant`; 12 under `token-locators`, as before), laid out
`#[repr(C)]` `text`, `code`, `prov` with a two-byte `Catcode` (`#[repr(u16)]`) so it has no pad byte and `code` stays
at byte 4 (`token_layout_code_at_byte_4`; see Cost). It is not part
of TeX's token: `PartialEq` ignores it (so `\ifx`, `\meaning`, xstring, `\pdfstrcmp` compare as pdflatex), it is never
written or dumped, and whatever builds a token from characters (`\string`, `\detokenize`, `\scantokens`, `\write`,
`\csname`) builds one without it. The kernel `\title` and `\author` (sect05.rs) stamp their store once the frontmatter
has its copy: `\lx@field@mark\gdef\@title{title}` / `\lx@field@mark\def\@author{author}` (base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_fields.rs) redefine the
store with the same tokens, each carrying "token *i* of field *F*" (`field_prov`: 2 bits field, 14 bits position), and
record the field's extent (`lx_field_extent_<F>`): the position of every token of the value that makes ink — a letter,
an other character, a control sequence, an active character; not a space, brace, `$`, `^`, `_`, `&`, `#`, whose effect
the tokens around them cover. Each `\title` (`\author`) call's positions follow the previous call's
(`lx_field_base_<F>`), so a copy of an earlier value (`\let\oldtitle\@title`, then `\title{Short}`) is no print of the
current one (fms1 re-review finding 7; guard `field_prov_earlier_value_copy_kept`), and a print is judged on the
current call's positions only (`lx_field_range_<F>`: a run's cover is clipped to them, and a run that consumes an
earlier call's positions is joined with none — round 3 joined `\title{A Title}`'s print with the next call's and lifted
both: round-3 review finding 2, probes r12, r13; guards `field_prov_title_calls_kept`, `field_prov_edef_calls` (also the
copies in reverse order), `field_prov_author_calls_kept`, `field_prov_title_after_maketitle_kept`); a field whose calls
pass 16,383 tokens in all is not stamped (and no earlier copy of it is whole).
Nothing is added to the store, so every token operation sees exactly what pdflatex sees (the round-1 in-band marks made
`\ifx\@title\same`, `\equal`, `\IfStrEq`, `\pdfstrcmp` false, `\StrLen` 6 for "Same", `\@gobble`/`\@car`/`\StrLeft`
take a mark, and `\csname\@title\endcsname` err — fms1 review finding 3; guard `field_prov_token_tests`, every line =
pdflatex). An empty or blank value is left unstamped.

The provenance travels the way the tokens do: copies keep it (macro bodies, arguments, `\edef`/`\protected@xdef`,
titling's `\thetitle` set by the after-slot from the stamped store); the expansion of a stamped token inherits it
(gullet `invoke_expansion` and the partial-expansion loop, `inherit_field_prov`: an `\and` in `\@author` expands to
author ink); a case change keeps it (`\uppercase`, the kernel `\MakeUppercase`'s `\lx@latex@changecase` change the
character, not the provenance). What a stamped token digests to carries it (stomach `invoke_token`: the box or whatsit's
`fieldProv` property), with what its invocation consumed of the value: its own position up to the next stamped token
still in the pushback (`gullet::field_cover_of`: a primitive's or constructor's arguments, `\hspace{1em}`'s `1em`,
`\\[2pt]`'s `[2pt]`, a formula from its `$`), merged with the cover of a boxless invocation just before it (a font
switch, `\relax`, a macro still to be expanded: `token::field_cover_set_pending`; a macro's position and arguments are
covered by its expansion's boxes). Each such cover is recorded in digestion order in the field ledger
(`token::field_ledger_push`, the box's `fieldSerial`). The document builder (core `Document::absorb`) turns the boxes into
runs of field ink: a box of field *F* opens a run with `<?ltx-field-mark begin F id?>` where its ink goes (the open text
node closed first), the next boxes of *F* at that absorb level continue it while they go on in the value's order, and
the run closes with `<?ltx-field-mark end F id serials?>` (the ledger serials of the boxes it absorbed) before the
first box without that field, or when the absorb that opened it ends (a table cell's, an environment body's). A box
whose cover ends at or before a position a box of the run started at reads the value again: it
closes the run and opens one of its own (`\StrLeft{\@title}{3}\@title`, the second print's `T`; a construct's own box
absorbed around what its argument made, `\textsc{One}`'s whatsit after `One`, covers it and goes on). A re-read from
the value's first position starts where a macro's expansion does (all its boxes at the macro's position), so a run is
also no whole print when it holds a box of one character of the value twice (`lx_field_chars_<F>`, the letters and
other characters: `\StrLeft{\@title}{1}\@title`'s two `T`s; a print digests each character once). Round 3 made such
a line one run covering the whole value and lifted "TwiTwice Title" (round-3 review finding 4, probes r4, r5; guards
`field_prov_reprint_order_kept`, also fragment/whole/fragment, and `field_prov_whole_twice_lifted`: the whole title
twice on one line is two whole prints, each lifted). What a field-ink whatsit absorbs is its ink, whatever its parts'
provenance. No run opens in math, at any depth of an `ltx:Math` (an `\mbox` in a formula is no print of the field).
A run's cover is what the ledger recorded for the boxes it absorbed (`token::field_ledger_cover`), and for what an
alignment took between and right after them: a row's end marker (a value's `\\` set in a `tabular`), digested and
consumed by `digest_alignment_body` and never absorbed, is kept on the alignment's whatsit
(`document::field_ink_taken_serials`, `FIELD_TAKEN_PROPERTY`) and taken (`token::field_ledger_take`) only when
`Document::absorb` absorbs that whatsit: an alignment never shown — in an unused `\setbox`, `\sbox`, `{lrbox}` —
takes nothing (round 4 flagged the marker at digestion, so the `\\` of such a tabular joined title fragments printed
around it, or completed a print it ends, and they were lifted — round-4 review finding 2, probes s25, s27, s28, controls
s26, s29; guards `field_prov_unshown_alignment_kept`, `field_prov_unshown_alignment_trailing_kept`; a box holding the
alignment used twice takes it twice, `field_prov_alignment_box_used_twice_lifted`). Never an entry absorbed elsewhere or never absorbed: round 3 extended a run over the
ledger's next entries of the field that no run held, so a fragment beside the rest of the value in an unused
`\setbox`, or in a formula's `\mbox`, was taken for whole and lifted (round-3 review finding 1, probes r19, r20; guards
`field_prov_unused_boxes_kept` — also `\sbox`, `\savebox`, `{lrbox}` — `field_prov_math_mbox_kept` and
`field_prov_box_in_math_and_text`, where the formula use of a box was lifted with its paragraph). A box used twice is in
each run that absorbs it (`field_prov_box_used_twice_lifted`). A run set in invisible ink (`\phantom`, `\vphantom`:
`<ltx:text class="ltx_phantom">`) is no print and joins none (`field_prov_phantom_kept`). The marks are processing
instructions (no node of content to the block built around them; an element mark made a `{center}` a logical-block —
settled dead end), and a run's two marks carry its id, so they pair by construction, never with another print's (the
round-1 begin/end pairing took `\StrLeft{\@title}{5}`'s begin and `\StrGobbleLeft{\@title}{6}`'s end and removed the
paragraph between them — finding 2; guard `field_prov_fragments_kept`). One print split by the structure it is set in
(article's author `tabular`s: one run per cell, `\and`'s `\end{tabular}…\begin{tabular}`) is joined back: a run that
goes on with the field's later positions, with no ink between the two, is one run with the one before when both
consume the current call's positions only and their covers, with what the alignment took between them (the cells'
`\\`), cover every extent position from where the first stopped to where the second starts (`field_ink_runs`;
1605.00182, 0706.0979, 1004.2125; guard `field_prov_author_tabular_lifted`). A second print
starts over and stays a run of its own, and two slices with a gap (`\StrLeft{\@title}{2}\par\StrRight{\@title}{2}`,
nothing of the gap digested) stay two runs, neither whole (round 2 joined them by their endpoints and removed both —
re-review finding 2, probe q16; guard `field_prov_two_slices_kept`). What an alignment took right after a run's last
box, of its field and continuing its cover, is the run's too, past an entry that covers no position of the extent (the
space the cell drops before it): a value's closing `\\` (1605.00182's `\author{… \\ }`; guard
`field_prov_author_trailing_cr_lifted`).
The work is gated: none in a conversion that stamped no field (`note_field_prov_stamped`), and none after the
placement settled the ink — the builder marks no run and the stomach records no ledger entry
(`token::field_ledger_live`, `field_ledger_settle`; guard `field_ledger_take_cover_and_settle`). That thread state is
per conversion: `document::reset_field_provenance` (the stamped gate, the ledger, its settled flag, the pending
cover) runs at every conversion's start, in `Converter::prepare_session`, not only in `reset_thread_engine` — a
persistent `cortex_worker` thread, a streaming restart and the CLI's supplements convert on one thread without an
engine reset, and round 4's settled ledger made every document after the first lift nothing (round-4 review finding
1, probe two/; guard `field_prov_second_conversion_lifted`, two conversions on one thread).

**The lift.** Where the frontmatter is placed — `\lx@frontmatterhere` (the `\maketitle` flush) and the fallback's
non-abstract branch (the first sectional unit or `\end{document}`) — `lift_marked_field_ink` runs once
(`lx_field_ink_settled`, `Document::settle_field_ink`: the open run closed, no runs after) and removes each run's ink,
with the wrappers it empties (not a `labels` one), when:
- the run is the whole field: its cover holds every position of the field's extent (`covers_extent`), a macro's too,
  so a slice the document takes of it (`\StrLeft`, `\StrMid`, `\@car`, `\@gobble`) is its own text and stays — also one
  that stops before a macro of the value (`\StrLeft{\@title}{5}` of `About \nm`: round 2 judged the first and last
  character only and lifted "About" — re-review finding 2, probe q2; guard `field_prov_slice_before_macro_kept`), while
  a print of a value holding a macro, `\\[2pt]`, `\hspace{1em}`, a font switch and a formula is whole
  (`field_prov_args_whole_lifted`);
- the run is in the document's title block: no body text precedes it in the document's content order
  (`field_runs_after_body_text`): no text before its begin mark, the text before it in its own block too, except a
  field's ink (between a run's marks: a title before its author), what is set apart from the page's flow (a frontmatter
  element, a note, a float, an error's markup, an index mark — round-4 review finding 4, probe s31,
  `field_prov_indexmark_lifted` — `ltx_phantom` ink, the `_Capture_` marks), and the text of a TeX box that does not
  hold the run. A box is decided by the TeX mechanism, not by the element it builds (main-session call 2026-10-17 on
  round-4 review finding 3), and a box marks only the element its own constructor opened, at the point it opens it
  (main-session call on round-5 review finding 1, option B; `Document::mark_field_box`, the `_fieldbox` bookkeeping
  attribute stripped at finalize): a constructor declared `mode => "restricted_horizontal"` outside math
  (`DeclaredMode::restricted_box`; `Constructor::digest_to_whatsit` sets the `fieldBox` whatsit property and the first
  element its absorption opens, before it absorbs anything, is marked, `Document::open_element`; one that opens none
  marks nothing; the digest-time mark waits for the live ledger only, not for a stamped field, since a header box may be
  digested before the body declares `\title` — the stamp is applied at absorb time, int22 on the r6 review finding 1): `\hbox` (so `\rightline`/`\leftline`/`\centerline`, each `\hbox to\hsize`, and `\colorbox`,
  color.sty's `\color@b@x`), `\mbox`, `\makebox`, `\raisebox`, `\fcolorbox`,
  `\scalebox`/`\resizebox`/`\rotatebox`/`\reflectbox`, amsmath's `\text` and `\eqref` outside math (an `\mbox`, an
  `\hbox`), `\shortstack`, `\put`, the pstricks frame boxes, `\turnbox`; `\framebox`/`\fbox` (no declared mode: its text
  branch, `\@frameb@x`'s `\hbox`); the capture of `insert_block` — `\vbox`, `\vtop`, `\parbox`, a minipage, a `p`
  column, a framed box (framed, mdframed, ascmac, a cuted strip, a tabularray box) — the mark riding its rename, its
  paragraph move and the lone child that takes its attributes, while a capture unwrapped into the context marks nothing;
  an environment whose begin code opens a box group (`TexGroup::Box`, latex.ltx's `\setbox\@tempboxa\vbox\bgroup`),
  checked behind the field-ink gate; an alignment's container (armed around its `open_container`). An element merged up
  by the font collapse (`auto_collapse_children`: an `\mbox` alone in its paragraph) leaves its mark on the element it
  merged into, which then holds only that box's material. Material a `\vbox`/`\vtop` absorbs straight into its context
  (a `\vbox` in a `\vbox`) marks nothing: round 5 marked "the current element if still empty", so
  `\noindent\vbox{\vbox{\hbox{X}}} Lorem…` marked the empty paragraph and its body text stopped counting (probes b2,
  b10, b11; guards `field_prov_nested_vbox_body_kept`, `field_prov_nested_vtop_body_kept`,
  `field_prov_nested_vbox_quote_kept`). Not boxes: `mode => "text"` constructors (`\textbf`), `\textsuperscript`
  (latex.ltx's `\mbox` is inside math), `{center}`/ `{flushright}` (`aligning_environment`'s capture is unmarked). Of
  the 54 constructors declared `restricted_horizontal` (each audited against its package), those that are no TeX box in
  the original: `\@index` (`\index` writes, prints nothing; `ltx:indexmark` is set apart anyway),
  `\lxDeclare`/`\@lxDefMathDeclare` and `\textbb` (bbold's font command; both open no element, so mark nothing),
  `\lx@acm@addresspart@` (acmart's `\institution`/`\city`…, plain text of `\affiliation`; marked, inside the
  frontmatter's contact, which is set apart), and `\tablenotemark` (an `\rlap` box in agupp.sty and the old aastex,
  `\textsuperscript` in aastex701.cls:8494; marked, but emitted as an `ltx:note`, which is set apart in a table or out
  of one, deluxetable_sty.rs:226-227). Round 4 took the element names
  `ltx:inline-block`/`inline-logical-block`/`inline-para`/`tabular` for boxes, so `\makebox`, `\mbox`, `\fbox`,
  `\raisebox` and `\rightline` (all an `ltx:text`) were body text and `\parbox` not. A cover's header box (the
  preprint-number `\parbox` of 0706.0979 and 1605.00182, a `\rightline{LA-UR-…}`, a `\makebox[\textwidth][r]{…}`, an
  `\mbox{preprint …}`, a `\colorbox`, an `\fcolorbox`, a `\scalebox`) is no body text
  (`field_prov_header_parbox_lifted`, `field_prov_header_rightline_lifted`, `field_prov_header_makebox_lifted`,
  `field_prov_header_mbox_lifted`, `field_prov_header_colorbox_lifted`, `field_prov_header_fcolorbox_lifted`,
  `field_prov_header_scalebox_lifted`; probes r16, r17, h1-h4). Paragraph material in a list environment
  (`{flushright}`, `{center}`, `quote`, an aligned display) is body text (`field_prov_header_flushright_kept`), and so
  is material no box constructor opened an element for (`\unhbox`/`\unvbox`, a capture unwrapped): the print kept
  (fail-safe). A letter
  that ends `\noindent\@author` signs it where pdflatex prints the name, and keeps it, its body in the paragraph flow
  (round 2 lifted it at the `\end{document}` fallback — re-review finding 3, probe q3; guard
  `field_prov_signature_after_body_kept`), in `{flushleft}` or in a `{quote}` in the signature's own paragraph (round 3
  took aligned and quoted text, and the text of the print's own block, for no body, and lifted the signature —
  round-3 review finding 3, probes r9, r18; guards `field_prov_letter_flushleft_kept`, `field_prov_letter_quote_kept`).
  Header cases that therefore stay (kept, as before S1): a header line before the title block in the flow or in a
  list environment — plain text (`Preprint ABC-123\hfill\today`, probe r11; `field_prov_header_text_kept`),
  `{flushright}` (`field_prov_header_flushright_kept`), a centred subject line; and text the title block sets before a
  print (a `\textsuperscript{*}` after the title, a `by`, an affiliation
  line before a second print: review probe q9, whose three prints round 3 lifted), which keeps the prints after it;
- the frontmatter displays the field, by the XSLT's rule: no `<ltx:titlepage>` at document level (beside one the title
  template is skipped and a creator renders nothing, LaTeXML-structure-xhtml.xsl:374-375, :687-692 = Perl :358-359)
  and a document-level `<ltx:title>`, resp. author `<ltx:creator>` (round 1 also lifted an author print beside a
  titlepage, leaving the HTML without an author — finding 1; guard `field_prov_author_beside_titlepage_kept`); so a
  print beside or inside a titlepage is the displayed copy and stays (1304.0681, 1503.03277);
- every ancestor of both marks is a title-block wrapper (`is_field_ink_wrapper`: para, p, logical and inline blocks,
  text, emph, a cover tabular) and none is framed: never inside a titlepage, a float, a note, a frontmatter element or a
  frame (`\fbox{\@title}`), as the dedup (68s review finding 4);
- the prints fill their lines: the paragraph or table cell around each mark holds nothing but the runs being lifted
  (all fields judged together, until none drops out: a title and its author on one line go together — finding 5;
  guard `field_prov_title_author_one_line`) and line breaks (`\centerline`'s, which go with it), so a mention in prose
  (`This report, \@title, …`, `Title: \thetitle`) keeps its words.

**Every whole print is lifted** (user ruling 2026-10-17, "lift every whole print"): a title or author the document
prints N times as a whole in its title block shows once, in the frontmatter element (field_mark_uppercase: pdflatex
"UPPER TITLE" twice, here the `<h1>` only).

The lift is judged where the frontmatter is placed, mid-build: `\noindent\@title\maketitle{} and then …` (re-review
probe q15) lifts the title from a paragraph that the document's text continues, which is right because latex.ltx's
`\maketitle` begins with `\par`, so the print is a paragraph of its own; a print and `\maketitle` inside one `{center}`
(probes q13, q14) is not lifted by provenance (the dedup, or kept, as before S1).

Residuals (missed lifts; the print stays, as before S1): a value that ends in a primitive's argument
(`\title{Foo\vspace{2pt}}`) or in a macro whose arguments its expansion drops is no whole print (nothing stamped
follows to bound what it consumed); a value holding a `\footnote` (`\title{Foot Title\footnote{…}}` printed, round-3
review probes r7, r8); a value built from an earlier one (`\let\oldtitle\@title`, `\title{\oldtitle\\[1ex]\large Sub
Title}`: the expansion of `\oldtitle` carries the earlier call's positions, so the current call's `\oldtitle` is never
covered, probe r14); an `\edef` copy of an earlier call whose value the next call repeats (`\edef\xa{\@title}
\title{Same Title}`, probe r15: the copy carries the earlier call's positions); the header cases above; a value whose
print digests one of its characters twice (a document macro that sets its argument twice inside `\title{…}`), taken
for a re-read (above).

Every mark goes with the lift; marks still in the tree at `\end{document}` are removed with their ink kept
(`settle_field_marks`), and the core finalize drops a stray one (document.rs, `FIELD_MARK_TARGET`). A lifted title
print sets `lx_title_ink_dedup_done`, so the dedup is left for a copy no provenance explains. Each lift logs
`Info:frontmatter:field_ink`. `\pdfstringdef` is a `\gdef` here (hyperref_sty.rs) and the `pdftitle=` RDF value the
unexpanded keyval (Perl's `ToString`).

Cost: no `Token` growth (8 bytes; the `token-locators` origin handle `loc` cannot carry it without making that build
the default, 12 bytes per token); the stamping, the expansion inheritance, the covers and the absorb runs touch only
stamped tokens and the boxes absorbed before the placement settles the ink. The measured cost (user ruling 2026-10-17:
accepted, plus one profiling pass) was the token layout: Rust's default layout put `prov` at byte 4 and `code` at 6
with a pad byte, so every move of a token on the gullet's read path (`Option<Token>`, `CheckedRead::Tok`, the `Result`
slot of `read_internal_token_checked`) became a field-wise copy (agent_reports/2026-10-17_fms1_profile.md). `perf stat
-e instructions:u`, bench builds, 3 runs each, against the base a034d4e7f5: empty article +1.29 % (round 2) → +0.65 %
(`repr(C)` + two-byte `Catcode`; `repr(C)` alone +1.14 %, the pad byte still copied as a 3-byte blob); 2311.18489
+3.27 % → +1.66 % (938.6M / 950.7M / 944.7M and 4738.0M / 4892.8M / 4816.8M instructions). XML identical; peak RSS +0.1-0.5 % (round 2).
What remains is the read path's token handling, not reworked (one bounded pass): `read_internal_token_checked`'s
return writes three stores (`text`, `code`, `prov`; base two, round 2 four with the pad), and the `Option<Token>`
niche test of the pushback pop is still a 64-bit mask on the whole token.

Not in S1 (stages S2-S5 of the study): the lock is unchanged, no call observer, no mechanism deleted; bindings' own
`\title`/`\author` (revtex4_support, ams_support, iopart_support, mn2e_support, …) do not stamp; the deposit of a
refused class `\maketitle` still nulls `\@title`/`\@author`, so a class's title page prints nothing stamped; display
stays "lift" (the in-place display is S5, after a ruling). A/B: see SYNC_STATUS (fms1). Repros
sectioning-frontmatter/field_mark_*, field_prov_*; guards `perfect_kernel_batchfms1`.

### 719. appolb.cls (Acta Physica Polonica B), not in TeX Live and mostly not shipped, is bound over OmniBus

appolb.cls is not in TeX Live and 15 of the 17 sampled papers that use it do not ship it, so the class is OmniBus's and its `\PACS`
(appolb.cls:322, 2210.03396's v3.5 copy) was undefined (13 papers of the int19 census: 0712.3606, 1007.2277, 1101.3125,
1108.2782, 1605.06550, nucl-th0308018, physics0501160). As the 64u bindings for absent journal styles (#493-496), a
contrib binding (appolb_cls.rs) loads OmniBus, which serves the class's frontmatter as before, and adds what the class
defines that the papers use or its template invites: `\PACS` as the pacs classification ("PACS numbers:"), `\received`
as `\date`, `\eqsec` (:578-582, equations numbered within sections), `\headtitle`/`\headauthor` (:299, :304) as
running-head notes, the text abbreviations `\ie`/`\eg`/`\cf`/`\etal`/`\ibid` (:1019-1033), `\e` (:1059) and
`\lambdabar` (:1036-1048), and, as the binding replaces a shipped copy, the class's other public commands as it defines
them: `\preprint` (:278-282, with `\ifPreprint`/`\prepNo`; a preprint note, made where `\maketitle` sets `\prepNo`, :399,
so a `\preprint` after `\maketitle` shows none), the `\volume`/`\No` counts and `\pageno`
(:283-285), `\ifRedakcja` (:83), `\WERS` (:311), `\anymode` (:1019), `\half`/`\Half` (:1053-1057), `\Tr` (:1061), `\Eq`
(:1063), `\seteqprefix`/`\reseteqprefix` (:1065-1066); its lettered-equation environments `{eqletters}`/`{eqlettarray}`
(:627-648, :1096-1112) are not bound (no paper uses them). The binding also serves the 2 papers that ship the class (0801.2427, cond-mat0205657),
which read it raw before with 0 errors: the address is now a contact and the PACS a classification, where the raw
class set the address inside the personname and the PACS as a paragraph (its empty "(Received )" line is gone). It is
a stand-in for the author's file (latexml_core binding/author_files.rs `AUTHOR_FILE_STAND_INS`): `\IfFileExists{appolb.cls}`
finds it only where the paper ships it. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch71a::{appolb_pacs, appolb_running_heads_and_abbreviations, appolb_class_commands}`.

### 720. tkz-euclide's pre-v3 `\usetkzobj`/`\usetkztool` are defined over the current package (TL 2025: undefined)

tkz-euclide v1-v2 loaded its object files with `\usetkzobj{all|<objects>}` (tkz-tools-eu-modules.tex:18-58, still in
TeX Live but no longer read); since v3 the package loads every object itself (tkz-euclide.sty:173-199) and the loaders
are gone, so a paper written for the old API errs under TL 2025 ("Undefined control sequence"). User ruling 2026-10-17:
the binding serves both versions. The contrib binding (tkz_euclide_sty.rs) reads the real package and defines the two
loaders, where neither is defined (a paper's own older copy keeps its own), as macros that take their arguments and load
nothing, since everything is loaded. Witnesses 1506.03598, 1612.05374, 2005.14485, 1906.04134, 1608.04592; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch71a::tkz_euclide_old_usetkzobj`.

### 721. A TeX macro's undelimited argument that is a command reading a mandatory argument is read with its own arguments, the call the author wrote, with a Warning that TeX errs there (amsmath/amsfonts accents, mathstyle scripts; TeX: an error; Perl: no diagnostic)

amsmath's accents (amsmath.sty:754-797, `\mathaccentV`'s fifth argument, `\mathaccent"…{#5}`), amsfonts' `\widehat#1`/
`\widetilde#1` (amsfonts.sty:78-87) and breqn/mathstyle's `\sb`/`\sp` (mathstyle.sty:126-127,
`\mathsub{\protect\subsupstyle#1}`, the math-active `_`/`^`) take their accentee or script as an undelimited macro
argument and brace it, so a macro after them is the item with its whole expansion (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #945; breqn's, SYNC
71a (7)). The bindings pass that argument to LaTeXML's own accent or script through one helper (amsmath_sty.rs
`undelimited_argument`: `\lx@ams@mathaccentV` for amsmath, `\lx@undelimited@argument` for the others), which reads a
single command by its definition, never its name (user ruling 2026-10-17; `classify_undelimited_argument`, looking
through a robust wrapper's parameterless `\protect <cs>` to `<cs>` — a robust command's `\protect \cs␣`, the binding's
`\ensuremath` = `\protect\@ensuremath` (`\hat\ensuremath{x}`: pdflatex 5 errors) — and an alias's one-token body,
amsmath.sty:892 `\def\Hat{\hat}`):
- **no mandatory argument** (`\alpha`, `\nabla`, `\infty`, `\relax`, `\bf`, `\muu`, `\newcommand{\tasknum}[1][]{…}`, an
  undefined command): braced, as TeX braces it, with no diagnostic — `\hat\relax x` is the hat over an empty nucleus
  and x after it, as TeX's `\showlists`. Under amsmath's `\mathaccentV` an amsmath accent (`\hat\vec x`) is the nested
  accent: braced, itself over an empty nucleus (`\macc@nested`, :832-870; `\showlists`: the hat over the vec over an
  empty box, x outside). Only that reader nests: under amsfonts' `\widehat#1` or breqn's `\sb#1` an amsmath accent is a
  command reading a mandatory argument (`\widehat\hat z`: pdflatex 7 errors; breqn's `y^\hat z`: 6, "Argument of
  \mathaccentV has an extra }"), read as the next case;
- **a mandatory argument** (`\mathbf`, `\text`, `\mathrm`, `\newcommand\nv[1]`, `\DeclareRobustCommand\vv[1]`, amsfonts'
  `\widehat`): the command read with its own arguments, the call the author wrote. A macro's arguments are read by its
  parameters (an ltcmd command's by its signature: `m`, `o`/`O{…}`, `s`, through the `\cs code` of an all-`m` one) and
  reverted, and the call braced, so the accent or script takes the call's whole expansion: `\hat\foo x+y`
  (`\def\foo#1{}`) is the hat over `\foo x`'s empty expansion and `+y` after it, `\hat\pair{a}{b}` over `(a,b)`,
  `\hat\nv x` (`\nv[1]{#1_1}`) over `x_1`, `\hat\vq[a]{x}` (`{om}`) over `\vq[a]{x}`. A primitive or constructor
  (`\mathbf`, `\sqrt`, `\text`) is left unbraced: the item it makes is the call, its arguments read at digestion
  (`\hat\mathbf{x}` a hat over the bold x, breqn's `x_\text{abc}` a subscript "abc"). A call missing an undelimited
argument where the next token ends or structures the current list (`read_call_arguments`, `ends_the_list`: by meaning a
column end — `&` or a `\let` copy, `\cr`, `\crcr`, `\span` — and a catcode-6 token; by name `\par`, `\\`, `\end`, `\]`,
`\)`; the end of the input) is left unbraced, its arguments read so far put back, as TeX leaves the tokens: the braced
call would take a cell's `&` or a row's `\\` into its group (`\hat\pair{a} & x` in `cases` keeps both cells, `\hat\nv
& = 1` and `a &= \hat\nv \\ y &= 2` in `align` their cells and rows). A `\def` with a leading delimiter
  (`\def\lp(#1)`), an ltcmd signature with a delimited or embellishment argument and a binding closure without a
  parameter list are left unbraced for the item to read with what follows. Each occurrence gets one
  `Warning:malformed:<reader>` naming the reading made, e.g. "amsmath's \hat takes \pair alone as its argument, where
  TeX errs: \pair reads an argument of its own; read as \hat{\pair{a}{b}}" ("read as \hat{\mathbf…}, \mathbf with its
  argument" for a constructor; breqn's names `_`/`^`, what the author types), located at the source line (a heading's,
  item's or theorem's text is digested from a token list; the innermost source mouth's location is given). pdflatex:
  "Argument of \select@group has an extra }", "Argument of \text@ has an extra }", 5-9 errors for one such accent;
- **a binding closure** (an expandable definition without a token body, or a conditional): unbraced as before, since
  a closure may read past the brace; the Warning only where it declares a mandatory parameter, the one case in which
  TeX's macro would err.
One Warning per source occurrence: a digestion that re-reads a source the document typesets where it stands gives none
(`tex_math::REREAD_COPY`, set by `\lx@reread@copy`): the toc copy of a heading or caption without a `[short]` (sect04.rs;
`\lx@toc@copy@text` for the kernel's, longtable's and listings' captions, where a `[short]` the same as the caption — as
`\@dblarg` gives it — counts as the caption), the reference forms of a tag (`\lx@make@tags`: an `\item[…]` label's
typerefnum, a `\tag{…}`'s refnum), natbib's label copies (written to the .aux; a full compile errs nowhere — pdflatex run three times on
`\bibitem[{$\hat\mathbf{x}$}(2000)]` gives 0 errors — so no Warning is TeX's own count). A
`[short]` title or caption is its own source, digested once, into the toc: TeX errs on it only when the list is typeset
(`\tableofcontents`, `\listoffigures`), and it warns once regardless, because we digest and keep it.
Why not error as TeX does: content before PDF fidelity (priority order 2026-10-06), where TeX's recovery loses the
formula — under the braced form 2210.10207 lost 11,424 words — and the shape is rare (7 occurrences in 7,500 sampled
1505/1905/2305 papers, most of them in unused macros: 1905.01764 7, 1505.00442 1); why the Warning: the source is not
valid TeX, and the reading is ours (ruling: never an Error, never silent). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch71a::{amsmath_accent_macro_argument, amsmath_accent_ltcmd_argument,
undelimited_argument_reads_the_whole_call, undelimited_argument_call_stops_at_the_list_end,
undelimited_argument_through_a_robust_wrapper, amsfonts_widehat_macro_argument, breqn_script_macro_argument,
undelimited_argument_warning_once_per_occurrence}`.

### 725. latex209.def's LaTeX2e-command traps apply to `\usepackage`, `\listfiles`, `\lrbox` and `\@xargdef`; the `\ensuremath` trap is held while bindings call it where their 2.09-era originals do not

**TeX**: `\documentstyle` inputs latex209.def, whose :79-91 wrap `\usepackage`, `\listfiles`, `\ensuremath`, `\lrbox`
and `\@xargdef` in `\@latex@e@error`, enabled by `\@documentclasshook` (:137): each use after the class errs "LaTeX2e
command … in LaTeX 2.09 document" and then runs; :105-123 let the document define the 2e-only names it lists.

**Perl**: none of latex209.def is applied (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #925).

**Rust** (int20, user ruling 2026-10-17): tex_job.rs `\lx@latex@ix@definitions` applies :79-123 and :137 except the
`\ensuremath` wrapper. Our bindings call `\ensuremath` in code their originals write without it — AASTeX 4
aaspp4.sty (1995, shipped with astro-ph9606031) `\def\fd{\hbox{$.\!\!^{\rm d}$}}` against aas_support_sty.rs
`\ensuremath{\@fd}` (Perl-origin aas_support.sty.ltxml L499), REVTeX 3, emulateapj — so the trap fired on binding code
pdflatex never runs: astro-ph9606143 7 → 9, astro-ph9701025 1 → 15, cond-mat9906271 0 → 6, astro-ph9809336 45 → 48,
astro-ph9806372 2 → 4 (A/B over the 250 `\documentstyle` papers of the census sample, none of them calling
`\ensuremath` in the source). The trap lands with a kernel-internal ensure-math for binding code (SYNC row). Residual:
latex.ltx's "`\usepackage` before `\documentclass`" (`\@fileswithoptions`) that pdflatex adds is not reproduced. No census paper uses
`\usepackage` after `\documentstyle` (0806.0904 redefines it: `\def\usepackage#1{\input{#1.sty}}`, no trap in pdflatex either). Guard `perfect_kernel_batch70b::documentstyle_usepackage_errs_as_latex209`.

### 731. A stand-in binding is followed by the paper's copy of its file, which only provides ("a stand-in's copy provides")

**TeX**: `\documentclass{svjour3}`, `\usepackage{aas_macros}`, `\input tcilatex` read the author's file the paper ships;
every definition in it, and everything it registers for later, takes effect.

**Perl**: `FindFile` prefers the `.ltxml` (Package.pm:2113-2133): the binding loads and the copy is never read, so an
extra command the copy defines and the paper uses is undefined (aas_macros.sty:94-97 `\kms`, 1309.5950).

**Rust** (72a, user ruling 2026-10-17, memory `feedback_rulings_2026_10_17_od721_h1`): after a binding on
`AUTHOR_FILE_STAND_INS` (author_files.rs) has loaded, the copy the paper ships — the request as the paper wrote it
(`fallback_request` for a versioned fallback: `icml2026` → icml2025.sty), found in the paper's source directory or a
`{filecontents}` file, never TeX Live's — is read raw at the same point, origin `File` (content.rs `read_stand_in_copy`,
from `input_definitions_impl` after the binding's `\ver@` and from `input`'s `.tex` route), before the load's
`\AtEndOfClass`/`\AtEndOfPackage` code runs. The rules:
0. *Identity.* The copy is read only when it is the file the binding stands in for (content.rs
   `copy_is_the_stood_in_file`; 72a r3 rule): (a) its `\Provides(Expl)?(Class|Package|File)` names the binding that
   answered (the file itself when the binding is of its name; #744), or a file the binding is built on — one its own code loads (`state::note_stand_in_file`,
   `stand_in_built_on`) —, a declared macro read as its definition in the copy says, as `\ProvidesClass` expands its
   argument (r4: cimart.cls:13-14 `\def\ClassName@CiM{cimart}\ProvidesClass{\ClassName@CiM}`, 2412.00032), whatever
   the version (1609.03892's fcs.cls of 2016, older than the `\fcssetup` the binding
   models; 2308.11432's `\ProvidesExplClass{fcs}`; 2011.13564's IEEEtai.cls, IEEE's own, `\ProvidesClass{IEEEtran}`, the
   class the binding loads; apjfonts.sty, 1202.3442); else (b) it defines at least a quarter of the binding's public
   command set, the letters-only names its own code assigned with those of a stand-in its own code loads
   (`state::stand_in_public_names`, `State::stand_in_last_load`, merged at `end_stand_in_load`: the diagrams binding's
   diagrams.tex; not a file it loads otherwise, `StandInLoadGuard::suspend`, nor a stand-in such a file loads —
   `StandInLoadGuard::loaded_by`, r4: OmniBus's `RequirePackage!("aas_macros")`, omnibus_cls.rs:71, swelled asme2ej's
   set from 22 names to 87 and nature-pre's from 3 to 68, so 2309.12017, 2102.01782 and 2111.09589 went unread). A binding with no public name of its own
   reads no undeclared copy (aipcheck.tex, mssymb.tex, citesort.sty, revtex.sty: 45 of the simulation's copies). The quarter is the
   gap of a bimodal distribution: over the reviewer's simulation of the census's 4,346 distinct copies
   (`scratch_356a0c47/rev72a/ident_sim2.json`; approximate: the binding's `.rs` names, no nested stand-ins), the
   undeclared copies' shares fall 124 under a tenth, 28 between a tenth and four tenths, 1,028 above; the quarter
   admits the 1,047 the r2 rule read by names, and its absolute (20 names) and copy-side (a quarter of the copy's
   names) clauses admitted none beyond it, so they are gone. Per clause on the simulation under the r4 rule
   (`scratch_72a/r4/tools/ident_r4.py`): declaration 3,071 (2,987, and 84 of a binding whose public set is empty),
   names 1,046 (cimart's one copy now by declaration), empty set and no matching declaration 45 not read, 133
   rejected (107 arxiv/PRIMEarxiv/icml2019 copies their binding reads raw itself, rule 4), 51 whose binding file the
   simulation could not map; the one copy near the quarter (0.225-0.275) was cimart's. The simulation's public sets
   approximate the runtime's (nature-pre: 5 there, 3 here, so its two copies read at 1 of 3). An author's own
   file that only shares the name is not read (base behaviour): hep-ph9609379's diagrams.sty, fifteen `\special`
   PostScript macros sharing one name (`\diagram`) of the diagrams binding's 270 (r1: its `\Bullet` called the
   binding's `\diagram`, 1 → 101 Errors and a Fatal); 2411.02780's equations.sty, which is annotate-equations.sty
   renamed (`\ProvidesPackage{annotate-equations}`; r1: 2 → 99 Errors over xkeyval's `\usevalue`). Logged at Info.
   Reading such a file raw, as TeX does, is an open row.
1. *Ownership* (a routed copy's declared text names: rule 14; a copy under the binding's own name supplies none). A
   name is the binding's when it was assigned while the stand-in binding loaded (origin.rs `StandInLoadGuard`,
   `State::stand_in_meanings`: its `DefMacro!`s, `Let!`s, `RawTeX`, the bindings it required) at an origin of
   LaTeXML's own, its guesses included (`Fallback`: the OmniBus base a class binding loads, whose `\received`
   WileyNJDv5.cls:5071 replaced, dropping 2609.19994's dated frontmatter — OD #408's yielding is to the document, and
   the copy is not the document), or its meaning is a definition made under that very name at origin `Unknown`, `Pool`
   or `Binding` (a pool's `\maketitle`, another binding's `\citep`), or under one of the semantic layer's own `\lx@`
   names (79i: the pool's `\let\label\lx@label`, sect11.rs — no file defines an `\lx@` name; a shipped aastex7.cls's
   `\def\label` writing the `.aux`, aastex7.cls:635, aastex701.cls, siamltex.cls, emulateapj.cls, jasatex.cls, stood
   for the document and recorded no label: 2508.00291, 2510.05388, 2604.27071, 1205.2995, 1409.5957, 1412.0148; 16 of
   24 such proj98 papers now resolve every reference, 519 → 158 dangling; guard
   `perfect_kernel_batch79i::a_copy_redefining_label_keeps_the_documents_labels`); an environment is owned when `\begin{X}` or
   `\end{X}` is, or `\X` or `\endX` with them, and its names are decided together (r5): once the copy's code has kept
   one aside, the others it defines are kept too, though the first now carries the copy's meaning (cimart.cls:295-315's
   `\newtheorem{theorem}` left the binding's `\begin{theorem}` with the copy's `\end{theorem}`, a group open at the
   end: 2412.00032, 2408.07575's `{example}`); a plain macro's `\end…` partner alone does not make it owned (plain's
   `\endgroup`, a copy's `\group`). OmniBus's theorem autoload stubs (`\begin{theorem}` … `\begin{alg}`, which step
   aside for an environment declared since) are `Stub`, not a definition of the environment, so a copy's `\newtheorem`
   declares it whole (omnibus_cls.rs; pdflatex "Definition 1.1", "Theorem 1.2" on the reviewer's probe thm_copy).
   *Text defaults* (main-session ruling 2026-10-17, 72a r5): a public macro without parameters expanding to text
   (`\refname`, `\bibname`, `\abstractname`, `\contentsname`) that the base class the binding loads assigned last —
   a class its own code loads, and the classes that class loads, the pool's article/report/book and the OmniBus guess
   (`StandInLoadGuard::suspend_for`, `State::stand_in_base_defaults`) — or LaTeXML's kernel before the binding, is not
   owned (`state::unowned_text_default`): the copy's `\def`/`\renewcommand` of it holds, and its `\newcommand` defines
   it (`copy_provides_text_default_yields`, sect08.rs), as the real class's would over article.cls's — MRM.cls:3191
   `\def\refname{REFERENCES}` (2506.14995's PDF), ws-rv9x6.cls:91 `\newcommand\bibname{References}` (2301.03442).
   One the binding's own code assigns, or a binding it requires (natbib's), stays owned; natbib's `\bibname`/`\refname`
   are provided as natbib.sty:1093-1094 provides them (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #960). The format's names (`Plain`, `LatexDump`, `Format`), the document's world (`File`, `Document`), the
   other guesses that yield (`Fallback`, `Stub`, `Borrowed`) and `\let` copies of such meanings are not — except a
   `\let` LaTeXML's own code made while a stand-in binding loads, recorded as it is made (`State::binding_lets`,
   `let_i`, r4: not every pool `\newif` flag; the object a `\let` copies carries its source's name; aas_support_sty.rs's
   `\let\subjectheadings\keywords`, astro-ph0011001). Measured and
   declined (72a r2): narrowing ownership to the binding's own code, so that a copy's redefinition of a macro a package
   the binding loaded defined stands as in TeX, released the class bindings' frontmatter and layout macros to the copy
   (`\title`, `\author`, `\thanks`, `\keywords`, `\@makecaption` in 146 of 400 census papers, the NFSS size commands,
   the `\the<counter>`s) and brought back aastex7's three Fatals; constructors and primitives kept owned did not
   cover them (they are macros). The case it was for, 2411.02780, is rule 0's.
2. *Assignments.* Every meaning assignment of the read (`install_definition`, `assign_meaning`: the `\def` family,
   `\let`, `\chardef`…, the LaTeX declarators) to an owned name holds only inside the copy's own code: the binding's
   meaning is kept aside and put back when the read ends (state.rs `note_copy_provides_assignment`,
   `leave_copy_provides_frame`), so for the document it acted as `\providecommand`, while the copy's load-time logic
   sees what it defined, as in TeX — aipproc.cls:559 `\ifnum\pageref>0` after its option's `\chardef\pageref`
   (astro-ph0105128), epl2.cls:1317-1318's save-and-wrap of `\bibitem`, which the epl binding makes too and which a
   kept `\let` would turn into a self-call (0906.2627, 1102.2776, 1203.4765: Fatal loops before the rule). This
   refines the brief's "declined" by mechanism (the census hazard 4: a declined scratch name changed the copy's
   load-time logic); a name the code leaves as it found it (`\protected@edef`'s `\protect`) is not logged. Everything
   else stands as TeX makes it: the copy's extras, kernel scratch, earlier raw files' names. Not while the state is
   unlocked (a binding's `before`/`after` code run for the copy, an `AddToMacro!` append); the copy's own code runs
   locked, as a raw read does, also its `\AtEndOfClass` code run inside `\documentclass`'s unlocked after-digestion
   (asme2ej.cls:1230-1244 `\AtEndOfClass{… \def\newtheorem …}`, 2210.14434). A name the copy `\let`s to its own
   version of an owned name takes the binding's meaning back with it (`CopyProvidesFrame::assigned`): emulateapj5.sty:386
   `\def\keywords`, :394 `\let\subjectheadings=\keywords` (astro-ph0011001, a "Subject headings:" paragraph where the
   binding makes `<keywords>`). *Counters* (main-session call 2026-10-17, 72a r3): a counter's representation
   (`\the<ctr>`, `\p@<ctr>`) and reset list (`\cl@<ctr>`; `\@addtoreset`, `\numberwithin`, `\counterwithin`, a
   re-`\newcounter`) are owned only when the stand-in binding's own load assigned them (`counter_part`,
   `copy_provides_keeps_counter`): the pool's article defaults yield to the copy, as article.cls's own would to the real
   class — jheppub.sty:313-314 `\renewcommand{\theequation}{\thesection.\arabic{equation}}` and
   `\numberwithin{equation}{section}` number (2.1) as its PDF does (2112.14648, 2607.20603; r2: "(1)" … "(60)"). The
   read is no raw class read for K11 (`\lx@class@loaded@raw`): the binding owns the title page. *A command saved again*
   (77w): a `\let\org\X` of the copy, where `\org` already holds an earlier meaning of `\X` (a `\let` copy made under
   `\X`'s name) that the binding's load assigned, while `\X` still holds the binding's later meaning (the copy's read
   has not assigned `\X` itself) and that meaning reaches `\org` (its body, or a body it names, transitively:
   `state::meaning_reaches`), is declined in the copy's own code too (`state::copy_provides_keeps_saved_meaning`, Info):
   `\org` keeps the meaning TeX gives it, `\X` before the redefinition. The binding (or a file it read) made the same
   save-and-wrap, and the wrapper saved into `\org` calls itself when the copy's own code uses it: myjmlr.cls and
   jmlr_mod.cls (jmlr.cls copies, rule 12) run `\let\jmlr@org@newtheorem\newtheorem` (jmlr.cls:753-754; the jmlr
   binding's jmlrutils.sty makes the same wrap) before their own `\newtheorem{example}`, which looped to the timeout
   (1506.02582, 2304.14217). A `\let` whose new meaning does not reach the name, or whose source the copy's read has
   just assigned, is no such wrap and stands: pgf's scratch `\let\pgfutil@reserved@c\pgfutil@reserved@b`, run by
   `\usetikzlibrary` while a self-named sn-jnl.cls copy is read, was declined at int40a and the copy's
   `\usetikzlibrary{snakes}` lost (2207.07492: 0 → 6 Errors), and where `@b`'s loop body names `@c` the declined `\let`
   left pgf's recursion spinning to the timeout (2101.08181's lmcs.cls copy: 3 s → Fatal Timeout); guards
   `perfect_kernel_batch77w::{copy_loads_a_tikz_library, copy_runs_its_own_loop}`.
3. *Locks.* A locked name is refused as for any file, but without the records a raw class's takeover leaves
   (`\lx@dropped@<name>`, `<cs>:redefined`, defaults; OD #265, #500): `copy_provides_refuses_locked`, so no replay of the
   copy's `\maketitle` body.
4. *No second read.* A copy already read raw — by its canonical path (content.rs `RAW_READ_PATHS`, kept out of the
   dumped state; `load_tex_definitions`) or as `<file>_raw_loaded` — is not read again: the 17 stand-ins whose
   bindings `InputDefinitions!` their copy (arxiv,
   cvpr, iccv, PRIMEarxiv, wacv, icml2019, pasj00/01/02, tlp, cimento, JINST, aistats2026, compositio, hha, jhrs,
   czjphys; iccvw by source).
5. *Hooks.* `\AtEndOfClass`/`\AtEndOfPackage` code the copy registers runs at the end of its load inside the copy's
   mode (`\lx@copy@provides@begin{N}` … `\lx@copy@provides@end`, `copy_provides_wrap`; aa.cls:71's `{abstract}`).
   Code it defers to the document — `\AtBeginDocument`, `\AtEndDocument`, `\AtEndPreamble`, `\AfterEndPreamble`,
   `\AfterEndDocument`, `\AddToHook` (lthooks' `\AddToHook code` stands in while the copy is read) — is not registered
   (`copy_provides_defers`, one Info per copy and seam): it is the class's document-time machinery the binding has taken
   over. On the census sample it fixed no Error and caused 3 Fatals (aastex7.cls:459's `\AddToHook{enddocument}` patch
   reads the kernel's `\enddocument` up to `\@checkend`: 2504.00922, 2605.15371, 2607.03848), 5 Error rows (PoS.cls,
   JHEP.cls "\abstract{...} should appear before \begin{document}"; ieeeaccess.cls's `\EOD`; aipproc.cls's
   `\layoutstyle`) and printed layout checks ("The page layout violates the ICML style", 2407.02750). The 72a brief's
   rule 5 asked for the hooks to run under the rule; main-session decision 2026-10-17 (72a r2, on this evidence: 0
   papers fixed, 3 aastex7 Fatals, junk text): they stay unregistered, the binding owning the document-time machinery.
   Likewise decided: the copy-local overlay of rule 2 stays, nested loads are real loads (rule 6) with the `\ver@` test
   scoped to the copy's own `\usepackage` lines, and (72a r3) counter ownership follows the stand-in binding's own load
   only (rule 2). *Direct hook writes* (77w): the copy's own write to LaTeX's hook macros — `\g@addto@macro
   \@begindocumenthook{…}`, ltxgrid's `\prepdef\@begindocumenthook` (qm2008_abs.cls:3233, snp.cls) or a `\def` of
   `\@begindocumenthook`/`\@enddocumenthook` — is the same document-time code and is not registered either
   (`state::copy_provides_defers_hook_write`, from `install_definition`): ltxgrid's page grid ran over the revtex4
   binding's names at `\begin{document}`, 7 "Missing number" Warnings each in 0805.2253, 0806.0481, 0805.4759 (guard
   `perfect_kernel_batch77w::copy_writes_document_hook`, which pins "UNHOOKED" where pdflatex prints "HOOKED"). Its cost
   is `\AtBeginDocument`'s: a hook body that defines names the document uses loses them.
6. *Nested loads.* A package or class the copy loads (`\RequirePackage`, `\usepackage`, `\LoadClass`) is a real load,
   the mode suspended for it (`input_definitions`; a file it pulls in by `\input` is part of the copy, #744): a package the binding did not load loads whole (bmvc2k.cls:139's
   `tabularx`, colm's `multirow`, ws-rv9x6.cls's `ws-crop9x6`), a loaded one is the usual no-op, and `\LoadClass` of
   the loaded class is quiet. These are the lines the binding's dependency scan stands in for, so the copy's
   `\usepackage`/`\RequirePackage` takes the scan's `\ver@` test (`require_package` → `marked_loaded_unrecorded`,
   latex.ltx:18750 `\@ifl@aded`; DIVERGENCES #605): a package the document marked loaded is skipped (sn-jnl.cls:311
   `\usepackage{program}` under sn-jnl-setup.sty's `\AddToHook{class/sn-jnl/before}`, 2201.11056). Every other
   `\usepackage` keeps the records-only test (rulings 2026-10-14/16). Unlike `end_provide_only` (OmniBus's provide-only load, OD #408), these files are not
   marked unloaded after: OmniBus loads part of a file that a later request must load whole; the copy's nested load
   is that file's whole load.
7. *Options.* The copy's `\DeclareOption`s and `\ProcessOptions` run its own handlers inside its code (a handler
   name the binding declared is the binding's, rule 2, and comes back as the binding left it: run and `\relax`ed); its
   `\NeedsTeXFormat`/`\ProvidesClass` are quiet, `\ProvidesClass` recording its version.
8. *Diagnostics.* An Error raised in the copy's own code stays an Error (user ruling 2026-10-17, "Keep as Errors";
   round 1's demotion to a Warning is removed). The copies' Errors became binding work: pnas-new.cls:229
   `\RequirePackage[explicit]{titlesec}` (the binding now passes `explicit` where the copy does: 1907.12289,
   2509.24970, 7 Errors each), ieeeaccess.cls:21-23's `\@IEEEusingAfourpapertrue` (IEEEtran.cls:268-270's flags, now
   in the IEEEtran binding: KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #957), ieeeaccess.cls:131 `\definecolor{accessblue}{spotcolor}
   {PANTONE3015C,1.0}` (color.sty:117-122 accepts a model whose `\color@<model>` exists, which spotcolor.sty:71
   defines: the colour keeps its earlier definition — the ieeeaccess binding's CMYK, ieeeaccess_cls.rs:32 —, at Info;
   a name the driver's model defines first takes the alternate the model's binding gives, `\lx@color@alternate@<model>`
   — the spotcolor binding keeps each `\AddSpotColor`'s CMYK, spotcolor.sty:31-41, scaled by the tint —, else black;
   color_sty.rs `driver_color_model`, `driver_alternate_color`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #958; 2007.03025, 2009.04554,
