   2011.07807, 2209.03883, 2209.12464, 2609.20467). Open: aipcheck.tex:53-54 reads
   `\fmtversion` as `#1/#2/#3` (pre-2020 LaTeX; TL 2025's is `2024-11-01`, pdflatex errs the same: 0806.2199, 3
   Errors).
9. *Not covered.* An extra macro's body, run later in the document, is the author's command and keeps TeX's effect,
   calling the binding's meanings of owned names (neurips_2024.sty's `\TEST`, defined inside its `\@maketitle`, stays
   unreachable: 2406.07381).
10. *Setter defaults* (72a r3). A frontmatter setter the copy calls (`\author`, `\date`, a binding's `\copyrightinfo`)
   stores the class's default, as in TeX, rather than adding an element: while the copy is read, the frontmatter queue
   is the copy's defaults (base_utilities/frontmatter/queue.rs `frontmatter_queue_name`, `frontmatter_copy_defaults`; a removal applies to
   the same queue, so atlasdoc.cls:824's `\date{}` under `cernpreprint` clears its `\date{\today}`). At `\maketitle`
   (`\lx@store@defaults` → `hand_copy_frontmatter_defaults`) a default is handed to the frontmatter only when the
   document did not set its kind — decided by the call, whatever its value (r4): a setter of the kernel's fields
   (`\author`, `\date`, `\title`, whichever binding defines it) called outside the copy's read, observed from the
   copy's first default on (`definition::origin::watch_setter_calls`, `state::note_setter_call` in
   `Expandable::invoke`: inst_support's accumulating `\author{}` queues and clears nothing), or an entry of its tag and
   role queued or removed (`\date{}`'s `\lx@clear@frontmatter`) — and, for the kernel's fields (`\@author`, `\@date`,
   `\@title`), only when the copy's own title page prints the store (`frontmatter_stores::copy_title_page_prints`: the
   `\maketitle`/`\@maketitle` it defined — `\renewcommand`, refused or overlaid, or `\DeclareRobustCommand`'d — and
   the raw page styles, read as K11's `ClassReaders` reads a raw class's title page, `reads_of`, so a
   `\csname…\endcsname` or `\@nameuse` name is followed; a branch of a `\newif`/kvoptions switch that is now false is
   skipped, `\unless` inverting it, and a conditional written as data, `\let\ifX\iftrue` or `\newif\ifX`, opens no
   level; a title-page name with neither a copy's nor a raw file's meaning is the binding's, which prints the
   frontmatter: a copy's `\renewcommand\maketitle{\begingroup\@maketitle\endgroup}`); the binding's title page prints
   them when the copy defines none. The walk is `ClassReaders`' reading, not its survey: the survey indexes the
   meanings in force, while a copy's own versions of owned names live in its overlay. Without `\maketitle` none shows, as in pdflatex. atlasdoc.cls:189-190 (r2: two
   identical `<creator>`s in 1805.01649, 1806.07355, 1807.02012, 1902.05892, 1904.03536; a `<date>` the 2019 class
   prints only in `\ATLAS@TitleHeader` under `datetop`, :567, which `cernpreprint` skips: 1902.05892, 1904.03536).
   jgcc.cls:397's `\copyrightinfo{}{}` (2309.03819, 2401.15504) prints nothing, as amsart.cls:723-727's
   `\@setcopyright` prints no copyright without a year (ams_support_sty.rs `\lx@ams@add@copyright`, the one test
   of both `\copyrightinfo`s; Perl's ams_support.sty.ltxml:139 adds ", ", KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #959). The walk's roots
   are broad and err toward keeping a default: every raw `\ps@…` page style and `\@oddhead`/`\@evenhead`, so a default
   a copy prints only in a running head shows in the document, which LaTeXML has no running heads for.
11. *Renamed natbib copies* (72a r4, main-session scope). A class copy that loads a renamed copy of natbib —
   NJDnatbib.sty (WileyNJD-v2/v5/MRM.cls, `\ProvidesPackage{NJDnatbib}` :29) and bmvc2k_natbib.sty (bmvc2k.cls:710,

   with the options the class gave it (`njdnatbib_sty::natbib_fork_options`); the copy, read after, provides only.

   `square,comma`; `natbib.sty_keyval_setter` → `\lx@natbib@repeat@options`, content.rs `apply_new_options_on_reload`,
   the mechanism hyperref's `\hypersetup` uses), at Info, only where TeX would see them (r6, `natbib.sty_repeat_clash`):
   the first load was a compiled binding's own early one (`<file>:requested_by_binding`, the requester's `Binding`
   origin, recorded at the first load: sv_support's natbib, which svjour3.cls:67-68 loads only under its `natbib`
   option, 2604.22515; sn-jnl's, which sn-jnl.cls:1654-1665 loads with the style's options, 1012.4730, 2604.20688,
   2107.02450, 2409.07188), or the request carries a renamed copy's own options (`natbib.sty:options_of_a_renamed_copy`,
   set by `natbib_fork_options`: in TeX the fork's own `\ProcessOptions` runs). Otherwise the first load was the
   document's world's — the document's, a raw class's, or a class binding's that records its load as the class's own
   (jmlr.cls:150, acmart.cls:299-300: `natbib.sty:requested_by_binding` false) — and LaTeX keeps the first options and
   stops with "Option clash for package natbib", an Error here as there (the reviewer's probes nat_twice, jmlr_numbers,
   pdflatex author-year); elsarticle (elsarticle.cls:1243), jheppub (jheppub.sty:37) and acmart under its `natbib`
   boolkey (acmart.cls:131-138) record theirs too (r7). A raw file's own repeat after an early binding load — a copy
   that loads natbib itself — is the load TeX sees and ends the early-load state (r7, #733). jheppub's binding loads
   natbib with jheppub.sty:37's `[numbers,sort&compress]` (2112.14648, 2607.20603); jcappub's natbib is
   jcappub.sty:32's, read from the copy (2405.09762). Residual: the repeat rule sets only natbib's style options
   (`numbers`, `authoryear`, `super`, brackets, separators, `nobibstyle`/`bibstyle`), in natbib's declaration order
   (r8); `sort`, `compress`, `sort&compress`, `sectionbib` of a repeat load do nothing (natbib's binding does not sort
   or compress; `sectionbib` takes effect only on the first load); hyperref's repeat setter applies after any first load
   (unchanged; hyperref's kvoptions clash in TeX). r5: MRM's binding had loaded natbib optionless before
   MRM.cls:2441-2442's `\usepackage[numbers,super]{NJDnatbib}`, so 2506.14995 was author-year where its PDF has
   superscripts; the binding no longer loads natbib, the class's copy does, binding-in-original-space). The defaults the
   PDF shows, by NJDnatbib's version (r5; the class-family rule's dispatch on a conflict): a v5 copy (md5 277c41da:
   2602.03829, 2408.07575, 2609.08425) heads a chapterless class's bibliography "REFERENCES" (:1052
   `\bmsection*{…{{REFERENCES}}…}`), an amsart one `\refname` (:1065); a v2 or MRM copy (2fa96b7a: 2101.06297,
   2211.16474; 6838c57e: 2411.11493, 2206.08798; 4b333a37: 2506.14995) natbib's `\section*{\refname…}` (probe

   class or the copy's own `\bibsection` set by v5's `\bmsection` (its overlaid meaning, `state::stand_in_copy_meaning`,
   read by the binding's `\AtEndOfPackage` after the copy); "chapterless" is decided by `\chapter`, as the fork's
   `\@ifundefined{chapter}` does (r6, `state::class_defines_chapter`): a stand-in copy that (re)declared `\chapter` (its
   overlay, or declined by the lock: ws-rv9x6.cls:499), a `\chapter` of the document's world or a binding's own, or the
   kernel's under book or report — not LaTeXML's kernel `\chapter`, which the OmniBus base keeps defined under every
   class binding today, and not a `chapter` counter, which WileyNJDv5.cls:5728 and MRM.cls:2160 declare
   (`\newcounter{chapter}[part]`) with no `\chapter` (the reviewer's probe njd_v5_ctr, pdflatex "REFERENCES"). Where a
   chapterless class leaves `\chapter` undefined (the separate `\chapter` batch 72b), the answer is
   `\@ifundefined{chapter}`'s. A copy's counter is declared for real (r6, `state::copy_provides_keeps_counter`,
   `new_counter`): the binding keeps its numbering only for a counter its load declared (`\c@<ctr>`) or numbered (the
   `\the<ctr>` of an existing counter); OmniBus's `\thechapter` autoload stub with no `\c@chapter` does not count, so

   `\appendix` (latex_constructs `begin_appendices`) numbers within chapters only where the class has `\chapter` by the
   same rule, not by a `chapter` counter alone (WileyNJD-v2.cls:2410's bookmark counter: 2211.16474 "Appendix A", not
   "0.A"); appendix.sty's and titlesec's chapter tests still read the counter (`has_chapter_counter`). Every version's
   superscript carries its postnote inside, ", p. 5" (:366-368), through natbib's `NATBIB_SUPER_POSTNOTE_INSIDE` switch
   the fork's binding sets. ws-rv-har.sty (World Scientific's natbib derivative, :16 `\ProvidesPackage{ws-rv-har}`;
   2301.03442, whose 28 citations were "(?)", pdflatex "(Mayor et al. 2011)"; 1602.07982 ships it, loads ws-rv-van) is
   bound the same way (`ws_rv_har_sty.rs`), with its own heading: a class with `\chapter` (:676, the same
   `state::class_defines_chapter`) `\bibname` (:681-685; ws-rv9x6.cls:91 "References"), else `\refname`; amsart
   `\refname` (:686-687). A copy's `\newcommand` of a text default (rule 1) defines it only where the real class lacks
   the name: the copy loads no base class (ws-rv9x6.cls:91 `\newcommand\bibname`), or no base class it `\LoadClass`es
   defines it (article.cls has no `\bibname`). What a base class defines is told by its load, not its text (r7, #732:
   `state::ClassLoadFrame`): the macros its load frame assigned, a class loaded while the copy's `\LoadClass` is open
   included. A name the base class defines is the real class's already: LaTeX's "Command … already defined" Error, the
   first definition kept (r6, `state::copy_provides_text_default_clashes`, sect08.rs; the reviewer's probes newcmd_base
   and nc_chain: pdflatex 2 errors, "References", "Figure 1"). A name made `\relax` is definable, as LaTeX's
   `\newcommand` finds it (the copy's own `\let\refname\relax` before its `\newcommand`, or a raw base class's; r7).
   `\def`/`\renewcommand` redefine as before. A copy's own load of a package its stand-in binding loaded on its behalf
   (`<file>:loaded_by_stand_in`, the innermost stand-in binding whose load made the first load — a `.sty`, `.cls` or
   `.tex` stand-in's, `StandInBindingName`, the last since 77w r3: mssymb.tex's amsfonts; the request's copy,
   read before the load's provides-mode suspension, `requested_by_copy`, is that binding's — `state::copy_provides_binding`)
   is that load, which TeX sees alone: its options apply, at Info, with no "Option clash" (77w; a modified elsarticle.cls
   copy's `\RequirePackage[square,…]{natbib}`, 1811.10063). Another stand-in's copy repeating the load with other
   options meets LaTeX's "Option clash", as in pdflatex (77w r2; the review's finding 6, guard
   `perfect_kernel_batch77w::another_copys_repeat_load_clashes`; the `.tex` stand-ins' record,
   `tex_stand_in_names_its_package_loads`).
12. *The declaration route* (77w, user ruling 2026-10-20, extending 2026-10-17's "a binding always wins over a shipped
   copy"). A `.sty` or `.cls` the paper ships under a name with no binding of its own that declares itself another file
   a binding stands for is that binding's request (content.rs `provided_binding`, from `input_definitions_impl` ahead
   of the raw read of a file found while interpreting definitions, Step 2, and of the versioned fallback, Step 3, which
   reads no copy): `\usepackage{natbib_vw}` whose file `\ProvidesPackage{natbib}` loads the natbib binding,
   `\documentclass{qm2008_abs}` whose file `\ProvidesClass{revtex4}` the revtex4 binding. The declaration is the file's
   first `\Provides(Expl)?(Class|Package|File)` outside a comment (`file_declaration`, shared with rule 0 (a), the
   declared-macro form included; a later one does not count: qm2008_abs.cls embeds textcase.sty's
   `\ProvidesPackage{textcase}`, :3680), read up to the file's first top-level `\endinput` (a code line of it alone
   outside a brace group, where TeX stops: a declaration in a documentation trailer after it is not the file's — 77w r2,
   the review's finding 8; `file_declarations`); not a bundle — a file declaring three or more distinct files is several
   files in one, read raw as before (77w r2, main-session decision 2026-10-20: 1312.3078's cauchy.sty declares theorem,
   exscale, epsfig and apacite; routed to the theorem binding, theorem.sty's load guard
   `\@ifundefined{theorem@style}{}{\endinput}` ended the read, 8 undefined apacite `\BB…` Errors; qm2008_abs.cls's two
   stay routed; guard `perfect_kernel_batch77w::provides_route_skips_bundles_and_trailers`); of the request's kind (a `.sty`'s `\ProvidesPackage` or `\ProvidesFile{X.sty}`,
   a `.cls`'s `\ProvidesClass` or `\ProvidesFile{X.cls}`); naming another file, compared without regard to case; whose
   binding is the registry's, matched as a request is without regard to case, or the one its versioned fallback reaches
   (`aistats2023` → aistats). The binding loads with the request's options as a versioned fallback's does
   (`fallback_request`/`fallback_target`; `\ver@<request>` is the binding's), its load a stand-in load
   (`StandInLoadGuard`; `fallback_provides` names it, `loading_for_a_provides_route`), and the copy is read after it by
   rules 1-11, identity by the declaration (rule 0 not asked); `<binding>:options_of_a_renamed_copy` is set for the load
   (rule 11). Info `fallback`: "The paper's natbib_vw.sty declares itself natbib: loading the natbib.sty binding, then
   the copy as its stand-in's". Not routed: a request with a binding of its own; a file the search paths do not find
   in the paper's source (a TeX Live file, e.g. TL's dated rollback copies `multicol-2019-10-01.sty`, keeps the
   versioned fallback); a copy naming itself (NJDnatbib, bmvc2k_natbib, ws-rv-har, hbnatbib, aistats2e: their own
   bindings, or raw); another kind (a `.sty` that `\ProvidesClass{revtex4}`); a name no binding answers. No per-name list
   is replaced: the renamed natbib forks with bindings (NJDnatbib, bmvc2k_natbib, ws-rv-har) and aistats2e/aistats2eM
   declare their own names, so their registrations stay. Census (77w): of the 1,677 shipped `*natbib*.sty` (1,509
   papers), 389 declare `natbib` under another name (90 new routes: modnatbib 21, natbib_vw 16, natbib_jrm 11,
   my_natbib 7, natbibsty 6, …; 299 the versioned fallback reached before, natbib209 137, natbib2 134, whose copies are
   now read too); over a 3 % corpus sample (87,937 papers) 491 papers (≈0.56 %) request a shipped file that the rule
   routes, 186 of them reached by the versioned fallback before (by binding: aastex 102, neurips 42, IEEEtran 24,
   longtable 23 — aalongtable.sty —, rotating 22 — rotating_pr.sty —, jheppub 22, aa 16, article 13). Perl: `FindFile`
   finds no `.ltxml` for the request (Package.pm:2113-2133; `FindFile_fallback` reduces by name only, :2141-2210); by
   default it reads no raw style, warns the file missing and loads the bindings its dependency scan names (natbib: the
   citations resolve, the copy's extras are lost), and under `--includestyles` it reads the copy raw, whose citations read
   `\b@<key>`, which no `\bibitem` writes: "?" and a "Citation undefined" Warning per citation (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
   #1014; 0802.4100 142 Warnings, 1003.3017 62, astro-ph0512042). Residual: a binding loaded already is not run again
   and its copy is not read (its options reach it, rule 11); a file whose first declaration follows a long stretch of
   its own code is routed by it all the same (adassconf.sty, astro-ph0101121: html.sty's embedded
   `\ProvidesPackage{html}`, :1374, after 391 definitions of its own, so it routes to the html binding; it converts
   cleanly, +17 words; main-session decision: leave, SYNC row); where the
   copy departs from the binding's class the binding's markup stands (2209.10785's cidr.cls comments out acmart's
   `natbib=true` default, so the acmart binding's natbib meets the document's `\usepackage[numbers]{natbib}`: LaTeX's
   "Option clash" Error, where pdflatex loads natbib once; 1401.1086's confSt.cls, an aamas2013 copy, and 2312.16264's
   arxiv.cls, an egpubl copy, meet those bindings' author-block gaps, 4-6 Errors and a merged creator, as a copy under
   the binding's own name does; 2605.07897's bytedance_seed binding raises its honest "merged_creators" Error on a
   parboxed author row). A/B (77w r3, base 529dc1b543, 471 papers: 161 natbib-census papers requesting their copy,
   280 sampled routes, 30 witnesses; plus 200 random ships/controls, byte-identical): Errors 144 → 123, Fatals 0 → 0,
   Warnings 12,652 → 8,787, words +1.5 %, "?" 2,608 → 109, "Citation undefined" Warnings 3,707 → 39; title
   +37/−11, creator +29/−2, contact +66/−14 papers (the losses: raw classes' duplicated frontmatter now printed
   once, 2210.16202 82 "Japan" → 10 as its source); 4 papers worse in Errors: the three above and 1312.3078's
   bundle, read raw again since r2. Guards
   `perfect_kernel_batch77w::*`; repros `tools/perfect_kernel/repros/stand-in-copies/provides_route/`.
13. *A standard-class derivative* (77w r2; user rulings 2026-10-20: "a shipped class declaring a LaTeX standard class
   stays routed; fix the bindings so the route loses nothing", then "call out arXiv overrides of standard classes in the
   sections patching them"). A class the paper ships that declares one of LaTeX's own classes — its file in the
   format's base distribution, `tex/latex/base/` (article, report, book, letter, proc, slides, minimal; content.rs
   `is_latex_base_class`) — is not that class but an arXiv-side override of it: aip-cp.cls:24 `\ProvidesClass{article}`
   (AIP Conference Proceedings, not in TeX Live; 1506.04050, 1604.08112), mf.cls (0709.4467), antonio.cls (1808.10740),
   articlegm.cls, articlefederico.cls, HERON.cls and mbook.cls (`book`: 1903.06504, nucl-th0703058), avh.cls
   (`report`). Every section of the copy that differs patches the kernel's class, which the binding models with two
   kinds of names: the class's text (`\refname`, `\figurename`, `\@ptsize`), which the copy may change, and LaTeXML's
   structural markup of it (`\appendix` → `<ltx:appendix>`, book's `\frontmatter`/`\mainmatter`/`\backmatter`, the
   sectioning, the counters' ids), which the copy's equivalent code cannot give (user refinement 2026-10-20: honor the
   derivative's patches "without losing the entire binding support for high quality XML such as frontmatter"). The
   provides mode of rules 1-11 kept the binding's meaning for each and lost the patches, silently: aip-cp's
   accumulating `\author[aff1]{…}` (aip-cp.cls:235-258) kept the last of five authors under the locked kernel
   `\author`, its `\affil` list was lost, mf.cls's size file left no nominal font size, HERON.cls's and mbook.cls's
   affiliation contact went. So the copy is read after the binding's load as a raw
   class is (`read_standard_class_derivative`, Info "The paper's X derives from a LaTeX class: read as a raw class over
   its binding"), and its patches are recognised by the raw-class mechanisms, section by section:
   - *frontmatter setters* — a locked kernel name it redefines (`\author`, `\title`, `\maketitle`, `\abstract`, …) is
     refused with the records a raw class's takeover leaves (`\lx@dropped@<name>`, `<name>:redefined`; state.rs
     `install_definition`): the kernel `\author` appends each call (#253, `\lx@add@authors@adaptive`) and replays the
     class's own setter for its flags and stores (#482, #534), its `\maketitle` deposits what the frontmatter does not
     carry (#265: aip-cp's `\aipaffil`), and the title-page stores reach the frontmatter API (K11,
     `\lx@class@loaded@raw` at the binding load's end; `store_setters::mark_raw`);
   - *the class's text names* — its `\newcommand` (or `\providecommand`) of a declared text name (rule 14's list: the
     kernel's `state::COPY_TEXT_NAMES` and the names a binding declares) that the standard binding assigned in its own
     load defines it, the derivative being read in the class's place (`state::standard_class_binding_name`,
     latex_constructs `is_definable_latex`) — aip-cp.cls:875-878 "REFERENCES", "FIGURE 1"; HERON.cls:682
     `\bibname{References}`; Lowx2013.cls:629 `\abstractname{ }`; article_saj.cls:631
     `\newcommand\refname{\noindent\tenrm REFERENCES\vskip-.5cm}` (2212.09079, 2402.12725). Its body is not checked
     (rule 14's safety check is the routed copy's, whose definition otherwise gives way to the binding's): the
     derivative is read as a raw class, whose `\def` and `\renewcommand` of the same name stand unchecked (applied here,
     the check fails closed on `\noindent`, a constructor, and prints article's "References"). Every other `\newcommand`
     of a name the binding defined is "Ignoring redefinition" (78h r2, user ruling 2026-10-21): a caption format (a
     derivative's `\newcommand\fnum@table{TABLE~\thetable}` keeps the article binding's "Table 1"; 78h r1 let every name
     that only prints yield, "TABLE 1"), book's `\@chapapp`, and the four names 77w r3 let yield as bodies without
     control sequences that the list does not hold — `\@ptsize`, `\@pnumwidth`, `\@tocrmarg`, `\@dotsep`
     (article.cls:52, :503-505, which full copies `\newcommand`): no output changed on the 78h r2 A/B's 69 derivatives
     (a copy's size option `\renewcommand\@ptsize{1}` sets it, as before; the TOC layout is LaTeXML's). A derivative's
     `\def` of any name stands as a raw class's (*everything else*, below). The names are those of the standard
     binding's own load (`state::stand_in_last_load_names` when the derivative's read begins,
