### 732. article, report and book assign their classes' names in their own load; what a base class defines is told by its load frame

The class bindings `article_cls.rs`, `report_cls.rs` and `book_cls.rs` assign the names classes.dtx gives each class in
its own load — article.cls:613-622, report.cls:712-722, book.cls:718-727: `\contentsname`, `\listfigurename`,
`\listtablename`, `\refname`/`\bibname`, `\indexname`, `\figurename`, `\tablename`, `\partname`, `\chaptername`
(report, book), `\appendixname`, `\abstractname` (article, report) — with the values LaTeXML's kernel predefines, so
output is unchanged. Perl assigns only `\refname` (article.cls.ltxml:98) and `\bibname` (report.cls.ltxml:100,
book.cls.ltxml:100) there, the rest in its kernel (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:719-722, "These actually should be in
article/report/book"). The kernel predefinitions stay (Perl's; a class with no such binding still has the names).

Every class load is a frame (`state::ClassLoadFrame`, entered at `binding::content::input_definitions` for a `.cls`
with options handled): the macros assigned while it is open outside LaTeXML's kernel layers — the class binding's own,
a raw class file's, a package's it loads — and a name a lock kept from a definition it made are recorded as the class's,
with the macro's identity. Two readers:

1. A stand-in's copy's `\newcommand` of a text default (#731 rule 1) clashes ("Command … already defined", an Error as
   in TeX) when a base class of the copy defines it: a class its own `\LoadClass` requested, or one loaded while that
   is open (`State::copy_class_loads`), so a chained `\LoadClass{mybase}` over article finds article's names (the
   reviewer's probe nc_chain: pdflatex 2 errors, "Figure 1", "References"), a raw base class's own definition counts
   (nc_namedef: `\expandafter\def\csname bibname\endcsname`, 1 error), and its document-time code does not
   (nc_cond: `\AtBeginDocument{\def\bibname…}`, 0 errors). This replaces r6's scan of the base class file's text and its
   per-thread cache keyed by class name, which reached the next paper a worker converted on the same thread.
2. A text default whose meaning is still the macro a class's load assigned is the class layer's, not LaTeXML's semantic
   layer's (`state::class_layer_definition`), as the kernel predefinitions are: a stand-in copy's redefinition of it
   stands, as the real file's does over article.cls's. Over the 415 A/B papers this changed 4, each as its PDF:
   emulateapj.cls:470's `\def\abstractname{ABSTRACT}` (1202.3442), aipproc.sty:49's `\def\refname{REFERENCES}`
   (astro-ph0105230, astro-ph9912326, hep-ph0102191) — the article binding's `\refname` had been the binding's.

A base class's `\let<name>\relax` before a copy's `\newcommand` leaves the name definable
(`base_class_name_made_relax`), and so does the copy's own earlier assignment of it in the same frame
(`\let\refname\relax` then `\newcommand\refname`; pdflatex 0 errors, "Works Cited"). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch72a::copy_newcommand_through_a_chained_base_class`,
`class_load_record_does_not_reach_the_next_document`, `copy_newcommand_of_a_base_class_name_errs`; repro
`stand-in-copies/text_defaults/chain/`.

### 733. A raw file's own repeat load of natbib after a binding's early load is the load TeX sees

A class or style binding often loads natbib (`RequirePackage!`) before or where the real file does not (#731 rule 11,
`<file>:requested_by_binding`): the document's later `\usepackage[opts]{natbib}` then applies its options, as the first
load TeX sees. When the real file — a stand-in's copy read after its binding — loads natbib itself (`File` requester:
neurips_2024.sty:71 `\RequirePackage{natbib}`, icml2024.sty:95), that load is the one TeX sees: its options apply and
join the first load's options (`<file>_loaded_with_options`), and the early-load state ends, so a document repeat with
new options is LaTeX's "Option clash for package natbib" Error, the first options kept (the reviewer's probes
neurips_rep, icml_rep: pdflatex 1 error, author-year; 2410.08709 the same shape). A copy that comments its load out
leaves the early load in place, and the document's options apply (2506.00573, 2506.01987, 2506.08967, 2506.17103,
2506.18071, 2506.22567: numbered, as their PDFs). The clash test reads the options passed to the package too
(`\opt@<file>`, as latex.ltx's `\@if@ptions` does): 2110.14346's `\PassOptionsToPackage{numbers, compress}{natbib}`
before neurips_2020.sty's load, then `\usepackage[numbers]{natbib}`, raises no clash, as in pdflatex. A repeat's options
run in natbib's declaration order, as `\ProcessOptions` runs them (natbib.sty:238-263), and their
`nobibstyle`/`bibstyle` decide whether a later `\bibliographystyle`'s `\bibstyle@<style>` still sets the punctuation: an
explicit bracket, separator or `numbers` option gobbles it, so 2506.08967 (`[square,numbers]` after neurips' early load,
then `plainnat`) and 2506.05937 (neurips_2025.sty `[numbers]`, a late `plainnat`) stay numbered throughout, and
`[square,authoryear]` ends gobbled, as in TeX (r8, `natbib_sty::NATBIB_STYLE_OPTIONS`). Perl ignores a repeat load's
options (Info) and has no early binding loads of natbib to tell from the class's. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch72a::natbib_copy_repeat_ends_the_bindings_early_load`; repro
`stand-in-copies/natbib_forks/natbib_copy_repeat_ends_the_early_load.tex`. Residual (SYNC 72a row (m)): the bindings
revtex4_support, achemso, apacite and mnras load natbib other than their real files do and are not marked as the file's
own load; a document repeat after them still applies its options.

### 734. A `\chapter` call in a class without chapters is LaTeXML's numbered chapter, with one Warning; the name stays undefined (TeX: undefined control sequence; Perl: the kernel's `\chapter`, `undefined:\thechapter`)

**Perl behavior**: `\chapter` is defined in every class (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:557), so a call in an article
digests LaTeXML's chapter, whose counter does not exist: "Counter 'chapter' was not defined", `\c@chapter` "is not a
register", and `Error:undefined:\thechapter` in each tag (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #962).
**Rust behavior**: `\chapter` is undefined after a class without chapters loads (#179). At `\begin{document}`, after the
begin-document hooks have run (a package's `\AtBeginDocument` test gets TeX's answer), a `\chapter` still undefined is
given a stand-in, `\lx@chapterless@chapter` (sect01.rs `supply_chapter_fallback`, `kernel_autoload::name_undefined_fallback`):
the name stays undefined — `\@ifundefined{chapter}`, `\ifdefined` and `\meaning` in the body answer as TeX does
(blindtext.sty:243 `\blinddocument` makes no chapter under scrartcl) — and where the undefined token is met
(`kernel_autoload::undefined_fallback`, at the gullet's and the stomach's undefined-CS sites; a thread-local flag
answers at once until a stand-in is named) the stand-in is read in its place: LaTeXML's ordinary numbered chapter
(`\lx@kernel@chapter`, the pool:557 definition) with a chapter counter of its own where the class made none
(`NewCounter('chapter')`, without report's reset of the sections), and on its first use one `Warning:undefined:\chapter`
(`kernel_chapter_with_warning`, sect04.rs). Its text: "The class defines no \chapter, so TeX stops here with an
undefined control sequence; LaTeXML's \chapter is used"; when the class was answered by a binding not its own (a prefix
alternate or a versioned fallback: neither `<class>.cls.ltxml_loaded` nor `<class>.cls_raw_loaded`, recorded at
`\documentclass` as `\chapter:class@stood@in`), "The binding answering class <class> defines no \chapter; LaTeXML's
\chapter is used", which claims nothing about TeX: the real class may have chapters (0909.2812's mn_thesis.cls has them
through mnphd.cls → report, bound by the prefix alternate `mn`; its report now comes from the dependency scan).
The chapters carry LaTeXML's labels ("Chapter 1", refnum, typerefnum, toc title), which the PDF never shows: pdflatex
stops at the call and sets the title as text (user ruling 2026-10-17: the fallback is LaTeXML's ordinary numbered
chapter). The user ruling supplies LaTeXML's chapter "at `\begin{document}`"; it is supplied there as a stand-in rather
than as the definition (main-session ruling: `\chapter` stays undefined after `\begin{document}`, only a call reads it),
so that body-time tests (blindtext, hvfloat's test documents, the #179 witnesses) keep TeX's answer. Edge cases: a call
in the preamble or in a begin-document hook meets the undefined name as TeX does (one `Error:undefined:\chapter`, the
title as text) and its undefined-error stub is cleared at `\begin{document}` (`\chapter:error@stub`), so the body's calls
read the stand-in (repro sectioning-frontmatter/chapter_in_the_preamble_errs_and_the_body_chapter_converts);
`\csname chapter\endcsname` in the body (and `\expandafter\ifx\csname chapter\endcsname\relax`) makes `\chapter`
`\relax`, as in TeX, and a later call sets its title as text without a diagnostic (the hypbmsec, splitidx, chemscheme,
examplep and wrapfig2 test shapes); `\let\mychap\chapter` copies the undefined meaning, so `\mychap{…}` is
`Error:undefined:\mychap`, as TeX; a body `\edef` holding `\noexpand\chapter` makes a chapter where TeX stops.
**Why**: the author meant a chapter, and the content is kept (the OD #721 precedent: the author's reading plus one
Warning, never silent, never an Error); pdflatex stops at each call ("Undefined control sequence") and sets the title as
text.
**Witnesses**: 1403.2269, 1511.03874, 1606.03650, 2504.00704 (1 → 0 `undefined:\chapter`); 0909.2812 (1 → 0, its
report's chapters); 0907.3938's pre.cls `\let\chapter\part` after `\LoadClass{article}` is the class's own chapter, kept by #179
(a), where it was retracted; 0802.3014 and 1507.01872 call it inside an undefined preamble macro's argument (pretex's
`\UInewAction`), before the stand-in exists.
**Guard**: `perfect_kernel_batch72b::{chapter_in_a_chapterless_class_is_the_kernel_chapter_with_a_warning,
a_preamble_chapter_errs_and_the_body_chapter_reads_the_stand_in, a_raw_class_meets_chapter_undefined_while_it_loads,
appendices_follow_the_class_chapters}`; repros sectioning-frontmatter/{chapter_call_in_a_chapterless_class,
chapter_undefined_in_a_chapterless_class, chapter_in_the_preamble_errs_and_the_body_chapter_converts,
appendix_after_a_chapter_in_a_chapterless_class}.
**Upstream**: not filed.

### 735. jmlr's article `\chapter` is LaTeXML's chapter, with the class's error text as one Warning (TeX: the class's error; Perl: no jmlr binding, the kernel's `\chapter`)

**Perl behavior**: no jmlr binding; OmniBus and the kernel's `\chapter` (pool:557), numbered by no counter
(`undefined:\thechapter`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #962).
**Rust behavior**: jmlr_cls.rs defines `\chapter`, as jmlr.cls:743-745 does (`\artchapter`, `\let\chapter\artchapter`;
:950-959 `\jmlrbookcommands` switches to `\bookchapter`), so a package's `\@ifundefined{chapter}` takes the chapter
branch, as TeX's (pdflatex "X=C."). A call in an article reads LaTeXML's numbered chapter through
`kernel_chapter_with_warning` (#734's), with one `Warning:latex:\chapter` "Class jmlr Error: Chapters not permitted in
articles; LaTeXML's \chapter is used"; the class's chapter counter (:732) is made at the call, marked as the stand-in's
(`\chapter:stand@in@counter`; `has_chapter_counter` ignores it, for every binding that reuses the helper), so the
article's `\appendix` letters the sections as jmlr.cls:720-729 `\artappendix` (`\let\appendix\artappendix`) does:
pdflatex "Appendix A. AppSec", ours "Appendix A" (72b r2: "Appendix 1.A", numbered within the stand-in's chapter).
**Why**: the OD #721 / #734 precedent: TeX's error is the class refusing what the author wrote; the author's chapter is
kept, with a Warning that names the class's error.
**Witnesses**: the 72b review's jmlr probes (jmlr.cls TL 2025; rev72b/r2/jma for the appendix); no arXiv paper calls it (3 jmlr papers of the 72b A/B,
unchanged).
**Guard**: `perfect_kernel_batch72b::bindings_whose_class_has_chapters_define_them`.
**Upstream**: not filed.

### 736. A stand-in class binding loads the base class its real file loads; the copy's one class slot is the net

latex.ltx lets a class file `\LoadClass` once (:18800 lets `\LoadClass` to `\@twoloadclasserror`, :18938-18942, "Two
\LoadClass commands"): a document has one class. A stand-in class binding (#731) has loaded the base class it models the
class on — ceurart_cls.rs and atlasdoc_cls.rs OmniBus, which loads article — before the paper's copy is read, and the
copy's own `\LoadClass{Y}` then loaded a second class over the first. ceurart.cls:62 `\LoadClass{scrartcl}` raw-read
scrartcl, scrkbase and typearea over article, whose `\@ptsize` of 0 sends typearea.sty:1400-1413 off its path ("DIV for
0.0pt", then Fatal "Conditional limit of 48000000 exceeded": 2509.11496 9 E / 1 F and 0 words, 2608.23214, 2310.02658,
2505.16276; 74 ceurart papers in 2509, 39 in 2506); atlasdoc.cls's `\LoadClass[titlepage, 11pt]{\ADOC@mainclass}`
(scrartcl) redefined `\@startsection` and `\@sect` under the binding (2509.01219: "`\@startsection` has been changed" and
"Unexpected definition of \@sect", which #737 shows were LaTeXML's; its 3x "Bad type area settings" are true, pdflatex
logs the same 3; +26-33 % instructions).

Now (`binding::content::binding_base_class_stands_for`, at the top of `load_class`): when the copy's own code loads a
class (provides-mode on; a file the copy loads is a real load, its `\LoadClass` is not the copy's), the class is not
loaded yet (`\ver@Y.cls` undefined — the binding's own base class is a repeat load: cimart.cls `\LoadClass{article}`),
the class load open now — the binding's — loaded a class (`state::ClassLoadRecord::classes`, the classes loaded while a
class's frame is open), and the paper does not ship Y (`shipped_with_paper`, the copy test's), Y is not loaded: Info
"the binding's base class (book.cls) stands for the copy's \LoadClass{article}: not loaded" (svmult; daj's names
article.cls), and the binding's
classes become the copy's base classes (`state::note_copy_base_classes`), so a copy's `\newcommand` of a name they
define errs as over the real class (#732; newcmd_base and nc_chain keep their 2 Errors). A class the author ships is
read (the reviewer's nc_chain `\LoadClass{mybase}`, nc_namedef, nc_cond, nc_letrelax), and a class that shipped class
loads is the copy's too: copy → mybase.cls → `\LoadClass{Y}` meets the classes the binding's load loaded
(`state::open_class_load_classes` reads them from the copy's first class load, `State::copy_class_loads`, not from
mybase.cls's empty frame; int23, 72a review r7 NIT 8; probe and guard
`perfect_kernel_batchint23::a_shipped_intermediate_class_meets_the_class_slot`). Decided by mechanism, no class
names. Perl never reads the copy (Package.pm:2113-2133 prefers the `.ltxml`), so it has neither the Fatal nor the copy's
extras.

The base class (r9; "a binding defines in the original package's conceptual space", "stub bindings load their real
dependencies"): a stand-in class binding loads the class its real file `\LoadClass`es, under the file's own option
logic, so the copy's own `\LoadClass` is a repeat (`\ver@Y.cls` defined), as in TeX, and the copy's code after it meets
Y's interface. Enumerated over every stand-in `.cls` (the copies of every 25th arXiv paper, and every 3rd for the
classes that sample misses; `\LoadClass` target against the class each binding loads):
ceurart → scrartcl (ceurart.cls:59-62: its options, the rest passed to scrartcl with `a4paper,twoside=false`; 64
copies in the 1/25 sample, 112 papers in 2506+2509), atlasdoc → its KOMA class (`atlasdoc_cls::main_class`: v13
`\ADOC@mainclass`, scrbook for `BOOK`, scrreprt for `REPORT` (true by default), scrartcl for `cernpreprint`/`preprint`/
`PAPER`/`CONF`/`PUB`; v3 scrbook or scrartcl; v1 scrartcl, article without `koma`/`atlasstyle`; 47 copies), lmcs →
amsart `[11pt,reqno]` (55), pnas-new → extarticle (its options passed, 44), jgcc → amsart `[11pt,reqno]` (2),
czipreprint → amsart `[reqno]` (3 in the 1/3 sample), clear2025 → jmlr `[pmlr]` (2; it had jmlr's binding under its own
name, so `\ver@jmlr.cls` was undefined). A binding that had OmniBus as its base keeps what OmniBus gave it where the real
base class has nothing: `omnibus_cls::provide_over_base_class` loads OmniBus provide-only over it (`ProvideOnlyGuard`,
as `\documentstyle` loads it over a class, sect01.rs) — ceurart's `{keywords}` (OmniBus's `ltx:classification`, which
the r8 trial without it lost: -10 to -15 words a paper), `\email`, `\affiliation`. The binding's own definitions follow
as before. Witnesses: 2509.11496, 2608.23214, 2310.02658, 2505.16276 (ceurart: 1 E → 0, the copy's `\KOMAoptions{DIV=10}`
now defined), 2509.01219 and census 1605.06035, 1805.01649, 1806.07355, 1807.02012, 1902.05892, 1904.03536 (atlasdoc:
6-11 E → 0), 2309.03819, 2401.15504 (jgcc: `\address`, `\email`, `\copyrightinfo`).

The slot stays as the net for a binding still out of step with its file: Perl's svmult binding loads book
(svmult.cls.ltxml:34) where svmult.cls and svmono.cls `\LoadClass{article}` (238 + 6 copies; SNmult 22 in the 1/3
sample, served by svmult's binding), and daj's binding emulates tocbase (not in TeX Live) over article. There the copy's
code is written for Y and a command of Y's interface it calls before anything else defines it is undefined, an Error
as the copy's own Errors are (user ruling 2026-10-17; book's interface covers article's, so svmult copies meet none).
latex.ltx's two-`\LoadClass` Error itself is not emulated in general (a document's own second `\LoadClass` still loads
it: the reviewer's probe scr2, `\documentclass{article}` then `\LoadClass{scrartcl}`, is Fatal on 67int21 too; SYNC 72a
row (n)). The raw KOMA base gets the standard classes' semantic layer, its ids, `\appendix` and quiet sectioning check,
as every KOMA document does (#737). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch72a::copy_load_class_is_the_bindings_base_class` (ceurart, atlasdoc, jgcc:
0 E / 0 W / 0 F, title, keywords, author and section whole) and
`::copy_load_class_meets_the_class_slot` (svmult); repros `stand-in-copies/class_slot/`. Residual: `atlasdoc_cls::main_class`
keys on the copy's version (its `{koma}` and `{REPORT}` options), not on the class its `\LoadClass` names, so a modified
copy that names `article` or `book` itself gets the KOMA class of its version; the slot then stands that class for the
copy's (SYNC 72a row (r)).

### 737. The KOMA classes, read raw, get the standard classes' semantic layer: ids, `\appendix`, and a quiet sectioning check

**TeX**: `\documentclass{scrartcl}` (scrreprt, scrbook) is KOMA-Script's class: its `\newcounter`s (scrartcl.cls:5045-5127,
scrreprt.cls:5530-6051), its `\appendix` (scrartcl.cls:4842-4867: counters reset, `\thesection` = `\@Alph\c@section`,
`\appendixmore`; scrreprt.cls:5305-5335 and scrbook.cls:5284-5314 at the chapter level, `\@chapapp` = `\appendixname`),
and a check that the kernel's `\@startsection` and `\@sect` are still latex.ltx's (scrartcl.cls:3292 + :3326, :3520 +
:3552), which passes: pdflatex writes no Class Warning for a minimal document.

**Perl**: no KOMA binding; the class is "missing" and OmniBus (article) loads (`Can't find binding for class scrartcl
(using OmniBus)`), so a KOMA paper has the article's ids (`S1`, `S1.E1`, `S1.F1`) and `<appendix>` elements, and none of
KOMA's own commands.

**Rust** (72a r10; main-session call, row (p) option b): the classes are raw-read (scrartcl_cls.rs, the memoir
precedent, batch 53) and koma_script.rs adds the semantic layer the article, report and book bindings give:
1. *Ids* (`koma_counter_ids`): after the raw load, each sectioning and float counter the class declared gets the ids of
   the standard class's binding (article_cls.rs:86-107 for scrartcl, report_cls.rs:94-130 / book_cls.rs:100-136 for
   scrreprt and scrbook: `idprefix`, `idwithin`, `nested`), through `counter::dialect::define_counter_ids`, the id half
   of `new_counter` split out; the registers and reset lists stay the class's. Before: `section1`,
   `section1.subsection1`, `equation1`, `figure1` (124 of 126 ceurart/atlasdoc papers of 2506+2509 under 72a r9, every
   KOMA paper under 67int21).
2. *Appendix* (`koma_appendix`): `\appendix` is `\@appendix` — `start_appendices("section")` for scrartcl, `("chapter")`
   for scrreprt/scrbook, as article_cls.rs:148-152 and report_cls.rs:178-182 — then KOMA's own, whose lettering,
   `\@chapapp`, one-time hook and `\appendixmore` stand. Before: more `ltx:section`s, their ids colliding with the body's
   (`section1a`), in 26 of the 27 ceurart/atlasdoc papers with an appendix (2509.11496, 2506.00694).
3. *The sectioning check* (`koma_pre_load`): KOMA's copies of the two kernel workers (`\scr@saved@startsection`,
   `\scr@latex@sect`) are set to the kernel's — LaTeXML's native `\@startsection` (sect04.rs) and `\@sect` router
   (latex_constructs_rust_only.rs) — and locked against the class's definitions of them, so the class takes pdflatex's
   branch and writes neither "`\@startsection' has been changed" nor "Unexpected definition of \@sect!" (both on every
   KOMA document since the classes were raw-read; CONTROL repro sectioning-frontmatter/koma_sectioning_check_warns of
   batch 60m, which judged them true). Neither copy is called on that branch: the dispatcher KOMA puts over
   `\@startsection` is refused by its lock, and `\scr@startsection` is LaTeXML's `\@startsection` (`koma_post_load`).
4. *Front matter* (`koma_book_matter`, scrbook only; int23, 72a review r7 SHOULD 1): scrbook's `\frontmatter`,
   `\mainmatter` and `\backmatter` (scrbook.cls:5272-5283) switch `\if@mainmatter`, by which KOMA numbers a chapter
   (:5573-5576); LaTeXML's sectioning numbers by `no_number_sections`, which `\frontmatter` and `\mainmatter` now also
   set before KOMA's own code runs, as book_cls.rs's do (Perl book.cls.ltxml:112-118). Before: 2506.17485 "Chapter 1
   Abstract", "Chapter 2 Introduction", every number one too high; now "Abstract", "1 Introduction", as its PDF.
   Residual: the flag unnumbers every level, where KOMA unnumbers only the chapter outside the main matter and keeps
   a section's number without the chapter's (scrbook.cls:6030-6036 `\if@mainmatter\thechapter.\fi`), so `\backmatter`
   is left to KOMA: a back-matter chapter is numbered (2508.01496's appendix
   "Appendix A", PDF "Appendix"), its sections keep KOMA's numbers ("13", as scrbook.cls numbers them; with the flag
   set there, every reference to them lost its number: -201 words); a section inside a front-matter chapter is
   unnumbered (KOMA "1"). book_cls.rs's `no_number_chapters` (78a, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1016) does not serve here: an
   unnumbered KOMA chapter still resets the counters within it (scrbook.cls:5573-5600, `\cl@<chapter>` with
   `\@stpelt` from v3.15), which the kernel's unnumbered unit does not, so 2508.01496's appendix figures would number
   on from the last main chapter (16 figures off by one; PDF "Figure 1" … "Figure 16").
Divergence from Perl: KOMA's own commands are defined (the raw class), and under scrreprt/scrbook the ids are report's
(`Ch1.S1`), not Perl's article ids. With it, ceurart's `\title[mode=<mode>]` (ceurart.cls:381-500: the optional
argument is a key list; `mode=sub`, and `\subtitle`, the subtitle) maps onto the frontmatter (ceurart_cls.rs: `title` the
main title, `sub` `ltx:subtitle`, `trans`/`transsub` notes as acmart's `\translatedtitle`, `alt`/`ascii` the notes
`alternativetitle`/`asciititle`: ceurart.cls:435-483 prints them as further title lines in styles of their own, an
alternative title and the title in ASCII, so they stay apart from the main title), where the kernel `\title`
took the keys for a short title and the last call won (19 of the 112 ceurart papers of 2506+2509: 2509.11492,
2509.11496); and OmniBus declares book.cls:53's `\if@mainmatter` with its `\mainmatter` (omnibus_cls.rs), which
scrlayer.sty:102-110 expects ("\mainmatter defined without \if@mainmatter!" on 111 of the 112 under 72a r9, where OmniBus
is provided over scrartcl; pdflatex quiet). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch72a::{koma_classes_take_the_kernel_branch_without_warnings,
koma_ids_and_appendix_follow_the_standard_classes, ceurart_title_mode_sub_is_the_subtitle}`,
`perfect_kernel_batchint23::scrbook_front_matter_chapters_are_unnumbered`; repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/scrbook_front_matter_chapters_are_unnumbered`,
`sectioning-frontmatter/koma_ids_and_appendix_{scrartcl,scrreprt,scrbook}`, `koma_sectioning_check_warns`,
`stand-in-copies/class_slot/ceurart_title_mode_sub`.

### 738. An `\index`/`\nomenclature`/`\glossary` entry is typeset only where its list is printed (user ruling 2026-10-18)

**TeX**: `\index` writes its entry `\@sanitize`d and `\protected@write`-expanded to the `.idx` (latex.ltx:17710-17726),
`\glossary` after `\makeglossary` to the `.glo` (:17727-17741), `\nomenclature` to the `.nlo` (nomencl.sty:208-245); the
entry is typeset only when `\printindex`/the `.gls` input/`\printnomenclature` reads makeindex's `.ind`/`.gls`/`.nls` —
with all the document's entries, the ones after the command too. Without a print command nothing is typeset, so an
entry's `_` or `\|` is no TeX error; makeindex itself rejects a nomencl line holding a second `|` or `@` ("Extra `|'",
the `.ilg`), braced or not.

**Perl**: every phrase is digested at the `\index`/`\nomenclature` (pool `\index`; Perl's nomencl is raw and prints no
list); `\glossary` inserts a phrase only outside `ltx:p` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #281).

**Rust** (73a): the entry's tokens (expanded as the write expands them; nomencl's with `\theequation` fixed) are kept
under an id (latexml_core stomach.rs `defer_print`) and the anchor `\lx@deferred@print{id}` stands where the entry was
made; when the list is printed (`{theindex}`, makeidx/imakeidx `\printindex`, the `.ind`/`.gls` stand-in
`\lx@makeindex@output`, nomencl's `\printnomenclature`) `resolve_deferred_prints` digests them in document order (from a
low-water mark, so repeated resolutions scan each entry once) and the anchors absorb the marks, so a list keeps its
marks where the entries stood; once printed, a later entry is digested at once. A list never printed typesets nothing:
no `<ltx:indexmark>`/`<ltx:glossarydefinition>`, and no HTML head keywords from index phrases (the webpage stylesheet's
source) — the document has no index; that loss is accepted as the ruling's consequence (main session 2026-10-18; raw
undigested marks were declined). `\glossary` follows the same rule (main-session call 2026-10-18 under the ruling).
A nomencl entry makeindex would reject (a `|`/`@` in its prefix, symbol, description, or table-mode unit and note,
nomencl.sty:228-232) is left out of the printed list with a Warning. Under streaming (and the adaptive eager phase's
soft yield) a fragment is built before a later print could fill its anchors, so a yield digests every pending entry at
once, as Perl does: a streamed conversion then holds marks of an unprinted list where the eager one has none, and a
printed list's marks can differ too — the streamed entry is digested at the yield, under the definitions then in force,
the eager one at the print, under the later ones (an entry `\index{\x}` with `\x` "FOO" at the yield, redefined "BAR"
before `\printindex`: streamed "FOO", eager "BAR") — the second documented exception to the `--streaming` byte-identity besides #456 (the `--streaming` help text; the sweep's
`streaming_sweep::STREAMING_DIVERGENT_FIXTURES` compares `cluster_regressions/verb_in_index.tex` without its
`<indexmark>`s and
`114_streaming_cluster_regressions::streaming_yield_typesets_pending_index_entries` asserts the divergence). Witnesses
1112.3972 (20 → 0 Errors), 2506.02168 (1 → 0, `\printnomenclature` ahead of the entries). Repros
index/{index_entry_typeset_only_when_printed, printed_index_keeps_its_entries,
nomenclature_entry_typeset_only_when_printed, glossary_entry_typeset_only_when_printed},
index-bib/index_entry_ampersand_is_literal_list_printed_first; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch73a::{index_entry_is_typeset_only_when_printed, printed_index_keeps_its_entries,
nomenclature_entry_is_typeset_only_when_printed, glossary_entry_is_typeset_only_when_printed,
index_entry_ampersand_is_literal_list_printed_first, nomentbl_unit_with_a_bar_is_rejected}`.

### 739. AASTeX 6+'s `\tablecaption` before `\begin{deluxetable}`, or in a `{longrotatetable}` around a plain `tabular`, is kept on the table, unnumbered (user ruling 2026-10-18)

**TeX**: aastex701.cls:8417-8418 (aastex631.cls alike) `\def\tablecaption#1{\gdef\@tablecaption{#1}}` stores the caption,
`\deluxetable` empties the store at the table's start (:11303-11304 `\let\tablecaption\deluxetablecaption
\deluxetablecaption{}`) and `\startdata` prints it above the tabular only when it is not empty (:11391-11399); a long
table (`\startlongtable`, or a deluxetable in `{longrotatetable}`, whose `\global\startlongtabletrue` holds until a long
table ends, :11609) prints its numbered caption always, empty or not (:11568/:11575). A caption given before the table
is lost in the PDF and the table takes no number; in a `{longrotatetable}` (:12245-12286) around a plain `tabular` the
store is never printed, and its `\label` names the last numbered unit (2204.03327's aux: `tab:allesFitted` = 4.1.5).

**Perl**: `\let\tablecaption\caption` (deluxetable.sty.ltxml:77) — outside a float an Error ("outside any known float").

**Rust** (73a): `\tablecaption` is stored outside a float (deluxetable_sty.rs `\lx@deluxe@tablecaption`; scoped to its
group, the class's store is `\gdef`, so a caption a group closes on is not left for an unrelated table) and directly in
an aastex `{longrotatetable}` (aas_support_sty.rs, `in_longrotatetable_body`). The next deluxetable takes the store at
its start; at its print point (`\lx@deluxe@print@caption`, `\startdata`, above the tabular) it sets its own caption,
numbered, else the kept one — **unnumbered** (`\lx@deluxe@unnumbered`, the kernel's starred caption: no counter step,
no list entry), so every later "Table N" and `\ref` is the PDF's (main-session call 2026-10-18; 2204.03327's
`tab:wasp43_res` is 3) — or, in a long table, numbered, kept or empty, as the PDF numbers it. A kept caption holding
a `\label` takes an id step (`\lx@deluxe@id@step`, Perl `RefStepID`: no counter, no list entry; main-session call
2026-10-18), so that `\label` — which pdflatex never runs ("??") — names the table, not the document or section (Perl
`floatToLabel` takes the nearest ancestor with an id); a `\ref` to it shows what Post CrossRef `generateRef` finds
walking up from the table (CrossRef.pm:686-695: the requested `refnum` on the table, then its parents, the title only
when none has one), i.e. the enclosing section's number, linked to the table. A kept caption without a `\label` takes
no id, so a `\label` written after the stored caption names the last numbered unit, as TeX's (2204.03327's aux:
`tab:allesFitted` = 4.1.5). The first `\begin{tabular}` directly in a `{longrotatetable}` sets a caption still stored,
unnumbered; one no `\begin{tabular}` took (a `tabular*`, `tabularx` or `longtable` in it, or a `\tablecaption` after
the tabular) is set at the longrotatetable's end, in its group (`\lx@lrt@end@caption`; a held longtable keeps its own
number and id); the longrotatetable is then that table's float; around a deluxetable (or a `{table}`) it is the page's setting, the
deluxetable its own table; a `\tablecaption` stored there and not taken by the held table is lost, as in the PDF
(an overwritten store behaves the same way). In a `{longtable}` the `\tablecaption` is the caption only while the longtable has none —
numbered, the longtable's own `\caption` (tag and list entry), as the PDF counts the longtable (`\ref` 1, the next
table 2); after a `\caption` it is stored, never printed there (1903.10014, #740). In another float it is the float's `\caption`, as Perl. The author's caption is kept where the PDF
loses it, content before PDF fidelity; the numbering stays the PDF's. The emulateapj and AASTeX 5 stores are TeX's
(#740). Witnesses 2204.03327 (2 → 0, its two `{longrotatetable}` captions kept), 1511.09213 (the deluxetable's `[h]`
placement read again). Repros class-bindings/{aastex_tablecaption_before_deluxetable, tablecaption_inside_the_table_wins,
stored_tablecaption_scoped_to_its_group, longrotatetable_around_a_tabular_is_its_table,
longrotatetable_tablecaption_goes_to_its_table, kept_tablecaption_is_unnumbered, longtable_keeps_its_printed_caption,
longrotatetable_caption_without_a_tabular, kept_caption_label_names_the_table, longtable_tablecaption_is_numbered};
guards `perfect_kernel_batch73a::{aastex_tablecaption_before_deluxetable, tablecaption_inside_the_table_wins,
stored_tablecaption_scoped_to_its_group, longrotatetable_around_a_tabular_is_its_table,
longrotatetable_tablecaption_goes_to_its_table, kept_tablecaption_is_unnumbered, longtable_keeps_its_printed_caption,
longrotatetable_caption_without_a_tabular, kept_caption_label_names_the_table, longtable_tablecaption_is_numbered}`.

### 740. emulateapj's and AASTeX 5's stored `\tablecaption` is printed by every table's head (Perl: an Error outside a float)

**TeX**: emulateapj.cls:1293-1294 (1010.4329's copy :1217-1218) `\gdef\@tablecaption{#1}` stores the caption globally and
never empties it; every `{deluxetable}` prints the store, numbered, at its `\tablehead` or `\startdata` (:1325, :1333;
the copy's :1249, :1257), so a `\tablecaption` before or in the table (before its head) is its caption and a table
without one repeats the last (pdflatex: "TABLE 2 / Stored One."). AASTeX 5's aastex.cls:1280 `\gdef\pt@caption` is
emptied only `\AtBeginDocument` (:1305) and printed by every deluxetable's `\startdata` (:1507), empty or not.

**Perl**: `\let\tablecaption\caption` (deluxetable.sty.ltxml:77) — outside a float an Error ("outside any known float").

**Rust** (73a): the store (`\lx@deluxe@caption`, `\iflx@deluxe@persistent`, the default) is the classes' own: every
`\tablecaption` stores it globally — outside a float, in a table, in a float (which also sets it as its `\caption`, as
Perl) — and every deluxetable prints it at its print point (deluxetable_sty.rs `\lx@deluxe@print@caption` at
`\startdata`; emulateapj_cls.rs where the data opens, at `\tablehead` or `\startdata`), numbered, above the tabular;
an empty store is the number alone, set at the table's end (#664). A caption given in the data, after the print
point, is stored for the next table and kept for this one's end, unnumbered (#664); the next table without a caption
of its own prints it again, as pdflatex, but without its `\label` (`\lx@deluxe@shown`, `\lx@deluxe@caption@nolabel`):
the label names the table that shows the caption first, where pdflatex's names the repeat (it runs only there), and no
label is defined twice. A store printed by two tables from outside both (`\tablecaption{…\label{t1}}` before them)
defines its label twice, as pdflatex ("Label multiply defined"; ours warns nothing). In a `{longtable}` a `\tablecaption` is the caption only while the longtable has none, else
stored (1903.10014's AASTeX 5 longtable keeps its printed `\caption{Observing Log…}`, and "Summary of targets", never
printed, is not set); emulateapj's is numbered there, its `\tablehead` printing it (1810.10130). Witnesses 1010.4329
(4 → 0, each caption above its tabular), 1903.10014 (1 → 0). Repros class-bindings/{emulateapj_stored_caption_repeats,
longtable_keeps_its_printed_caption, emulateapj_startdata_ends_head, emulateapj_repeat_drops_the_label}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch73a::{emulateapj_stored_caption_repeats, longtable_keeps_its_printed_caption,
stored_tablecaption_scoped_to_its_group, emulateapj_repeat_drops_the_label}` (its emulateapj half),
`perfect_kernel_batch68y::emulateapj_startdata_ends_the_head`.

### 741. A neurips copy's stored `\@projectpage`/`\@emailaddress` are the paper's contacts (TeX: printed as text at its abstract's end; Perl: no binding for the setters)

**TeX**: 2605.09681's neurips_2026.sty copy adds `\newcommand{\projectpage}[1]{\gdef\@projectpage{#1}}` and
`\emailaddress` (:410-411; the distributed style has neither) and prints the non-empty stores at the end of its renewed
`{abstract}` (:445-458): "Project Page: \texttt{…}", "Email Address: …".

**Perl**: neurips.sty.ltxml defines neither; the copy's abstract is not read, so the values are lost (with the copy's
setters) or `\projectpage` is undefined (without).

**Rust** (73a r4; user 2026-10-18, option C, superseding int23's Fallback-origin setters): the binding defines no
setter — the copy's own are provided as usual (#731) and store — and its `\end{abstract}` (neurips_sty.rs, the kernel's
`\lx@end@abstract` after) emits a non-empty `\@projectpage` as a `role=url` contact named "Project Page: " and
`\@emailaddress` as a `role=email` contact named "Email Address: " (`\lx@neurips@contacts`, `\lx@add@contact`), where
the copy's abstract prints them — frontmatter, not text. Without such a copy nothing is defined: `\projectpage` errs
undefined, as in TeX. Witness 2605.09681 (both contacts kept). Repros stand-in-copies/neurips_contact/copy_setters_are_contacts
(with the copy) and stand-in-copies/neurips_no_copy/projectpage_undefined_without_a_copy (in a directory without one); guards `perfect_kernel_batchint23::neurips_copy_setters_are_contacts`,
`perfect_kernel_batch73a::neurips_projectpage_undefined_without_a_copy`.

### 744. A stand-in copy's `\input` files are part of the copy; its syntax ends with its load; its declaration names the binding that answered

**Decision** (int23 fix round 2; refines #731; main-session ruling 2026-10-18 "`\usepackage`/`\RequirePackage` from a
copy are real loads; files a copy pulls in by `\input`/`\@input`/`\InputIfFileExists` are part of the copy"):
1. *Input files.* `input_definitions` suspends the copy's provides-mode only for a package or class load
   (`handleoptions`: `\RequirePackage`, `\usepackage`, `\LoadClass`); a file the copy reads by `\input` (`\@input`,
   `\InputIfFileExists`: the `.clo`/`.cfg` it ships) is read in the copy's mode, so its definitions of names the binding
   owns hold only inside the copy's code, its `\AtEndOfClass` code is wrapped as the copy's own (`copy_provides_wrap`)
   and its document-time hooks are not registered. A binding such an `\input` reaches is a load of its own (the mode
   suspended around `_load_binding`). Before: svjour.cls:86's `\InputIfFileExists{sv\CurrentOption.clo}` read
   svepj.clo, whose :280-284 `\AtEndOfClass{\let\maketitle=\epj@maketitle}`, and svepjc3.clo, whose :57/:71
   `\def\maketitle` (re-read by its own `\AtEndOfClass{\@input{svepjc3.clo}}`), replaced the binding's title page:
   "Address(es) of author(s) should be given", "Noname", "??", `Error:\@institute` in place of the affiliations
   (0901.1015 -1,500 words, 1012.5412, 1111.3868, 1512.01957, 2411.18962, 2107.02119).
2. *Syntax at the end.* A class or package copy ends as a real class or package load does (`load_tex_definitions`'
   expl3 cleanup, `handleoptions` for a `.cls`/`.sty` copy): latex.ltx's `\@popfilename` turns off the expl3 syntax a
   `\ProvidesExplClass` turned on. Before: fcs.cls:70's expl3 catcodes stayed on for the whole document — spaces
   ignored, `\theta_` undefined (2606.16349 recall 95.9 → 14.6; 2308.11432). An `\input` copy (`.tex`) restores
   nothing, as TeX's `\input`.
3. *Identity.* Rule 0's declaration test reads the binding that answered: a declaration naming the requested file
   counts only when the binding is of that name. The class prefix fallback (Package.pm:2700-2716) answers a renamed
   file too: 1705.03989's aaart.cls, amsart declaring itself `aaart`, under `aa`; read as aa.cls, its amsart code over
   the binding raised 3 more Errors (2 → 5). It now goes to the command-set test (1 of aa's 30 names: not read). The 2
   remaining Errors (`\address`, `\subjclass` undefined; pdflatex 0) are the fallback's, Perl's too (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
   #970).
Divergence from Perl: Perl reads no copy (#731). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchint23::{a_copy_option_file_keeps_the_bindings_title,
a_renamed_class_under_a_fallback_is_not_read}`, `perfect_kernel_batch72a::copy_identity_by_declaration_and_command_set`
(the fcs case now with spaced text and `$a_1$`); repros `stand-in-copies/option_files/`,
`stand-in-copies/identity/{declared_expl_class_is_read,renamed_class_under_a_fallback_is_not_read}`.

### 745. Typewriter whitespace is kept only where an auto-opened element reaches text

**Decision** (int23 fix round 2; narrows #47): `open_text`'s exception for whitespace-only typewriter text (and an
explicit `\ `) applies only where the current element can reach `#PCDATA` directly or through auto-opened elements
(`can_contain_node_somehow`); elsewhere Perl's rule stands and the space is dropped (Document.pm `openText`: initial
whitespace where `#PCDATA` cannot go). An `{algorithmic}` set in `\ttfamily` (WileyNJDv5.cls:6953
`\algrenewcommand\ALG@beginalgorithmic{\ttfamily}`) put the space before its first `\item` straight into the
`ltx:listing`, whose model is `listingline*`: `Error:malformed` in a minimal document, schema-invalid output in
2608.15322, 2602.03247, 2607.19926. fancyvrb's indentation (#47's case, 2605.00468) lands in a paragraph the builder
auto-opens and is unchanged. Guard `perfect_kernel_batchint23::a_typewriter_algorithmic_drops_the_leading_space`; repro
`listings-algorithms/typewriter_algorithmic_drops_the_leading_space`.

### 746. `\setlength` on a non-register runs its code

**Decision** (73b; rc_struct6 row 4): latex.ltx:10253 `\def\setlength#1#2{#1 #2\relax}` is code TeX executes. When what
`#1` begins with, past spaces and `\relax` (and expanded, as TeX's `get_x_token`), is neither a register nor a prefix,
the braced `\setlength` (sect12.rs `assign_braced_length`) puts `#1 #2\relax` back unexpanded and lets it run, where
the `Variable` read reported "A <variable> was supposed to be here" and dropped both arguments. IEEEtran templates' empty
`\setlength` line before an `\item` (2201.08831, 2401.09168) took `\item` and `F` as its arguments: the item lost its
first letter and the conversion an Error; now the item runs (pdflatex 0 errors). The preamble runs it too: what it
typesets there starts a paragraph, whose `\everypar{\@nodocument}` (latex.ltx:9137) is TeX's "Missing
\begin{document}"; LaTeXML fires no preamble `\everypar` (stomach.rs `pending_everypar`), so the code is followed by
`\lx@setlength@nodocument`, which runs `\@nodocument` when the code, begun in vertical mode, left it horizontal
(fancyheadings' `\headrulewidth`, a macro since 2.0: `\setlength{\headrulewidth}{0pt}` prints "0.4pt 0pt" and raises
that Error, pdflatex 1; guard `perfect_kernel_batch73b::setlength_on_a_macro_in_the_preamble_errs_as_tex`). `\addtolength`
keeps the error, as `\advance` reads a variable. An undefined name run this way is LaTeXML's undefined command: its
Error, and an `<ERROR class="undefined">` element where it stood (`\setlength{\bibsep}{0pt}` without natbib: pdflatex 2
Errors, ours 2, "0pt" printed by both). Perl:
latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:4603 `{Variable}` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #971). Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch73b::setlength_on_a_non_register_runs_its_code`; repro
`parameter-conditional/setlength_on_a_non_register_runs_its_code`.

### 747. A `\DeclareMathAlphabet`'d alphabet takes one argument

**Decision** (73b; rc_struct6 row 10): `\DeclareMathAlphabet{\cs}{enc}{fam}{ser}{sh}` defines `\cs{}` as the stock
alphabets are bound (`\mathrm{}`, sect07.rs; amsfonts' `\mathbb{}`): a bounded constructor carrying the font of
`lookup_tex_font`, as latex.ltx's alphabet sets its argument alone (`\select@group`). Perl's `DefPrimitiveI(cs, undef,
undef, font => …)` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2686) is a switch to the end of the group: `\mathfoo{AB}c` set `c` in the
alphabet too, and under mathalfa's `bb=ams` (mathalpha.sty:116 `\DeclareMathAlphabet{\mathbb}{U}{msb}{m}{n}`, after
`\let\mathbb\relax`) `\frac{\mathbb{W}_c}{w}` read `c` in msbm, where it sets nothing: "Missing sub/superscript
argument" (1810.09080). `\@fontswitch` (`{\foo XY}` for a `\DeclareOldFontCommand`) reads the font from the definition
as before (sect13.rs `math_alphabet_font`); in text the alphabet warns "should only appear in math mode", as the stock
ones. KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #972. Guard `perfect_kernel_batch73b::declared_math_alphabet_takes_one_argument`; repro
`fonts-nfss/declared_math_alphabet_takes_one_argument`.

### 748. A counter stepped in math whose label text cannot set is labelled as math

**Decision** (73b; rc_struct6 row 5): `label_stepped_counter` (counter/dialect.rs) digests the step's refnum and tags
(Package.pm:770 `DigestText(T_CS("\\the$ctr"))`, then `\lx@make@tags`) as text. TeX keeps `\@currentlabel`
unexpanded (latex.ltx:14963-14967) and typesets it only where `\ref` prints it. For a step made in math, the text digest
is held (`DiagnosticsHold`); if it raised an Error, it is discarded and the label digested again with `\the<ctr>` as
`\ensuremath{\the<ctr>}`, local to the label. `\renewcommand{\theconsta}{{\kappa_{\arabic{consta}}}}` with
`\refstepcounter{consta}` in a formula raised three "Script _ can only appear in math mode" per step (1609.03070: 93,
1904.00290: 57). A label text sets keeps Perl's digest, byte-identical (an equation stepped in math keeps its text tags).
Not the 70c timing redesign (labels digested only where printed): a mechanism-local fallback. Part of the surpass: a
`\ref` to such a label in text now prints the math label, where TeX typesets `\@currentlabel` (`{\kappa_{1}}`) in text
and errs ("Missing $ inserted"). KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #973.
Guard `perfect_kernel_batch73b::refstepcounter_in_math_sets_a_math_label`; repro
`macro-state/refstepcounter_in_math_sets_a_math_label`.

### 750. A `\bibitem` label's reference forms are typeset only where a `\cite` prints them

**Decision** (70c; rc_struct4 row C1; user ruling 2026-10-18: text TeX writes to an auxiliary file and typesets only
when printed is digested only where it is printed): `\@lbibitem` (latex.ltx:17746-17749) typesets the label in the list
as `\item[\@biblabel{#1}\hfill]` and writes it to the .aux as `\bibcite{key}{label}`; only a `\cite` of the key expands
`\b@key` (latex.ltx:17761-17771). So `\lx@bibitem` (sect11.rs) reads its `[label]` undigested and splits the entry's tags
(base_utilities/util_text.rs `tag_forms`): the role-less tag, `\fnum@@bibitem` = `{\@biblabel{\the@bibitem}}`, is digested at the
`\bibitem` through the class's own `\@biblabel`; the forms a reference prints (refnum, typerefnum, autoref, the
cleveref forms) are deferred under the deferred-print list `b@key` (73a's latexml_core `defer_print`, #738), resolved
when a `\@@bibref` names the key (sect11.rs `cite_prints_keys`: the kernel's `\cite`, natbib's, biblatex's, the `.bbl`
styles'), at once when one already has. `\nocite` prints nothing and does not count. The streaming yield's fallback
typesets every pending form at the spill, as Perl does. Under mn2e/mnras without `usenatbib`, whose bindings now define
the class's `\def\@biblabel#1{}` (mn2e.cls:1370, mnras.cls:1636), a `\bibitem[\protect\citeauthoryear{…}{…}]{key}`
label no longer errs for an uncited key (pdflatex 0 errors) and keeps its one Error when a `\cite` prints it (pdflatex 1
per citation). An entry nothing cites (or a keyless one) has no refnum tag; the bibliography XSLT shows the role-less tag,
else the refnum. natbib's entries (`\lx@NAT@lbibitem`) and unlabelled `\bibitem{key}` are unchanged, and so is any
`\bibitem[label]` while natbib (its own or a renamed copy: `\NAT@ifcmd`, natbib.sty:809) is loaded: natbib parses the
label at the `\bibitem` and writes the parsed author and year, so no `\cite` expands it; the label is digested there
once, as the optional argument it was, and the tags made from what it digested to (a copy's delimited `\citeauthoryear`,
natbib.sty:1014, read raw out of that context ran past the label's end: 1003.3017's natbib_vw.sty; repro
`index-bib/mn2e_natbib_copy/natbib_copy_citeauthoryear_label_cited`, pdflatex and Perl 0 errors). Divergence from
Perl, which digests the label and every form at `\bibitem` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:4096-4102). An autoload the
label calls loads its package before the entry is read, where Perl's digestion of the label loaded it (sect11.rs
`\lx@bibitem@autoloads`; a package that takes `\bibitem` over then reads the entry): crckapb's `\citeauthoryear` is
natbib's (#731), whose parser, loaded inside the tags, took `\the@bibitem` as its own number for ever (astro-ph0007279;
guard `perfect_kernel_batch77r::bibitem_label_autoload_loads_before_the_entry`). Witnesses
0812.1037, 1105.2318, 1306.6339, 1805.00040. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch70c::*`; repros
`index-bib/mnras_bibitem_label_{uncited,nocite_only,cited_before,cited_after}`, controls
`index-bib/bibitem_numeric_label_cited_and_uncited`, `index-bib/mnras_usenatbib_bibitem_label_cited`.

### 753. A table of contents inside a frontmatter container goes after it; `\tableofcontents` begins as a heading

**Perl behavior**: latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:725-743 binds `\tableofcontents`, `\listoffigures` and `\listoftables`
to `<ltx:TOC …>` constructors inserted where they stand. Inside a balanced `{abstract}` (`abstract_model` = Block.model,
no TOC) that is `malformed:ltx:TOC <ltx:TOC> isn't allowed in <ltx:p>` (or `<ltx:abstract>`), the TOC left inside, the
document invalid; after a brace-less `\abstract` the same, since the TOC does not end it (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #978).
**Rust behavior**: (1) `insert_toc` (sect04.rs) puts the TOC of an insertion point inside a frontmatter container
(`ltx:abstract`, `ltx:acknowledgements`, `ltx:keywords`, `ltx:classification`, `ltx:creator`) at the nearest open
ancestor that admits it (`Document::float_out_of_frontmatter`: Perl's `floatToElement`, Document.pm:1052-1077, closing
form; the container cannot auto-close, so the insertion point comes back): after the abstract, and the text after it
stays the abstract's. Elsewhere the TOC is inserted as before (in a `{quote}` the inline logical block of #271's bridge).
(2) The kernel's three begin `\par\@startsection@hook` (in `\lx@kernel@tableofcontents`/`…listoffigures`/`…listoftables`,
`\protected` as `\section*` is robust, still the user name's only token before `\lx@kernel@listbody`: tocbasic.sty:1175-1179's
`\edef` of `\newcommand*\csname listof\tb@nt@types\endcsname{…}`, KOMA's `\DeclareNewTOC`, expands `\listoffigures`
and must meet one token), as the `\section*{\contentsname…}` they are in article.cls,
report.cls and amsart.cls (`\chapter*` in book.cls) does: a paragraph ends, and after a brace-less `\abstract` or inside
an unclosed `\abstract{` the TOC ends the abstract as a `\section` does (sect05.rs `\abstract`), the hook's other
members running as at any heading (the frontmatter fallback of a document without `\maketitle`, a bibliography's end).
A raw class's own `\tableofcontents` replaces the kernel's, as before. The rule for a TOC differs from a `\section*`
inside a balanced abstract, which document.rs's sectioning leniency still keeps in place without an Error (Perl errs
there, `<ltx:section> isn't allowed in <ltx:abstract>`; a nested second one errs in both): the TOC follows the schema
and Perl's own placement of an element its context refuses.
**Why**: pdflatex prints the TOC inside the abstract's quotation (`\section*` in the `quotation` list), where the schema
has no place for it; after the abstract keeps both whole and in order. Witnesses — a balanced abstract ending with
`\tableofcontents{}` (LyX; amsart/article/revtex4): 1011.3976, 1310.0349, 1509.04736, 1404.7641, 0809.1270, 1509.03167,
1706.09575, 2105.04928, 2401.08592, 2403.19281, 2408.04858, 2408.11452, 2509.01284; mid-abstract 1602.08755; an
unclosed `\abstract`/`\abstract{` (article/report): 2007.03709, 2202.05904, 2411.02384, 2506.07991, 2512.04732,
2602.15970, hep-lat9910044; mdpi's template under article 2104.05770; sapthesis 1603.02077 (its `\mainmatter` after
the TOC was read inside the unclosed abstract, its chapters' sections unnumbered: now numbered as in the PDF). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch74a::{toc_at_the_end_of_a_balanced_abstract_follows_it, toc_mid_abstract_follows_it_and_the_text_stays,
toc_ends_an_unclosed_abstract, toc_ends_an_unclosed_braced_abstract, lists_of_figures_and_tables_follow_the_abstract,
toc_outside_the_frontmatter_is_unchanged}`; repros `sectioning-frontmatter/{toc_inside_balanced_abstract_at_its_end,
toc_inside_balanced_abstract_mid_text, toc_ends_an_unclosed_abstract, toc_ends_an_unclosed_braced_abstract,
lists_of_figures_and_tables_inside_abstract}`.

### 754. A frontmatter body left open at `\end{document}` ends there and keeps its text (Perl: an empty document)

An abstract (or keywords) is read as a deferred frontmatter body up to its terminal (`\lx@add@frontmatter@until …
\lx@end@abstract`, base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_fields.rs). Left open — an unclosed `\begin{abstract}`, an unbalanced `\abstract{`, a
brace-less `\abstract` no sectioning command ends — that body ran to the end of input: it held the finalizer and the
rest of the document, and nothing placed it, so the output was an empty `<document/>` with 0 errors (Perl: resources
only, 1 error). pdflatex prints every word. `\end{document}` now begins with `\lx@end@open@frontmatter` (sect02.rs):
when the nearest open frontmatter body is such a body, its terminal is read first, the body ends with its text (one body
per pass, so keywords left open inside an abstract end both, int26 review p8), and the end-document code runs at the
document's level, as an unclosed `{itemize}` keeps its list (65c). Diagnostics as pdflatex's: the
unclosed `\begin{abstract}` is LaTeX's error (`\@checkend`: "\begin{abstract} … ended by \end{document}"; Perl errs
too), raised once, on the first pass, naming the innermost environment begun with `\begin` (`\@currenvir`:
stomach.rs `begun_environment` — `\begin`'s `current_environment`, or `lx@until@begun`, which the kernel's
`\begin{abstract}`, no environment frame of its own, leaves in its body's frame; the IEEEtran binding's
`\begin{IEEEkeywords}` now sets `\@currenvir` as `\begin` does), and only at the body's own level (an environment open
inside it, a `{minipage}`, keeps its Warning, as before). A begin code called as a command opens no environment LaTeX
checks, so it reports nothing: the brace-less `\abstract`, mn2e's `\keywords{…}`, spconf's `\keywords …` (an int26 A/B
fix: four papers had gained a spurious Error, 1004.2791, 2201.07008, 2309.07195, 1401.5657); the unbalanced `\abstract{`
reports its open group (`until_terminal_inside_group`). A heading after an unclosed `\begin{abstract}` ends it (#755).
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #980. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch74b::{braceless_abstract_unclosed_at_end_document_keeps_its_text,
braced_abstract_unclosed_at_end_document_keeps_its_text, environment_abstract_unclosed_at_end_document_errs_and_keeps_its_text}`;
repros `sectioning-frontmatter/{braceless,braced}_abstract_unclosed_at_end_document_keeps_the_document`,
`sectioning-frontmatter/unclosed_abstract_at_end_document_keeps_the_document`.
**Why**: the status code must be honest (user 2026-10-18): a whole document lost with 0 errors counted as a success.

### 755. A sectioning heading inside an abstract ends the abstract (Perl: an error, the heading nested)

User ruling 2026-10-18: "A \section inside an abstract should close/complete the abstract". `\@startsection` (sect04.rs)
at section level or above (`\part`, `\chapter`, `\section`, starred or not) first reads `\lx@heading@ends@frontmatter`
(sect05.rs): when the nearest open frontmatter body is an abstract or keywords, its terminal is read before the heading,
so the body ends with the text before it and the heading starts the document's body with the text after it — as the
brace-less `\abstract` already ended at `\@startsection@hook`. Keywords alike (int26 A/B fix round): an environment's
begin code called as a command has no extent — mn2e.cls:993-1003 and mnras.cls:1122-1131 `\keywords` open a `\list` no
`\endkeywords` closes, spconf's and ieeeconf's are labels — and the text the author gave it ends where the paper's first
section begins; read as the open body, the whole document went into `<ltx:keywords>`, every section an Error
(`<ltx:section> isn't allowed in <ltx:keywords>`, then in `<ltx:section>`): 1004.2791, 2201.07008, 2309.07195 (28
Errors → 0, words unchanged). A keywords body a command form opened inside the abstract ends with it
(base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_fields.rs `\lx@end@abstract`; ieeeconf `\begin{abstract} … \keywords \MyKeywords \end{abstract}`, 1401.5657). The `\end{abstract}` that follows is then a no-op; one a
heading-ended `\begin{abstract}` never gets is LaTeX's "\begin{abstract} ended by \end{document}" at `\end{document}`
(sect02.rs `\lx@end@open@frontmatter`). Not inside a replayed class begin code (its `\section*{\abstractname}` is the
class's own heading, discarded with the replay, #482), and not where a class rebinds `\section` inside the abstract
(frontiersFPHY's `\absection`: a run-in label, no heading). An abstract the heading closed before its first line (the structured-abstract idiom, scrartcl
`\begin{abstract}\section*{Abstract:} …`, 1507.08575) holds nothing and adds no entry: `\lx@add@frontmatter@until`
keeps no body that typesets nothing (abstract, keywords, classification), so an empty environment leaves no empty
element either (Perl: an empty `ltx:abstract`). Lower levels (`\subsection`…`\subparagraph`) do not close
it; pdflatex sets the heading inside the abstract's text block either way. Perl: `<ltx:section> isn't allowed in
<ltx:abstract>` (1 error); ours kept it nested, schema-invalid (74a row (b)). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch74b::{section_inside_balanced_abstract_closes_it,
environment_abstract_unclosed_at_end_document_errs_and_keeps_its_text, keywords_command_form_ends_at_first_section,
keywords_label_inside_abstract_ends_with_it}`; repros `sectioning-frontmatter/{abstract_section_closes_the_abstract,
keywords_command_form_ends_at_first_section, class_keywords/keywords_label_inside_abstract_ends_with_it}`.

### 756. The `\maketitle` replay gate reads a class body as TeX runs it (Perl: the class body is never run)

`body_vocabulary_is_defined` (sect05.rs; the gate of the #265 `\maketitle` replay and the #482 setter replays) asks
whether every control sequence a refused class body would run is defined. It now reads the body as TeX does:
- the parameter text and replacement text of a `\def`/`\gdef` (any prefix) and the default and body of a
  `\newcommand`-family definition are stored, not run (tex.web §473 `scan_toks` with `xpand` false): they are checked
  where the body calls the macro, once (`BodyDefinee`), and a macro the body never calls is not checked;
  `\edef`/`\xdef` replacement texts are expanded as they are defined (§1218) and stay checked in place;
- the delimiters a called macro's parameter text matches (`Match`/`Until` parameters, tex.web §392-399) are
  matched, not run (`delimiter_positions`); the arguments themselves stay checked;
- what a called macro's body defines counts as defined after the call;
- `\futurelet` defines what it lets, as `\let` does (§1221);
- a token `\ifx`, `\ifdefined`, `\string` or `\meaning` only compares or shows is not checked (#906).
The gate itself never reports: a parameter text is read by its own `gate_parameters` — `None` (no delimiters matched,
the call's arguments checked as tokens) for one holding an argument of the enclosing macro (an `ARG` token), a doubled
`#` or parameters out of order — and never by `parse_def_parameters`, whose ParamSpec Fatal is sticky (a class
`\renewcommand{\author}[1]{\expandafter\def\csname tp@au#1\endcsname##1{##1}…}` marked a clean paper Fatal). A name `\csname` makes has its tokens run in place, and an `\expandafter` chain expands the one token after the
replacement text's brace (`expandafter_definee`: `\expandafter\def\expandafter\x\expandafter{\y\z}` defines `\x` and
checks `\y`); the rest of either's replacement text is stored like any `\def`'s (tex.web §473), so only an
`\edef`/`\xdef` reads it in place (round 3). A called
macro's definitions count only for a control sequence undefined here, from its live branches and outside the stored
replacement texts of the definitions it makes (`callee_definees`), so a real meaning is never shadowed. A body whose own
definitions call one another more than 8 deep is refused with an Info, not admitted unread.
jpsj.sty:170-173's own `\twocolumn`, replayed with its `\maketitle`, sets `\@twocolumntrue` globally, so its `{full}`
equations become `ltx:float[figure]` with their two rules (cond-mat0011490), as pdflatex lays them out (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
#901: `\twocolumn` sets the flag).
sig-alternate-05-2015.cls:726-737's `\maketitle` defines `\@makefnmark` (article.cls:206, reading `\@thefnmark`, which
latex.ltx defines only when a footnote is made): "not replayed: it uses \@thefnmark" stopped 204 of the 3,000
sample papers' replays, which now run (1505.04771's `\toappear` "pre-print of an article appearing at KDD'16"; the
ACM copyright/permission blocks of 0712.1016, 1301.5612, 1609.02839, cs0404029; the NeurIPS venue lines of
1506.04304, 1704.05155, 2111.02813; 2407.00478's author notes). nowfnt.cls:552-583's `\author` calls
`\nowfnt@splitauthor#2,!,!,\@nil` and reads the `\nowfnt@lastname` it defines (1912.00312: the replay now runs; its
`\maintitleauthorlist` is a separate residual, SYNC_STATUS 75a). A/B over those 204 papers and 40 more (the
two-refusal `\maketitle` and wiley/nbdt/CSML papers of the sample) against 67int27: E 1,933 → 1,924, F 2 → 2, no paper
with more errors, none losing more than 1 % of its words, no doubled creator. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch75a::{maketitle_replay_skips_stored_replacement_text, maketitle_replay_skips_called_delimiters,
maketitle_replay_gate_reads_csname_def_silently, maketitle_replay_expandafter_def_reads_in_place,
maketitle_replay_gate_stores_csname_and_expandafter_definitions}`; repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/class_title_page/maketitle_replay_{skips_*,gate_reads_csname_def_silently,expandafter_def_reads_in_place,
gate_stores_csname_and_expandafter_definitions}`.

### 757. A class's append to a locked command it redefined extends the class's own definition (Perl: lost)

When the lock refuses a redefinition that is the locked binding's replacement text with tokens appended or prepended
— etoolbox's `\appto`/`\preto` (`\edef#1{\expandonce#1…}`) and latex.ltx's `\g@addto@macro` build it from the meaning
they read — and the class's own refused definition of the name is on record (`\lx@dropped@<name>`, #265), the record
becomes the class's definition with the same tokens appended or prepended (state.rs `extended_refused_definition`), as
in TeX, where the class's definition is the meaning the append reads. wiley-article.cls:420-466 renews `\maketitle` and
:576 `\appto`s to it: the record held the kernel's body and the append, so the replay ran nothing of the class's title
page (1911.06213, 31 sample papers logging the refusal twice); vmsta.cls:691's `\appto\maketitle{\hypersetup…}` after
its own `\maketitle` (:534-545) likewise (1506.02940, 1801.00977: the received/revised/accepted/published dates, the
affiliation and the keywords the class alone prints are now kept). Parameterless token bodies only; any other
refused definition is recorded as before. Residual: vmsta's title page also prints its journal header with the
values the document did not set left empty — "Modern Stochastics: Theory and Applications () 51–65 / DOI:" and an
empty `<ref href="http://dx.doi.org/">` (1506.02940; the shape the `\submitted` entry of #758 was withheld for, page
furniture by ruling; SYNC_STATUS 75a row (d)). Guard `perfect_kernel_batch75a::maketitle_class_append_extends_class_body`;
repro `sectioning-frontmatter/class_title_page/maketitle_class_append_extends_class_body`.

`STORE_SETTERS` (latexml_core/src/binding/store_setters.rs) gains `corraddress` → `ltx:note[role=correspondence]`,
`corremail` → `ltx:note[role=email]`, `fundinginfo` → `ltx:note[role=funding]`, `papertype` → `ltx:pubnote[role=type]`

sig-alternate's `\toappear` and vmsta's `\publishedonline`/`\received` wrap their argument (not pure stores; #756/#757
print them with the class's title page), bullsrsl's `\correspondance` stores into `\BSRSL@CorrEmail` (rule (a) needs an

### 759. What a refused setter's replay added to the class's own record reads as empty in the title-page deposit (Perl: never run)

The #482 replay of a refused class `\title`/`\author` keeps the class's lists; what the body added to a list for the
call's argument — vmsta.cls:296-315 `\g@addto@macro\@@@authors{…\name@m@front{#2}…}` — is the class's record of the field
the kernel's frontmatter carries. For each macro the kept replay changed (its assignment journal with the value before,

tail appended to the value before, the head prepended, the text inserted between the old value's common head and
tail (before a list's end sentinel), or the whole value when the replay overwrote the macro — joins
`lx_replay_records` when it holds the argument (sect05.rs `note_replay_records`), and `\lx@replay@records` takes each
recorded part out of its macro, locally, in the `\@maketitle` deposit and the `\maketitle` replay, as they null
`\@author`. What other code put in the same list stays: a class `\workplace` appending to the author list keeps its
text, in either call order, whether it appends or inserts before a sentinel. Once #757 let vmsta's own `\maketitle` replay, it printed the author and affiliation a
second time (1506.02940, 1801.00977). Residual, awaiting a ruling (SYNC_STATUS 75a row (e)): a record that does not
hold the argument — vmsta 2018+'s `\csxdef{author\the\c@author}` and its list of names — is not found, and its title page
prints the author line beside the creators, and its e-mail line — recovered content, kept nowhere else — twice (it is

maketitle_replay_keeps_other_setters_in_shared_list,
maketitle_replay_keeps_other_setters_in_sentinel_list}`; repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/class_title_page/maketitle_replay_{reads_class_author_list_as_empty,keeps_other_setters_in_{shared,sentinel}_list_*}`.

**77i.** The records are now read before a clean replay puts the stores back, so a store the body itself defines that
holds the argument is a record too and stays set (#482's 77i addendum; a document's `\gdef\myauth{#1}` read in the
