### 760. A document's `\halign` redefinition runs where a binding's alignment reaches `\halign` (Perl: never runs)

In TeX every amsmath alignment environment and every `\ialign`-based one (latex.ltx `\@array` for array/tabular/
tabularx, plain `\ialign` = `\everycr{}\tabskip\z@skip\halign`, `\eqalign`, `\matrix`, `\oalign`, eqnarray, longtable,
amscd, blkarray, IEEEtrantools, numcases) executes the token `\halign`, so a macro `\halign` runs just before the
primitive it finally reaches. Our bindings build those alignments in Rust (`\lx@begin@alignment`) and never executed
`\halign`; only those bindings run the prelude below — a document's or raw-loaded package's own `\ialign` does not, since
`\ialign` is `\let` to `\halign` (plain_base.rs, as Perl's plain_base.pool.ltxml:118). `\lx@begin@alignment`'s before-digest (tex_tables.rs `run_halign_redefinition_prelude`) now digests the
redefinition's expansion in the group the alignment starts in, just before it, and treats the primitive it ends with as
the alignment already being built. latex.ltx's `tabbing` builds its lines from boxes and never executes `\halign`: its
alignment carries `ALIGNMENT_WITHOUT_HALIGN` (latex_constructs `tabbing_bindings`) and runs no prelude. Only the
conservative shape runs: a parameterless macro whose expansion ends with a token meaning the primitive — a constructor
declared `halign_primitive` (core `Constructor::halign_primitive`): the primitive itself under any name (cryptocode.sty:950
`\let\@pc@halign\halign`) or, inside a pgf picture, its SVG stand-in `\lxSVG@halign`, which `\lxSVG@installcommands` lets
`\halign` to. A redefinition that does not end with the primitive, reaches it only through another macro (one macro
level only; pdflatex runs the two-level shape — a deliberate limit, guard
`halign_redefinition_not_ending_with_the_primitive_is_not_run`), or reaches it in mid-expansion is not run at all. Global
side effects of a redefinition run once per binding alignment, against TeX's measure-then-set: amsmath's measured
environments run their `\halign` twice (align, gather, gather*, multline, flalign, alignat; `split` in an equation four
times). Material the expansion typesets precedes the alignment, as on TeX's
list (pdflatex typesets it with 0 errors); in math contexts it is digested as math where TeX sets it as text in the
alignment's `\vcenter` (`aligned`, `matrix`, `split`: content kept, its mode differs). Where the alignment is the display
itself (`$$\halign`: amsmath's align/gather families, eqnarray, IEEEeqnarray — `ALIGNMENT_IS_DISPLAY`) TeX errs
"Improper \halign inside $$'s" and deletes it (tex.web §776 `flush_math`): a Warning names it and it is dropped.
cases.sty's `numcases` is not one: its `\halign` is inside a `\vbox` (cases.sty:73-75), and the material is kept.
amsmath's `multline` is a display too but is not marked (exception): its material is kept in the formula, the safe
direction.

cryptocode.sty:950-957 (and its `mode=text` branch :760-770) redefines `\halign` inside `\pseudocode` to bind `\@pc@lb`
to the alignment's `\\` and `\\` to its line-numbering wrapper. Without the prelude every pseudocode line after the
first lost its number, silently, and `mode=text` erred `undefined:\@pc@lb` (its `\@pc@modeend` closes the `{varwidth}`
holding the text-mode `\@pc@lb` before the wrapper calls it). Run 340: 27 papers with `undefined:\@pc@lb` (witnesses
1804.05141, 2106.03626, 2107.06049, 2108.04600, 2202.07253; 2107.05054 in TikZ nodes, 11 errors → 0; 2410.11134 95 →
481 numbered lines): all 27 now 0 Errors, every pseudocode row its own numbered row, words unchanged. Perl does not load
cryptocode.sty at all (raw loading off), so it has neither the numbering nor the error. Six amsmath/tabular-heavy papers
without cryptocode convert byte-identically. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch76a::*`; repros
`kernel-alignment/{cryptocode_halign_redefinition_numbers_lines, halign_redefinition_skips_tabbing_and_keeps_material}`.
**Why**: the author's content — every line number pdflatex prints — and an error-free log, by the TeX semantics of
`\halign` rather than a cryptocode special case.

### 761. Only a titlepage with ink hides the document title in HTML (Perl: any titlepage hides it)

LaTeXML's HTML stylesheet skips the document's `ltx:title` whenever the document has an `ltx:titlepage` child
(LaTeXML-structure-xhtml.xsl, Perl's :358-359), taking the cover to carry the title. An empty cover —
`\begin{titlepage}\thispagestyle{empty}\vspace*{2cm}\end{titlepage}` before `\maketitle`, which pdflatex prints as a
blank page and then the title — builds an empty `<ltx:titlepage/>`, so the HTML showed no title at all (only the
`<head>` `<title>`), with 0 errors (68t; silent-loss inventory #22). The rule now skips the title only beside a
titlepage with ink: text, or a graphic, picture, formula or SVG. A cover that prints the title keeps hiding the
duplicate, as before. Repro `sectioning-frontmatter/empty_titlepage_keeps_the_title`; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch74b::empty_titlepage_keeps_the_title`.

### 762. biblatex `\printbibliography` applies its entry filters (Perl: ignores the optional argument)

`\printbibliography[type=…]`, `nottype=`, `subtype=`, `notsubtype=`, `keyword=`, `notkeyword=`, `category=` and
`notcategory=` narrow the `.bbl`'s datalist as biblatex does (biblatex.sty:9526-9615 `\blx@key@type` …
`\blx@key@notcategory`): the entries of an `entry` datalist are filed by type, `entrysubtype` and comma-split keyword
while the `.bbl` is read (:8707-8711, :8385-8390); the filters apply in the order given and AND together, keeping
datalist order. **Repeated keys**: a key given twice is two filters (`keyword=author,keyword=latent` keeps the entries
with both; witness arXiv 2406.11014), except that `type` and `subtype` share one toggle (`blx@tempb`, :9532-9566): the
second of them is biblatex's error "'type' used multiple times" (or 'subtype') and an empty list. A positive filter
whose value no entry has is biblatex's Warning ("Type 'online' not found") and an empty list; an unknown `not*` value
is a no-op; an empty list is LaTeX's Warning "Empty bibliography" (`\blx@warn@bibempty`, :1511) and prints nothing, not
even its heading (:9866-9868). **Categories**: `\DeclareBibliographyCategory` (:11207) and `\addtocategory`
(:11218-11244) keep global lists (primitives, with biblatex's two errors). biblatex files a category's keys through the
`.aux`, so pdflatex prints every list with the categories the whole previous run filed; the binding decides category
membership once the whole document is digested, and digests no entry a list does not keep: each entry of a list
filtered by categories is deferred where it stands (`\biblatex@defer@entry`, the deferred-print mechanism of #738,
list `biblatex@category`) and built at the end of the document, before the hidden list, if it passes
(`\biblatex@select`), from the data its refsection's `.bbl` gave it, with its bibliography's `xml:id` prefix and its
font; the list's heading is built in place, wrapped in `\biblatex@if@selected[list]`, and a list that keeps no key is
"Empty bibliography" (an `\addtocategory` after the list counts). Under `--streaming` a fragment's yield builds the
pending entries with the keys filed up to then (guard
`114_streaming_cluster_regressions::streaming_builds_a_category_list_when_absorbed`). **Hooks**: an `\addtocategory` in code the binding never runs — a hook
or bibmacro (`\AtEveryCitekey`, `\AtEveryBibitem`, `\AtDataInput`, `\(re)newbibmacro`, …), a declaration
(`\DeclareBibliographyDriver`, historian.bbx/publist.bbx; `\DeclareFieldFormat`, `\DeclareIndex{Name,List,Field}Format`;
`\defbibcheck`; `\DeclareCiteCommand`'s code, musuos.cbx) — what they were given is kept and scanned, with the macros
it calls, as hgbbib.sty:113's `\@AssignToBibCategory`; a category name that is a macro parameter
(`\addtocategory{#1}{…}`) may be any. Such a category is unknown: a filter on it is not applied (one Info per category
and document), and a `\bibbycategory` with such a category prints the one unfiltered list — fail-safe: the list may
hold entries pdflatex leaves out (probe 6 of the 77a r2 review: pdflatex prints that list empty, its driver filing the
keys as the list prints), never an empty one pdflatex would fill. **Numbers**: an entry's label number is biblatex's:
with `defernumbers=false` its place among the numbered entries of its refsection's datalist (biblatex.sty:8891-8923
`\blx@bbl@labelnumber`: every entry but a `skiplab`/`dataonly` one or one with a `shorthand`), so it has one number in
every list of its refsection (`\printbibliography[type=book]` then `[nottype=book]`: Books [1][2], Articles [3][4],
citations "[2, 3, 1, 4]", as pdflatex) and its own in another refsection's; with `defernumbers=true` (package option or `\ExecuteBibliographyOptions`) the next
number of the refsection when the entry is first built, kept by every later list (:9216-9283 `\blx@addlabelnumber`),
`resetnumbers=true`/`<n>` restarting the count for entries not yet numbered (:9759-9765; without `defernumbers` it is
biblatex's Warning and ignored). Each built `ltx:bibentry` carries it as `ltx:bib-data` `labelnumber`
(`\biblatex@bbl@number`), which MakeBibliography prints and cites by in a biblatex bibliography (make_bibliography.rs
`given_number`, read from the list's own copy of the entry — a key several refsections print is numbered in each; a
`.bib` field `labelnumber` under natbib is no label; the list keeps its order); its own count restarted at 1 in each `ltx:bibliography`, so the filtered lists of one `.bbl` gave
two entries one label (witness arXiv 2406.00136: "[5,…] [7,…] [1,…] [1,…]" where pdflatex prints "[9,…] [11,…] [5,…]
[1,…]"). An author-year style numbers nothing. An entry with a `shorthand` takes no number: in a biblatex bibliography the
shorthand is its label (:8920 `\let\abx@field@labelnumber\abx@field@shorthand`; make_bibliography.rs `given_label`),
cited by it (2406.00136's keyword list is [HTT] [HA] [SAG] [Ker]; the other list [1]-[17]), on both routes: on the
`.bib` route (no `.bbl`, no `labelnumber`) the list numbers only the entries that print a number, each keeping its own
id (make_bibliography.rs `number_entry`; it printed `[Balbes & Dwinger] [2]`-`[5]`, pdflatex [1]-[4]). Only biblatex's: the
handlers that digest the label fields `shorthand` and `labelalpha` are the biblatex binding's (defined with its
loading of the BibTeX pool), and `given_label`/`given_number` read a label only in a biblatex bibliography — under
natbib/BibTeX those `.bib` fields are raw `ltx:bib-data` as in Perl and no label (`shorthand={\undefinedmacro TB}`
raised `Error:undefined`, a `labelalpha={Knu84}` printed [Knu84] and was cited "[, 1]"; pdflatex + bibtex 0 errors,
[2, 1]). **`\bibliographystyle`** is ignored, as biblatex does (blx-compat.def:13-17, loaded by biblatex.sty:16416), its error
"'\bibliographystyle' invalid for 'biblatex'" reported as a Warning (ignoring it keeps the labels; 64zf's honesty rule): the kernel's, left after `\printbibliography` by a natbib
template, rewrote the list's `bibstyle` to the `.bst`'s name, so the list was no longer a biblatex one and printed
[1]-[5] for `[Knu84; Böt01; Balbes & Dwinger; Goo94a; Goo94b]` (77a r5 review probe bs/a_alphabetic; pdflatex 1
error). **Entries no list prints**: once a list leaves out an entry of its
datalist, the entries no list of a refsection printed are built at the end of the document in a hidden
(`ltx_nodisplay`) bibliography — only those: each list records the entries it prints as it is digested
(`\biblatex@printed`, `\biblatex@select`), so none is built again in the hidden list (an entry two lists keep is
typeset twice, as in pdflatex) — numbered as above (0
with `defernumbers=true`, the label biblatex gives an entry it never numbered, :8898-8909): biblatex reads the whole
`.bbl` at `\begin{document}`, so pdflatex labels their citations and prints their `\fullcite` (cs-techrep's
`notcategory=selfref` with "Please cite as: \fullcite{selfref}", arXiv 2405.19762). **`\bibbycategory`** (:9955-9998) prints `\printbibliography[<options>,
category=<name>,heading=<name>]` per declared category: a category with no keys is skipped silently, none with keys is
"Empty bibliography", none declared "No categories found"; a non-void category whose keys the refsection never cites
prints nothing (biblatex prints its heading). **Headings**: `heading=<name>` titles the list with the argument of the
sectioning command of the author's `\defbibheading{<name>}[<title>]{<code>}`, `#1` the `title=` or the heading's
default; biblatex.def's own headings, and code with no sectioning command, keep the default title; an undefined
heading is no error here (biblatex's "Heading '…' not found"). **Refsections**: a `\printbibliography` prints its own
refsection's list (`section=`, else the current one, :9827 `\blx@tempe`), refsections numbered as biblatex numbers
them (`\refsection`/`\newrefsection` from 1, back to 0 at `\endrefsection`, :10776-10778, :10874; a citation after
`\end{refsection}` links to refsection 0's list; the `refsegment` environment and `\newrefsegment` open a segment
only `segment=` reads, no-ops here); a `.bbl` with none
of its own number, and refsections opened at headings (`refsection=section`, not counted), print every refsection's
list as before. A citation refers to its own refsection's entry (biblatex: a `\cite` in refsection <n> is to that
refsection's entry, with its number): refsection <n>'s lists are `lists="refsection<n>"` and its citations
`inlist="refsection<n>"` (`CITE_UNIT`, the chapterbib/bibunits mechanism), falling back to the default list as every
unit list does (#59); refsection 0 and refsections opened at headings keep the default list (probe r1 of the 77a r3
review: "A [1, 2]" linking to its own list, where the citation linked to refsection 2's [3]; witnesses arXiv
2308.00515, 2507.16315). Before, every call printed every entry at 0 errors (silent-loss inventory #21); the ar5iv Perl binding
(biblatex.sty.ltxml:857-862) declares `\printbibliography[]` and ignores the argument (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #983). Witness
arXiv 2406.00136 (`[keyword=alph]` then `[notkeyword=alph]`): 21 + 21 entries → 4 + 17, as pdflatex. **Not modelled**:
refsections opened at headings (`refsection=chapter|section`, biblatex's `\blx@refpatch@sect` heading patch, a no-op
here) are not counted, so each `\printbibliography` prints every refsection's list and their citations go to the
default list (arXiv 2406.01695: 8 calls → 96 lists, 566/566 citations outside their chapter's list; SYNC row 21);
`check=`/`\defbibcheck`, `filter=`/`\defbibfilter`, `segment=`, a `\printbibliography[sorting=…]` (its own
refcontext's datalist; the default one prints), `omitnumbers`, `prefixnumbers`/`labelprefix` (and the `resetnumbers`
they imply), biblatex's
Warning "Split bibliography detected", the package-level `sorting=` on the `.bib` route (no `.bbl`; `sorting=none` still lists alphabetically), any filter on

is built in a category list from its own refsection's (a snapshot), but a crossref'd parent from the last one read. Code `biblatex_sty.rs` `bbl_filter`, `bbl_print`, `blx_selected`, `blx_unmodelled_categories`,
`blx_unprinted_bibliography`, `blx_heading_title`, `blx_target_refsection`, `blx_refsection_list`;

`\ifentrycategory{<key>}{<category>}`
answers from the categories filed so far (it took three arguments and printed both branches); `\ifcategory`, a
question about the entry being typeset, is always false. **Why**: the
author's split bibliography — which entries pdflatex lists under each heading, and the one label each entry has.

### 763. an.cls, apa.cls and cclayout.sty title-page stores are the frontmatter (Perl: OmniBus for the classes, an Error on `{subject}`)

Under the raw classes (OD #444) three class stores that only a class's own title page prints were lost with 0 errors
(silent-loss inventory #11, #23). Each is now the frontmatter element where the class or package defines its setter:
- **an.cls** (Astronomische Nachrichten; not in TeX Live, the papers ship it): `\abstract` is the class's `\aaabstract`
  (an.cls:98 `\AtEndOfClass{\let\abstract=\aaabstract}`, :414 `\gdef\@abstract{#1}`, read by `\@maketitle` :718), so
  the text was a plain paragraph of the deposited title block. A new stand-in binding (latexml_contrib `an_cls.rs`,
  listed in `AUTHOR_FILE_STAND_INS`) reads the shipped copy raw and redefines `\aaabstract` as `\lx@add@abstract`
  before the end-of-class hook copies it; without a copy it is OmniBus, with the loader's missing-file status and
  "Can't find binding for class an (using OmniBus)" Warning (latexml_package `shipped_class::omnibus_without_copy`,
  which the cimento, compositio, jinst and apa-family stand-ins share; the binding's presence had kept the loader from
  raising it). Witness astro-ph0611016 (0 errors before and after; the abstract now `ltx:abstract`, its text once).
  v1.03 (2002/07/04, astro-ph0306340) prints the class's label before the store (`\@maketitle` :662
  `\noindent{\bfseries\abstractname}\ \@abstract`; v1.09a and later comment it out): there the setter passes
  `name={\abstractname}` and the title-page deposit takes that line out of `\@maketitle` (sect05.rs
  `note_title_page_part`, a `\lx@replay@records` record), so no lone bold "Abstract" paragraph stays in the title
  block; `\abstractname` is not changed. With the store given empty, a paper using the class's `{abstract}`
  environment keeps the deposited title block (keywords line, © line), which the deposit dropped while `\@abstract`
  was undefined there. The binding's name makes it the prefix fallback (Perl Package.pm:2717-2728: `my ($alternate)
  = grep` :2723, the Warning :2728) for classes whose name starts with `an` and that have no binding: andp2012.cls
  (1504.05091, 1810.06303) is read raw by it as before, with no `\aaabstract` to redefine — XML byte-identical — plus
  the "Can't find binding for class andp2012 (using an)" Warning; so is the 2014 v1.12 an.cls, which defines
  `\abstract` itself (:422; 1810.02388, 2103.06625).
- **apa.cls** `\acknowledgements` (:461 `\long\def\@acks{#1}`, printed by the doc/jou title pages :1262-1267,
  :1549-1557, and in man mode as a closing section :760-764) is `ltx:acknowledgements` named by `\acksname` ("Author
  Note"), in every mode (apa6_cls.rs `define_notes`, beside `\note`). In man mode this moves the text from the class's
  closing `\AtEndDocument` "Author Note" section (:760-764 `\section{\acksname}\@acks`, which the raw class
  produced) into the frontmatter: semantic markup over PDF placement. `ltx:acknowledgements` is `Inline.model` (the
  schema, as Perl's), so each paragraph of a multi-paragraph argument is a line of it (#766), where the man-mode
  section had kept `<p>`s.
- **cclayout.sty** (cc.cls:229-230): `\Abstract{…}` (:66) and `{subject}` (:76-81) are `ltx:abstract` named
  `\ccabstractname` and `ltx:classification` named `\ccsubjectclassificationname` (latexml_contrib `cclayout_sty.rs`,
  which reads the package raw first); `{keywords}` stays K11's collected-body reroute.

Perl has no binding for any of the three: an.cls and apa.cls fall to OmniBus (an abstract, and `<acknowledgements
name="Acknowledgements">` with `\note` undefined, 1 Error), cc.cls to OmniBus with `{subject}` undefined (1 Error,
"68Q15, 68Q17" a plain paragraph). Repros `sectioning-frontmatter/class_notes/{an_abstract_store_is_the_abstract,
an_v103/an_v103_abstract_label_is_its_name, an_abstract_environment_keeps_the_title_block, apa_acknowledgements_kept,
cclayout_abstract_and_subject_kept}`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch74b::{an_abstract_store_is_the_abstract,
an_v103_abstract_label_is_its_name, an_abstract_environment_keeps_the_title_block, an_without_its_class_warns,
apa_acknowledgements_are_kept_in_every_mode, cclayout_abstract_and_subject_are_kept}`. **Why**: the authored text in its
semantic element, error-free, by the class's own setter rather than its unset title page.

### 764. A shipped class's pre-2020 `\@pushfilename` is read with the pop of its era (TL 2025 pdflatex: errors; Perl: OmniBus)

pasa.cls (2013/04/01 v1.0, Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia; shipped, not in TeX Live) redefines
`\@pushfilename` at :45-52 with the LaTeX2e kernel's body before 2020-10 and calls it once, bare. latex.ltx's 2020-10
`\@pushfilename` also pushes the default hook label and the file path (`\@expl@push@filename@@`,
`\@kernel@currpathstack`; its last token, `\@expl@push@filename@aux@@`, reads the three tokens that follow — the
`\xdef\@currname{…}` of `\@onefilewithoptions`) and its `\@popfilename` pops both, so every package loaded after the
class — its own `\usepackage{graphicx}` at :1339 first — popped a hook label nobody pushed: "LaTeX hooks Error: Extra
\PopDefaultHookLabel" once per load, 13-39 Errors per paper and nothing else (pdflatex on TL 2025 stops with the same
and "File ended while scanning use of \@p@pfilepath@aux"; the class compiled cleanly on the LaTeX of its era). The
kernel's push cannot stand in for the class's copy, because the bare call at :52 would feed its last token
`\newlength\trimwidth`. The pasa binding (pasa_cls.rs, an author-file stand-in) therefore reads the class with the pop
of the same era (`\expandafter\@p@pfilename\@currnamestack\@nil`, locked while the class is read) and restores the
kernel's push and pop after it, so every load balances: the 13 sample papers (1307.3127, 1501.02922, 1510.05346,
1703.06635, 1802.01188, 1407.1937, 1607.08620, 1602.04538, 1401.2223, 1705.02067, 1609.00634, 1511.02959, 1703.03169)
go from 13-39 Errors to 0, word counts unchanged. Packages the class loads get the class's hook label rather than their
own (no hook label is pushed for them, as on the LaTeX of the era). Repro `loader/pasa_era_pushfilename_balanced`
(with a pasa.cls stub); guard `perfect_kernel_batch77c::pasa_era_pushfilename_balances_package_loads`.

### 765. Author-name separators beside a control word, a line break or a mark, and in a mark's math (Perl: " and " between spaces only)

Perl's author splitter knows the word "and" only between two space tokens (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:678), and so did
ours, with the ties and `{\ and}` added. TeX skips the spaces after a control word, so `Ann Able\space and Bob`, jfm's
`Badr~Kaoui$^{3,4}$\break and Jens~Harting`, `Chang Liu \ns and Dennice F. Gayme` (jfm.cls:1025 `\newcommand\ns{\kern
.5em\relax}`), `\linebreak and`, a line ending in `\` (latex.ltx:558 `\def\^^M{\ }`), `\thanks{…}and`, `and\;`,
svmult's `Ann Able\orcidID{…} and\\ Bob Baker` and `Sun$^\ast$\&Fei` hold no space token beside the separator pdflatex
prints between the names; every such pair became one author, flagged `Error:frontmatter:merged_creators` or silently
("Lyubov Sveshnikova andVladimir Ptuskin"). Two other shapes merged too: cimento.cls:1525-1526 (every shipped copy)
`\newcommand{\atque}{{\normalfont\MakeLowercase{and\ \ignorespaces}}}`, whose "and" the separator-macro reader
(`separator_macro_text`) gave up on, and a comma written inside a name's mark math (`Wittor$^{1}, $Brüggen`,
`Iacobuta$,^{5,6,7}$ Mabel`, `Manoj$^{2},$ Chandra`), which the split never sees (it does not look inside math).

`split_author_names` now writes these as the split reads them first (`spaced_name_separators`, base_utilities/author_block/separators.rs, at
the line's top level and again in each wrapper's content the split re-reads): the word "and" between two word
boundaries, or `\&` after one, becomes ` and ` / ` \& `, the spacing beside it dropped: spaces, ties, the spacing
commands of `leading_spacing_end` (`\newline` among its parameterless ones, `PARAMETERLESS_SPACING`), the line breaks
of `SEPARATOR_LINE_BREAKS` (`\\`, `\break`, `\linebreak`, `\allowbreak`, `\^^M`) and parameterless macros whose body is
only spacing (`prints_only_spacing`, a spacing command's braced argument its own: `\hspace{1em}`); a space before
declarations that typeset nothing ahead of the word (`\sc Ann Able \rm and`, the frontmatter `LAYOUT` list) goes too.
A boundary is a space or tie, a control word that is no letter or accent command (`parts_words`: a name of two
characters or more, or of one letter — tex.web §354-356, after which TeX skips the spaces), a note's or mark's argument
(`\thanks{…}`, `NAME_ANNOTATIONS`), a group whose text does not end in a letter or a control symbol, or a math span
holding only a superscript. A control symbol skips no space and prints inside the word: `\-` (a discretionary hyphen)
and `\/` (an italic correction) keep "and" in it (`Rol\-and Smith` is "Roland Smith", `Bertr\/and Smith` "Bertrand
Smith"); a spacing one (`\,`, `\;`, `\ `) is a gap. A letter, a letter command (`\L`, `\ss`, `\dj`, `\th`, `\ng` and
their capitals, T1) or an accent's argument beside the word keeps it in its name ("Rand", "Anders", `Zo\"{e}and`,
`{\O}and`, `\textbf{Bak}and` which prints "Bakand"), and `AT\&T` stays one word. The split's name-count gates — the
whole-line group, a wrapper piece (`names_in_wrapper`) and the per-author bindings' cautious split
(`split_author_line_cautious`: amsart, revtex) — count the names with these separators written
(`separated_name_count`), so `{\bf Ann Able\break and Bob Baker}`, `{\bf Ann Able\thanks{…}and Bob Baker}` and amsart's
`\author{Ann Able\break and Bob Baker}` split as their top-level forms do (1801.10166: `\parbox[t]{\textwidth}{Philip
F.~Hopkins\altaffilmark{1}, \&\ Jonathan Squire\altaffilmark{1}}`, merged with `merged_creators` before). A comma at the edge of a math span holding only a superscript mark
moves outside it (`$^{1}$,`, `,$^{5}$`), where the existing rule gives a mark glued after the comma to the name before
it. `separator_macro_text` reads `\ignorespaces` as printing nothing and applies `\MakeLowercase`/`\MakeUppercase`/
`\lowercase`/`\uppercase` to its group's letters, or to the one token after it when no group follows. SHARED with Perl (it merges every one of these, silently); a reading of
the author's intent, beyond what pdflatex prints: TeX drops the space after a control word, so a pair the author typed
apart can print glued (`The ATLAS\thanks{x}and CMS Collaborations` "ATLAS∗and CMS", `Bob Baker \LaTeX and Cat`
"LATEXand Cat", a macro whose expansion ends in a word before `and`; 2005.00317 `\thanks{…}and`) and is still two
creators here; a group ending in a note (`{Ann Able\thanks{x}}and`) continues the word and is not split. A/B (67int29 vs 77d) over the 78 `merged_creators` papers of
the projection samples: 29 of the 55 sole-cause papers to 0 Errors — the six cimento papers (0711.2584, 0801.3557,
1402.1844, 2109.08173, 2309.14694, hep-th0703055), nineteen S2 papers (1311.3650, 1503.04190, 1505.06278, 2005.00317,
1912.02168, 2509.22118, 1504.03105, 1607.04619, 2004.02831, 2404.12084, 2502.11348, astro-ph9704233, 1707.03934,
2401.17237, 2506.15327, 2509.11693, 2403.07875, 2512.18788, 2603.27055), three S3 papers (1610.00129, 2108.04461,
2402.11182) and 1911.02873, whose `\&` now parts the last name while the first two (`FLORIAN REETZ$^1$ \ns PRIYA
SUBRAMANIAN$^{2,3}$`, apart only by a mark and jfm's `\ns`, which also spaces a name's words: `TOBIAS M.\ns SCHNEIDER`)
stay one creator; the merge check (`flag_merged_creators`) reads a personname's `ltx:sup` as ending the name before it
when its text alone reads as fewer than two names, so that creator keeps its `Error:frontmatter:merged_creators`; `merged_creators` also gone from 1012.2722, 1109.2895,
astro-ph9804111, gr-qc0308071; Errors 239 → 207, 0 papers worse, every split checked against the source. On 239
multi-author control papers from pop67int23 one output changed (2409.19958, svmult `and\\` split, its
`merged_creators` gone). 1012.2722's Error count holds: icrc2009.cls's raw `\IEEEauthorblockN` (`#1\crcr`, :3310-3322), re-applied to
each name the wrapper held, errs once per name ("\noalign cannot be used here"), now three names. Not covered: 1706.05664
(its `$^{1}, $` names reach pasj01's own per-author `\author`, not this split) and the S6 shape of the root-cause (a
class's list `\author`; S4 and S5 are 77n's, below).
Not caught either: a pair still merged with nothing but glued text to show it ("Ann Ableand Bob Baker") — "Ableand
Bob" cannot be told from "Ferdinand Smith" by its text, so the merge check does not try. Repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/{author_and_after_a_control_word, author_and_beside_a_line_break,
author_separator_macro_lowercase, author_comma_in_mark_math, author_and_inside_a_word_stays_the_name,
author_and_after_a_break_in_a_wrapper}`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch77d::*`.

**77n: separators inside a wrapper (S4), note commands among the names (S5).** A wrapper's names split inside it
(`names_in_wrapper`) when what follows the wrapper prints nothing but marks and notes, its spacing and paragraph breaks
aside (`without_spacing`: `\emph{Wenzhuo Ouyang, Atilla Eryilmaz, and Ness B. Shroff} \vspace{-9pt}\par \vspace{-5pt}
\thanks{…}`, 1108.3768), and a piece of marks and notes only, inside the wrapper, is the name's before it
(`notes_to_the_name_before`, which also leaves out a line break at a piece's edge: `{Ann Able},~\IEEEmembership{…},\\
{Cat Cole}`) instead of keeping the wrapper whole (`Chia-Hsun Chuang,\thanks{…} \thanks{…} and Yun Wang` in a parbox,
1205.5573; 2112.09769, 2603.10769, 2209.12464). Each name keeps the wrapper's styling (`\emph`, `\uppercase` — the case
TeX prints —, a group's declarations); a layout box (`LAYOUT_BOXES`: `\parbox[pos]{width}{…}`, `\mbox`, `\makebox`,
`\hbox`) styles no name and is left out, with the paragraph layout its content opens with (`\centering`), its other
opening declarations put around each name (`\parbox{…}{\centering\large A, B}`: both large): spconf's
`\name{{\parbox[c]{\textwidth}{\centering A$^{1}$, B$^{2}$, …}}}` (2504.03146), and a name list already split from
its parbox no longer puts each name in a text-wide box of its own (1801.10166, 1011.3045, 2306.06320). A command over an
optional argument is content, not an opening declaration (`{\parbox[c]…}`), and a control word's optional argument,
glue (`\vskip 0.3in`, `\hskip`, `\kern`), a graphic's file name and a link's address are no name text
(`visible_name_text`; hep-ph0107182, whose REVTeX 3 cautious split read "0.3in" as part of the last name;
`\href{…}{\includegraphics[scale=0.06]{orcid.pdf}\hspace{1mm}Hossein Bahak, Farzaneh Taheri}`, 2312.07592). The word "and" opening or closing a wrapper is a separator of the line
(`hoist_wrapped_separators`: mdpi's `\mbox{and {Thomas~P.} Krichbaum $^{5}$}`, 2108.09054), and a row ending in a
wrapped comma reads as unfinished (`names_list_continues` reads the row with its wrapped separators hoisted:
`\textbf{Seth Ebner}$^{\diamondsuit}$\textrm{,} \\ \textbf{Brandon Smock}, …`, 2512.18601). The note commands of a
name (`is_name_annotation`) are `NAME_ANNOTATIONS` with `\footnotetext` (revtex4-1 2201.11098; amsppt
`D. Logachev\footnotemark \footnotetext{…}`, 2209.04044), elsarticle's `\corref`/`\fnref`/`\tnoteref` (`… and Anil
Bhardwaj \corref{cor1}`, 1201.6291) and `\institute` (ecai.cls 2020:450 `\newcommand{\institute}[1]{\thanks{#1}}`,
2008.02735), and a document's own note macro, one whose every argument goes into a `\thanks` or `\footnote` of its
body (`is_note_macro`: `\blackthanks`, 2506.03876; a macro printing an argument itself is none). An author block's
`\begin{footnote}{text}…\end{footnote}` is read as LaTeX reads it, `\footnote{text}` and the rest
(`note_environments_as_commands`: the comma after the first note parts `Velibor \v{Z}eli` and `Du\v{s}an Zorica`,
1703.02032; the environment's `\begingroup`/`\endgroup` is not kept, as it would open in one name and close in the
next), and its math-active `^`/`_` (catcode 12, mathcode "8000, as mathstyle.sty:233-236, :251-258 sets them from
`\begin{document}`, which breqn loads) are
the superscript and subscript TeX reads (`math_active_scripts`; 2504.02633, and 2404.16541, whose affiliation marks
had left an author with no name). SHARED with Perl for S4 and S5 (SplitTokens passes over groups,
Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:152-165: latexml 0.8.8 keeps each wrapped list one author, and every note command among names
merges them too), except the `{footnote}` environment, which Perl, not keeping an environment whole, splits at its
inner comma with its `\begin` and `\end` in different authors (6 Errors on the repro). Bindings: IEEEtran's grades
become their names' membership contacts inside a wrapper too, a note's argument aside (ieeetran_cls.rs
`name_memberships`); authblk's unlabelled `\author` holding the word "and" is a list (`\lx@add@authors@list`: `Ajay
Chandra$^{1}$\orcidlink{…} and Harprit Singh$^2$\orcidlink{…}`, 2405.16615, preprint.cls + authblk); ecai's `\author`
holding a top-level `\and`, or the current class's `\author[A,D]{…}`, is read as a per-author class's
(`\lx@add@authors@append`), so the 2020 class's `\author{A\institute{…} \and B$^1$}` gives two authors and the current
class's one-name `\author[A,D]{…}` stays one; any other block is one author as written, as Perl adds it (1606.03244's
`\`-parted names with a `\\` line of more names). r2: authblk's comma and `\and` lists are added after the authors
before them (`\lx@add@authors@list`, not the replacing `\lx@add@authors`, as authblk.sty:114-145 always appends:
`\author{Ann Able\thanks{Dept. X, Univ Y}}\affil{…}\author{Bob Baker\thanks{…, …}}`, sent there by the note's comma,
replaced Ann Able, 0 Errors, int31a too — AIAA new-aiaa.cls papers 2610.21324 and 2008.05535 kept 1 of 3 authors;
Perl's `\and` branch replaces the same way, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #992); consecutive unlabelled `\affil`s go to every
author given since the last `\affil` (authblk.sty:115-116's `\AB@thenote`); "others" and "et al." closing a list name
no one (`is_name_qualifier`: `Cat Cole, et al.`), and an "and" opening a wrapper before them stays in it, in its font
(`Ann Able \emph{and others}`, r3). r3 (the r2 review): every unlabelled authblk `\author` showing a superscript mark
outside its notes is a list too (`has_author_marks`; since r4 only when they end what it prints), so its marks request
the affiliations they label on every path (`\author{Ann Able$^{1,2}$}\author{Bob Baker$^{2}$}` had left Bob Baker
without affiliation 2, his mark requesting nothing on `\lx@add@creator`); an unlabelled `\affil` goes to at most the
authors since the last `\affil`
(`annotate=run:N`, `affil_run` in authblk_sty.rs — `run` capped at N — so a mark-picked affiliation, which reaches its
authors only once matched, does not leave them to read as new: `\author{Ann$^1$}\affil{$^1$X}\author{Bob}\affil{$^2$Y}`);
a mark glued to a footnote symbol (`$^{1*}$`, `\textsuperscript{a\dagger}`) is that mark and the symbol shown
(`split_glued_symbol` in `rewrite_symbol_superscripts`), else its one request `affiliation:1*` matched nothing (the
article `\author` the same: the 06_cluster_frontmatter neurips fixture's Wenqi Shao had no affiliation); a superscript
inside a word — a letter on each side, its operand no mark list and the letters after it not the word "and" — is the
name's spelling, shown in place (`rewrite_in_word_superscripts`: `Craig M$^{\mathrm{c}}$Rae`, 2505.09041, which as a
request left the name "Craig MRae"; `I$^2$R`, `NLP$^2$CT`, `DM$^3$L`, which stay words; but `Hiroshi Ito$^{1,3}$and
Tetsuya Ogata`, 2605.00471, and `Bipasha Kundu$^{1}$and Cristian Linte`, 2604.27101, are marks); and the comma
ending a marked affiliation's line is its own when the next line continues it ("Université Laval,\\ pavillon …",
1507.08653; `trim_trailing_separator` trims it only before the next marked institution). r4 (the r3 review): an
`\affil` expanding with no author queued (inside `\author{Ann \affil{Univ X}}`, read at the flush; after `\maketitle`)
runs uncapped (`annotate=run`), and the engine reads a cap below 1 as none and records no run that reached no one
(2605.01689's DSSL block had gone to no one, `annotate=run:0`); an `\affil` whose mark combines labels
(`\affil{$^{1,2}$Univ X}`) keeps authblk's run, the marked path labelling by the first label only; and a single authblk
name is a list only when its marks end what it prints, notes, spacing and an `\affil` aside (`author_marks_end_name`:

### 766. A paragraph break inside an inline-only frontmatter item is a line break (Perl: the paragraphs run together)

A frontmatter item is digested in text mode (Perl `digestFrontmatterItem` → `DigestText`), where `\par` closes no
paragraph, so an item whose element holds only inline content — `Inline.model`: no `ltx:p`, but `ltx:break` —
ran its paragraphs together into one text: apa.cls's `\acknowledgements{We thank …\n\nCorrespondence to …}` (#763)
read "…agency. Correspondence…". By user ruling (2026-10-18) such a paragraph break is a line break of the item.

Mechanism: the item's text is digested in a mode frame of its own (`digest_frontmatter_item`; the body of a keywords or
classification environment, `\lx@add@frontmatter@until`, in the frame it began in), and the field and that frame's depth
(the number of frames binding `MODE`) are noted there (`note_frontmatter_paragraphs`). A `\par` digested at that depth
records the field on its whatsit (tex_paragraph.rs `\lx@normal@par`, `frontmatter_paragraph_field`); a box, an
alignment cell or math inside the item begins a deeper frame, where the `\par` is the ordinary one — in a box or a `c`
cell it ends nothing, as in TeX (tex.web §1096 `end_graf`: `\date{\begin{tabular}{c}D1\par D2\end{tabular}}` "D1D2") —
while a group (`{\bfseries …}`) begins none. At construction, where the schema is loaded (Perl too reads the model only
when it builds the document; WISDOM #100), the `\par`'s constructor (base_utilities/frontmatter/queue.rs `frontmatter_paragraph_break`)
walks up from the insertion point to that field's element; when the element is inline-only and no element on the way
holds paragraphs of its own (a minipage, a note), it inserts a marked `ltx:break` when the item's content so far ends
in other content — not before its first content, not after another such break (a run of `\par`s, in a group too) —
and closes nothing. When the item element closes, the marked breaks left at its end are dropped
(`drop_trailing_paragraph_breaks`). Otherwise the `\par` is the ordinary one: an `ltx:abstract` (`Block.model`) keeps its
`<p>`s, an `ltx:note` its one run of text, a box absorbed outside its item (a reused title) is untouched. No token of the
item is changed.

Where it shows: `ltx:acknowledgements`, `ltx:keywords`, `ltx:classification`, `ltx:pubnote`, `ltx:contact`, `ltx:date`
and `ltx:title`. In the standard classes `\title` and `\date` are not `\long` — pdflatex stops with "Paragraph ended
before \date was complete" — so those two are reached through `\long` setters (apa's), bindings, or an `\endgraf`. An
author's name is digested in a frame of its own inside its `ltx:creator` item, so a `\par` in it ends nothing, as before.
A macro whose string body is a single space tokenizes as an empty line, `\par` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #984): amsppt's
`\usualspace`, biblatex's `\bibnamedelimi` and axessibility's `\auxiliaryspace` (the Perl/ar5iv bodies), and the
Rust-only bindings' `\And`/`\AND`/`\Ands` (colm2025_conference, jmlr, jmlr2e) are explicit space tokens now (colm's
`\Ands` had made "Carol <break/>Dan"; `X\bibnamedelimi Y` had split a paragraph). Repros `sectioning-frontmatter/inline_item_paragraphs_are_line_breaks`,
`sectioning-frontmatter/class_notes/apa_acknowledgements_paragraphs_are_lines`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch77f::{inline_item_paragraphs_are_line_breaks, apa_acknowledgements_paragraphs_are_lines,
single_space_macros_are_spaces}`. **Why**:
the author's line structure is content; merging two paragraphs into one sentence run misreports it.

### 767. A raw class's title-page stores are judged by a speculative run of its title page; an off-table store no kept run typesets is handed on (Perl: dropped)

Silent-loss #5 (a), the generic rule for the stores K11's table (`STORE_SETTERS`) does not name (75a row (a);
agent_reports/2026-10-18_k11_offtable_reach.md), and the 77h/77i follow-ups on what the title page prints. **Perl** drops
a raw class's title page whole (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1105 `\global\let\@maketitle\relax`, its refused
`\maketitle`, State.pm:502-517), and with it every value only that page prints.

**Which stores.** At the raw class's end (frontmatter_stores.rs `survey_off_table_stores`) every one-argument command
the class defined without an `@` in its name, outside the table and the kernel's setters, whose body is a pure store of
its argument (`setter_stores`) into one control sequence of the class's that only its title-page code reads — rule (a)'s
reader scan with the class's own `\@title`/`\@author`/`\@date` counted as title-page code, LaTeX's `\@maketitle`
printing them (`ClassReaders::read_only_by_the_title_page_or_fields`) — is recorded with its class default
(`lx_offtable_stores`; Info names them) and the label its title page prints before it (`ClassReaders::label_in`, below).

**TeX decides what the title page prints** (`before_title_page_runs`, called at the head of `\lx@deposit@maketitle`,
sect05.rs, in the state the deposit and the replay meet). Each candidate store is given a unique sentinel value and
title-page code is digested speculatively (sect05.rs `speculative_title_page_run`: output discarded, every assignment
undone by the assignment journal, diagnostics discarded, terminal output muted under a guard that also ends on a panic
(`SuppressLogOutputGuard`, reset in `reset_thread_engine`), groups left open closed in a reading context of their own;
frontmatter frozen and no setter replayed while it runs). Each run is made twice, the stores given letters sentinels
(`LxSentinel<a-p>zZ`, mixed case, matched lower-cased) and then digits ones (`9090<1-8>0909`, `sentinel`; the second run only when the first printed a
sentinel, `sentinel_runs`): a store is printed by it when both its sentinels reach the digested text
(`sentinels_printed`) — a numeric context consumes the digits while TeX's "Missing number" recovery typesets the letters
(`\setcounter{page}{\@fp}`, gammas.cls:305, kluwer.cls:1049; review probe `num`, where one sentinel invented
`<pubnote>17</pubnote>`). A store run (1) finds printed whose value is plain text (characters and spaces) is confirmed
by one more run with the document's own values (`confirmed_printed`): its letters and digits must be in that run's
text, in their case unless the sentinel run printed the mixed-case sentinel in another (`\MakeUppercase`,
`\MakeLowercase`) — `\ifx\@vc\@open OPEN\else\@vc\fi` with "open" prints the class's word, not the value (review probe
`ctx2`, which invented `<pubnote>open</pubnote>`). Letters and digits only (`alphanumerics`), on both sides: TeX typesets
`'`, ``` `` ``` and `''` as ’ “ ”, `--` as a dash, and 77i r4's comparison of the source characters lost "Women’s
Workshop" and "“Quoted” words" (review probes `q3`, `q4`; 0 errors). The
digested text is `ink_text` (base_utilities/util_text.rs): box characters, never a whatsit's reversion, and only the arguments a
whatsit shows (`shown_arguments`, by declared parameter type: none of an image; a verbatim argument only when the
whatsit's constructor prints it, the arguments `VERBATIM_PRINTERS` names for it (`(name, shown mask)`: llncs's `\url`,
`\nolinkurl`, aas's `\@@email`, `\lx@doi`, `\harvardurl`, each its one argument; a two-verbatim `\href` would name
its second); a constructor's replacement is compiled, so what it puts in its element cannot be read off the whatsit —, never a reference's or citation's key, `\ref{\@vb}` printing "1" (review probe `ctx3`, which
invented `<pubnote>sec:intro</pubnote>`); url.sty's and hyperref's `\url` keep their text in an argument of their own;
`\href{<url>}{Home}` prints "Home"; never keyvals; review probe `logo`'s `\includegraphics{\@logo}` and
`\href{\@url}{Home}`). The print run typesets footnotes and `\thanks` (`\@firstofone`: a store the title page prints in
one is printed, review probes `fn`, `fnt`); it gobbles `\label`, `\index`. A Fatal of a speculative run that is not a
resource Fatal of the conversion (deadline, memory budget, token budget, conditional ids) and whose run was undone is
the run's alone — a runaway limit of the run's own expansion (the pushback, a recursion) too, the latch unset
(`unlatch_runaway_fatal`) and the box lists and conditionals the run left open unwound (user ruling 2026-10-19:
VisionStyle.cls's `\MakeUppercase` of a title holding its non-robust `\small` loops in pdflatex too, astro-ph0203021;
guard `perfect_kernel_batch77r::speculative_title_run_runaway_is_discarded`) — a sentinel value
may cause it —: it is discarded with the run's diagnostics (an Info says so) and run (1) printed nothing
(`SpeculativeRun::Aborted`, which `decide_unset_nulls` counts as no "fewer characters": `\relax` stays); an aborted
deposit or replay run, (2) or (3), is no run (`sentinel_runs`): the walk decides, since a Fatal the sentinel value alone
caused does not stop the real deposit printing the store. Three
runs: (1) the class's whole title page with the document's values (`title_page_print_tokens`: its refused `\maketitle`
when replayable, else LaTeX's, which runs the class's or a binding's `\@maketitle`, else article.cls:209-229's printing
of the fields; a call of the kernel's `\maketitle` from the class's, `\let\@origmaketitle\maketitle`, runs LaTeX's
`\@maketitle` there), with the off-table stores the document set and the rerouted stores handed to the frontmatter as
candidates (`lx_sentinel_printed`); (2) and (3) the deposit and the replay exactly as they then run
(`title_page_deposit_tokens`, `title_page_replay_tokens`, shared with `\lx@deposit@maketitle`), the off-table candidates
given sentinels (`lx_sentinel_deposit`, `lx_sentinel_replay`). A class's own booleans (sigplanconf.cls:87-90
`\def\@true{TT}`/`\def\@false{FL}`, :1118 `\if \@copyrightwanted …`), `\newif` switches (aiaa-tc.cls:199-200
`[handcarry]`), `\@ifundefined`/`\ifx…\@empty` tests, and what it only boxes or puts in a running head (`\setbox`,
`\markboth`: degruyter-journal-a.cls:574-586, 620, 1704.03582; acmlarge.cls:1021, 1508.03599) are then what they are in
pdflatex. A run that errors still gives its text (TeX's recovery typesets on; an internal our emulation of the class
lacks becomes an `<ltx:ERROR>` holding its name). Without a run (a journal already open, or a run whose assignments
could not be undone, `SpeculativeRun::Unavailable`; an Info says so, for sweeps to count) the stores' readers are walked
instead (`walked_title_page_reads`: the live code, `\newif`/kvoptions switches and `\if`/`\ifx` on parameterless macros
of characters evaluated, `evaluated_switch`; only the code that runs, `executed_code`).

**Labels.** The label a title page prints before a store is read off the class's code (`ClassReaders::label_in`,
`line_label_before`: label material and layout from the line's start — the macro's start, a `\par`, a `\\`, an
environment's `\begin{…}`/`\end{…}`, another value, the open brace of the store's group — up to the store; the phrase
right before the store, a sentence before it in the line staying where it is: `\footnote{Funded. KW: \@keywords}` names
the keywords "KW:" and the footnote keeps "Funded.", review probe `fnm`), and is the entry's name only when TeX's output
says so: at `\maketitle`, before the stores are handed on (`\lx@store@defaults`), one more speculative run of the whole
title page with the labelled stores given letters sentinels must print the label's text right before the store's
sentinel (`verify_title_page_labels`, `printed_right_before`, letters and digits compared: the class's `Author's
keywords:` is typeset "Author’s keywords:", review probe `ap`; once per document). `\href{mailto:\@vg}{\@vg}` read
"mailto:" off the URL argument (review probe `ctx3`; modernposter.cls, skdoc.cls have the shape), which the page does not
print. A rejected label stays in the title page and the entry is unnamed; without a run, a label in a group that is a
control sequence's argument (not a font command's) is rejected.

**What is handed on** (`hand_untypeset_stores`, at `\lx@store@untypeset` after the deposit and the replay): each
off-table store the document set (no longer the class default, not blank; once per store, sigplanconf.cls:939-942's
`\copyrightDOI` and its `\let` `\copyrightdoi`) that run (1) printed and no kept run typeset (run (2) or (3) for a kept
deposit or replay, `lx_title_page_{deposit,replay}_kept`), in the order the title page prints them, with no visible label
of ours — the meta XSLT shows a note's `@role` as a visible label (LaTeXML-meta-xhtml.xsl:79-85), which 77i r1's
`note[role=<setter>]` made "titre:", "auteurs:", "copyrightDOI:" — as: the document's `ltx:title` when the class's own
refused `\title` hands its argument to the store's setter and the document has no title (`class_field_setter`:
jfpc.cls:122 `\renewcommand{\title}[1]{\titre{#1}}`, its `\@title` :176-186 printing `\@letitre`); the document's authors
(`\lx@add@authors@adaptive`) when there is no creator and the store holds the names the class's own `\@author` prints —
the one its refused `\author` hands its argument to (:126 → `\auteurs`), else the first store its `\@author` reads
(`lx_offtable_author_reads`); a store the class's `\@author` prints beside the names (jfpc.cls:188-191
`\@lesinstitutions`, `\@lesmels`) rows of the creators' author block (`\lx@add@store@authorblock`, `role=authorblock`,
as an `\author` call's tail is, its label as printed before it) — the creators' data, attached to them as any
affiliation is, where 77i r2's `pubnote` made them a note on the document (under the default `ltx_authors_1line` layout
both are hover popups, LaTeXML.css:74-88 and :107-120: the gain is what the rows are, not where they show); a store
that only repeats the creators' names — the class prints no label before it, every word of each of its lines (split at
`\and`, `\\`, `\newline`, `\par`) is a word of a creator's name, and every creator's words are among its words — is a
duplicate, not handed on (`repeats_creator_names`; "Corresponding author: \@corr" with one author's name is a role, kept:
review probe `corr`); any other store an `ltx:pubnote` (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:634, a note about the document),
its `\and` between authors' blocks a line break, named by the label the title page prints before it with the space
printed before the store kept as a tie (jfpc's `\@lannee`: `name="Actes JFPC~"`, "Actes JFPC 2015", :177, as
acmart_cls.rs:178's `name={Price:~}`). 1503.05530 had lost its title, authors, institutions and e-mail. The same run (1) settles #6b (`settle_placed_stores`, `\lx@store@hand`): a handed store's
setter called again after `\maketitle` only re-sets the store when run (1) printed the store (OD #154 addendum).

**The deposit's unset stores** (77h/23b; `decide_unset_nulls`, `\lx@captured@stores`): a rerouted store the paper never
set, still undefined, is defined in the deposit and the replay — undefined, it raised an error that dropped the whole
deposit (an.cls:532 `\ch@ckobl{institute}{…}` runs in the class's own `\maketitle`; the "Key words" line lost, 23b) — as
`\relax` or `\@empty`: a "prints fewer characters" rule over the text TeX typesets for each candidate, from speculative
runs of the deposit and the replay (all `\relax`, all `\@empty`, then each store alone `\@empty`; a tie keeps
`\relax`): `\relax` where a class tests
`\@ifundefined{@pubinfo}`/`{@recdate}` (ptptex.cls:88-104; hep-th9803240, 1309.6905, 0911.1235, 0708.3877, 0801.2466,
1009.4028, 1007.1507, cond-mat0411234; jpsj 0903.1491, 0912.1097, 1101.2977, 1203.5392), `\@empty` where it tests
`\ifx\@institute\@empty` after its own `\maketitle` defaulted the store so (no orphan "Institute:").

**Duplicates and furniture.** A store a kept run typesets is not handed on (CONTROL
`offtable_store_typeset_by_the_deposit_stays_there`); one printed only under a switch that is off, or only in a box or a
running head, is not printed and not handed on (the page-furniture ruling); page-furniture and metadata stores read by
code outside the title page are not recorded (nature_djm `\pubdate`, cedram `\CDRorcid`). nowfnt.cls:798-804's
`\maintitleauthorlist` ("AUTHORS FOR COVER PAGE", 2308.02698 main.tex:44) is the cover's author block printed beside
the abstract page's `\author[n]{Surname, First}`/`\affil` lines (main-session decision under the page-furniture ruling:
print flourish dropped, semantic notes kept, no content lost): in 2308.02698 it holds the names alone, a repeat of the
creators, dropped (`repeats_creator_names` — by words, as nowfnt's `\author[1]{Sung, Yoonchang}` gives two creators,
SYNC_STATUS row "nowfnt creators"); in 2108.12618 it carries the affiliations and e-mails, which reach the document
nowhere else (nowfnt's `\affil` is not captured), and stays a pubnote, its `\and` line breaks between the authors (77i
r2 ran "…mkokotov@gmail.com Matan Gavish"). **Cost:** the speculative runs digest title-page code at most 8 + 2 + N
more times per raw-class `\maketitle` (the print, deposit and replay runs, each with letters and digits sentinels; the
label run when a store is labelled and the confirming run when a store found printed has a plain value; N = unset
rerouted stores, `decide_unset_nulls`'s all-`\relax` and all-`\@empty` runs then one per store; measured +0.03–0.29%
`instructions:u` in 77i r3 — 1309.6905 +0.03%, 1503.05530 +0.07%, 1603.03011 +0.29%, the r3 review's run of 1603.03011
+0.23%, 10.0017e9 → 10.0251e9 — and, over r3, +0.06% (1503.05530), +0.23% (1603.03011), +0.98% (1309.6905: its labelled keywords add the label and
confirming runs) in 77i r4). **Residuals:** what the assignment journal does not undo — the raw-read paths list
(`RAW_READ_PATHS`, content.rs:2166) and the pending field-provenance cover (`FIELD_COVER_PENDING`, token.rs:884) —, unlikely to
be reached by title-page code; a run whose assignments could not be undone (its groups changed) keeps the global
assignments it made with sentinel values (a class's `\xdef\@x{\@store}` would carry "LxSentinel…zZ" into the document),
and the walk then decides; a test of the value takes its branch with the sentinel's value, not the document's —
`\ifnum\@x<100 No.~\@x\fi` with 7 takes the other branch with the digits and `\romannumeral\@va` prints neither sentinel
(pdflatex prints "No. 7" and "iii"; the store counts as not printed and is not handed on: review probes `ctx2`, `ctx`) —
the confirming run checks only what the sentinel runs found printed, so it does not recover these, and a plain value
whose letters TeX prints as other characters (a font's ligature glyph) would fail it; a label with an accent
(`R\'esum\'e :`, `\textbf{Mots-cl\'es :}`) is not read off the code (`label_item`), and a heading-style label before an
abstract the kernel's `\abstract` owns (`\begin{center}{\bf Abstract}\end{center}`, `{\bf Abstract.}`) is not this
mechanism's: both stay orphan paragraphs, as on base (SYNC_STATUS "Silent-loss inventory" #6a residual); a constructor
outside `VERBATIM_PRINTERS` that prints a verbatim argument (a binding's two-verbatim `\href`, jhep_cls.rs) does not
count it printed; a store the class prints only behind a label macro it defines at `\maketitle`
(bullsrsl.cls:747-765 `\BSRSL@CorrespIntro` "Correspondence to:", 2401.09121, 2410.19120) is a pubnote without that
label, a hover-only popup (SYNC_STATUS row "bullsrsl correspondence"). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch77i::{offtable_stores_read_by_class_author_are_the_creators,
offtable_store_typeset_by_the_deposit_stays_there, offtable_store_the_class_title_hands_on_is_the_title,
offtable_store_the_title_page_does_not_print_is_not_handed_on, unset_store_reads_as_the_title_page_tests_it,
store_read_as_a_number_is_not_printed, store_in_an_image_path_or_link_target_is_not_printed,
cover_author_list_is_dropped_only_when_it_repeats_the_names, store_label_is_printed_text_not_a_link_target_or_key,
store_label_is_the_phrase_printed_before_it, labelled_role_store_naming_one_author_is_a_note,
store_tested_against_a_word_is_not_printed, store_values_typeset_with_quotes_are_printed,
store_label_with_an_apostrophe_names_the_entry}`, `perfect_kernel_batch77h::an_without_institute_keeps_the_title_block`,
`latexml_core` `suppress_log_output_guard_restores_on_drop_and_unwind`.

### 768. A tcolorbox listing environment's box title is the listing's title (Perl: raw tcblistings, the box not read back)

tcolorbox prints a listing box's `title=` in the box's title bar (tcolorbox.sty:162-163 `\tcbtitle`, :214
`title/.store in=\kvtcb@title`); `\newtcblisting`/`\NewTCBListing` environments and `\newtcbinputlisting` commands are
boxes around `\tcblisting{…,options@for=name}` / `\tcbinputlisting{…}` (tcblistingscore.code.tex:301-378). **Perl**
raw-loads them (tcolorbox.sty.ltxml:27). **Rust** delegates them to listings (OD #410), which typeset the listing
without the box and had dropped every box option but the counter, the mode and the listing file — the "Example N: …"
or "Listing N: …" of each box was lost with no diagnostic (silent-loss row #16).

Now the box options are set in a group as the box sets them (`tcolorbox_sty::tcb_resolve_listing_mode`, for the
environments and for `\newtcbinputlisting`; inside another box, where tcolorbox's `every box on layer N` is `reset`, the
enclosing box's title is cleared first), the resolved `\kvtcb@title` is parked (`tcb_pending_title`) and the listing
takes it as its listings `title=` when it has none (`listings_sty::lst_process_display_with` → `\lstlisting@maketitle`):
an unnumbered `ltx:float class="ltx_lstlisting"` whose `ltx:caption` (and `ltx:toccaption`) is the title, always above
the code — the box's title bar is above whatever listings' `captionpos` says (the box gobbles `\lst@MakeCaption`, so
`captionpos` never reaches it; 2409.11413 setup.tex:86 and 2402.13846 headers/lqa/listing.tex:35 set `captionpos=b`). Not in the list of
listings (tcolorbox reads the body back `nolol`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #988). The box's `listing remove caption`
(tcblistings.code.tex:69-72, on by default through `reset@listings`, :88-93) is honoured the same way: it gobbles
`\lst@MakeCaption`, so listings' own caption, title and list entry are not made — the box title is the only one
(2409.11413's `\lstset{title=\lstname}` had emptied all 13 "Listing N: …" titles; a raw box's read-back runs with
`\lst@MakeCaption` = `\@gobble`, which `lst_process_display_with` reads as such). The box frame and colours are not
drawn; a box with `detach title` (title not in the bar) keeps none. `\newtcbinputlisting`'s `[init]` options go through
tcolorbox's own init processor under the command's name (`\tcb@proc@options@init`, tcblistingscore.code.tex:374-377), so
`use counter=` gives each use `\thetcbcounter`, and a box without a counter has an empty `\thetcbcounter`
(tcolorbox.sty:2335-2337 `\tcb@proc@counter@no`, key `no counter` :2258; 2605.21082's `title={\textbf{code~\thetcbcounter}: #2}` prints "code : …",
`tcolorbox_sty::tcb_counter_step_code`). `\newtcbinputlisting` also carries the box's phantom code (a per-use `label=` /
`hypertarget=`, at the listing's first line as for the environments) and follows the box's mode as `\tcbinputlisting`
does (tcblistingscore.code.tex:195-220, `tcb_pending_layout`): `listing and text` (the default) typesets the file again
after the listing, `text and listing` before it, `text only` alone, `listing only` not. An absent begin-line argument
stands in the options as xparse passes it: an `O{}` its empty default (an empty `\def` splices to nothing;
neoschool.cls:5168-5214 `\ifx\relax#3\relax` had titled all 40 `{code}` boxes, and its unspliced stand-ins raised 44 of
its 141 pgfkeys errors), a LEADING `O{default}`/`D[]{default}` its default and a leading `o`/`d[]` xparse's no-value
marker (the `\lstnewenvironment` arity's default is the slot's stand-in, `tcb_xparse_listing`; its empty default had
made `\IfNoValueTF{#1}{Code}{Code: #1}` "Code: " and `O{Default}` empty). The raw `{tcblisting}` environment is
unchanged: it draws the box (a picture), title included.

Residuals: `blend into=listings` (its `before title` "Listing N: " prefix), `before title=` and `attach title to upper`
are not captured; `adjusted title`'s `\vphantom` renders as a hidden span with width; a `text only` listing
environment still shows its code (the delegation always displays it; `\newtcbinputlisting` honours the mode); a
`text only` input listing has no listing to carry its title (a paragraph before the text) or its label (dropped); the `comment` modes' comment
is not typeset; `captionpos=tb` keeps Perl's `eq 't'` reading for a listings title (bottom only). A box `label=`'s
`\ref` prints the enclosing section's number, not the box's counter (Perl identical; SYNC silent-loss row "tcolorbox
box label").

Witnesses 2405.01480, 2405.02221, 2405.02462, 2405.03285, incgraph-doc (and the same template shipped unused by the
main file in 1912.06298, 2105.06630, 2301.07825, 2302.14514, 2410.04867) (`\newtcblisting[use
counter=example]{example}[2][]{title={Example~\thetcbcounter: #2},#1}` and its `\examplefile`, in the shipped
docsiamonline/docsiamart template), 2405.01576, 2409.11413, 2508.16690, 2605.21082, neoschool. Repros
`listings-algorithms/{newtcblisting_keeps_its_counted_title, new_tcb_listing_keeps_its_title,
newtcbinputlisting_keeps_its_title, new_tcb_listing_empty_optional_is_empty,
newtcblisting_without_a_counter_has_an_empty_counter, tcb_box_title_replaces_the_listings_title,
tcb_box_title_stays_above_under_captionpos_b, new_tcb_listing_leading_o_absent_is_no_value,
new_tcb_listing_leading_optional_keeps_its_default, newtcbinputlisting_keeps_its_label,
newtcbinputlisting_follows_its_mode}`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch77m::*` (same names). **Why**: the title is
authored content (often the listing's number and name, the target of the text's references); the switch to
tcolorbox's own definitions (the raw `{tcblisting}` path) was measured and not taken in this batch — it loses a box
`label`'s target (raw tcolorbox puts it on the nearest labelled ancestor, a section or `<document>`) and the
`\NewTCBListing` begin-line reading (`perfect_kernel_batch59::{tcb_listing_label_names_its_listing,
tcb_listing_keeps_its_hypertarget, tcb_listing_begin_line_edge_cases}`, `perfect_kernel_batch40_43::newtcblisting_xparse_leading_optional`).

### 769. A caption is a paragraph of a vertical box, read as its macro argument (Perl: `PBoxContents` read live; the trailing `\label` last)

A float caption is set as a paragraph in a vertical box: latex.ltx's `\@makecaption` sets `#1: #2\par` in a `\vbox`
when it does not fit one line, amsart.cls:1386-1392 always (`\vbox{\noindent…}`), so `$$…$$` in a caption is display
math. **Perl** builds `\@@caption` and `\@@toccaption` from `PBoxContents` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3368-3371;
TeX_Box.pool.ltxml:200-213: `readBoxContents` in `internal_vertical` with `\lx@enterhorizontal` in front). **Rust** had
`\lx@@caption{}` / `\@@toccaption{}` with `mode => "text"` — restricted horizontal, where `$$` is an empty formula
(tex.web §1138) and the formula's `_` text: "Script _ can only appear in math mode" ×2 per caption, the display lost
(1005.1555, 1907.01498, 2310.11556, 1404.2359). Now both take the ported `PBoxContents` (tex_box.rs, with
`\lx@enterhorizontal`), so the display is an `ltx:equation` in an `ltx:inline-block` of the caption, the text after it
an `ltx:p` there; Perl's output puts the `ltx:equation` straight in the caption and its list copy (`<ltx:equation>
isn't allowed in <ltx:caption>` and `… in <ltx:toccaption>`, 4 Errors on the repro).

Departures from Perl's reading, each for a caption the engine set as text before: (1) the material is the braced
argument, digested from a mouth of its own (as `HBoxArgContents` digests an unbraced one), not read live up to the
box's own `}`: the caption is always a macro's argument (`\@caption@@@`, `\lx@format@caption@@`), tokenized before
`\lx@@caption` reads it, and a formula it leaves open ends with it — an author's `$` in a math `\qty` unit (2512.12866:
`$t \approx \qty{29000}{fm/$c$}$`) made the live reader take the caption's `}` as the formula's and read on through the
float and the document (10 → 17 Errors). (2) The box's mode is `inline_internal_vertical`, which ends no paragraph
around it with a `\par`, and `\lx@enterhorizontal` fires no `\everypar` (`stomach::enter_horizontal_without_everypar`,
as Perl's `enterHorizontal`, Stomach.pm:422-433): in an aas `\references`, whose `\par` opens an entry and whose
`\everypar` would too, a caption in a float made phantom entries ("<ltx:bibitem> isn't allowed in <ltx:table>";
LaTeX's floats reset `\everypar`, latex.ltx `\@floatboxreset`). (3) A `\label` after `\caption` goes in front of the
caption's material as `\lx@caption@postlabel` (`\@caption@postlabel`), where Perl appends a `\label`
(latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3175): the paragraph ends with a final display's `ltx:equation` open, which the label took
(2310.11556, 1404.2359 lost the figure's label), while LaTeX's `\label` names what `\caption`'s `\refstepcounter`
stepped (latex.ltx:17391-17393), the float; under its own name the scan for the caption's own labels does not take the
caption's text as its argument (a stray `\fi` there closed the scan's `\ifx`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #641), and the toc copy
drops it. A `\label` the author writes inside the caption right after a display is the residual Perl shares: LaTeX's
`$$…$$` steps no counter, so `\@currentlabel` is still the float's and the reference reads its number (as ours does),
but the label lands on the unnumbered `ltx:equation` it follows (`floatToLabel`, the nearest labelled element still
open), so the link targets the display, not the float — Perl the same, in a caption as in running text (review probe
cap2 `fig:inner`; moving it is a change to `\lx@label`'s target rule, not this caption's).
(4) `\@@add@caption@counters` reads the list extension (`\ext@<type>`) by expansion, as it reads `\@captype`: digested,
its letters began a paragraph in the float's vertical list whose horizontal mode outlived the counters (every float
body after its caption was in horizontal mode).

The caption's size is now Perl's: a paragraph of the current `\hsize` (`repack_paragraph`'s `width`, Perl #2798), where
it was the natural width of one line or the leaked paragraph around it. Floats sized from it change: panels side by
side whose caption widened them past the line no longer break the row (2107.02579's 0.3\textwidth subfigures), a
caption in a minipage no longer opens the paragraph the capture pruned (`ltx_pruned_first` gone), and rotated floats
take the caption's paragraph height (graphrot.xml's `sidewaystable`, `perfect_kernel_batch65a`'s transforms).
Residual: a tabularray `talltblr` caption is set at the float's `\hsize` (tabularray_sty.rs `\lx@tblr@caption`) where
tabularray sets it at the table's width (tabularray.sty:6444-6452, :6481-6492), so a talltblr beside another table in
one float is now a row of its own (`perfect_kernel_batch57::tabularray_tall_table_in_a_{captionless,captioned}_float`;
pdflatex: side by side). Giving `{lx@tblr@box}` the table's width as its size (`cached_width` in its `after_digest`) does
not reach `arrange_panels`, which sizes the panel from the box node's own content; reach ~0 (3 of 6,000 projection
papers use talltblr/longtblr, none side by side, all byte-identical).
Repro `captions-floats/caption_display_math_is_display_1005.1555`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch77k::{caption_display_math_is_display, caption_without_display_is_one_text_run}`.

### 770. A revtex `\preprint` number the class does not print is metadata (Perl: always a pubnote)

`\preprint` stores the number for the title page, which prints it or not by the class family's own rule. **Perl** makes
every call a displayed pubnote (revtex4_support.sty.ltxml:71 `\lx@add@pubnote[role=preprint]{#1}`). **Rust** follows the
class (user rulings 2026-10-06 display toggles, 2026-10-09 unprinted metadata → RDFa), choosing the branch before it
reads the argument (revtex4_support_sty.rs `\preprint`, `preprint_printed`):
- REVTeX 4.1/4.2: the title page prints the store (aps4-1.rtx:216-221 `\ps@titlepage`, aip/aapm/sor alike) under
  `\preprint@sw` — `preprintnumbers`/`nopreprintnumbers`, an unset switch following the `preprint` style (`preprint`,
  `manuscript`, `checkin`; revtex4-2.cls:5927-5930, revtex4-1.cls alike) — and `\frontmatter@init`, a document hook
  (revtex4-1.cls:2094, :2517-2519), empties it, so a preamble `\preprint` is not printed.
- REVTeX 4.0 (revtex4.cls; `revtex@preprint@v4.0`, set by revtex4_cls.rs, which also serves revtex4-2): the store is
  emptied once at load (:4618-4619), so a preamble call is printed too, and the `preprint` style forces `\preprint@sw`
  on after the options (class init hook, :3811-3812), so `nopreprintnumbers` does not hide it there.
- REVTeX 3/3.1 (revtex3_support_sty.rs, also under aipproc): aps.sty:965-968 defines `\@preprint` only under
  `\ifpreprintsty` and `\@maketitle` prints it (:1006-1010), with no reset — printed in the preprint style wherever it
  is called (305 of 8,247 REVTeX 3 papers of 9601-0001 are preprint style with a `\preprint`), decided in TeX by
  `\ifpreprintsty`.
A printed number is Perl's pubnote, its argument read as TeX reads it (`Fe$_{2}$YZ`, `DESY~11--210` as on the page;
a text `_` errs as in pdflatex). An unprinted one is an `ltx:rdf property="dcterms:identifier"` per `\\`-separated number
at the argument's top level (a `\\` in a group or an environment — a `\parbox`, FERMILAB's `{minipage}` with
`{flushright}` — is the block's own), read as an identifier (Semiverbatim, in the identity encoding), KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
#990. The class options are recorded by revtex4_cls.rs and revtex4_1_cls.rs (`revtex@preprintsty`,
`revtex@preprintnumbers`), REVTeX 3's by revtex3_support (`\global\preprintstytrue`). Witnesses 2408.13616,
1912.04576, 2110.00437 (unprinted, 4.1), 1207.6705 (unprinted, 4.0), 1205.1463 (a preamble `\preprint` dropped, two
printed); repros `sectioning-frontmatter/revtex_preprint_number_is_an_identifier_2408.13616`,
`…/revtex3_preprint_style_prints_the_number`, `…/revtex_printed_preprint_is_read_as_tex`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch77k::{revtex_preprint_number_is_an_identifier, revtex_printed_preprint_is_read_as_tex,
revtex_unprinted_preprint_splits_only_top_level_lines, revtex3_preprint_style_prints_the_number,
revtex40_preprint_numbers_follow_the_class}`.

### 771. A blkarray block's preamble formats its rows; its delimiters are dropped (Perl: no blkarray binding)

blkarray.sty:868-922 `\BA@beginblock` is a `\noalign` that parses the block's preamble; its rows use the block's columns
(`\BA@col@use`, :838-839, keyed by the block) until `\BA@endblock` restores the blockarray's. The binding
(blkarray_sty.rs; Perl has none, the raw package hangs both engines) had gobbled the block preamble, so
`\begin{block}{*{2}{>{$\footnotesize}c<{$}}}` lost its `$` wrappers and the cells' own `$x_{1}$` were text in the
display (1706.05431, 2207.06508, 2210.16910). Now `\begin{block}{spec}` is a hidden `\noalign` (no row of its own) that
parses the spec with blkarray's `>{}`/`<{}` column types, local to it, and puts the block's columns in place of the
alignment template's for the rows that follow; `\end{block}` puts the saved template back (a stack,
`lx@blkarray@preambles`). The delimiters `(` `)` `[` `]` `\{` `\}` `\Left` `\Right` (:1998-2003) are read as no column
and dropped: they draw a bracket beside the block's sub-region, which the `array` alignment cannot express (the
binding's documented simplification). The text arguments of `\Left{label}{delim}` and `\Right{delim}{label}` — the
block's side labels, which pdflatex prints beside the bracket — are dropped with them (base and the earlier binding
dropped them too; review probe b3 "M", "N"; SYNC_STATUS row "blkarray side labels"). Repro
`alignment-bindings/blkarray_block_preamble_formats_its_rows_1706.05431` (control
`blkarray_block_cells_in_text_control`); guards `perfect_kernel_batch77k::{blkarray_block_preamble_formats_its_rows,
blkarray_block_text_cell_in_display_errs}`.

### 772. The AISTATS styles' title-block setters are the frontmatter, one binding for every year (Perl: no binding)

Every AISTATS template — aistats2e.sty (2010-2011), its margin variant aistats2eM.sty, aistats2012.sty, aistats2014.sty
… aistats2027.sty — prints its title block in place inside the document's `\twocolumn[…]`: `\aistatstitle`,
`\aistatsauthor` and `\aistatsaddress` (aistats2027.sty:173/248/355, aistats2eM.sty:102/171/252, the same in every
year) typeset the title and centred author and address tables and never reach `\title`/`\author`. **Perl** has no
aistats binding: the shipped copy is read raw (or, without it, the three are undefined), and the document has no title
and no creators — the HTML head falls back to the first section heading. **Rust** had the same, through a stub
registered under `aistats2026` only (the versioned fallback strips `aistats2027` to `aistats`, which nothing answered).

Now one family binding, `latexml_contrib/src/aistats_sty.rs`, answers `aistats` (the years the versioned fallback
strips to it: aistats2012, aistats2014 … aistats2027), and by name `aistats2026`, `aistats2e` and `aistats2eM` (a letter
follows their digits, which the fallback does not strip), as Perl's icml.sty.ltxml answers the ICML years. It reads the
paper's copy raw (`fallback_request`), then, where the copy defines them:
- the first `\aistatstitle{T}` is the title (`\title`; it also keeps aistats2022.sty:172's `\gdef\@supplementtitle{#1}`
  for that copy's `\makesupplementtitle`, 1910.09056); a later one prints in place as the copy does (2610.11580's
  supplement "Supplementary Material" heading, which a second `\title` would drop);
- `\aistatsauthor{A₁ \And A₂}` with the `\aistatsaddress{a₁ \And a₂}` under it are authors: column by column
  `A₁ \\ a₁ \And A₂ \\ a₂` when the row has several columns and the address as many (`\And`, `\AND`, `\ANDD`), in as
  many rows (`\AND`), and the address is no key to marked names (two or more distinct marks in it: 2312.06786's two
  marked affiliations over a second row of e-mails go by mark; one mark is a note's, `$^*$equal contribution` or
  `Univ A$^*$` twice, and the columns still pair — 1905.11190, 2405.18281, 2011.03885, 2301.11862, 2410.15516), read as the kernel `\author` reads name, affiliation and e-mail lines (2610.11580,
  1002.4058) — the PDF prints column i under author i. The binding reads ahead from the row, brace-balanced, through what prints nothing (spaces, `~`,
  paragraph ends, vertical space, definitions, size and font declarations, the copy's `\runningauthor`/`\runningtitle`,
  groups) to the address, stopping at anything that may print, the next `\aistatsauthor` or the block's end; the
  material between runs first, then the pair (29 of 2,843 papers: `\runningauthor` 1804.04378, 2402.12508; `\vspace`
  2003.03080, 2305.16147; `\medskip` 2602.12181; `~` 1603.09584; `\newcommand` 1302.5348, 1902.01239, whose macro is
  then defined when the address is read). Otherwise — a row of one column, whose address the copy centres under every
  name (2510.09534's `Jeong$^\ast$ \quad Zhai$^\ast$ \quad Ro\v{c}kov\'{a}`), columns that do not match (1806.02924's
  four names over one address), or an address after printed material — the names are one author list rebuilt
  from their columns (`\ANDD` a column break, not an undefined command inside a name), and the address goes through the
  kernel's `\lx@add@affiliation@shared[annotate=run]`: marked, each `$^1$` line to the authors showing the mark
  (1910.09056: Wood gets UBC, MILA and CIFAR); unmarked, each column an affiliation of every author of the row (columns
  printed alike once), its e-mail lines the authors' e-mails placed as a marked list's are — one for each
  author in their order, else the block's (1806.02924's `\{asuggala, …\}@cs.cmu.edu`, 1311.1894's
  `\{honda,takemura\}@…`): the row is the authors queued after the last affiliation, as `annotate=run` attaches one
  (2006.04012's, 2310.19690's later row), else the last author list (2010.08573's second `\aistatsaddress` of e-mails
  under a paired row), and a list not one for each author is one block contact an address, not the raw line
  (1802.07182). A shared affiliation attached to every author it serves is the kernel convention (Perl's
  `annotate` the same); the PDF prints it once. Each row (`\lx@add@authors@list`) adds to the rows before;
- the setters' arguments are read where they stand: a macro without parameters whose meaning the paper made inside the
  `\twocolumn[…]` group (1302.5348's `\newcommand{\UMDAddress}{…}` between `\aistatsauthor` and `\aistatsaddress`; a
  global macro renewed there) is replaced by its expansion, as the queued frontmatter is digested after that group ends,
  where the meaning is gone (`state::meaning_is_group_local`); a column that assigns or tests a meaning
  (`\renewcommand{\Uni}{…}\Uni`, 2511.05163's `\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.0}`) is left as it is;
- a submission under review (`\statePaper` not 1: no `accepted` option, nor aistats2027's `preprint`) prints
  "Anonymous Author" and "Anonymous Institution" where the copy has that block (aistats2020.sty … aistats2027.sty; the
  2e, 2012, 2014 and 2019 copies print the names either way), and so does the conversion (user ruling 2026-10-06,
  display toggles as the PDF shows them).

The copy's running-head measurement inside `\aistatsauthor` is not run, so its
`\PackageError{Document}{Running heading author exceeds size limitations}` (aistats2026.sty:289-295) no longer needs
the former stub's placeholder `\@runningauthor`. `\runningtitle`/`\runningauthor` (page furniture) stay the copy's.
Witnesses 1002.4058, 1302.5134, 1302.5348, 1303.0449, 1103.0941 (2e), 1202.1568 (2eM), 1102.1492 (2012), 1311.1894
(2014), 1806.02924 (2019), 2604.21432 (2020), 1910.09056 (2022), 2405.15172 (2025), 2605.03921, 2510.09534 (2026),
2610.11580 (2027); 7 of 6,000 sampled papers, each with no title and no creators before. Repros
