### 773. A second `\documentstyle` raises LaTeX's error and loads no class (Perl: applies latex209 and the class again)

latex.ltx:18617-18618 `\documentclass` makes itself `\@twoclasseserror` (:18944-18947, "Two \documentclass or
\documentstyle commands", the rest gobbled), and `\documentstyle` (:18622-18624) ends in `\documentclass`, so a second
class declaration only errs. Perl's `\documentstyle` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:97-129) loads the class every time.
Now the document's first `\documentclass` or `\documentstyle` sets `lx@class@declared` (sect01.rs `CLASS_DECLARED`)
and a later `\documentstyle` raises the LaTeX error and loads nothing; a second `\documentclass` is unchanged (it still
loads, sect01.rs `retract_chapter_before_class_load`). A first declaration no binding and no file answered — the
OmniBus fallback (tex_job.rs `\lx@documentstyle@impl`'s last branch; after `\documentclass`, OmniBus newly loaded
and the class's own `.cls_loaded`/`.cls_raw_loaded` unset) — does not count (main-session ruling 2026-10-19): the real
`\documentstyle` after it loads. astro-ph9812142's line 1 is `#\documentstyle[psfig,epsf]{/disk/3/roud/home/Texstuff/aa}`
— the `#` is no comment: pdflatex says "You can't use macro parameter character #", runs that `\documentstyle`, and
stops at the missing class (no PDF; TL 2025 has no aa.cls either) — and its line 2 `\documentstyle[psfig,epsf]{aa}`
gives aa's `\thesaurus`, `\offprints` and bibitem tags (1 Error, the stray `#`; 3,433 words, as 67int19b). latex209.def's
definitions (`\lx@latex@ix@definitions`, since 70b) apply once per document: applied again, they saved the settled
`\normalsize` as `\original@normalsize` and the two called each other (Timeout:Convert); a second class load after the
fallback runs again under the 2e-command traps' `\@gobble` until its own `\@documentclasshook`. Repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/documentstyle_twice_loads_one_class`, `sectioning-frontmatter/documentstyle_after_a_missing_class`;
guards `perfect_kernel_batch77r::{documentstyle_twice_loads_one_class, documentstyle_after_a_missing_class_loads_the_class,
documentstyle_after_a_missing_documentclass_loads_the_class}`.

### 774. A siunitx unit's own `\DeclareSIUnit[<options>]` apply where it is a command's whole unit (Perl: stored, ignored)

siunitx.sty:6684-6694 keeps a unit's options from `\DeclareSIUnit[<options>]{\unit}{…}` and applies them when that unit
is the whole unit argument of `\qty`/`\SI`/`\unit`, before the command's own options. Perl's siunitx binding stores the
options and never reads them, so a unit declared with `number-unit-product={}` keeps the default thin space. The Rust
binding applies them (`six_begin_processing_for_units`), and an explicit empty value for a token-list key is empty, not
`true`: 2504.05919's `\DeclareSIUnit[number-unit-product={}]\%{\char`\%}` prints "85%" as pdflatex does; 1501.03532's
per-unit `number-unit-product = \ ` puts its interword space before nm/dBm. 77r r2; repro
`package-bindings/siunitx_unit_named_by_its_own_char_code`; guard `perfect_kernel_batch77r::siunitx_*`.

handing the placeholders over had replaced their title and authors with "Paper title: Preparation of papers for

### 776. A Cyrillic text symbol set in a Latin letter's slot (T2A/T2B/T2C) is that Cyrillic letter (Perl: the Latin letter)

**TeX**: t2aenc.def:230-237 (t2benc.def:230-239, t2cenc.def alike) declares `\CYRII`/`\cyrii`, `\CYRJE`/`\cyrje`,
`\CYRQ`/`\cyrq`, `\CYRW`/`\cyrw` — and in T2B/T2C `\CYRDZE`/`\cyrdze` — at the slots of I i J j Q q W w (S s): the LH
fonts draw the shared glyph, so the PDF shows the letter, while its text layer reads Latin (pdftotext "Iван"). X2
(x2enc.def:244-273) uses the same slots for the same ten letters, and OT2 puts `\CYRJE`/`\cyrje` at J/j (ot2enc.def:96,
124, slots 74/106).

**Perl**: `\DeclareTextSymbol` decodes the slot through the encoding's fontmap (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2614-2625, a
`CharDef` of the slot; t2a.fontmap.ltxml), so `\cyrii` — which a UTF-8 `і` becomes (t2aenc.dfu) — is Latin `i`:
Ukrainian "Іван" and Serbian "ј" come out spelled with Latin letters, wrong for search, hyphenation and speech.

**Rust** (77s): a text symbol naming one of those letters is the letter when its slot decodes to an ASCII letter, in any
encoding (`cyrillic_letter_in_latin_slot`, latex_constructs/sect08.rs); the slot still decodes as Latin, so a Latin `i`
typed in T2A text stays Latin, and a letter with a slot of its own (`\cyrdze` at T2A 175) is unchanged. X2 and OT2 had
no fontmap (Perl neither: no x2/ot2.fontmap.ltxml), so their symbols decoded to nothing and the letters were dropped
without a diagnostic; 77u gives them maps whose slots are already the Cyrillic letters (#777). Repro
`fonts-nfss/t2a_cyrillic_i_and_je_are_cyrillic`; guard `perfect_kernel_batch77s::t2a_cyrillic_i_and_je_are_cyrillic`.

### 777. T4, X2 and OT2 have font maps; a text symbol of an encoding with no map warns when dropped (Perl: no maps, the letters lost)

**TeX**: t4enc.def (fc, the "African Computer" fonts) declares the African Latin letters as composites of its own
commands — `\DeclareTextComposite{\m}{T4}{y}{175}` (:164) — and `\m`'s own body is an `\errmessage` ("Non existent
modified letter", :36-39) for a letter it has no slot for. x2enc.def and ot2enc.def put Cyrillic letters in the Latin
letters' slots (X2's extended Cyrillic: `\CYRAE` 65 … `\cyrizh` 122; OT2's wncyr transliteration: `A` А, `C` Ц, `Q` Ч).

**Perl**: no t4/x2/ot2.fontmap.ltxml, and its LaTeX.pool `\DeclareTextComposite` is ignored, so the encodings fall back
to OT1 (`Couldn't find font encoding`): `\m{y}` reaches t4enc.def's `\errmessage` and the letter is lost (2405.01972:
44 Errors in Rust before this, Perl's `\errmessage` a Note; pdflatex 0), an X2/OT2 `\DeclareTextSymbol` defines
nothing (`\cyrje` prints nothing, no diagnostic), and Latin letters typed in OT2 text print themselves where pdflatex
prints Cyrillic ("Moskva" for Москва).

**Rust** (77u): `t4_fontmap.rs` — the lower half T1's (the fc fonts are EC-shaped), the upper half fccoding.mf's glyphs
as fc.rme's Appendix D "T4-to-UCS correspondence" maps them, its slips corrected (139 Ń, 150 Ʒ, 152 Ė, 162 ɛ, 172 ʃ,
173/174 ŋ/ʋ), the letters Unicode has no character for as combining sequences (E̱, Ɛ̃ …) and fj as two letters;
`x2_fontmap.rs` — T2A's upper half and accents, x2enc.def's letters in the Latin slots (Unicode from x2enc.dfu; Ԛ/Ԝ/Ԩ/Ҏ
where it has none); `ot2_fontmap.rs` — wncyr10's glyphs (wncyr10.afm) with ot2enc.def's letters, and the fonts'
ligature program (wncyr10.tfm's LIGTABLE, 78 pairs: `sh` ш, `shch` щ, `ya` я, `e1` э, `N0` №, `[[` «, run as TeX
runs it, the result read again with the next character), so OT2's transliteration reads as the PDF prints it
(1405.1988, 2510.25931 "sh"; letter by letter it was "сх"). A `\DeclareTextAccent` whose slot holds a combining mark
(T4's `\G` 159, `\U` 188, `\I` 191) uses that mark, T2A/X2's `\C` (slot 19, ‶) the double grave, and one for a
command another encoding's file already declared as a text command still defines this encoding's command (OT2's
`\U{i}` й after X2's or T2A's `\U`; latex.ltx's `\DeclareTextCommand` always does). A `\DeclareTextSymbol` of an encoding that still has no map
(tipa's T3 until 77x, #781) keeps its empty body but warns once per symbol where it is used, naming the encoding
(`\lx@unmapped@text@symbol`, sect08.rs) — the loss is no longer silent. Witness 2405.01972: 45 Errors → 1 (the
`substitutefont.sty` TL 2025 lacks), "weeɓitanay", "jooɗodi", "o ƴetti" in place; its `\textipa{\textltailn}` (T3) now
warns. Repros `fonts-nfss/{t4_modified_letter_help_is_not_expanded, t4_african_letters_print,
x2_ot2_cyrillic_symbols_print, x2_ot2_cyrillic_letters_and_composites, ot2_transliteration_ligatures,
text_symbol_of_an_unmapped_encoding_warns}`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch77u::{t4_modified_letter_prints,
t4_african_letters_print, x2_ot2_cyrillic_symbols_print, x2_ot2_cyrillic_letters_and_composites,
ot2_transliteration_ligatures, second_encoding_accent_composes, text_symbol_of_an_unmapped_encoding_warns}`.

### 778. A `\p@<counter>` reference form is applied to the expanded number, as `\refstepcounter` stores it (Perl: typed unexpanded at the step)

**TeX**: latex.ltx:14963-14964 `\refstepcounter` stores `\protected@edef\@currentlabel{\csname p@#1\expandafter
\endcsname\csname the#1\endcsname}`: `\p@<counter>` is expanded once, with the expanded `\the<counter>` after it, inside
the definition's braces, and a robust command in it stays; a `\ref` prints the stored text.

**Perl** (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1001): the reference form is typed at the step unexpanded (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:1028
`\lx@@therefnum@@` `{\normalfont\csname p@#1\endcsname\csname the#1\endcsname}`, :1081-1085 the typeref forms), so a
`\p@` that takes arguments reads the `\csname the…` tokens themselves: 1902.09345's `\renewcommand{\p@equation}{\gobblesomeargs}` (a
robust nine-argument command keeping the ninth) read `\csname`, `t`, `h`, … and past the tag (18 errors in Rust, the
first SI equation lost; pdflatex 0).

**Rust** (77u): `\lx@@p@the@@` (base_utilities/defs/tags_refnums.rs), shared by the refnum and typerefnum forms, expands latex.ltx's form
as `\protected@edef` does (`with_unexpandable_protect` + `do_expand_partially`: an `\edef`'s expansion, which keeps
`\protected` macros, bounded by the form's braces) and returns the text: "Equation S1" → refnum "S1", as pdflatex's
`\ref`. Only a `\p@<counter>` that does something is applied so: with the kernel's empty one (`\@definecounter`,
latex.ltx:10144) the number is typed as written, as before — an itemize's `\tikz` bullet, a number LaTeX never stores,
does not survive an `\edef`. The common forms are the same text as before (`\p@enumii` = `\theenumi`, `\labelformat`'s
argument-taking `\p@`). Residual: the form is still TYPESET
at the step, where pdflatex typesets it only at a `\ref`, so a form that cannot typeset (a nine-argument `\p@` before a
one-token number) still reads past its tag — our argument reader takes a `}` as an undelimited argument (Perl
Gullet.pm:732-744 alike; tex.web §395 stops at it, "Argument of \x has an extra }"), SYNC_STATUS C11. Repro
`parameter-conditional/p_form_applies_to_the_expanded_number`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch77u::{p_form_applies_to_the_expanded_number, p_forms_of_the_kernel_keep_their_reference}`.

### 779. `\normalfont` and `\reset@font` select the document's `\familydefault`, `\seriesdefault`, `\shapedefault` and `\encodingdefault` (Perl: `\rmdefault`, `\mddefault`, `\updefault`, the encoding kept)

**TeX**: latex.ltx:14113-14122 `\DeclareRobustCommand\normalfont{\fontencoding\encodingdefault \edef\f@family{\familydefault}
\edef\f@series{\seriesdefault} \edef\f@shape{\shapedefault} … \selectfont}`, `\let\reset@font\normalfont`: every reset —
`\begin{document}`'s `\init@series@setup` (:13902-13920), a footnote's `\reset@font\footnotesize` (:17659), `\textnormal`
(:14216), `\@eqnnum`, a float's `\@floatboxreset` — returns to the document's defaults. A
`\renewcommand\familydefault{\sfdefault}` document (helvet's and cmbright's idiom, lrec2026.sty's tgheros branch,
acmart/aamas's sigchi-a mode, posters and theses) is set in the sans family throughout.

**Perl** (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:5194-5195): `\normalfont` is `\fontfamily{\rmdefault}\fontseries{\mddefault}
\fontshape{\updefault}\selectfont`, and `neutralizeFont` (TeX_Box.pool.ltxml:218-221) the serif `textDefault`: such a
document was serif from its first reset on — the body after `\begin{document}` once 77u ran `\init@series@setup`, every
footnote, tag and `\textnormal` before.

**Rust** (77u r2, user ruling 2026-10-20): sect13.rs `\normalfont` is latex.ltx's (`\fontencoding\encodingdefault`
first, then the three defaults); `neutralize_font` (base_utilities/fonts_defs.rs: notes, tags, index entries) takes the family,
series and shape `\familydefault`/`\seriesdefault`/`\shapedefault` name when the font table knows them
(`font_code_named` reads a literal or a chain of parameterless macros without expanding, as on every tag), the encoding
as before. A sans-default document's text carries `font="sansserif"` throughout (the document root keeps LaTeXML's serif
default, so the attribute sits on the text runs), as its PDF (CMSS10/CMSSI10, CMSS8 footnotes); `\textrm` stays serif.
Two consequences of the reset now reading the document:
- A default the font table does not know (`\familydefault` = `droidserif`, droidserif.sty:101 under `[default]`, which
  cmpj3.sty loads, 2603.23615) would keep the font in force, as `\selectfont` does for any unknown family; `\normalfont`
  first puts serif medium upright in force (`\lx@normalfont@base`), so it resets to LaTeXML's serif as Perl's
  `\rmdefault` did.
- The `.bib` session (bib_session.rs) runs after the document in its live state, so its `\normalfont` read the defaults
  of the document's end: cmpj3's `\ukrainianpart` after the bibliography (`\renewcommand\familydefault{\sfdefault}`) made
  the entries sans where pdflatex's bibliography, typeset in place, is serif. `\lx@bibliography` (sect11.rs) records the
  reset as the defaults stand there (`lx@bibliography@normalfont`), and the session digests that.
`\normalfont` restoring the encoding is latex.ltx's too: after `{\fontencoding{OT1}\selectfont <c> \normalfont <d>}` in
a T1 document `<d>` prints as written (pdflatex), no longer ¡d¿; 0710.2028's `\cyr`
(`\renewcommand\encodingdefault{OT2}\normalfont`) now prints its OT2 transliteration in Cyrillic ("Там даже …", as the
PDF). The bindings that stand for a package or class setting the default do so as the original does (77u r3):
cmbright_sty.rs runs cmbright.sty:26-28, acmart_cls.rs sigchi-a's `\@ACM@sigchiamodetrue` and `\familydefault`
(acmart.cls:238-240, :888-890). Residuals (SYNC_STATUS "Font-Selection Chain Residuals" 5-7): `\textnormal` in maths
(`\textnormal@math`) keeps its fixed serif font; a `.bib` entry's author names and year carry no sans; a family the
font table does not know falls back to serif only in `\normalfont` — opensans.sty's `[default]` (:160-161,
`\opensansfamily`) stays serif. A formula's tokens are written against the text default, not the sans text (#780). Repros
`fonts-nfss/family_default_sets_the_body`, `fonts-nfss/family_default_survives_a_preamble_switch`,
`fonts-nfss/unknown_family_default_resets_to_serif`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch77u::{family_default_sets_the_body,
family_default_survives_a_preamble_switch, unknown_family_default_resets_to_serif}`,
`06_cluster_bibliography::bib_entries_take_the_defaults_where_the_bibliography_stands`; golden
`tikz/ac-drive-components.xml` (its node text CMSS, "Control unit" CMSSBX10 as pdflatex).

### 780. A formula's token fonts are written relative to the text default, not to the enclosing text element, and MathML reads the context font inside the formula only (Perl: written against the enclosing text element, that relative font read whole)

**TeX**: a formula is set in the math fonts of the current math version (fontmath.ltx: `\mathversion{normal}`'s CMMI
letters, CMR operators and digits, `\mathsf` CMSS), never in the text family, series or shape around it: `$y$` in
`\emph` of a `\renewcommand\familydefault{\sfdefault}` document is CMMI10, `\mathsf{G}` in `\textit` CMSS10, `$y$` in
`\textsf{\emph{…}}` of a serif document CMMI10 (pdflatex, `pdffonts`). Size and colour do reach the formula.

**Perl** (Core/Document.pm:385-410 `finalize_rec`): every node's font is written relative to the font declared on its
nearest written ancestor, so a token is written against the text element enclosing the formula — in a theorem body
`y` gets no `font` and `+` `font="upright"`. Post/MathML.pm:278 then takes the enclosing text element's `font` as the
context (`find_inherited_attribute`), and :677 reads a token's own `font` whole, falling back to that context. The two
halves agree only while the text family is serif: against `sansserif italic` the italic `y` is written `font="serif"`
(the shape matches, the family differs) and read as upright serif, `mathvariant="normal"`; `\mathsf{G}` is written
`font="upright"` and loses its sans (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1002).

**Rust** (77u r3): `finalize_rec` (document.rs) resets the declared family, series and shape to the text default's
(serif, medium, upright) at an `ltx:Math`, keeping size and colour, so a formula's tokens are written the same wherever
it stands — `y` is `font="italic"`, `+` has none, inside `\emph`, a theorem body or a plain paragraph alike. An
`XMText` (`\text`, `\mbox`) is text, set in the font around the formula (amstext's `\text` takes `\f@family`,
`\f@series`, `\f@shape`): its content is written against that font, as Perl writes it. `math_context_font`
(latexml_post mathml/mod.rs) reads the tokens' presentation and content context font only between the `XMath` and its
`ltx:Math` (where none can be written), so a token without a `font` is upright serif, not the text around; an
`m:mtext` falls back to the text font around the formula (`ctx_text_font`, Perl's `$LaTeXML::MathML::FONT`). In a serif
document an italic context's letters were plain `<mi>` by inheritance and now are by their own `italic`; the MathML
changes in two cases, both to TeX's fonts. A `\bm`/`\boldsymbol` letter or a `\boldmath` formula in italic text is bold
italic where Perl's MathML read the bare `bold` as bold upright (1503.06160 `\bm{B}` in lemmas, pdflatex CMMIB10). A
formula in a text element nested in another — `\textbf{Momentum:} $m_t$` in a theorem body is written
`<text font="bold italic">Momentum:<text font="medium">$m_t$</text></text>` — took the nearer element's relative
`medium` alone as its context, so its letters were upright (`mathvariant="normal"`); they are italic, as TeX sets them
in CMMI (2601.02609, 30 letters; 2608.12539, 24; 2603.28663, 2603.28316, 2607.18880). The XML of a formula in italic or
bold text differs from Perl's (theorem goldens re-blessed). 77u r2's sans
`\normalfont` (#779) made the Perl shape hit every sans-default document's italic and bold text: 2608.14133 (1,890
letters upright), 2608.31026, 2605.03549, 2604.00146, 2607.19982, 2606.05381 (theorem bodies), 2604.16675. Repros
`fonts-nfss/math_fonts_do_not_follow_a_sans_text_font`, `fonts-nfss/math_fonts_in_sans_italic_text_of_a_serif_document`;
guards `perfect_kernel_batch77u::{math_fonts_do_not_follow_a_sans_text_font,
math_fonts_in_sans_italic_text_of_a_serif_document}`, `perfect_kernel_batch56::letters_in_an_italic_context_stay_plain_mi`.

### 781. tipa's T3 has a font map, its diacritics are combining marks and its tone letters Unicode's; a text accent's default is its encoding's (Perl: no T3 map, the IPA lost; `\DeclareTextAccentDefault` ignored)

**TeX**: t3enc.def (tipa, FUKUI Rei) declares the IPA symbols at the tipa fonts' slots (`\DeclareTextSymbol\textschwa
{T3}{64}` …), and tipa's input convention makes the ASCII slots IPA letters (digits, capitals, `@ : ; " |`; tipaman §3:
`\textipa{[D@"lIm@]}` is [ðəˈlɪmə]); tipa10.tfm ligates `""` to ˌ and `||` to ǁ (tipa.mf:66-67). Its diacritics stack a
slot of the font on the letter: `\upper@accent`/`\lower@accent` (t3enc.def:268-294) put `\hbox{#2\char#4}` above or
below `\hbox{#5}`, `\ipaclap` and `\ipabar` (:330-354) overlap a glyph or rule a bar; in T3 the kernel accents are
t3enc.def's (:489-516, a `*` form below the letter: `\~*{a}`, `\r*{n}`), and tipa.sty:387-464 adds `\|`, `\*`, `\:`,
`\;`, `\!` composites. tone.sty draws a contour from tone-letter parts (slots 128-145, :37-58). tipa.sty:283-344
`\DeclareTextAccentDefault{\textsubring}{T3}` makes the accent usable in other encodings: latex.ltx:9985-9986, `\?\cs` →
`\UseTextAccent{T3}\cs`, which (:9958-9965) sets the accent in T3 and its argument back in the caller's encoding.

**Perl**: no T3 fontmap and no tipa binding (tipa.sty is not read by default: `\textipa` undefined); with the raw file
the symbols are empty and the input letters OT1's ("D@”lIm@"); `\DeclareTextAccentDefault` is ignored
(latex_base.pool.ltxml:361-362) and `\UseTextAccent` reads two arguments (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1004).

**Rust** (77x): `t3_fontmap.rs` — every slot the glyph tipa.mf's parts draw there (tipadiac, tipapnct, tiparoml,
tipasym1-4, tipagerm, tipasc, tipatone `cmchar` names), as the IPA letter Unicode has for it by t3enc.def's command
name, cross-checked against tipauni.sty's table, and the two ligatures. Where the glyph the font draws and its IPA
meaning part, the slot is the IPA meaning, as tipauni.sty maps it (user ruling 2026-10-20, 77x r2): `!` the alveolar
click ǃ U+01C3 (tipapnct.mf draws an exclamation mark; tipaman2.tex:1105 "(post)alveolar click"; 2606.11542 "!Xoon"),
`&` ɞ U+025E (the font draws the superimposed tilde, which `\textsuperimposetilde` keeps as U+0334), the corner 94 the
no-audible-release mark U+031A (2601.02906, 2609.04232), `\textsubbar` (slot 9 below, `\b` in T3) the minus sign below
U+0320 ("retracted", tipaman2.tex:1461); the open corner 95, which tipauni.sty does not map (tipaman gives it another
meaning), stays the spacing ˹ — so a `\textopencorner x\textcorner` bracket pair (2604.00122's Quine corners) is ˹x̚.
Kept as drawn: `|` `{` `}` the click letters ǀ ǁ ǂ (tipasym1.mf's pipes), the baby gamma 200 the ram's horns' ɤ
(U+0264's former name), 175 ꭢ (tipasym4.mf:299 "Open O-E Ligature"). The marks t3enc.def:213-219 sets after the letter
they modify — `\textrthook` 36, `\textpalhook` 37, `\textcorner` 94 — are the bare combining marks
(`DeclareFontMapMultichar`), which attach to that letter (`t\textrthook` t̢, `k\textcorner` k̚), not to the no-break
space a standalone combining mark is decoded on; so are the tie bars typed `<` `>` (60, 62), between the letters they
join (`\textipa{t<s}` t͜s). Slots with no Unicode character decode to nothing, and a text symbol at one warns where it
is used (`\lx@unmapped@text@symbol`, now for an empty slot of a mapped encoding too): the Celtic palatalization mark 32,
the hooktop 35, the tone-letter parts 128-145 and stem 191, the left-hooktop long i/y and Viby i/y 166, 167, 182, 183.
`t3enc_def.rs` reads t3enc.def raw, then sets the `a` form of `\upper@accent`/`\lower@accent` as the slot's combining
mark above or below (`t3_accent_mark`: the tilde 3 is U+0303 above, U+0330 below; the round cap 16 U+0311/U+032F; the
stroke 34 below the syllabicity mark U+0329; the tone accents 152-159 U+1DC4 U+1DC5 U+1DC8 U+1DC9 U+030D U+030E U+1DC0
U+1DC1), decoded in the font `#2` selects and applied as the kernel's `\accent` (`\lx@applyaccent`: `\'a` á,
`\textdotbreve{a}` ă̇, `\t{ts}` t͡s); the `b` (box) form stays raw (tipa.sty:477 `\sups`). `\textsuperimposetilde` is
U+0334, `\ipabar` the stroke overlay U+0335 over a character run (`\textbarc` c̵, `\textcrg` ɡ̵; over another
construction — `\textdoublebaresh`'s `\hb@xt@` box, :535-537 — t3enc.def's raw `\ipabar`, which r1's overlay printed as
TeX source), and the made letters Unicode has are its letters (`\textbarb` ƀ, `\textbard` đ, `\textbarg` ǥ, `\textcrtwo`
ƻ, `\textcrinvglotstop` ƾ, the kerned `\textdzlig` ʣ, `\textdctzlig` ʥ, `\texttctclig` ʨ). In T3 text, outside math, the
kernel accents and `\|` take T3's command (an expandable macro to the native accent elsewhere; a protected step to
T3's). The subscript W set above (`\textoverw`) has no Unicode mark: the letter prints alone with a Warning.
`tone_sty.rs` reads tone.sty raw and writes `\tone`/`\stone` as the Chao tone letters ˥˦˧˨˩ (U+02E5-02E9) and `\rtone`
as the left-stem ones (U+A712-A716): `\tone{51}` ˥˩; a level outside 1-5 keeps tone.sty's boxes, which print nothing,
with a Warning (witnesses 2601.19932, 2602.10003). t3enc.def or tone.sty read a second time (`\input{t3enc.def}` after
tipa.sty) keeps the commands the binding saved the first time (saving its own wrappers made them expand to themselves:
Fatal:Timeout). sect08.rs: `\DeclareTextAccentDefault` is latex.ltx's, `\UseTextAccent` is robust as latex.ltx's
`\DeclareRobustCommand*` (an alignment's look-ahead for `\omit` stops at it), restores the caller's encoding for the
argument (`\textsubring{g}` in T1 text is g̥, not ɡ̥) and calls `\<enc>\cs` directly — with no such command, or in math,
the argument alone: tipa's `\;` `\!` `\:` in `$a\;b$` set the letters as pdflatex does, while an accent proper in a
formula loses its mark (`$\textsubring{n}$` is n, pdflatex n̥ with "invalid in math mode": residual). It reads its
argument (#3) itself: an `&`, `$`, `}`, `\end` or, in an alignment, a row end is not taken — pdflatex reads it and errs,
losing the cell, formula or group it ends (amsmath loaded before tipa: `\!\! &`, `,\;$x$`; witness 2609.13770's
`\crefname{section}{\S\!}`; 2605.00132 and 2607.12821 exercise the robust form and its math path) — the
accent is set alone with a Warning (once per accent and token). amsmath_sty.rs re-asserts the kernel's `\,` `\!` `\:`
`\;` `\negmedspace` `\negthickspace` as amsmath.sty:155-175 declares them again
(`latex_constructs::define_amsmath_tmspace_commands`), so tipa loaded before amsmath leaves them the spacing commands
(r1 regressed 2603.03017 E 0 → 12, 2605.00529 E 0 → 66 with 16,534 words lost, 2608.02769 E 0 → 14: `\!` read the `&`,
`$` or `}` after it). The kernel `\accent` (math_common.rs) performs the assignments between its number and its
character as tex.web §1123/§1270 do — protected macros expanded, `\relax` skipped, the NFSS font switch
(`\lx@fontencoding`, `\selectfont`) an assignment — so `\UseTextAccent{OT1}{\'}{e}` (`\add@accent`'s `\accent19
\fontencoding{OT1}\selectfont e`) is é (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1004). tex_fonts.rs: the `--`/`---` dash ligatures are not
T3's (tipa10.tfm has none). Other encodings' empty slots the new Warning exposed: OT4 and LY1 slot 17 is the dotless j ȷ
(ot4enc.def:82, ly1enc.def:42; Perl's ot4/ly1 fontmaps leave it undef, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1005: the Perl-synced
golden `tests/encoding/ly1.xml` now shows ȷ there); LAE 198-203 (`\shaddanasb` … `\shaddakasra`, laeenc.def:83-97) are shadda with the vowel, as arabi's
DTP Naskh LAE font draws them and LFE 0xC6-0xCB (the default aealmohanadb has no glyph there); LAE `\Decimalchar` (251,
no glyph in any LAE font) keeps the Warning. Witnesses 2405.01972 (`\textipa{\textltailn}` ɲ, `\textipa{\!b}` ɓ,
`\textipa{gO}` ɡɔ), 1802.05444. Repros `fonts-nfss/{t3_tipa_input_letters_print, t3_tipa_symbols_print,
t3_tipa_diacritics_compose, t3_tone_letters, t3_accent_outside_t3_text, t3_slot_without_unicode_warns,
t3_tipa_then_amsmath_align_negspace, t3_tipa_then_amsmath_tabular_negspace, t3_tipa_then_amsmath_thickspace_before_math,
t3_tipa_after_amsmath_accent_at_boundary, t3enc_def_loaded_twice, t3_ipa_meaning_slots, t3_ipabar_built_symbols,

`perfect_kernel_batch77x::*` (the same names), `perfect_kernel_batch77u::text_symbol_of_an_unmapped_encoding_warns` (now
a document-declared encoding).

### 782. A binding may port a non-`\long` TeX macro as one: its arguments stop at a `\par` (Perl: every binding macro reads `\long`)

**TeX**: a macro not declared `\long` stops reading its arguments at a `\par` — "Paragraph ended before \x was
complete", the call dropped, the `\par` read again (tex.web §392, §396; #442). amsppt.sty:799-818's `\footnote` and
`\footnotetext` read their text so (`\nextiv@##1`, `\DNii@[##1]##2`).

**Perl**: every `DefMacro`/`DefConstructor` reads its arguments across paragraphs (Expandable.pm stores `isLong` and
never reads it); amsppt.sty.ltxml:268's `\footnote[]{}` constructor took every paragraph after a note whose `}` never
came (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1012).

**Rust** (77v): `ExpandableOptions::short` — a binding's macro made with `short => true` checks its arguments for
`\par` as #442's TeX-declared macros do, wherever it is made (`Expandable::checks_par`, expandable.rs). amsppt_sty.rs's
`\footnote` and `\footnotetext` are such macros, handing the text to the note constructors. 79m: ams_support_sty.rs's
`\title`, `\subjclass`, `\keywords`, `\dedicatory`, `\translator` (amsart.cls:457/551-568, amsbook.cls, amsproc.cls:
`\renewcommand*`, `\newcommand*`, `\def`), so a `\subjclass{…` whose `}` never comes stops at the paragraph's end
(KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1150; 2212.11488). No other binding is changed: a binding's macros stay `\long` unless the
original's non-`\long` reading is the point. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch77v::amsppt_footnote_argument_runs_past_par`,
`perfect_kernel_batch79m::an_unclosed_subjclass_ends_at_the_paragraph`.

### 783. A document's `\newtheorem` replaces a binding's theorem of the name, also where the real class declares it (Perl: replaced, every `\newtheorem` redefining)

**LaTeX**: `\newtheorem{X}` of a defined `\X` is refused (latex.ltx `\@nthm`, amsthm.sty:78-80 `\@ifdefinable`):
"Command \X already defined", the first declaration kept. Under llncs.cls (`\spnewtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}…`), a
document's `\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[section]` is refused and its theorems print "Theorem 1.".

**Perl**: `\newtheorem` refuses nothing; every declaration replaces the previous one.

**Rust** (77v r2/r3): a second `\newtheorem` is refused, as in LaTeX, only when the document's world (the document, a
raw file it loaded) made the first; a binding's declaration — and a binding's guess made while the document is read,
through `\lx@guess@newtheorem` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1008) — claims no name, so the document's replaces it. A binding's
theorem set is in general more than its class declares (elsart_support's `{rem}` under arxbj, 1205.2947; tac's under
2407.21129's `\newtheoremrm{examples}…[section]`), where the document's declaration gives the theorem the title pdflatex
prints (its number need not match: tac.cls's `\@@newthm#1[#2]#3[#4]` drops both counter arguments and numbers every
theorem on the one `\subsection` sequence, "0.1. Theorem", "0.2. Proposition", which the tac binding does not model —
SYNC row); telling the class's own theorems apart per binding is not done. Where the real class does declare the name, the document's
declaration wins here and LaTeX's refusal is lost: llncs + `\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[section]` gives "Theorem 11"
(the declaration as llncs's kernel numbers it, its `\@thmcountersep` empty: KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1111; "Theorem 1.1"
before 78q r2) where pdflatex prints "Theorem 1." with an error. Guard `perfect_kernel_batch77v::llncs_document_newtheorem_replaces_the_class`
(repro class-bindings/llncs_document_newtheorem_over_class).

### 784. A jfm copy's caption: its own `\@makecaption`'s label format, or caption with its options (Perl: no jfm binding, article's "Figure 1:")

**LaTeX**: the jfm.cls copies without caption set `{\normalfont\scshape #1\ifrem@fullpt\else .\fi} #2` (0712.2739's
:953-958, ~41 of 49 sampled jfm papers): "Figure 1." with the label in small caps, `\removefullpoint` dropping the
period once; the newer copies load caption with their own options (2608.01828's :1837 `labelsep=period`).

**Perl**: no jfm binding; OmniBus (article) prints "Figure 1:".

**Rust** (78a): jfm_cls.rs requires caption through `shipped_class::require_shipped_packages`, with the copy's
options (a bare `RequirePackage!("caption")` dropped them); a copy whose `\@makecaption` uses `\ifrem@fullpt` gets its
label format as the figure's and table's title format (`\format@title@<type>` = `\lx@tag[][. ]{…}`, as amsart's
ams_support binding) and its label font as `\fnum@font@<type>` (`\scshape`), with `\removefullpoint`. The copy's own
`\@makecaption` stays declined (the kernel's caption), so its layout (centred short captions, `\small`) is not
modelled. The label format and font are installed at `\begin{document}` only where caption is not loaded
(`\AtBeginDocument{\@ifpackageloaded{caption}{}{…}}`; `\ifrem@fullpt`/`\removefullpoint` are defined either way): the
document's caption package — or subcaption's or subfig's, which load it — replaces the class's `\@makecaption` in
pdflatex ("Figure 1:" in the text font, the sub-captions' "(a)" at their size; 10 of the 40 copies with their own
`\@makecaption` in the 78a census, which is not complete — a 40k-zip sample found 23 more: 1711.01065, 2205.10181,
2507.07213 subcaption, 1805.00129 and 1612.03374 subfig, 2008.04616 caption), the old subfigure package does not, nor
floatrow, which loads caption's kernel alone (floatrow.sty:39 `caption3`; 2312.13002, 2111.12004): caption3 falls back
to the caption binding, which then defines `\lx@caption@kernel@only` (caption_sty.rs), and the class's format stays;
nor `\usepackage[caption=false]{subfig}`, which loads `caption3` too (subfig.sty:129-141; subfig_sty.rs, 78a r3).
subcaption (subcaption.sty:43) and subfig without that option (:129-139) load caption even after floatrow's `caption3`,
so they clear the mark (78a r3). Residual: a document's own `\usepackage{caption}` after a `caption3` load — floatrow's,
or `[caption=false]{subfig}`'s — keeps the class's format, as the caption binding is not run again (RED
class-bindings/jfm_caption/jfm_copy_caption_package_after_subfig_without_caption, the rev78a3 re-review's finding 1). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch78a::{
jfm_copy_captions_end_the_label_with_a_period, jfm_copy_caption_package_keeps_its_options,
jfm_copy_caption_yields_to_caption_loaders, jfm_copy_caption_kept_with_subfigure, jfm_copy_caption_kept_with_floatrow,
jfm_copy_caption_kept_with_subfig_without_caption, jfm_copy_caption_yields_to_caption_loaders_after_floatrow}`.

### 785. An unnumbered heading runs its title format's after-code (Perl: the title font alone, titlesec's after-code dropped)

**LaTeX**: titlesec typesets a starred title with the same `\ttlf@<sec>` as a numbered one, without the label: the
format, `<before>{title}` and the after-code (titlesec.sty:740-818). tufte-common.def:1613-1619's `\chapter` format
opens `\begin{fullwidth}` in the format and closes it in the after-code.

**Perl**: `\@@unnumbered@section` digests `\lx@format@title@font@@{type}` before the title
(latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:666-670); titlesec.sty.ltxml:42-57 drops the after-code.

**Rust** (78a): the starred title runs `\lx@format@title@font@@{type}` before it (as Perl; the port had lost it, a
Rust-only defect — SYNC "Rust Error Fixes") and `\lx@format@title@after@@{type}` after it (base_utilities/defs/tags_refnums.rs:
`\format@title@after@<type>` when defined). titlesec_sty.rs defines `\format@title@after@<sec>` as its after-code
(empty for `rightmargin`/`wrap`/`drop`, and for an `explicit` after-code that names the title): the format's
`\begin{fullwidth}` is closed in the title (the tufte manuals: 0 errors, the starred titles in the class's italics).
Guards `perfect_kernel_batch78a::{unnumbered_section_takes_the_title_font,
titlesec_after_code_closes_an_unnumbered_title}`.

### 786. biblatex's `\citeauthor` and a numeric style's `\textcite` print the name, and a nameless entry in a textual numeric citation keeps its brackets, natbib's too (Perl: no biblatex binding; CrossRef.pm:541 drops every bracket of the citation)

**biblatex**: `\citeauthor` prints `\printnames{labelname}` in every style (biblatex.def:2497-2506); numeric.cbx's and
alphabetic.cbx's `\textcite` print the name, then the bracketed label ("Hampe [1]").

**Perl**: no biblatex binding (the contrib binding ports the upstream draft's `_cite_fallback`, which sends both to the
plain `\cite` outside an author-year style: "[1] showed it").

**Rust** (78a): biblatex_sty.rs's `\citeauthor` is the author-year form (`\@@bibref{Authors}`) in every style; a
non-author-year `\textcite`/`\Textcite`/`\citet` is natbib's numbers-mode textual citation (Perl natbib.sty.ltxml:161-171,
`Authors Phrase1NumberPhrase2`, the pre- and postnote inside the brackets). An author-title or verbose style's
`\textcite` prints "Name [1]" too, where biblatex prints the title. Witnesses 2402.17192 (style=ieee), 2410.22329.
Guard `perfect_kernel_batch78a::biblatex_citeauthor_and_textcite_print_the_name_in_a_numeric_style`.

An entry with no name (no author, editor or key tag) under such a textual numeric citation keeps the brackets around
its number, for that entry alone (latexml_post crossref.rs `nameless_numeric_show`, 78a r2): biblatex "No Author Misc
[2]" (numeric.cbx:23-41 prints the `labeltitle` before the bracket) is "[2]", natbib numbers mode's "Smith [2], ano [1]"
(plainnat's key-prefix label) "Smith [2], [1]". Perl's CrossRef.pm:541 turns the whole citation's `show` to `refnum`
("2"; "2, 1"). Residuals: the biblatex `labeltitle` (and natbib's key-prefix) is not printed; `\citeauthor` of a
nameless entry prints its number ("3"), where biblatex prints nothing. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78a::biblatex_numeric_textcite_without_author_keeps_its_brackets`,
`bibref_show::natbib_numbers_citet_merges_same_authors`.

### 787. nicematrix's `\Block{i-j}<tokens>{content}` sets the tokens before the content (Perl: no nicematrix binding)

nicematrix.sty:7258 `\__nicematrix_Block_i: { m m D < > { } +m }`: the `<…>` argument is set before the content in the
block's box. nicematrix_sty.rs's `\Block` read `{}{}` only, so the `<\bfseries>` was the content (OT1's `<`/`>`, "¡Tall¿").
Rust (78a): `OptionalAngled` reads it; present, the content is `{<tokens><content>}`. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78a::nicematrix_block_angle_tokens_apply_to_the_content`.

### 788. `\pdfxform` keeps its box as the form, `\pdfrefxform` places it (Perl: `\pdfxformname` only)

**pdfTeX**: `\pdfxform <box>` makes a form XObject of the box (voiding it) and numbers it in `\pdflastxform`;
`\pdfrefxform <n>` places the form, as often as it is referenced (pdfTeX manual §`\pdfxform`, §`\pdfrefxform`).

**Perl**: pdfTeX.pool.ltxml:96 defines `\pdfxformname`; neither primitive.

**Rust** (78a): pdftex.rs's `\pdfxform` keeps the box (global value `pdfxform@<n>`) and `\pdfrefxform` returns it, as
`\copy` does. xsavebox's `\xsbox`/`\xusebox` (xsavebox.sty:120-122, :298, :325 through pdfbase's
`\pbs_pdfxform:nnnnn`/`\pbs_pdfrefxform:n`) printed an empty box of the content's size (biblatex-ext's open-access
symbols, biblatex-ext.tex:3938-4022). Guard `perfect_kernel_batch78a::xsavebox_saved_box_prints_its_content`.
### 789. A class's author name markup as its title page prints it: vmsta's `\fnm`/`\snm`/`\inits`

vmsta.cls (Modern Stochastics: Theory and Applications, VTeX; shipped, not in TeX Live) defines the name parts only
where its `\@@author` prints the author list (vmsta.cls:278-291): `\name@m@front` stores `\fnm{…}` and `\snm{…}`, drops
`\inits` and `\suffix`, and prints `\@fnm~\@snm` — "Yuliya Mishura" for `\author[a]{\inits{Yu.}\fnm{Yuliya}\snm{Mishura}
\corref{cor1}}`. The kernel's locked `\author` replaces the class's, and OXIDIZED_DESIGN #647's search found the class's
`\name@m` identities, OmniBus's `\inits` printing: 1508.02842's creator "Yu.YuliyaMishura". Perl has no vmsta binding
(`\fnm` undefined). Ours: a vmsta binding (latexml_contrib vmsta_cls.rs) reads the shipped class raw and sets
`\lx@author@markup@class`, `\lx@author@markup@provide` calls that `\lx@author@markup@begin` (base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_fields.rs) runs
first for the author content, before OmniBus's identity meanings — `\fnm` stores, `\snm` prints `first~surname`, the
initials and suffix dropped, for the author content only and undefined after it, as the class defines them only in its
title code. A first name no `\snm` follows is printed after the content (flushed with the markup's restore list), as
`\@fnm~\@snm` prints it there: `\fnm{Ivan}~Voronov` "VoronovIvan" (vmsta.cls errs on its undefined `\@snm` there; no
corpus paper has the shape). 71 vmsta papers (1508.02842, 1411.4499, 1601.01109). The 68v repro of #647
(`vmsta_name_parts`) now reads its cut-down class as `vtexnames.cls`, which no binding answers. Repros
class-bindings/vmsta/vmsta_title_page_name_parts, vmsta_first_name_without_surname; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch77t::{vmsta_title_page_name_parts, vmsta_first_name_without_surname}`.

### 790. entics.cls and entcs.cls are read raw with elsart's frontmatter interface

entics.cls (Electronic Notes in Theoretical Informatics and Computer Science) and its predecessor entcs.cls (ENTCS) are
shipped by the papers and generated from Elsevier's esl.dtx, as elsart.cls is: `\author[keys]{…}`, `\address[label]{…}`,
`\thanks[key]{…}` and `\thanksref{key}`, which is no command but a delimiter `\author` reads its argument by
(entics.cls:707-735, :860-930). Read raw, the kernel's `\thanksref` (a superscript of its key, sect05.rs) printed the key
in the name — 2212.08177 "Willem HeijltjesALL", 1812.00040 "Mauro LucciALLmyemail" — the `\thanks[key]` notes became
footnote texts of the document and the `\address` a paragraph of the body. Perl has no binding for either. Ours: an
entics binding for both names (latexml_contrib entics_cls.rs) reads the class raw and then elsart_support_core (the
elsart binding's frontmatter interface): `\thanksref{ALL}` requests the `\thanks[ALL]{…}` contact, the address is the
author's. Repro class-bindings/entics/entics_thanksref_names_its_note (a stand-in class written for it: entics.cls may
not be redistributed); guard `perfect_kernel_batch77t::entics_thanksref_names_its_note`.

### 791. A class-numbered `\institute` store goes to the authors by their numbers

A raw class carrying llncs's `\institutename` (llncs.cls:870-885; copied by preprint.cls:233-256) prints its
`\institute{A \and B}` list with each `\and` stepping the institute counter and printing the number before the next
entry, the first numbered 1. The K11 store path (`\lx@add@store@affiliations`, frontmatter_stores.rs) saw unmarked
entries and gave every author every entry (`annotate=all`): 2405.16615's two authors each held Imperial College and
Edinburgh. Ours: when the class's `\institutename` redefines `\and` with a `\stepcounter`, the store holds at least two
`\and` entries and no mark, and the queued authors' marks are all numbers, the entries are led by their numbers as the
title page prints them (`class_numbered_institutes`, base_utilities/author_block/affiliations.rs) and labelled by them, so `$^{1}$`/`$^2$` — or
the class's `\inst{1,2}`/`\inst2` (2512.08621) — pick one each. Perl reads such a class raw (its `\institute` the class's). Repro
sectioning-frontmatter/class_numbered_institutes_go_by_the_authors_marks (with numinst.cls); guards
`perfect_kernel_batch77t::{class_numbered_institutes_go_by_the_authors_marks, class_numbered_institutes_go_by_inst_marks}`.

### 792. An llncs `\\` line reading as an affiliation is the affiliation of the names over it

The llncs binding splits `\author` at `\\` as at `\and` (a Rust improvement over Perl's llncs.cls.ltxml, which splits at
`\and` only: 2606.19939's `Hiuyi Cheng \\ Dezhi Peng`), so `\author{Ann Able\\University of Somewhere\\\email{…}}` made
a creator "University of Somewhere" holding the e-mail. llncs.cls:1019-1036 sets `\@author` as one centred paragraph,
its `\\` a line break: the line is printed under the name; and its `\and` is inline text (llncs.cls:1013-1018,
`\unskip,` or `\lastand` in `\@maketitle`), so the names it joins share the row. Ours (llncs_cls.rs `\lx@llncs@author`):
in an author list with no marks and no `\inst` marks, read across the whole `\author` body (its `\and`, `\And` and `\\`
pieces in order), a line after a `\\` that reads as an affiliation (`reads_as_affiliation`; a piece after the inline
`\and` is names, `Ann Able \and the ATLAS Collaboration`, the rev77t2 re-review's L6) goes into the author content of
each name since the last line under names — an affiliation line or an e-mail line (`line_is_email_list`), after which
the next names start a new row —, as an `\email` there does (so `\institute`'s clearing of the queued affiliations
leaves it): `Ann Able \and Bob Baker\\ University of Somewhere` both names' (2604.11038's Simon Fraser University on its
three authors), `Ann Able\\ University of X\\ Bob Baker\\ University of Y` one each. A list with marks is split as
before, since a contact digested with the authors would come before `\institute`'s entries in the count
`labelseq=affiliation` numbers them by. Residual: an address line with no institution word (`Stanford, CA 94305`) still
reads as names, creators "Stanford" and "CA 94305" (as before); in a list with `\inst` marks a line under the names
stays a creator of its own (`University of X`, as before; the rev77t2 re-review's L11); a `\texttt{ann@x.org,
bob@x.org}` line under the names makes two creators (as before; L8). Repros
sectioning-frontmatter/llncs_author_line_break_affiliation, llncs_author_line_break_affiliation_rows,
llncs_author_and_is_inline; guards `perfect_kernel_batch77t::{llncs_author_line_break_affiliation,
llncs_author_line_break_affiliation_rows, llncs_author_line_break_affiliation_per_name, llncs_author_and_is_inline,
llncs_author_e_mail_line_ends_a_row}`.

### 793. IEEEtran's `\appendix` keeps the title of the `\section` that follows it

IEEEtran.cls:5719-5745 `\appendix[<title>]` is one appendix: it prints the heading "Appendix" (or "Appendix \\* <title>")
through the kernel's `\section*`, steps the section counter once (`\ref` "A") and redefines `\section` so that an
unstarred one throws its argument away (`\@IEEEdestroythesectionargument`, :5711-5713, a terminal warning only): the
common `\appendix` `\section{Proof of Theorem 1}` prints "APPENDIX" and loses the title. Ours (ieeetran_cls.rs): the
optional title is the appendix's (an `ltx:appendix`, refnum "A", tag "Appendix" as the class prints it). Without one, the
first unstarred `\section` after `\appendix` — past blank lines, spaces, comment lines, empty groups (2002.07641's
`\appendix{}`) and `\label`s, the labels then the appendix's — makes the appendix, its title kept; anything else next
(`\section*`, `\subsection`, text) follows an appendix with an empty title, the "Appendix" heading pdflatex prints
(witnesses 1903.01287, 1103.2068, 2002.03484, 2410.15995, 2401.07123: a blank line after `\appendix` had made the titled
section a second appendix "B"). Residual: a non-printing command or a float between `\appendix` and the `\section`
(2404.01875's `\setlength{\jot}… \allowdisplaybreaks`, 2007.07179's figure; 3 of ~140 IEEEtran `\appendix` files, rev78d2)
takes the heading path too, so the titled section is "Appendix B" and refs to it read "B" where pdflatex's read "A"
(int45b had one appendix "Appendix A" with that title). A later
unstarred `\section` is another appendix with its title, tagged by its refnum, "Appendix B", "Appendix C" (2401.07123),
where pdflatex prints nothing of it and a `\ref` to a label in it prints "A" — ours reads "B", "C". `\appendices`
after `\appendix` numbers its appendices from "A" with their letters, as the class (pdflatex "APPENDIX", "APPENDIX A",
"APPENDIX B"). Authored content first: the destroyed argument is the author's text. Repro
sectioning-frontmatter/ieeetran_appendix_with_a_title_is_one_appendix; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78d::ieeetran_appendix_with_a_title_is_one_appendix` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1022).
### 800. webofc.cls is read raw with the `\inst` frontmatter, its side caption a caption

webofc.cls (EDP Sciences' Web of Conferences: EPJ, MATEC, E3S, ITM, SHS, BIO; shipped by the papers, about 30 of the
30,000-paper sample) titles the A&A/Springer way: `\author{Ann Able\inst{1}\fnsep\thanks{\email{…}} \and …}` with an
`\institute{A \and B}` list its title page numbers (webofc.cls:217 `\fnsep`, :434-440 `\institute`, `\inst` =
`$^{#1}$`, `\email` = "e-mail: …"), and `\sidecaption` (:824-857) reads the float's body up to `\caption` to set it
beside the caption in a `\parbox`. Read raw (no binding; Perl has none and errs on `\sidecaption`, `\firstname`,
`\lastname`), the names kept their superscripts ("Andrea Shindler,1": 2301.07438), every author got every institute
(1411.7792), the e-mail was a thanks note's text, and a side caption was text in a parbox with no `<caption>` (the
html_feedback report on 2610.23498, the figure's label on its section). Ours (latexml_contrib webofc_cls.rs): the class
read raw (its packages as it loads them), then inst_support's `\institute`/`\inst` (as aa, llncs and the Springer
classes have them), its `\author` split at `\\` as well as at `\and` (as llncs's: the template's `\\The SND
Collaboration` line under the names, 1609.01040 and 2610.23498, a creator of its own, not part of the last name; the
break's `*` and `[…]` no text, #804), the e-mail the author's contact (`\lx@add@email`; a `\thanks` that held only the
e-mail leaves no note, #803: 2409.01693), `\sidecaption` layout only (as aa_support and sv_support), and the class's
`\@makecaption` label format, "**Figure 1.** …" with the period and the space after it in the bold (:786-812
`\@CaptionTitleFont #1\@FloatCounterEnd\@FloatCounterSep` in one group; `caption_sty::class_makecaption_label`, shared
with jinstpub, whose period is outside; caption, when the document loads it, replaces it). The kernel's frontmatter
`\fnmsep` rule (nothing before a `\thanks`/`\inst`/`\footnote` mark, `digest_frontmatter_item`) covers webofc's `\fnsep`
too. Repros class-bindings/webofc/{webofc_authors_take_their_institutes, webofc_sidecaption_keeps_its_caption,
webofc_author_line_break_options} (beside a minimal webofc.cls stand-in written for them: the shipped class states no
licence); guards `perfect_kernel_batch78e::{webofc_authors_take_their_institutes, webofc_sidecaption_keeps_its_caption,
webofc_author_line_break_options}`.

### 801. jinstpub.sty is jheppub's frontmatter with JINST's extras

jinstpub.sty (JINST's SISSA/IOP publication style, 2015/08/05 v1.0 and 2020/09/18 v1.1638; shipped by the papers, 23 of
the 30,000-paper sample, about 121 in 8 months) is jheppub.sty with JINST's journal name, an optional mark on `\note`
(:91-98), an optional placement on `\collaboration` (:145), newtx fonts, amsthm and wrapfig (:32-56), section-numbered
equations (:335), a bold caption label with a period (:362-378) and four reference shorthands (:384-387). Read raw
(neither Perl nor Rust had a binding), its `\maketitle` laid the stored frontmatter out as body text: the affiliations an
itemize, the e-mail and the keywords paragraphs, the author's `\note{Corresponding author.}` a footnote inside the
personname (2006.05543, 2303.10224). Ours (latexml_contrib jinstpub_sty.rs, as jcappub_sty.rs gives JCAP; both in
latexml_contrib, as Perl has neither): jheppub's binding, then jinstpub's packages, `\note[]{}`, `\collaboration[t]{}`
(with its "option b/c" warnings), `\numberwithin{equation}{section}`, the caption label format
(`caption_sty::class_makecaption_label`), `\erratum`/`\addendum`/`\ibid`/`\pos`. Its `\emailAdd` is jheppub's
binding's since 78f (#805): JINST's `\maketitle` prints every address on one shared "E-mail:" line under the
affiliations (:133-138, :219-224), so an address is the contact of the author whose name it spells, else of the n-th
author when the list is the authors' in order, else (the one address left) of the one author marked as the
corresponding author (#809), else of the group's only author or the author block (78e r2 placed
jinstpub's alone, `\lx@add@contact@placed`; with Perl jheppub's n-th rule 16 of 23 papers had an address on a wrong author:
2311.16063's bross@fnal.gov on Andrea Bersani, not Alan D. Bross; 2307.12991, 1910.06438, 2311.00870, 2605.30709);
an `\emailAdd{a, b}` list is an address each (2211.05026, 2409.03065, 2112.00370). For the spelling, the kernel's name
reading takes a macro whose arguments all go into a frontmatter annotation (`\lx@add@contact`, `\lx@add@note`,
`\lx@add@thanks`, `\lx@add@email`, `\lx@add@affiliation`) as a name annotation, as it takes a note macro
(`is_note_macro`, base_utilities/author_block/notes.rs): the corresponding author's `\note{Corresponding author.}` — the template's required
shape — is no part of the name the address spells, where its last word had made "author" the surname (2406.08712's
zhouyi@ for Y. Zhou, 2603.01867's yuanzy@ for Zhiyang Yuan).
The "Prepared for submission to JINST" header line (:22, printed first, :180) is page furniture, not kept; a paper's own
header (its copy's `\gdef\@fpheader{…}`, or its preamble's) is author content, a pubnote (role preprint) at
`\begin{document}`: 2103.06391 "Prepared for submission to JINST (FERMILAB-PUB-21-079-ND-SCD)", 2205.10526, 2311.06155.
The table of contents its `\maketitle` ends with unless `\notoc` (:241-249) is dropped and `\notoc` is a no-op, as in
jheppub's binding (Perl jheppub.sty.ltxml:97), so the family keeps one rule (main session ruling 2026-10-21; whether
JHEP/JINST should print it is a SYNC_STATUS row awaiting a user ruling). The binding stands in for the paper's copy
(`author_files::AUTHOR_FILE_STAND_INS`), so the copy is read after it (OD #731), its own definitions of the binding's
names holding only inside it: its page geometry stays (`\textwidth .72\paperwidth`, the 442pt that `\linewidth`-sized
figures had read raw). Residual: a copy whose own `\maketitle` adds lines (2103.11983's "Published in JINST as DOI:
10.1088/1748-0221/16/07/P07016") loses them, the binding owning `\maketitle` (jheppub the same; SYNC_STATUS). The older
JINST class (`JINST.cls`) keeps its own binding (jinst_cls.rs). Repros package-bindings/jinstpub/{
jinstpub_frontmatter_is_jheppub_s, jinstpub_emails_go_to_the_authors_they_spell,
jinstpub_edited_header_is_a_preprint_note} (beside a modified, shortened jinstpub.sty that keeps the original's
copyright and LPPL 1.3 notice); guards `perfect_kernel_batch78e::{jinstpub_frontmatter_is_jheppub_s,
jinstpub_emails_go_to_the_authors_they_spell, jinstpub_edited_header_is_a_preprint_note}`.

### 802. vmsta's e-mails and addresses are their authors' contacts

vmsta.cls (Modern Stochastics: Theory and Applications, VTeX; shipped, about 71 papers) prints its e-mails and addresses
only from its title page: the 2014-2018 copies write each `\email` to the `.aux` for a later run (vmsta.cls:242-256
`\@email` → `\emailauthor`) and append each `\address[label]` to `\@@@address` (:381-390); the 2018+ copies
(iosart2x-based) take `\ead[label=…]{…}` inside the `\author` (:1263-1297, the title page's e-mail line) and keep an
`\address` list (:871-920). The vmsta binding (OD #789) read the class raw, so the e-mails were lost (1508.02842's
`myus@univ.kiev.ua` nowhere in the output) and the addresses were paragraphs of the deposited title page. Ours
(latexml_contrib vmsta_cls.rs): `\author[labels]{…}` replays the class's own `\author` for its counters and lists and
makes the creator with its labels as annotations (`\lx@add@authors@append`), an `\address[a]` is the affiliation of the
authors labelled `a` and an unlabelled one that of the authors before it with none (`annotate=run`), an `\email` the
contact of the author it follows and an `\ead` that of the author it is in; where the class's own code runs `\ead` (its
replayed `\author`, its deposited title page) it only counts the address for the class's "At least one email address is
required!" check (:550-565) and keeps the e-mail block's font for the history line after it. Perl has no vmsta binding.
Witnesses 1508.02842, 1801.00977, 1411.4499, 1506.02940, 1601.01109 (2014-2018), 1805.02511, 1810.09681, 2001.02487,
1912.07948 (2018+). Open: the 2018+ copies' `\thanksref{cor1}` key in the name (SYNC "quality inventory" row 17). Repros
class-bindings/vmsta/vmsta_emails_and_addresses_are_contacts, class-bindings/vmsta_2018/
vmsta_2018_emails_and_addresses_are_contacts (cut-down classes beside them); guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78e::{vmsta_emails_and_addresses_are_contacts, vmsta_2018_emails_and_addresses_are_contacts}`.

### 803. A frontmatter note all of whose content became contacts is not emitted

An author's `\thanks{\email{…}}` — the A&A and Web of Conferences templates' `\fnmsep\thanks{\email{…}}` /
`\fnsep\thanks{\email{…}}` — digests the `\email` into the author's `email` contact (an annotation made while the note's
content is digested), which left the thanks note empty: `<note role="thanks"/>`, a visible mark opening a note with
nothing in it (2409.01693's "†" after Wolfgang Lucha holding only "thanks:"; 20 of 21 webofc papers of the rev78e
review). Ours (main session ruling 2026-10-21; `\lx@annotate@frontmatter@now`, base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_api.rs): a frontmatter
`ltx:note` whose digested content typesets nothing after one or more annotations were made while digesting it is
dropped, its pending stub removed — for every class whose `\email`, `\affiliation` or other contact setter runs inside a
`\thanks` (aa, webofc, …); the rule covers `ltx:note`s only, not contact-typed notes (elsarticle's `\fntext[f1]{\ead{…}}`
keeps an empty `<contact role="note"/>`, as before; synthetic, 0 corpus cases in the rev78e2 sample). An author's own
empty `\thanks{}` made no annotation and stays a note, as Perl keeps it (the kernel's empty-note behaviour is Perl's).
Residual: a note left holding only a separator or a lead word once its addresses became contacts — `\thanks{\email{a},
\email{b}}` a "," note, `\thanks{e-mail: \email{x}}` an "e-mail: " note (0902.3523's three "E-mail:" notes, 1610.04567's
","; as int45b) — is kept: no further rule (rev78e2). Perl (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml, `\lx@add@thanks` a `role=thanks` contact) emits
an empty thanks contact the same way. Repro class-bindings/aa_thanks_email_leaves_no_empty_note (and webofc's
webofc_authors_take_their_institutes); guards `perfect_kernel_batch78e::{aa_thanks_email_leaves_no_empty_note,
webofc_authors_take_their_institutes}`.

### 804. `\lx@splitting` at `\\` drops the break's `*` and `[…]` from the next piece

`\lx@splitting{op}{delimiters}{tokens}` (Perl Base_Utility.pool.ltxml, `SplitTokens`) cuts at the delimiter tokens
only, so a split at `\\` left the line break's star and optional spacing at the start of the next piece. No Perl binding
splits at `\\`; two Rust ones do, an author list printed as a paragraph whose `\\` is a line break: webofc's `\author`
(#800) and llncs's `\inst`-marked `\author` (llncs_cls.rs `\lx@llncs@author@split`). There `B\inst{2}\\*[2mm] C\inst{1}`
made a creator "*[2mm] C" (the rev78e review's finding 6; synthetic, 0 of 158 webofc papers). Ours: a piece after a
`\\` delimiter loses a leading `*` and `[…]` (`strip_linebreak_options`, which the kernel's own author splitting and
llncs's unmarked list already apply). Repros class-bindings/webofc/webofc_author_line_break_options,
sectioning-frontmatter/llncs_author_line_break_options_with_inst_marks; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78e::{webofc_author_line_break_options, llncs_author_line_break_options_with_inst_marks}`.

### 805. A class's e-mail list goes to the author an address spells, else in author order when the list is the authors'

jheppub.sty's `\emailAdd` (jheppub.sty:126-131; jcappub.sty and jinstpub.sty the same) stores the addresses for its
`\maketitle`, which prints them as one shared "E-mail:" line under the affiliations, attributing none. Perl's
jheppub.sty.ltxml:40-41 gives the n-th `\emailAdd` to the n-th author (`labelseq=author`), which names the wrong author
wherever the list is not in author order (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1030): in the 150 jheppub and 83 jcappub e-mail papers of
the sel78d 30k census, 7 and 15 addresses were on an author another name spells (2407.18115's Michael.Fucilla@ on
Renaud Boussarie and back, 2011.05971, 2212.09776; jcappub 1804.07528, 1806.05015, 2010.13504, 2310.18996, 2407.07862),
and an `\emailAdd{a, b}` listing two authors' addresses was one contact of the first (2406.03543, 2505.23122). Placing
each address by its spelling alone (jinstpub's 78e rule) puts the many addresses no name spells but the list's order
gives right (1303.3040's `zhl61@` for Zhen Liu, 2011.02499's `tpsg4@`/`tpsr@`, 2212.01400's `jss55@`: 40 in the jheppub
sample) on the author block. Ours (`\lx@add@contact@placed[owner=sequence]`, each class command call marked by
`\lx@sequence@call`; the flush's `sequenced_contact_labels`, base_utilities/frontmatter/place.rs), against all the authors of the same
frontmatter flush: an address goes (1) to the author it spells (`address_owners`); else (2) to the author at its place
when the list has one place for each author in their order — no address spells another author than the one at its
place (`addresses_in_order`'s reading of an author block's line), the place the address's, or else the call's (an
author's two addresses in one call, 1710.06069; `\emailAdd{divyeshsolanki98@…, srijuster@…}` for two authors read by
the address, 2308.02445); else (3) where `\lx@add@contact@placed` put it, the group's only author or the author block,
as the PDF's shared line leaves it (a list shorter than the authors orders nothing); and (4) the one address of the list
left on the block of a multi-author paper to the ONE author marked as the corresponding author, where there is one
(#809). Step (1) also
knows the owner a mark gives (iopart's `\ead` under its `\address`, #808: 2311.07087's second `\ead`, `sgess@`, under
`$^4$ SLAC`, is the fifth author's). Step (2) is the user's ruling of 2026-10-21: a list with exactly one address per
author that every spelled address agrees with is evidence of the order, so an unspelled address in it goes to the
author at its place (an inconsistent list sends its unspelled addresses on, to (3) and (4)); it is one function,
`author_order_step`, so a later ruling can switch it off in one change. A flush with no authors (the list after
`\maketitle`, 1903.05554) keeps Perl's rule. jheppub's binding (latexml_package jheppub_sty.rs) defines it, an
`\emailAdd{a, b}` an address each (`\lx@add@contact@list` = `\lx@sequence@call\lx@split@addresses`, which parts a
list at its commas and at an " and ", and writes out the addresses of a braced group of local parts before a shared
domain, `\{a, b\}@x`, in a list of plain text only: a list in markup, `\emailAdd{\mbox{a@x, b@y}}`, is one contact, its
markup kept; 2011.05971's bare `nikolay.bobev, anthony.charles, valentin.reys @kuleuven.be` is no address list, kept
whole); `\lx@add@contact@list` is a frontmatter call by its name, so an `\emailAdd` inside an `\author` stays that
author's one contact (`adds_to_frontmatter`, `is_note_macro`; an address-list contact digested inside another entry
is that entry's, placed by nothing of its own). jcappub and jinstpub (latexml_contrib) take it with the binding, so
the family has one rule (OD #801's jinstpub placement is this one's steps 1 and 4). A/B (int47a → 78f, release, `--preload=ar5iv.sty`; by the reviewer's
spelling test, `emailmatch.py`; E, F and W equal, 0 of 100 random controls changed): jheppub 150 papers (18 outputs
changed), addresses on their spelled author 360 → 386, on another spelled author 7 → 0, on the block 0 → 2 (1802.03677's gear8mike@, 2212.09776's inalecz@ for Ignacy Nałęcz, a `\l` the name
keys drop); jcappub 83 papers (17 changed), 174 → 196, 15 → 0, 0 → 8 (each a list shorter than its authors, none spelled: the n-th
rule's guess there, 1802.07622's `sma74@` likely right, 2407.07862's `hdel@` wrong, is no evidence); jinstpub 23 papers
unchanged. Residuals: a surname letter the name keys drop (`\l`, `ø`; 2212.09776) or a spelling they do not read
(`ue` for `ü`, 2211.05026; two-letter surnames, 2409.18288) leaves an address unspelled; an address that spells two
authors equally (1710.06069's `sjkim0305@` beside two Kims) goes by the order or to the block. Repros
sectioning-frontmatter/{jheppub_emailadd_in_author_order, jheppub_emailadd_one_call_lists_the_authors,
jheppub_emailadd_out_of_order_by_spelling}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch78f::{jheppub_emailadd_in_author_order,
jheppub_emailadd_one_call_lists_the_authors, jheppub_emailadd_out_of_order_by_spelling}`,
`perfect_kernel_batch78e::jinstpub_emails_go_to_the_authors_they_spell`.

### 806. iopart's `\ead` goes to the author it spells, not the last author

iopart.cls:363-364 `\def\ead#1{\vspace*{5pt}\address{E-mail: \mailto{#1}}}`, `\def\mailto#1{{\tt #1}}`: the address
prints as an address block of its own right after the `\address` before it, no name's. Perl's
iopart_support.sty.ltxml:54 `\lx@add@email{#1}` gives it to the last author (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1031): 2311.12551's
benedikt.maier@cern.ch, B. Maier's (author 5 of 7), on T. K. Årrestad; in the 162 iopart `\ead` papers of the census
A/B'd for 78f, int47a put 83 addresses (in 81 of the papers) on an author another name spells. Ours
(iopart_support_sty.rs): the #805 placement (`\lx@add@contact@placed[owner=sequence]`), so an address goes to the author
it spells, else the n-th author's when the `\ead`s are one for each author in order, else the one author requesting

address font, not the binding's `\let\mailto\ead` contact nested in it (0811.0981's `\ead{\mailto{edvard@…},
\mailto{chris.clarkson@…}}`: both addresses and a "," contact on Chris Clarkson; now each on its author). An `\ead`
inside an `\address{…}` is digested with the address and takes its labels, as before (1205.6797, 1607.05491: on the
address's authors, residual). An `\ead` list is split by `\lx@split@addresses` (#805), a shared domain
(`\ead{\{yangqq, yangjh\}@ipp.ac.cn}`, 2607.04241) each of its addresses written out. A/B (int47a → 78f, 162 iopart
`\ead` papers of the census; the reviewer's spelling test, `emailmatch.py`): 112 outputs changed, E/F/W equal;

author: 2205.06148's `daniel.haeupl@` for Häupl, 2311.07087's `sgess@`, 2607.04241's two Yangs); 19 papers only

### 807. An `\inst` mark after a comma is the name's before it

llncs.cls:894-896 `\def\inst#1{\unskip$^{#1}$}`, `\def\fnmsep{\unskip$^,$}` (aa.cls:759-760 the same with
`\unskip\hbox{…}`): the mark takes back the space before it and stands on the name before the comma, so `\author{Clara
Dehman,⏎\inst{1}\fnmsep\inst{2}\fnmsep\inst{3}\fnmsep\inst{4}\thanks{Email: …} Mario Centelles,\inst{5}\fnmsep\inst{6}
\and Xavier Vi\~nas…}` prints "Clara Dehman,¹,²,³,⁴⋆ Mario Centelles,⁵,⁶ and Xavier Viñas⁵,⁶,⁷". The author split
(Perl inst_support.sty.ltxml:33-35 `\lx@splitting{\lx@add@author}{\and\And,}`; ours `split_author_line`) cut at the
comma, so the marks and note opened the next piece: 2401.16957's four affiliations and e-mail note went to Mario
Centelles and his institutes 5-6, a piece of marks only, to no one (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1032). The kernel's
`marks_before_glued_commas` already moved a mark glued to the comma before it (`Ann Able,\textsuperscript{a}`); it did
not know `\inst`, and kept a mark after a space on the next name (`Ann$^1$, $^{*}$Bob`). Ours: `\inst` and a
`\fnmsep`/`\fnsep` between two marks are leading marks there (`leading_inst_marks_end`), and an `\inst` after the
comma's spaces or ties moves too, the spaces it takes back dropped — only where `\inst` is the convention's mark,
decided by its meaning (`inst_takes_back_space`, 78f r2): it starts with `\unskip` (a raw llncs.cls/aa.cls/svjour3.cls),
or it is the request the convention's bindings give it for that definition (`\lx@request@frontmatter@annotation`:
llncs_cls.rs, inst_support_sty.rs, sv_support_sty.rs; inside author content the one `\lx@author@withinst` saved); a class
that defines `\inst` only inside its title, where the names print, has its binding declare that meaning as
`\lx@title@inst`, which decides first (epl_cls.rs, epl2.cls:725 `\def\inst##1{\unskip${}^{##1}$…}`: 1201.1900's
`\author{Zhen Wang,\inst{1,2} Attila Szolnoki,\inst{3} …}`, each name its own marks).
Beamer's `\inst` (beamerbasetitle.sty:169 `\textsuperscript{#1}`) and a document's own `\newcommand{\inst}[1]{$^{#1}$}`
take back no space: `Ann Able\inst{1}, \inst{2}Bob Baker` keeps Bob Baker's 2 (rev78f probes c08, c09). Names that open
with their `\inst`s (`\inst{1}Ann Able, \inst{2}Bob Baker`) keep each its own, as leading superscripts do (`marker_leads`;
rev78f probe c01). Census (26,323 papers of sel78d's 30k): 15 aa/llncs
papers write `,\inst`, `, \inst` or `,~\inst`; A/B 7 of them changed, each now as its PDF (1604.07826, 1811.07968,
2011.09991, 2309.00573, 2404.01383, 2502.20626, 2503.07779: each author's institutes and note its own, where every one
after the first comma had moved one author on; no nameless creator; 1811.07968's B. Nikiel-Wroczyński, whose `,$^{8}$`
is no `\inst`, keeps the mark shown without an institute, where he had held the next author's), the other 8 unchanged. Repros
sectioning-frontmatter/{llncs_comma_before_inst_is_the_name_before, llncs_inst_leading_marks_keep_their_names,
inst_without_unskip_keeps_the_next_name}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch78f::{llncs_comma_before_inst_is_the_name_before,
llncs_inst_leading_marks_keep_their_names, inst_without_unskip_keeps_the_next_name}`.

### 808. iopart's `\ead` goes to the one author its `\address`'s mark names, and each iopart `\author` is a group

iopart.cls:363 `\def\ead#1{\vspace*{5pt}\address{E-mail: \mailto{#1}}}`: an `\ead` prints as an address block of its own
right after the `\address` before it (iopart.cls:246-248, "Use once for each address"), so in the PDF the address stands
inside that address's block, under its mark: 2407.14305's `rockfish3141@` under "¹ Graduate School … Waseda University",
Hidetomo Hoshino's alone. #806 placed it by the spelling or the author order only, so an address no name spells went to
the author block (78f r1) or, in Perl, to the last author (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1031). Ours: the binding's `\address`
records its block's mark (`\lx@address@mark@set`, base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_fields.rs: the operand of the block's one leading mark, none for
an unmarked block or one of several marked lines; the binding's `\author` clears it), and `\lx@iop@ead` passes it as the
contact's mark (`\lx@add@contact@placed[mark=address]`), a weak one: it places only an address that spells no one
(`placed_contact_owner(…, weak)`: 1111.5264's `johnwc@` under `$^6$`, which two authors request, is J W Conklin's `$^1$`,
and stays unplaced by it), on the one author requesting it (2311.07087's `sgess@` under `$^4$ SLAC`, Spencer
Gessner's), and only (a) where the list is no list in author order, which the flush still reads first
(`sequenced_contact_labels` step 2: 1902.07874's `\ead{…, b97202056@gmail.com, …}` of five authors after
`\address{$^9$ …}` is Che-Yu Chen's at place 3; 1710.02251's three `\mailto`s in one `\eads` after `$^{(2)}$` each the
author's at its place), and (b) in a document that writes an e-mail between its addresses, so places its e-mails by
address block (2407.14305, 2311.07087): IOP's guidelines ask for the `\ead` "after the postal address(es)", and an
`\ead` after the last `\address` of a document that writes them all so is under that address by position only — in the
A/B the mark named the wrong author in 3 of the 4 such papers (0910.0753's `wolfgang.muender@`, W Münder's, on C L
Henley; 1111.3344's `knarf@`, Frank Löffler's, on Gabrielle Allen; 1911.06133's `ledou@`, Pierre Le Doussal's, on
Thimothée Thiery; right only in 1209.0173, `jahan@` for Jahanfar Abouie), so there it places nothing
(`_unmarked`, the placement without the mark). A mark-placed address counts as placed for the corresponding-author step
(#809). An `\ead` digested inside an `\address{… \ead{x}}` is that address's, as before. Each iopart
`\author` now starts an author group (`\lx@frontmatter@group@start`, iopart.cls:225-231 typesets each call where it
stands): an `\ead` nothing else places is the group's only author's, a group of two leaves it to the block
(`\author{A. Bal and C. Cole}\address{KIT}\ead{zq1@…}\author{B. Maier}\address{ICL}\ead{yy2@…}`: yy2@ B. Maier's, where
78f r1 put both on the block; rev78f probe i03). A/B (78f r1 → r2, release, `--preload=ar5iv.sty`, all 278 iopart `\ead` papers of the census, E/F/W equal, 9
outputs changed): by the address mark rockfish3141@ and sgess@ placed, each its author's; the four documents whose
`\ead`s all follow the addresses unplaced by it; by the group 2309.16886's `admau@` (Adrian M. Escobar Ruiz, his
`\author`'s only name); the " and " lists of 0710.2104, 1003.0073, 1905.11073, 2308.11095, 2502.04065 an address each on
the author it spells, 1911.05451's `ccdxslj@` (no name spelled) the block's. int47a → r2 over the same 278: addresses on
an author another name spells (the reviewer's spelling test) 119, in 113 papers → 5 — 1205.6797 and 1607.05491 an `\ead`
inside an `\address` (residual, unchanged), 1902.07874 and cond-mat0404018 the test's false flags (each right), 1603.06724
an svjour3 `\institute` line (unchanged from int47a, not this binding) —; on the author they spell 206 → 367. Repros sectioning-frontmatter/{iopart_ead_under_its_address_mark,
iopart_ead_after_all_addresses_takes_no_mark, iopart_author_groups_own_their_ead}; guards

### 809. The one e-mail address left over goes to the one author marked as the corresponding author

A class's address list printed apart from the names (jheppub/jcappub/jinstpub `\emailAdd`, iopart `\ead`; #805, #806)
often lists only the corresponding author's address, which spells no name ("E-mail addresses: only for the
corresponding author", 2510.11030's template comment): #805 left it to the author block, Perl gave it to the first
author. User ruling 2026-10-21: the one address left on the block of a multi-author paper — after the spelling, the
list in author order and the group's only author — goes to the ONE author marked as the corresponding author, by a
"Corresponding author" note or a mark whose legend says so, else it stays the block's. Ours (`marked_corresponding_author`,
step 4 of `sequenced_contact_labels`): an author is marked (a) by a note in their own name that names correspondence
(`\note{Corresponding author.}`, jheppub's; `\thanks`, `\footnote`; a note given just after their `\author`, as it is
placed: 1909.06107), or (b) by a mark they carry whose legend names correspondence — an affiliation line's
(`\author[a,*]` under `\affiliation[*]{Corresponding author}`, 1304.1216's `\affiliation[f]{…Corresponding authors}`;
iopart's `$^{1,*}$` under `\address{$^*$ Author to whom any correspondence should be addressed.}`, 2504.15015) or a
note's: its own mark (jheppub.sty:84-89 `\note[*]{…}`, kept since this round, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1033) or, for a
jheppub-family `\note{…}`, which steps the footnote counter and prints its text under that number beside no name, the
n-th such note's number, written on the names it is about (`\author[a,1]`) — save where an affiliation is labelled
with that number too: there the number on a name is that name's request for the affiliation (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4), so
the note's counter number is no legend (`AuthorNote::numbered`; `\author[1]{Ann Able,\note{Corresponding author.}}`
`\author[1]{Bob Baker}` `\affiliation[1]{Univ A}`: Ann Able alone is marked, rev78f3 probe a6; the shape of 2005.05695,
2005.14143, 2405.09762, 1403.3797, 2101.00866), while a note's own mark (`\note[*]`) stays its legend. Exactly one marked author gets the
address; none, or two and more, leave it to the block (1802.03677: M.V. Smirnov's "Corresponding author." note is note
1, which J.J. Ling carries too; 2606.26596's `\note[*]{Corresponding authors.}` under two `*`s; a set: two noted authors
and a third under a "Corresponding author" legend are three). A legend or note that says something else ("Equal
contribution", 1510.03434's `\note[*]{Since October 1, 2015 at Karlsruhe …}`) marks no one, and a mark with no legend at
all says nothing of correspondence (2111.00753's two `$^{*}$`; 2602.07867's `\author[a,c,d,e,*]{Kun Zhang}`) — save
where the address itself names it the corresponding author's and exactly one candidate carries a `*` no legend explains
(2308.06532's `\emailAdd{zyxu@gzu.edu.cn(Corresponding author)}` and `\author[1,*]{Zhaoyi Xu}`). The candidates are the
authors the address may be of: its author group's, where the class marks groups (iopart's `\author`, #808; recorded on
the contact as `_group`), and of those the ones requesting the mark of the address it is printed under, where the
document places its e-mails by address block (`_marks`; rev78f2 probes i1, i2). A note names correspondence by a phrase
(`names_correspondence`, `CORRESPONDENCE_PHRASE`: "corresponding author(s)", "correspondence to/:/should…", "to whom
(any) correspondence…", "for correspondence" with no word between, so not "a test for the correspondence"; a note opening
with "Correspondence" only before ":" or "to", so not "Correspondence between …"), not by the word alone ("the AdS/CFT
correspondence"); English phrases only, as the census's frontmatter of this population (1,911 jheppub-family and iopart
papers) names correspondence in no other language. Witnesses 1901.08773 (`beril@`, A. Kopylov), 2510.11030
(`hjhspace223@`, J.-H. Ha), 2211.07892 (`yoomin@`, Y. M. Oh), 2308.06532 (`zyxu@`, Zhaoyi Xu); 1802.03677
(`gear8mike@`) and 2111.00753 (`lad@`) the block's. The 78e jinstpub guard's `info@lab.gov` goes to B. Baker, the
note in his `\author` and its number on no other name. A/B (78f r2 → r3 and int47a → r3, release, `--preload=ar5iv.sty`, 1,247 papers: the r2 A/B's 1,140, the review's 66
`\emailAdd` papers that name correspondence, and 41 more of the 1,911 whose frontmatter names it or writes `\note[`; no
"another TeX tree"): E 1,559, F 12, W 53,315 equal, 0 papers worse, 0 of the 100 controls changed; r2 → r3 4 outputs
changed, each right by its source: 1802.03677's `gear8mike@` the block's (the note's 1 on M.V. Smirnov and J.J.
Ling), and the `\note[*]` names whole — 2606.26596's Jia-Jun Wu, 1510.03434's José Zurita, 2404.00867's Paul J.
Steinhardt, who also gets back his affiliation b (#810) and the note; int47a → r3 221. Residual: a corresponding author named only in an
address or affiliation line of another class (1603.06724's svjour3 `G. Mazzarella [corresponding author]. \email{…}`) is
not read; the n-th note's number assumes the footnote counter starts the title page at 0; it counts only the `\note`s
written inside the names — a `\thanks` or `\footnote` there steps the same footnote counter but is not counted, and a
`\note` given apart from the names gets no number (rev78f3 probes a2 `\author[a,1]{Ann Able,}\note{Corresponding
author.}`, a4b `\note{Equal contribution.}` apart before `\author[a,2]{Bob Baker,\note{Corresponding author.}}`: the
later inner note's number is then one too low; 0 realised cases in the 1,247 A/B papers). A/B 78f r3 → r4:
1,251 papers (r3's 1,247 and 2005.05695, 2005.14143, 2405.09762, 2101.00866 — 1403.3797 among them —, release, `--preload=ar5iv.sty`): E 1,559, F 11, W 53,326 equal, 0 worse, 0 outputs changed (temp-dir paths masked; the five a6-shape papers place each address by its spelling, none left over; 1806.01746 times out on both).
