### 810. A label's spacing parts it also as digested

A class's optional `\author[*\,b,c]{…}` labels reach the frontmatter digested, the thin space a U+2009 character, which
`clean_frontmatter_labels` read as part of one label `*_b` (OD #52(o) parts the labels at the spacing as written:
`\,`, `~`, `\quad`), so Paul J. Steinhardt (2404.00867) lost his affiliation b and the `*` of his
`\note[*]{Corresponding author: …}`. Ours (`SPACING_IN_LABEL`, base_utilities/frontmatter/queue_digest.rs): the no-break, en to thin, and narrow
no-break spaces (U+00A0, U+2002-U+2009, U+202F) part labels as their commands do. Perl's cleanFrontmatterLabels parts at
commas only. Repro sectioning-frontmatter/jheppub_note_mark_apart_from_the_names; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78f::jheppub_note_mark_apart_from_the_names`.

### 813. A label after a raw counter step names the object the step numbers, which takes the step's number

LaTeX's `\label` writes the `\@currentlabel` of the last `\refstepcounter` and hyperref's anchor of that step
(latex.ltx:14963-14967); LaTeXML's (Perl latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3782, Document.pm:1098-1127 `floatToLabel`) climbs
to the nearest ancestor that may carry `labels`, and `\ref` prints that element's `refnum`. A step no constructor takes —
a raw `\refstepcounter` — numbers no element, so its labels landed on the enclosing section, whose number `\ref`
printed (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1038). tcolorbox numbers its boxes so: `\newtcbtheorem`, `\newtcolorbox[auto counter]` and
the like put `\addtocounter{\tcbcounter}{-1}\refstepcounter{\tcbcounter}` and the `label=` key's `\label` in the box's
phantom code (tcolorbox.sty:2311, :998, :1154-1161), placed inside the frame picture (:1925 `\pgftext`). Ours:
(1) the kernel's `\refstepcounter` primitive records the step it made with the tags LaTeXML makes for every step
(sect08.rs `\lx@refstepcounter@label`, dialect.rs `note_raw_refstep`; local, as LaTeX's `\@currentlabel`; any other
step forgets it), and a `\label` made while `\@currentlabel` is still that step's `\the<counter>` carries them
(`current_raw_refstep`, with the step's serial); (2) such a label may stop at an `ltx:picture` — the box the step is
made in (`Document::float_to_label_for`) — but not at an object another raw step numbered (the serial in the bookkeeping
attribute `_raw_refstep`: it climbs past, as Perl's); any other label climbs past a picture, as Perl's; the schema gives `ltx:picture`
`Labelled.attributes` and an optional leading `ltx:tags` (LaTeXML-picture.rnc/.rng, LaTeXML.model); (3) the object it
lands on takes the step's tags (`Document::take_raw_refstep_number`) when it has no number of its own and is not a unit
numbered by its heading (an `ltx:title` holder: an unnumbered `\section*` or theorem stays unnumbered); the role-less
display tag is not kept, the box printed its own number; (4) under cleveref, tcolorbox's `label type` (`\label[<box>]`,
:955-968, with `crefname`, :2270) gives the numbered box the type's cleveref forms, adding the roles the counter has no
name for (cleveref_sty.rs `\lx@cleverref@labeltype`, which numbered the box first — it had overwritten the enclosing
section's names); (5) the SVG post-processor keeps a labelled `picture` element — its id, `labels` and `ltx:tags` around
its drawing converted to SVG — where it replaces an unlabelled one (svg.rs). So `\ref` prints pdflatex's number and links
to the box: a delegated listing box (`\newtcblisting`, `\newtcbinputlisting`) labels its first listing line, which
takes the box counter's number. (6) A listing's start forgets the raw step (`forget_raw_refstep` in `\@@listings@block`'s
`before_digest`: listings makes `\@currentlabel` its line number's, lstmisc.sty:1228 `\lst@Init`, :1225), and a
tcolorbox listing box notes its own step again where its phantom code runs in the first line
(`\lx@lst@renote@raw@refstep`, `renote_forgotten_raw_refstep`). (7) An amsmath display's own `\label` names the step held
where the display starts (`hold_raw_refstep_for_display` in `ams_rearrangeable_bindings`/`ams_alignment_bindings`;
the display's `\label` is `\lx@ams@display@label`, an expandable wrapper of the `\label` it replaced that announces
its label, `mark_display_label`, until the kernel's `\lx@label` makes it; the outermost display start forgets one
announced and never made): amsmath's `\label` there is `\label@in@display` (amsmath.sty:1230-1236), made in the row's
tag cell after the cell group restored `\@currentlabel` (:1240-1252). A `{gather}` makes the display tag on every row
(:1621-1627), so a `{gather*}` row's label after a step in its cell is the section's (pdflatex 7), one after a step
before the display the step's, and an `{aligned}`/`{split}` in an `{equation*}` names the step before it (pdflatex 44,
45). The align family (`{align}`, `{flalign}`, `{alignat}`) and `{multline}`, starred or not, hold no step:
`\math@cr@@@align` makes the display tag only under `\iftag@` (:1833-1843), so an untagged row's label is the next
tagged row's (`\df@label` carried: `\begin{align} a&=b \label{n2}\notag \\ c&=d \end{align}` in a `\refstepcounter`
environment is equation 1) or none (`??`), never a held step (78g r2 gave the step, 41/42 for pdflatex's 1/2; review
probe rev78g2 al2.tex). A paragraph box in a display (`{minipage}`, `\parbox`, and the kernel's `\@arrayparboxrestore`)
leaves it (`leave_display_for_parbox`): amsmath's `\@arrayparboxrestore` restores `\label` to `\ltx@label`
(:1237-1238), so its label is made at once with the box's step (`\begin{gather*} a=b
\refstepcounter{foo}\text{\begin{minipage}{2cm}\label{z5}x\end{minipage}}\end{gather*}`: pdflatex 42). The kernel's `\label` a document saved
(`\AtBeginDocument{\let\originallabel\label}`, the `\labelrel` idiom of 2310.19138) labels at once, with the cell's
step ("a"). A label whose step is not the one that numbered an object climbs past it (the `_raw_refstep` mark; a
`{gather*}` row's `\label` after `\labelrel`'s on that row). (8) `\eqno` on a display a raw step numbered
joins that step's `ltx:tags` (`Document::merge_raw_refstep_tags`): `$$ \refstepcounter{foo}\label{x2} c=d \eqno(B) $$`
shows "(B)" and `\ref` prints the step's 42, as pdflatex. (9) A label after a raw step never stops inside an
`ltx:Math` (`within_math` in `float_to_label_for`): a box in math (`\text{\begin{tcolorbox}\label{t1}…}`, `\mbox`) has an
id the math's rendering does not keep, so a label on it dangles (78g r1-r3: `\ref` empty, "Missing Target"); it climbs
to where Perl's lands — the display, which takes the step's number when it has none (a `{gather*}` row, `\[…\]`: pdflatex
41, 43), or past an inline formula the section (pdflatex 42, ours 7, Perl the same). Residuals (pdflatex differs): an unnumbered listing's line
label prints the section's number (pdflatex the line's: listings steps `lstnumber` on every line; the
`ltx:listingline` of an unnumbered listing carries no number); a second raw step in one picture
(`\put(0,0){\refstepcounter{foo}\label{p:a}…}\put(50,0){\refstepcounter{foo}\label{p:b}…}`) labels the section (pdflatex
42: no element of the second `\put` may carry a label — `ltx:g` has no id, a tikz node is `svg:g`). Decided (main
session 2026-10-21): the section fallback stays, no `ltx:g` schema change; giving `ltx:g` `Labelled.attributes`, an id
and a leading `ltx:tags`, and the SVG post-processor an `id` on its `svg:g`, remains only this residual's future path.
An untagged `{align*}`/`{flalign*}`/`{multline*}` row's label, which amsmath never makes (pdflatex `??`, and "Multiple
\label's" at the next label), labels the row or the section as before (Perl the same); a kernel `\label` a document
saved, in a later `{align*}` row than a raw step made in a cell (`u&=v \refstepcounter{foo}\oldlabel{o2} \\ w&=x
\oldlabel{o3}`), names that step (ours 45; pdflatex the section's 7: the cell group restored `\@currentlabel`; review
probe rev78g2 obs.tex o3); a `$$…$$` label after an `{align*}` whose cell made a raw step names no step (`\refstepcounter{foo}
\lstinputlisting[numbers=left]{code.txt}` … `\begin{align*} u&=v \refstepcounter{foo}\\ w&=x \end{align*} $$ a=b
\label{d3} $$`: ours the section's 7, pdflatex the step before the display, 42; leak2.tex d3); a label after an `\eqno`
(`$$ \refstepcounter{foo} c=d \eqno(E) \label{x5}$$`) is the `\eqno` tag's "(E)" (pdflatex 43, the step's; int47a the
same; eqno.tex x5); an
object with its own number keeps it (`\begin{equation} p=q \refstepcounter{foo}\label{e4}\end{equation}` pdflatex 42,
ours the equation's; an `\item` likewise; a numbered `{align}`/`{gather}` row's number wins over the step of a
paragraph box or a box in its cell, `\begin{align} a&=b \refstepcounter{foo}\text{\begin{minipage}{2cm}\label{y7}x\end{minipage}}
\end{align}` pdflatex 48, ours 1; review probes rev78g3 pb2.tex y7, cr.tex w2); a raw step in running text labels the paragraph's section (`ltx:para` holds
no `ltx:tags`; Perl the same); and (pre-existing, not 78g's) cleveref's `\label[]` inside an `equation` gives "condition 1"
where pdflatex prints `??`. A/B (the sel78d census's 150 `tcb_label_ref` papers + 100 random): 8 papers changed
references, all 44 labels on boxes with pdflatex's `.aux` number; 2 others gained numbers on unreferenced boxes (their
inner ids shifted by one, the numbered object's tags first); 0 Error/Fatal changes. Residual too: a box whose listing
numbers its lines keeps the label on the numbered first line, whose line number `\ref` prints. Witnesses 2505.20088,
2311.09542, 2509.17784, 2602.03411, 2606.06976 (`\newtcolorbox[auto counter]`), 2402.06608 (`[blend into=figures]`,
the figure counter), 2506.01072 (`\newtcbtheorem`), 2609.20563 (`\newtcblisting`). Repros tools/perfect_kernel/repros/cross-references/; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78g::{tcb_box_label_takes_the_box_number, tcb_listing_box_label_takes_the_box_number,
picture_step_label_takes_the_step_number, tcb_theorem_cref_names_the_box_type, listing_label_names_no_step_before_it,
amsmath_row_label_names_the_display_step, unnumbered_display_label_takes_the_step_number,
picture_second_step_label_climbs, amsmath_saved_kernel_label_names_the_cell_step,
math_box_label_climbs_to_the_display}` (the last three and the align-family, `{multline*}`, `{aligned}` and minipage rows
of `amsmath_row_label_names_the_display_step` 78g r2-r4).

### 823. biblatex's own `.bib` fields are read by the biblatex binding only

The `.bib` reader's handlers for biblatex's field names (biblatex manual §2.2.2: `journaltitle`, `location`, `urldate`,
`titleaddon`, `addendum`, `maintitle`, `mainsubtitle`, `maintitleaddon`, `booksubtitle`, `booktitleaddon`,
`issuetitle`, `issuesubtitle`, `eventtitle`, `eventtitleaddon`, `venue`, `eventdate`, `editora`-`editorc`,
`annotation`, and the per-type variants that nest them in a host or event: 47 in all, batches 56ie, 56ii and 57) were
defined in the BibTeX pool (bibtex.rs), so every route read them — under natbib or the classic styles too, where a
`.bst` declares a closed field list without them (plainnat, apsrev4-1) and bibtex(1) never writes them to the `.bbl`.
Perl's pool has none of them (they are `\bib@field@default@default` data, BibTeX.pool.ltxml:346). A paper with no
`.bbl` printed what its PDF does not have: "Accessed: 2025-08-15" (2606.11822 [9]; 2602.10008's 54 apsrev4-1 entries),
"Note: <addendum>", the main title before the title, and a `journaltitle={\undefinedmacro Jt}` raised
`Error:undefined` where pdflatex has 0. Ours (78i, bibtex.rs `define_biblatex_fields`): the handlers are defined by
the biblatex binding after its `LoadPool!("BibTeX")` (biblatex_sty.rs, beside 77a r5's `shorthand`/`labelalpha`), for
both of biblatex's routes (a `.bbl`'s entries, a `.bib` rendered without biber), and on the BibTeX route only for the
fields the document's style declares in its `.bst`'s `ENTRY` list (`bst_declared_fields`: the `\bibliographystyle`
recorded as `BIBSTYLE`, the `.bst` found on the search path) — what bibtex(1) copies for the style to print:
ACM-Reference-Format.bst:38 `location` (printed after the event, :1318-1342; 2603.25517, 2601.12610), sn-mathphys.bst
and mdpi.bst `urldate` (2607.28080, 2511.08819, 2608.12223). Elsewhere the fields are raw `bib-data`, as in Perl. OD #289's `annotation` and 56ie's biblatex names (the entry for the subtitle and host rows) are biblatex-only
accordingly. Repros index-bib/natbib_biblatex_only_fields_are_raw_data (red int47a) and its twin
index-bib/biblatex_prints_its_own_fields, index-bib/bst_declared_biblatex_field_is_printed; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78i::{natbib_biblatex_only_fields_are_raw_data, biblatex_prints_its_own_fields,
bst_declared_biblatex_field_is_printed}`, `06_cluster_bibliography`'s biblatex field guards.

### 824. hyperref's PDF information strings are expanded when `\hypersetup` sets them

hyperref sets `pdftitle`, `pdfauthor`, `pdfsubject`, `pdfkeywords` (and the rest of its information keys) by
`\pdfstringdef\@pdf<key>{#1}` (hyperref.sty:3543-3600): expanded at once with the document's markup made harmless, the
string its characters. Perl records the value's source text (hyperref.sty.ltxml:133 `ToString`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
#1050), so `pdftitle={\mytitle}` was the metadata `<rdf content="\mytitle" property="dcterms:title"/>` (1210.7805
`\OfficialTitle`; resphilosophica.cls:311/:324 `pdftitle=\@title`, `pdfauthor=\authors` in every paper of that class).
Ours (78i, hyperref_sty.rs `pdf_string`): the value of `pdftitle`, `pdfauthor`, `pdfsubject`, `pdfkeywords` and
`pdfcopyright` is expanded by `\lx@pdfstringdef` — hyperref's `\pdfstringdef` in brief (:386-560): `\protect` empty, the
font and size commands their argument or nothing, `\\`, `~` and the other spaces a space, `\texorpdfstring` its PDF
branch, labels, index entries and error messages gobbled, then the document's `\pdfstringdefPreHook` — and, as for
hyperref's own `pdfusetitle` title (`\Hy@UseMaketitleString`, :6248-6266), `\thanks` and the note commands gobbled,
so that expanding the title makes no second note; the result's characters are kept (a control sequence still
unexpanded, a brace, a math shift, a script mark dropped: `$x^2$` is "x2" as in the PDF); puenc.def's text glyphs are
their characters in `\lx@pdfstringdef`'s group (`\DeclareTextCommand{\ss}{PU}{\80\337}` …: `\ss` ß, `\i` ı, `\j` ȷ,
`\o`, `\O`, `\ae`, `\AE`, `\oe`, `\OE`, `\l`, `\L`, `\dh`, `\th`, `\ng`, `\dj`, `\ij` and their capitals, `\SS` "SS",
latex.ltx:564's `\aa` å) and so are its text symbols (78i r3: `\textendash` :1082 –, `\textemdash` —, `\textsection` :184
§, `\textparagraph` ¶, `\textdagger` †, `\textdaggerdbl` ‡, `\textcopyright` ©, `\textregistered` ®, `\texttrademark`
™, `\textsterling` £, `\textellipsis` …, the `\textquote*` and `\quote*base` quotes, `\guillemot*`/`\guillemet*`,
`\guilsingl*`, `\textdegree` °, `\textbullet` •, `\textexclamdown`, `\textquestiondown`, with the kernel's names `\S`,
`\P`, `\dag`, `\ddag`, `\copyright`, `\pounds` and hyperref.sty:416-418's `\ldots`, `\dots`; each `\string`s its
character, which the utf8 input encoding makes active as the very command), `---`, `--`, `` !` ``, `` ?` `` are the
dashes and inverted marks hyperref substitutes in the expanded string (hyperref.sty:620-623; r2 "AB, 2, , , …",
"Pre--post---end", pdfinfo "A–B, §2, †, …", "Pre–post—end"), the text accents composed on the next character as the PU encoding composes them (`\"o` "ö";
on `\i` and `\j` the dotted letter, puenc.def:172-264 `\DeclareTextCompositeCommand{\'}{PU}{\i}{\80\355}`, so
`Mart\'{\i}nez` is "Martínez" and `\.{\i}` "i"), and the logos spelled (`\TeX`, `\LaTeX`: our logos are locked
constructors, which `\pdfstringdef`'s `\def\TeX{TeX}` cannot reach). The expansion happens when the key is
set, hyperref's own timing: `\hypersetup{pdftitle=\@title}` before `\title{…}` is the kernel's `\@title` as in the PDF
("title" — `\@` then the letters), one after it is the title, and a class's `\hypersetup` inside its `\maketitle`
(resphilosophica) sees its local definitions. Beyond hyperref: a `\and` in a PDF string is "; ", the separator of
hyperref's own `pdfusetitle` author (:6255), where `\pdfstringdef` makes garbage of it (pdfinfo "Ann Able [t]cBob
Baker"). The `\@pdf<key>` macros keep the value's tokens, as before (packages read them as text: nlctuserguide.sty's
`author={\@pdfauthor}`). Repros sectioning-frontmatter/{hyperref_pdfinfo_expands_macros (red 60m),
hyperref_pdfinfo_drops_notes_and_markup, hyperref_pdfinfo_text_symbols}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78i::{hyperref_metadata_is_expanded, hyperref_metadata_drops_notes_and_markup,
hyperref_metadata_text_symbols}`.

### 825. An AMS-TeX paper's own style is read raw unless it builds on another style

amstex.tex:1731 `\def\documentstyle#1{\W@{}\input #1.sty\relax}`. Perl's `\documentstyle` loads only a binding
(AmSTeX.pool.ltxml:71 `notex => 1`) and falls back to amsppt (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1051), so a paper's own style was
never read: amams.sty (Annals of Mathematics; math0402285, math9806089) defines `\annalsline`, `\received`,
`\startingpage` and a one-argument `\title`, which met amsppt's `\title … \endtitle` and read the whole paper as the
title (Fatal:Mouth:EoF, 0 words); 1412.7214's phd.sty its `\ThesisTitle`, `\Committee` and `\Contents` (16 Errors, 97
words). Ours (78i, amstex.rs): a style with no binding that the search path finds is read raw, as `\input` reads it —
unless it `\input`s another style (`\input amsppt.sty`, `\input ams-p.sty`: `inputs_a_style`), when it is a variation on
that style, whose changes are to internals of the style it builds on (gr-qc9507042's fic.sty redefines amsppt's
`\titlebox@`, `\thethanks@`; read raw over the amsppt binding it ended in a Fatal pushback runaway and 16 Errors), or
its parent is missing (math0406145's grubb-p.sty and 0803.2668's conm-p-mod.sty `\input ams-p.sty`, not in TeX Live):
then the amsppt binding stands in, as before. amstex.tex's `\Invalid@` (:251-252), with which such a style marks the
commands it disallows, is defined. amams.sty redefines `\ifdefined` (amams.sty:1099, a three-argument label test,
as pre-e-TeX styles did); LaTeXML's own macros test with the kernel's `\lx@ifdefined` (etex.rs, `\let` to e-TeX's
primitive: `\lx@latin@name`, the frontmatter stores' nulls, `\makeindex`, `\makeglossary`), which the redefinition
cannot reach; `\loggingall` and `\tracingnone` keep the public `\ifdefined`, as latex.ltx:662/:679 and Perl
plain_base.pool.ltxml:40/:56 do (78i r2; math0402285 3 → 0 Errors; repro parameter-conditional/kernel_ifdefined_survives_a_document_redefinition,
guard `perfect_kernel_batch78i::kernel_ifdefined_survives_a_document_redefinition`). The errors these papers still
raise are our emulation's, not the style's (`tex` converts math9906120 clean): amams's `\everydisplay{\lookforbreak}`
(amams.sty:585-590) over amstex's `\multline` (math9906120: 43 "Use \Bbb only in math", 43 "Script ^/_ can only
appear in math mode", Fatal:TooManyErrors, from JohanssonArchive.tex:250), its `\split` over amstex.tex internals the
AmSTeX pool does not have (`\ifinany@`; math9806089's 9 split errors); SYNC_STATUS "AMS-TeX papers read through their
own amams.sty". Repro
amstex/amstex_local_style_is_read (with a stand-in amslocal.sty written from scratch: amams.sty states no licence);
guard `perfect_kernel_batch78i::amstex_local_style_is_read`.

### 829. thmtools names an unnamed theorem by its environment, case-modified as its options say

thm-kv.sty:359 names a `\declaretheorem{<env>}` without `name=`/`title=`/`heading=` `\thmt@modifycase <env>`, which is
`\protect\MakeUppercase` by default and `\MakeLowercase` or nothing under thmtools' `lowercase`/`anycase` options
(thmtools.sty:35-39 passes them to thm-kv, thm-kv.sty:30-42): `\MakeUppercase` takes the first token only, so `{defn}`
is headed "Defn 1.2". Perl hardwires `\MakeUppercase` (thmtools.sty.ltxml:80-82) and ignores the options; ours had no
name at all ("1.2", typerefnum " 1.2"; 1505.04294's 90 theorems, 70 papers of the census without a name key). Ours
(78k, thmtools_sty.rs): the binding declares thm-kv's three options and defaults the name to `\thmt@modifycase` before
the environment's name. Repros package-bindings/{thmtools_unnamed_theorem_is_headed_by_its_environment,
thmtools_lowercase_option_lowercases_the_unnamed_theorem}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch78k::{thmtools_unnamed_theorem_is_headed_by_its_environment,
thmtools_unnamed_theorem_follows_the_case_option}`.

### 830. bibentry's store mode: `\nobibliography` keeps each `.bbl` entry for `\bibentry`

bibentry.sty:42-66: `\nobibliography{<db>}` and `\nobibliography*` read the `.bbl` with `{thebibliography}` and
`\bibitem` redefined so that each entry's text up to its blank line is stored as `\BR@r@<key>` (`\BR@c@bibitem#1 #2
\par`) and nothing is printed; `\bibentry{<key>}` `\nocite`s the key and prints the stored text without its final
period (`\BR@nodot`). Perl has no binding (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1059); read raw, our kernel's locked `{thebibliography}`
refuses the redefinition, so `\nobibliography*` printed the whole list and each `\bibentry` nothing (2505.07606: 29 empty
entries, two lists; 2210.16098: 48 lines "."). Ours (78k, latexml_contrib bibentry_sty.rs): `\lx@BR@store` reads the
`<jobname>.bbl` itself (the file `\bibliography`'s bbl route reads), tokenizes it under the standard catcodes and stores
each `\bibitem[<label>]{<key>}`'s tokens up to `\par`, the next `\bibitem` or the list's `\end` (where TeX's delimited
read would run on into the next entry when no blank line separates them); the stored text is digested where
`\bibentry` stands. A paper with no `.bbl` (only its `.bib`) stores nothing; each `\bibentry` then reports its key in a
Warning (pdflatex: its `\nocite`'s undefined citation). bibentry's `\def\bibliography` wrapper (bibentry.sty:74-75),
which resets the star's flag, is refused by the locked `\bibliography`, so the `\AtEndDocument` warning for a
`\nobibliography*` without a later `\bibliography` (:76-79) asks the kernel's count of `\bibliography` calls
(`lx_bibliography_calls`, sect11.rs `\lx@ifusebbl`) instead. bibentry's `\BR@b@bibitem`, `\BR@c@bibitem` and `\BR@nodot`
are defined as there for code that redefines them (tufte-common.def:876-882, whose margin citations are `\bibentry`s).
Repro index-bib/bibentry_prints_the_stored_entry; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78k::bibentry_prints_the_stored_entry`.

### 831. bibentry's `\nobibliography{<db>}` without the star keeps the list its citations resolve to

In TeX, `\nobibliography{<db>}` prints no list, but its `\bibitem`s (the original `\BR@bibitem`, bibentry.sty:49-53)
still write the `\bibcite` labels every `\cite` resolves to. Our citations resolve to the `ltx:bibitem`s of a
bibliography in the document: without a list every `\cite` would be a "Missing Entry for citation" (2210.16098's 33
`\cite`s, AAAI's `\nobibliography{aaai23}` idiom). By the charter's order (semantic markup before PDF fidelity), the
starless form stores the entries for `\bibentry` and builds the list where it stands, as before: the PDF's list-less
page differs; the starred form (followed by a `\bibliography`) builds none, so one list stands as in the PDF. Repro
index-bib/bibentry_nobibliography_keeps_the_list_its_citations_resolve_to; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78k::bibentry_nobibliography_keeps_the_list_its_citations_resolve_to`.

### 834. tabularray's `\SetCell[c=<n>,r=<m>]` spans columns and rows

tabularray.sty:2542-2615: `\SetCell[<outer>]{<inner>}` sets a cell's `r=`/`c=` span (`cell/outer` keys, :2611-2615) and
its style (`cell/inner`, :2617-2642); the author leaves the covered cells empty and tabularray typesets the spanned cell
over them. Perl's ar5iv stub maps `tblr` to `tabular` and has no `\SetCell`; ours had it as a no-op (#384), so "Wide"
(`c=2`) sat in one cell beside a stray empty `<td/>` and "Tall" (`r=2`) spanned no row. Ours (78l, tabularray_sty.rs
`tblr_span_cells`): `\lx@tblr@env` reads the table body whole, as tabularray's `+b` argument holds it (:3463; before,
only for `evaluate=`/`expand=`), and when it holds a `\SetCell` at a cell's start, after any row-level rule command, at
the body's own level (tabularray's extractor takes every table command at a cell's start, with its `[…]`/`{…}`
arguments, among the cell's own tokens unexpanded, :3770-3860 — `\hline`, `\hline[1pt]`, `\cline{1-2}`, `\midrule`,
`\cmidrule[…](lr){…}`, `\SetRow{…}`, `\SetHline`, …; the `*` and `[<space>]` of the row end before it, `\\[2pt]`;
2308.16907's 11 `\hline \SetCell`, 2507.01654, 2305.00635, 2502.18449, 2404.12789, 2601.16161, 2604.10925, 2606.09108, a 78l r1
draft taking only a first-token `\SetCell`; never one in braces or in a cell's environment), rewrites that cell (a body without one is put back as read): `r=<m>` becomes `\lx@tblr@cell@span{<m>}`, the row span `\multirow` sets (multirow_sty.rs
`\lx@multirow@setup`), and `c=<n>` turns the `n-1` column separators after the cell's text into the primitive `\span`
(`\lx@span`, as `\multispan` spans), so the cell keeps its columns' templates — their rules and the first one's
alignment, as tabularray's spanned cell keeps the first column's `halign`. A covered cell's text, if the author wrote
any, stays in the spanned cell (tabularray hides it; authored content is kept, FIDELITY_CHARTER §2). The inner keys stay
unrendered, `halign` (`l`, `c`, `r`, `halign=`) included: a `\multicolumn{<n>}{<halign>}` would replace the columns'
templates and drop their rules, which tabularray draws apart from the cell (`colspec={Q[l]|l}` with
`\SetCell[c=1]{c}`, 2408.02133; `\SetCell{c, gray9}` in a `c |` column, 2403.06461; both lost a `border` in a 78l
draft), so `\SetCell[c=2]{c}` over `l` columns is left-aligned where pdflatex centres it. `\SetCells` (every cell,
:2510) and the inner spec's `cell{i}{j}={r=…,c=…}{…}` spans are not modelled. Residuals: a row span over a cell below
that holds text is not applied — the cell below keeps its own cell and the spanned one spans no row (`\SetCell[r=2]{c}
T & … \\ Below & …`, where tabularray hides "Below" under "T"; the text stays, FIDELITY_CHARTER §2); a math table's
`tex=` reverts a spanned row with its `\span`s as `\hfil\hfil` (`\SetCell[c=2]{c} mx & \\` in a `$…$` tblr:
"mx\hfil\hfil\\"). Probe `tblr.tex` (sel78k; 25 sample papers call `\SetCell`/`\SetCells`); 78l review probes `tb.tex`,
`tb2.tex`. Repros alignment-bindings/tblr_setcell_spans_columns_and_rows, alignment-bindings/tblr_setcell_after_a_row_rule_spans;
guards `perfect_kernel_batch78l::{tblr_setcell_spans_columns_and_rows, tblr_setcell_after_a_row_rule_spans}`.

### 837. The frontmatter observer records and lexes the author calls, in shadow mode

Beyond Perl, infrastructure only: Perl reads an author block as tokens (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:676-700, `@authorsplits`
and `positionOf`), and so does our analyser (`base_utilities/author_block/`). FM S2a.1 (frontmatter model M3 stage
S2a, KERNEL_CAPABILITIES K23 step 1; design `agent_reports/2026-10-21_fms2_design_refresh.md` §2, defaults 1, 2, 6 and
9 adopted by the user 2026-10-21) adds an observer that reads what TeX prints instead, beside the conversion, in
`base_utilities/frontmatter/observer/`. It runs only under the runtime environment variable `LATEXML_FM_SHADOW=1` (read
once per process; a test sets the thread's override, `set_fm_shadow_override`), which stays **unset on the fleet**
(`cortex_worker` writes no dump; the shadow census runs through the local CLI), and decides nothing: a conversion's XML
and its log are the same with and without it (guard `shadow_switch_leaves_the_xml_unchanged`, over the review's
adversarial shapes: an `\aftergroup`, a `\thanks` holding a `\label` with a `\ref` to it, a `\footnote`, a `\gdef` and a
`\stepcounter`, an unclosed `\begingroup`, an undefined command, an `\input` in the field).
- **Ledger** (`ledger.rs`): a block per `\author`-family call — `\lx@add@authors@adaptive` (the kernel `\author`,
  policy `kernel`), `\lx@add@authors`, `@append`, `@list`, `\lx@add@author@split`, `\lx@ijcai@names` — with its
  `replace`/`sectioned`/`cautious` options, keyvals, the frontmatter queue's length and queued authors at the call (and
  the `epoch`, the flushes before it: each flush empties the queue, so a position is one queue's), and its positions in
  the author field: the kernel block's are `\lx@field@mark`'s own (S1, #715; the mark confirms the block it is the
  stored copy of), a binding call's are projected past every earlier stamp, as the new argument stamper
  `\lx@field@stamp{<field>}{<tokens>}` (frontmatter_fields.rs; no call site yet, S2b stamps the calls) would give them;
  past the 14-bit position budget (cumulative per document) the block is unstamped. Per `\title` call the S1 stamp. Per
  queued creator, contact or note (`queue_front_matter`, gated on the switch before anything is built) an API call,
  `inside` when the latest block's own expansion made it: nothing the input held at the block's call has been read since
  (core `gullet::input_unread_since`, a mark of the pushback and the mouth position). Nothing is recorded while the
  frontmatter is frozen (a replayed class setter, a speculative run, the rehearsal) or a stand-in copy reads its
  defaults. A block not rehearsed says why (`SkipReason`: out of positions, empty, no flush after the call, the
  rehearsal's own Fatal, not undone; one no journal could open for — the flush inside a speculative run — waits for the
  next flush, `Outcome::Deferred`, and reports `journal unavailable` if none rehearses it).
- **Rehearsal** (`rehearsal.rs`): at the flush (`digest_front_matter`) each block not yet rehearsed is digested from its
  stamped tokens in text mode, in a group of Layer-B event bindings (`\and`/`\And`/`\AND` a column, which one kept; `\\`,
  `\newline`, `\linebreak`, `\par` a row; `\thanks`, `\footnote`, `\footnotetext` a note reading its argument;
  `\footnotemark`, `\inst` marks; `\label` the note's label; `\lx@annotate@frontmatter` and the defined contact commands
  `\email`, `\url`, `\href`, `\orcidlink`, `\affil`, `\address`, … contacts; `\thefootnote` the title's footnote marks:
  the title's `\thefootnote` hook `\lx@title@thefootnote` when one is defined — the kernel's own, the one the printed
  title marks follow (78o r2, #851: rehearsal.rs `TITLE_FOOTNOTE_HOOK` is `latex_constructs::TITLE_THEFOOTNOTE`;
  article, report and book define it `\@fnsymbol\c@footnote`), else the kernel `\maketitle`'s `\@fnsymbol\c@footnote`
  — for a class numbering its title's marks otherwise: revtex4-2.cls:3040-3041 `\frontmatter@thefootnote` is
  `\@fnsymbol` by default and `\@alph` only under its `altaffilletter` option, :5978; guards
  `title_footnote_hook_overrides_fnsymbol`, `perfect_kernel_batch78o::declared_title_thefootnote_prints_the_marks_the_observer_labels`), through
  the speculative-run engine of #767 (assignments journalled and rolled back, diagnostics held and discarded, terminal
  output muted, the frontmatter frozen), with progress notes silenced (core `error::SilenceProgressNotesGuard`: an
  `\input` in the field reads its file again, and its `(Processing content …` note is not the conversion's) and with the
  field ledger put back after it (core `token::FieldLedgerScope`: the serials, the pending cover, the settled flag and
  the stamped gate as they were). The whole group — its opening, the digestion, its end — reads from a mouth of its own (`reading_from_mouth`,
  closed with whatever is left), under a current token of its own: what the group's end unreads (an `\aftergroup` of the
  block's, core `pop_stack_frame_with`) never reaches the document's input, and `egroup`'s template-brace check never
  sees the document's token. No counter is stepped: a bare `\footnotemark` prints `\thefootnote` with `\c@footnote` set
  only inside its mark, to the counter's value at the rehearsal's start plus the steps the block's `\thanks`,
  `\footnote` and bare marks made before it (`\footnotemark[<n>]` at <n>), as latex.ltx `\footnotemark`/`\@xfootnotemark`
  print. No `tabular[t]{c}`: a stray `&` digests as the `&` constructor's whatsit, which errs only when it is built into
  the document (tex_tables.rs) — never in the rehearsal, so nothing is held for it —, and the lexer reads it as a column
  separator. A Fatal of its own skips the block, a resource Fatal propagates.
- **Event lexer** (`events.rs`): the digested list into Name, Mark (its label; `symbol` when it prints only LaTeX's
  `\@fnsymbol` characters, whatever command printed it; its line's first ink), Sep (column with its command — `\and`,
  `\And`, `\AND`, or `column` `&` for an alignment tab —, comma — a mark printing only a comma, llncs's `\fnmsep`, is
  one —, the word "and" or a printed `\&`, a gap: ≥ 2 spacing items, one wider
  than an interword space, or one holding fill glue — `\hfil`/`\hfill`, tex_glue.rs `isFill`, always a separator —, with
  its item count, its natural width in em of the box's font from a spacing box's `width` property (`\hspace`, `\hskip`;
  fill glue 0) or the space characters printed, and `fill`), Break (the rehearsal's `\\` and also the kernel's
  `\lx@newline`, `\lx@parboxnewline` and `\@normalcr` whatsits: `\centering`/`\raggedright`/`\raggedleft` let `\\` be
  `\@normalcr`, a minipage `\lx@newline`, a parbox's body `\lx@parboxnewline`, past the rehearsal's binding; guard
  `breaks_survive_a_rebound_newline`), Contact, Note (label, inner contacts, `thanks` or `footnotetext`), Layout (a
  container, an alignment cell, a font change between runs) and, from the ledger, the API calls after the block; each
  with its span of the field's positions (`fieldProv`/`fieldSerial`, `gullet::field_cover_of`) and its ink. A
  container's content is the arguments it shows (util_text.rs `shown_arguments`, as `typesets_content` reads them) and
  its body: a placement keyword is none (the `[t]` of `\begin{tabular}[t]{c}` and `\parbox[t]`, the `[l]` of
  `\makebox[3cm][l]`, the `[b]` of `\begin{minipage}[b]`; an image, showing none of its arguments, is a Layout event of
its own, not its file name — 2503.08161's logos —; guard `placement_arguments_are_not_names`).
- **Dump**: the CLI writes `<dest>.fmshadow.json` (`write_fm_shadow`: the entries in call order and a summary) after the
  output; a failure to write it is a Warning, not the conversion's failure. `cortex_worker` writes none.
- **Core**: the status line's undefined macros and missing files are listed sorted (`error::get_status_message`): a hash
  map's order follows the symbols' interning history, which the rehearsal (or any new definition) changes; Perl
  State.pm:771 lists `keys %{$$status{undefined}}`, a random hash order, so either order is Perl's.

Departures from the design note §2 (for S2a.2): the per-block policy id is the hook's family (the policy table, keyed on
the binding owning the `\author` meaning and the hook, is S2a.2's); single-author API calls (`\lx@add@creator`,
authblk's unlabelled `\author`) are API calls, not blocks (the comparator's "no block" class); contacts are rebound only
where the document defines them (an undefined one errs, held, as in pdflatex); a Note carries no mark (only the optional
number given to it: the symbol its `\thanks` prints is not recorded); a font-change Layout event has no span; a gap's
em is its box's font's quad (10pt where it has no font); a font switched inside a run of ink is no event there: the
run stays one Name and the Layout event, which compares a run's first font with the previous run's, shows at the next
run (`Ann Able\begingroup\bfseries Bob \and Carl`: after the `\and`, before "Carl"; splitting the run at the switch
would split every name set with a small-caps surname — gretsi's `first \textsc{last}`, 2508.03934 — into two Names:
S2a.2's call; guard `font_switch_inside_a_run_keeps_the_name`); tokens an `\input` in the field reads come from the
file and carry no position, so their events have no span (guard `input_field_events_carry_no_span`); `\corref`, `\fnref`, `\thanksref` and `\ead` are not bound
(they digest as their binding defines them, read by what they print); a bare `\footnotemark`'s label is the kernel
`\maketitle`'s `\@fnsymbol` mark unless the title's own is declared through `\lx@title@thefootnote` (above; article,
report and book declare `\@fnsymbol`, a title-page class none — report and book print arabic there —, and revtex's
default is `\@fnsymbol` too, `\@alph` only under `altaffilletter`), and assumes the counter at
the flush is the one at `\maketitle`; a binding block's projected positions may coincide with positions a later real
stamp gives (spans are unique only within a block: key an event by (block index, span); once S2b stamps for real,
projected must equal stamped); an event ending its block stops short of a trailing delimiter (`\footnotemark[1]}`'s
`]`: core `gullet::field_cover_of` ends a cover at the field's next token, and there is none); a mark printing only a
`\ref` (A&A's `\inst{\ref{ipag}}`, 1809.08354) prints nothing at digestion — the reference resolves in post — and is
no mark (S2a.2: read the `\ref`'s label). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchfms2a1::*` (event lists of the design probes, the gretsi
repro, 2401.16957's `,\inst` shape and the SYNC rows 46-48, 53, 62, 64, 66 shapes; spans in two shapes, gap widths and
fill, footnotemark labels and `\and` commands, the `inside` flags; the stamper's provenance and base; XML and log
unchanged by the switch; the CLI dump only under it, 0 errors and 0 warnings; r3, review revfms2a1_2: placement
arguments, rebound line breaks, the `&` column, the title-footnote hook, a font switch inside a run, an `\input`'s
spans; engine unit test `shadow::tests::deferred_block_reports_the_journal_not_the_flush`); repros `sectioning-frontmatter/observer_*`
(the four symbol-line and mark-macro ones RED for their output, the S2b targets: witness 2304.13998's shape and the
design probes; `observer_rehearsal_aftergroup_stays_inside` and `observer_fill_gap_and_footnotemark_labels` GREEN, the
review's probes), `class-bindings/gretsi_v13_shared_mark_affiliation` (2508.03934).

**S2a.2: the resolver, the policy table and the comparator, still shadow only** (fms2a2; design note §2 points 1-9, §3
S2a, §5 defaults 4, 5, 6, 8, 9; the main session's S2a.2 notes). Under the switch the dump gains `resolved`: the ledger's
blocks and the API calls made apart from them, read into the tuples `ab_audit`'s `front.rs` extracts — each creator's
name without its marks, its requests (the marks shown on it), its affiliations, contacts and notes, the author block's
own (the XML's trailing nameless creator, #159) — each association with the rule that decided it and its source keyed by
(ledger index, span) (spans are unique only within a block; S2b's assertion that a projected range is the stamped one,
`ledger::projected_is_stamped`, is in place and off, `ASSERT_PROJECTED_IS_STAMPED`). Nothing of it reaches the output
(guard `perfect_kernel_batchfms2a2::resolver_leaves_the_xml_unchanged`).
- **Resolver** (`resolver/`, Layer C, class-independent; split by stage in r4): rows from `Break`, columns from `Sep(And)`/alignment tabs
  (unless the policy reads `\and` as inline); a line's type from its first ink — a mark-led line is labelled (unless it
  is the block's first line and its entries read as names whose marks a later line answers: the prefix convention), a
  column's first line or one whose name pieces each read as a name (`name_count`, `reads_as_affiliation`,
  `is_name_qualifier`) is a names line, a line of one link printing a name that name, a line of contacts a contact
  line, any other unmarked; names split at the separators, a name run that only layout parts one name (revtex's
  `\firstname{…} \surname{…}`, 1303.6104; a font switch or box never separates, decision 6d — an image does: a logo,
  review revfms2a1_3), a run of initials not ended by a gap (`V.G.~ Kagramanova`, 0802.4349), a qualifier after a comma
  the name's (`Robert W. Heath, Jr.`, `…, Student Member, IEEE`), an institution among the names the affiliation of the
  name before (`Chen Jia, SI-TECH Information Technology`, 2406.02959), a lone placement letter beside a box flagged
  (`flag:placement-letter`); a mark between a separator and a name the one nearer in the source (`Ann,$^{1}$ Bob` the
  name before, 0705.3409; `Ann$^1$, $^{2}$Bob` the next), an `\inst` after a comma the name before under the policy;
  ruling 1 — a mark's labels split at commas and spaces, a symbol run glued to a label two (`*1`), the name its text
  alone, a labelled entry to every name requesting it, a `fuzzy:<name>` label (svjour's `\institute` entries) to the
  name it spells; ruling 2 — a symbol-led line to every carrier of the character, an uncarried one the block's; an
  unmarked line under names the row above's, each line one contact (as today's `\\` lines: 0707.1113, 1404.0431),
  while an unmarked line under a labelled entry continues it (0803.3589); a note opening with a requested label that
  label's legend (2311.16145); the owner chain — the address's own label, the spelled author (`NameKeys`,
  `spelled_owners`), a class list's author at its call's place (one place per author, every spelled address at its
  author's: `_sequence`, #805), the group's only author, elimination (the line's one unspelled address and the one
  author without an address), the one author a note names the corresponding author (`names_correspondence`), the block;
  one contact per printed address (a braced `{a,b}@x` written out); a note emptied into contacts dropped, `\thanks{}`
  kept. API calls: a creator; a labelled contact (`label=`, a `labelseq=` place — a `\and`-list entry numbered piece by
  piece, #791 —, its leading mark, a `\label` a `\ref` mark names) to its requesters, the block's when none; an
  unlabelled one by its `annotate=` (the last author; `all`; `new`; `run[:<cap>]`, a second contact before a new author
  the same run's), its `\email`s its owners' too; a title's note (its parent `ltx:title`) is no creator's.
- **Lexer and rehearsal additions** (the events change only here): a mark printing only a `\ref` is a Mark labelled
  `ref:<key>` (A&A's `\inst{\ref{ipag}}`, 1809.08354; open question (a)); `\lx@request@frontmatter@annotation[<p>]{<l>}`
  (elsarticle's `\corref`, `\fnref`) a Mark labelled `<p>:<l>` printing nothing; a `\footnotemark[<n>]` reads <n>
  with `\c@footnote` at the rehearsal's start plus the steps the block's notes made before it, local to the mark
  (`\footnotemark[\arabic{footnote}]` after a `\thanks` prints that note's symbol, 2201.11183, 2111.13260; review
  rev78o2 finding 3; guard `footnotemark_number_reads_the_stepped_counter`); each API call's content (the queued
  command's last argument, inside the affiliation wrappers) is rehearsed and lexed at the flush, and its attributes and
  parent recorded; the binding owning `\author` is recorded at the call — the compiled binding whose load changed the
  meaning (`note_binding_load`, the loader seams of latexml_package and latexml_contrib `dispatch`; a pool's load is the kernel's), else
  `kernel`/`document`/`raw`/`fallback` by its origin — and with the hook is the policy key (notes decision 2, "no keyval
  in the binding files", superseded at 87a: each binding declares its conventions, below). A bare `\footnotemark` prints the kernel title hook `\lx@title@thefootnote`
  (`TITLE_FOOTNOTE_HOOK` = `latex_constructs::TITLE_THEFOOTNOTE`, 78o) when defined; else the policy entry's
  `title_marks`: `Fnsymbol` (the kernel `\maketitle`'s `\@fnsymbol\c@footnote`) or `Body` (the class's own
  `\thefootnote`: report's and book's title page, arabic). (r2: the revtex entry's inert `\frontmatter@thefootnote`
  field is gone — revtex4-2.cls:3040-3043 is `\@fnsymbol` by default, :5976-5978 `\@booleanfalse\altaffilletter@sw`
  after :3043's default, checked with pdflatex; `\@alph` only under `altaffilletter`.) The policy key is the binding
  owning `\author`, or — when that is the kernel's — the document class's binding with an entry (`ledger::policy_binding`:
  the first binding the class's load loaded that has one; `jpconf.cls`, `report.cls`, `book.cls` — iopart_support owns
  its `\author` itself),
  never over a package owning `\author` (authblk); an API call runs under the policy of the block before it.
- **Policy table** (`policy.rs`, Layer B; first match on (binding, hook), else `kernel`; since 87a each binding's own
  declaration, "The conventions' home" below): `revtex`
  (revtex4_support.sty; `annotate=new` declared by the binding's call), `authblk` (`thenote`: authblk's `\AB@thenote`
  under ruling 1, below; `state_counter` `Maxaffil`), `report`, `book` (`title_marks: Body`), `llncs` (`\inst` after a comma, `\and`
  inline: #791, #792, #807), `aa`, `inst_support`, `svjour` (`\inst` after a comma, #807), `jheppub`, `jcappub`,
  `jinstpub` (e-mail by spelling else call order, #801, #805, #809), `iopart`, `jpconf` (the same, each call a group:
  #806, #808, #841); each entry cites what it reproduces (since 87a checked at the declaration and over the
  re-resolver's list, ab_audit `fmshadow::tests::a_declared_familys_dump_re_resolves_under_its_bindings_conventions`).
- **Comparator** (`ab_audit fmshadow ROOT [-o PREFIX] [--keys F] [--re-resolve]`, latexml_oxide/bin/ab_audit/fmshadow/):
  per paper the shadow's tuples against the XML's (names without their `ltx:sup` marks, texts by their letters and
  digits; contacts of role `note`/`thanks` read as notes on both sides), each disagreement a row — kind (`name-split`,
  `affiliation`, `contact-owner`, `contact`, `note`, `block`), family (the policy key's binding), the deciding rule —
  **classified** when that rule holds an adopted ruling's change tag (`CHANGE_TAGS`) or the disagreement falls in a
  PDF-confirmed XML-wrong class (`XML_WRONG`, by name with its witnesses; r2, below), unclassified otherwise; a paper with no rehearsed block is "no block" and one whose rehearsal held an
  error "held", both outside the gate's denominator (notes decisions 1, 3); the block-final `]` span shortfall is not
  compared (texts are). `--re-resolve` resolves the dump's events again with the binary's resolver. Output
  `<prefix>.tsv`, `<prefix>.disagree.tsv`, `<prefix>.shadow.jsonl`, `<prefix>.summary.txt` (the per-family table by
  reach with the gate number, the share of a family's counted papers with an unclassified disagreement).
Measured (the census numbers and the PDF checks are in SYNC_STATUS "FM S2a.2"): far from the K23 class guard (under 0.5 %
per family) on every family but the smallest; S2b waits for further resolver rounds. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batchfms2a2::*`; engine unit tests `policy::tests::*`, `resolver::tests::*`; ab_audit unit tests
`fmshadow::tests::*`.

**S2a.2 r2: the resolver by defect class, the comparator made honest** (review revfms2a2: of 40 sampled unclassified
disagreements 31 were the resolver's, 8 today's XML, 1 normalisation). Still shadow only (XML byte-identical with the
switch on and off and against int53a, SYNC "FM S2a.2").
- **Notes** keep their whole text (their contacts' texts too: a note's text is its events' printed text, the rehearsal's
  contact constructors printing nothing); what is left once the contacts are taken out decides only ruling 4's "emptied",
  and an emptied note goes to `Resolved.dropped` (rule `ruling4:emptied`) for the comparison (2401.17399, 1607.05792,
  2603.01292). A note's legend label is its body's leading Mark event (the lexer adds it to the note's `inner`), never
  the flattened text (`$^{1}$Unit` read "1Unit"; 1909.02288, 2608.06122, 1903.10543, 2407.19826); the "any word of three
  letters" reading is gone.
- **Labels**: a `fuzzy:<name>` label stays whole and is matched by the name's letters, a mark command's argument and a
  formula dropped (`Luca Passalacqua (\Envelope)`, 0807.3898, 2403.09642); a creator's own `author:N` is the N-th
  creator, matched exactly (relocate.rs:42-50; 1804.09680, astro-ph0611539); every other label by Perl's chain
  (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:891-900): the exact request, then past the request's prefix, the label's, both
  (elsarticle's `fn:label1` answers `\address[label1]`, 1712.00945).
- **Names lines by evidence** (finding 6): a later line of a column is names only after a blank line, continuing a
  names row that ended in a comma or "and" (1403.0130), under a row with its affiliation line already when set in a font
  of its own (1009.1429, 1108.3744) or after the row's labelled lines (SYNC row 46), with marks or notes on its names
  (1403.5246), or as two or more name pieces — and then each piece must read as a name; one name-like piece without
  evidence is an affiliation ("Capital Fund Management", "Google DeepMind": 2606.07382, 2307.02318, 2305.16559,
  2609.09054); a line of e-mail addresses alone is never names (2210.05991). An IEEE ordinal before a name
  (`1\textsuperscript{st} Sertac`) stays with it, as today's personname (2412.10792, 2202.06596).
- **Marks in lines**: punctuation before a mark does not lead the line (`($^1$)`, 1004.4809); a mark set off by a space
  (source positions between it and the ink before) opens an entry of its own (`$^1$Arizona State University $^2$Rider
  University`, 2601.20069); a symbol some name shows that the lexer read as ink at a line's start is a Mark (`$\sharp$ -
  CBCL`, 1209.1360); marks trailing their text, each shown on another line, label it (2507.05750; not a lone
  `Harvard University$^{*}$`, 2307.02318).
- **Lines under names**: unmarked lines under a row whose names show non-symbol marks are one affiliation of every name,
  as today's `\\`-joined contact (0903.2366, 2303.09899; a footnote symbol is no such mark, 0707.1113); a line under a
  labelled entry continues it unless it is addresses alone, which the owner chain places (2509.12185, 0801.3376,
  0810.3062).
- **API intake** takes only creators and creator annotations (`resolver::creator_call`): no MDPI `reftitle`, no
  author-contribution note (2608.12223). **Contact roles**: the call's declared role wins over a `mailto:` link inside
  it (2506.17875), a url printing one e-mail address is an e-mail (1409.0496); the rehearsal binds `\email`-type
  commands only when the document's take an argument (jmlr2e's `\email` is a font switch: 2412.18293, 2305.17297);
  acmart's address-part key is no ink (1907.07713). An annotation of the new authors (`annotate=new`/`run`/`<n>`)
  before any creator reaches none (revtex collaboration lists declaring every `\affiliation` first, 2103.04797,
  0704.1604); an unqualified one is the block's (0709.0811).
- **Today's placements reproduced**: the amsart contact grid (insert.rs `distribute_upfront_contacts`; 2205.02163); a
  replacing `\author` keeps the latest call's authors (`\lx@clear@frontmatter`; 2502.11323, 2509.11381).
- **authblk** (`thenote`, review answer 6b): an unlabelled author requests `\AB@thenote` (the `affil` counter, stepped at
  the first `\author` after an `\affil`), an unlabelled `\affil` is labelled by it — when the marks show (a label given,
  or the counter past `\c@Maxaffil`, recorded at the block's call); else (block mode) the run, as the binding declares
  (authblk.sty:114-118, 148-151; 2605.25017).
- **Comparator honesty** (findings 8, 9, 14): the block's items are compared as a multiset (kind `block`) and `rule_of`
  searches them; an XML item is explained by the shadow's items only when it is two or more of them joined (the word
  "and" between allowed), no looser overlap; ORCID links compare by their identifier (the XML's `ref` href, in a contact
  or the personname); `ruling3:one-per-print` classifies only a joined item, the owner its other tag's; elimination is
  **not** a change — today's output applies it (#52's e-mail lines, `owners_by_elimination`, under user ruling R10 2026-10-20, 77p r10), and
  FIDELITY_CHARTER §4's owner order is silent on it (flagged to the main session). The XML-wrong classes, each confirmed
  on its witnesses' pdflatex PDFs: names parted by a wide space merged into one personname (2312.06207, 2303.02369,
  2512.16241, 2511.18287), a list of names in one personname (1512.06985, 1610.06365, 2211.02638, 2411.11150), an ORCID
  logo's glyphs read as "ID" after the name (2501.15882, 2405.19400); a name class applies only when it explains every
  XML name. Guards `perfect_kernel_batchfms2a2::{notes_keep_their_whole_text, fuzzy_labels_stay_whole,
  author_sequence_labels_place_their_contacts, prefix_fallback_answers_a_mismatched_label,
  note_legends_by_their_leading_mark, institution_lines_are_not_names, contact_roles_follow_the_call_and_the_address,
  marks_mid_line_and_trailing_label_entries, authblk_unlabelled_affil_is_its_thenote, report_title_page_marks_are_arabic,
  a_replacing_author_call_keeps_the_latest, ams_contact_grid_is_distributed}` (each red on r1), the r1 guards pinned as
  whole sequences; unit tests `resolver::tests::*`, `fmshadow::tests::{block_items_and_joined_pieces,
  xml_wrong_name_classes_explain_every_name}`.

**S2a.2 r3: the classified bucket's wrong classes, the pilot families' residuals** (r2's PDF sample: 18 of 59 classified
disagreements wrong; the revtex4_support and ams_support unclassified papers each read against its PDF). Still shadow
only (XML byte-identical against int54a with the switch unset and set, SYNC "FM S2a.2").
- **Marked entries of one call** are parted by their marks (`resolver::mark_led_pieces`): an API affiliation whose first
  ink is a mark, with a mark at a line start, after a break or after a separator, is an entry per mark, rule
  `api:split-by-marks` (cond-mat0510562, 1612.09425, 1809.03738, hep-ph0408045, 2509.08362, 1506.00848); a space,
  a break or a brace before the leading mark does not hide it (0902.0006, 2211.15148). A leading-mark entry's
  `annotate=new` run holds the role, as today's attaches it before moving it by its mark (1506.04004), a `label=` entry
  not (1712.00945).
- **Glued labels** part by the marks the other side shows (`part_glued_labels`, `parted_label`, tag `ruling1:parted`): a
  name's `12` under entries `1` and `2` (2103.10685), `1⋆` (2606.01911), an entry's `∗∗` where the name shows `∗`
  (1505.06831) — never a label some entry or name has as written, nor a class's numbering (`labelseq`, 1005.2409);
  a mark glued to the mark before it goes where that one went (`Oh,$^{1}$$^{,2}$`, 2306.15492).
- **Fuzzy labels**: one spelling no name whole answers by its names' surnames, as today's #159 reading
  (`resolver::surname_owners`, tag `fuzzy:surname`; 2011.14024, 2403.19676, 2106.12864); the ledger writes a label's
  parameterless macros out at the call (`ledger::label_text`: aastex's `fuzzy:\lx@aas@correspondent`, 2506.07978).
- **E-mails by evidence** (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4): a note's e-mail goes to the author it spells before the note's own
  (`answer_note_emails`, r7's `answer_note_links`; 1908.04020, 2304.00435), else to the author carrying the note's mark (main-session decision
  2026-10-22: the mark shown on that name is the evidence; it never goes by adjacency alone); a list with one address per author that every spelled address agrees
  with is in author order, for every class (`owner:order`; 2603.19610, 2512.22629, 2305.12998); an e-mail Contact given
  to a row of names, or printing several addresses, is placed address by address (0809.3237); an address's glued label
  is no part of it (`E-mail:lcai@…`, 1807.11339); addresses a names line prints as text are e-mails, not names
  (2507.03885).

session's decisions of 2026-10-22). Still shadow only (XML byte-identical against int63a with the switch unset and set,

- **A replaced `\author` call keeps nothing** (finding 1): the post-passes that count the authors or pick one read the
  live creators only (`Resolver::live`, no replaced call's) — the footnote-text pairing (`answer_note_texts`: a
  `\footnotetext[1]` built before `\maketitle` went into the first mark of its print, a replaced creator's, and was
  deleted with it — `\author{A\footnotemark[1]}` twice), a sole author's orphans and pre-author annotations, the class's
  address list (`answer_sequence`'s author order and spelling), today's upfront contact grid (`distribute_upfront`), a
  note's e-mail with no owner; the block's own items of the replaced call go with its creators (2510.26354's first
  `\author`, whose `firstname.lastname@h-its.org` the second call's addresses write out).
- **A resolved name is its printed text** (finding 2, the main session's decision): `new_creator` keeps a piece printing
  no letter or digit (r5's filter, review revfms2a2_4 finding 6, removed), its spaces collapsed, as the join paths keep
  it (1706.00234's "TIÊ ´N-SO . N PHẠM"); a zero-width character never reaches it (the lexer's `is_zero_width`).
- **A note's inner contacts** (decision 2, user ruling 2026-10-20 #4): an inner contact is its owner's when it is the
  note's only link and the note's mark is shown on the owner, or when it spells the owner (an e-mail by the owner chain's
  spelling, a url by its letters after the scheme and `www.`, `link_letters`: `owner:spelled`); an e-mail spelling
  another author of the block is that author's, as before (1908.04020); any other stays in the note's text, no contact,

- **Source order** (finding 1): a note `answer_note_links` keeps once every name is read came after the notes the source
  gives later (`\author{Ann Able\thanks{\url{ann@x.org}, \url{zed@y.org}}\thanks{Second note.} \and Bob Baker}` read

  under it. Once `resolve` ends each creator's notes and contacts, and the block's own, are in source order
  (`in_source_order`: ledger index, then span start; an item with no source keeps its place). The comparator sees note
  order now: the notes both sides hold, each side's in its order (`note_orders`), a `note-order` row when they differ,
  its rule the first out-of-place shadow note's (`order …`): unclassified unless a ruling placed that note — a legend
  ruling 1 places by its label is today's last, relocated, where the shadow keeps the source's order (2607.03557's
  `\textsuperscript{$\dagger$}Corresponding author` before its funding note).
- **An ownerless note's link** (finding 2, decision 4): `fallback` asks for an owner — a note no name holds (an address
  line's, a line's) gives its link to the author it spells or leaves it in its text, never to the block (the only link of
  `ann@x.org, bob@x.org\thanks{Code: \url{…}}` was a block url, and a sole author's by `sole_author_takes_the_block`).
- **A url is an author's only as the page it spells** (finding 3, decision 1): a url is spelled by its page
  (`link_page`: its last path segment, an `index.*` or `*.html` page after it aside, else its host), read from the link's
  target (an `\href`'s first argument) in all four placements — a co-author's, the note's owner's (`owner:spelled`), the
  only-link fallback, and so an ownerless one (the sole-author move sees none, above). A homepage
  (`sites.google.com/view/<name>`, `tu.berlin/disco/klimm`, `…/MarcinPitera`, `portal.research.lu.se/en/persons/<name>`,

  repository, a project or a file under an account stays in the note's text (`github.com/<user>/<repo>`,
  `…/resolution.git`, `<user>.github.io/<project>`, `…/<name>/accvideo.mp4`: 2008.12970, 2511.08416, 2103.05251,
  2503.02954, 2509.01952), and a page no name spells is no one's, the note's only link too (r2-r7's fallback made
  `\thanks{Code is available at \url{…}}` its owner's contact: 2409.18582, 2511.12997, 1607.05792, 1908.10122's doi,
  2509.14694's springer.com; 1401.0489's `people.cs.uchicago.edu/~laci`, a nickname, too). A link to an address

  wellman@mit.edu}`, 2010.09271, 1407.7882) is the address: read by its letters, the note's only link its owner's (r9:
  a `mailto:` link an e-mail read by the address it points to, every link contact carrying its target — below).

**S2a.2 r9: the r8 landing review's findings, the rehearsal's isolation** (review revfms2a2_8 findings 1-7; the SYNC row
"FM shadow rehearsal leaks"). Shadow only, and now so with the switch set too: int65's 725 papers, the 992 sectioning-frontmatter repros
and the 26,323-paper census byte-identical int73a → r9 unset and r9 unset → set (but a clock paper, 2109.00764, and a
time-budgeted math parse, 1001.0023, whose reruns agree).
- **A link contact carries its target** (finding 1): `Assoc::target` (the dump's `target`), where the link points — an
  `\href`'s first argument, a `\url`'s text, a `mailto:` link's address (`link_target`, `mailto_address`: its scheme and a
  `?subject=` query aside) —, its `text` the anchor it prints: Hankin's `\href{https://academics.aut.ac.nz/robin.hankin}
  {work}` was a url contact "work", the url lost (2210.15991). A `mailto:` link is an e-mail (`contact_parts`), placed by
  the address — its note's link by `place_note_link`, a block's contact by the owner chain on the address
  (`contact_event` → `place_line_contacts`) —, not the anchor (2309.10007's `tsamak`, `csamak`, `vkrovi`). S2b has the
  target to write; the comparison still reads the anchor, today's note text.
- **The API legend reads the text** (finding 2): an API entry a symbol leads is a legend note (r8) only when no piece of it
  reads as an affiliation (`reads_as_affiliation` of each name and contact it prints — an address and its label read as
  none —, not of the joined text, where any address answers "no") or when it is one piece its marks split an entry into
  (`api:split-by-marks`); the role change carries its own tag, `api:legend` (a change tag; `affiliation_rule_of` explains
  today's affiliation by it, not by `api:leading-mark`). IEEEtran's `\IEEEauthorblockA{{*Equal Contribution} \\
  \IEEEauthorblockA{Tsinghua University} \IEEEauthorblockA{National Supercomputing Center in Wuxi} …}` was one legend
  note of the starred names, both institutions out of the affiliation role (1903.06934); it is their affiliation again,
  as r7 read it (the entry whole — today's has the nested calls apart: unclassified, residual). 0812.1531, 1902.02631 and
  the census's other API legends stay legends.
- **Comparator honesty** (finding 3): the notes a ruling placed (a change tag) are taken out of both sides' orders and
  the rest must agree (`compare`'s `note-order`): `[L, A, B]` against `[B, A, L]` was explained by the legend L, A and B
  swapped; now unclassified, its rule the first of the rest out of order. Every rule of a (kind, text) key is kept
  (`TCreator::all_rules`, `Tuples::block_all_rules`) and each copy the XML lacks takes one, the copies it holds taking the
  rules that reproduce today's first (`surplus_rules`): 1910.01401's second ORCID copy, placed by `owner:adjacent`, read
  as the ruling's `note:adjacent ruling4:inner-contact` — unclassified now (the shadow is right: the ORCID is printed
  beside the name and in the note, today's holds it in the block alone; residual).
- **Rehearsal isolation** (the SYNC leak row; 2405.14627, 2603.26792, 2409.10200): two kinds of state the rehearsal
  changed and nothing put back. (1) A box the stomach stamped with a field provenance (`fieldProv`/`fieldSerial`,
  `invoke_token`) is stamped only when it has none; `\copy`/`\usebox` hands back the register's box itself, so the
  rehearsal's print stamped the shared box with a serial its `FieldLedgerScope` then dropped, and the conversion's print,
  finding it stamped, did not stamp it again — its field ink then wrapped it in an `ltx:text` with an id. The scope now
  journals the boxes stamped while it is open (`token::field_stamp_noted`) and unstamps them when it closes
  (`Digested::try_remove_property`): a stamp on a box that had none is all the stomach writes. (2) A meaning's standing as
  a fallback guess, kernel stub or borrowed package's (`state::fallback_meanings`, which a `\newcommand` may replace,
  `is_definable_latex`) is changed by an assignment beside the meaning and put back by no group end: the rehearsal's
  group-local `\let\AND\lx@fm@obs@AND` cleared OmniBus's `\AND` (the siamart binding loads OmniBus), so
  algorithmic.sty:161's `\newcommand{\AND}{\algorithmicand{} }` was refused and `\AND` printed the separator's plain
  "and". An assignment journal now saves a meaning's standing with its bindings at its first assignment
  (`AssignmentJournal::fallback`) and its rollback restores it — every speculative run's, not the rehearsal's alone.
- **Nits** (findings 4-7): the dump's `continued` optional (`Resolved::continued: Option`; a missing key an old dump, "any
  part" — an r8 dump's empty list no longer); `link_page` reads a `*.html` page right under the host as the page that
  spells its owner (`host/jsmith.html` "jsmith"; one under a segment stays that segment's, `~siegel/plan.html`), and a
  url is "printing addresses" only when it holds one (`addresses_in`), not any `@` (`medium.com/@user` a page);
  `in_source_order` sorts a span-less item after its block's spanned ones; `is_symbol_char` is the lexer's
  `is_fnsymbol`.

difference leaves the paper as today's, and what was written is read back against the reading (a Warning names the

**The conventions' home (87a, 2026-10-28; user ruling "in each binding", the audit's §3a item 1).** A family's
conventions are declared by its binding at load, not looked up in a table keyed on binding file names in generic
code: `declare_frontmatter_conventions(&FRONTMATTER_CONVENTIONS)` is the first statement of the binding's load, its
`FmConventions` (`observer::policy::Policy`: every field the table carried — `inst_after_comma`, `and_inline`,
`label_sequence`, `email_owner`, `call_is_group`, `title_marks`, `thenote`, `state_counter`, `and_word`,
`unmarked_notes`, `written`, `cite` — completed from `FM_KERNEL_CONVENTIONS`) kept in the state globally under the
declaring binding's file name (`frontmatter_conventions:<binding>`, one declaration per hook, `*` any; the first
matching in declaration order applies, a re-declaration replaces in place). `policy_for` and `has_entry` read the
state; a family that declares none is `KERNEL`, as the table's fallback was; `written` (revtex4_support, ams_support:
the default build's S2b writer) is the binding's own flag. The key is the one the ledger already recorded at the call
(`ledger::author_binding`, `ledger::policy_binding`), as the table's lookup was: a declaration reaches a binding only
while that binding's `\author` at the call is still the declaring binding's — loading the declaring binding is not
enough. revtex4_support's reaches revtex4, revtex4-1, revtex4-2; ams_support's ams_core's amsart, amsproc, amsbook and
amsaddr; iopart_support's iopart.cls, because iopart_support's own locked `\author[]{}` owns the call (all 122 author
blocks of the 97 iopart census papers keyed `iopart_support.sty`); `policy_binding` — the class's declaring binding under
the kernel's `\author` — reaches jpconf.cls, report.cls and book.cls (the census's only blocks where owner and key
differ: 57, 36, 33). Not reached today: the
aastex classes load revtex4 and then `aas_support`, whose `\author` (aas_support_sty.rs) takes the ownership — kernel
conventions, keyed `aas_support.sty` (every aastex-family census paper: aastex 45, aastex631 24, aastex63 13,
aastex62 7, aastex6 3, aastex7 3; 1005.0770, 1910.05363, 2604.19097); lmcs's own `\author` (lmcs_cls.rs) calls
`\lx@add@author`, no `\lx@add@authors*`, so the observer records no author block and no conventions are read
(2306.08266, 2108.06944, 2402.09138: 0 blocks under `LATEXML_FM_SHADOW=1`); OmniBus (inst_support's conventions by
default, loaded eagerly) is reached by ams_support's only when its `\subjclass` autoload (omnibus_cls.rs:820) or the
ambient `\curraddr` autoload (tex.rs:314) loads ams_support before `\author` (the 87a r2 re-review's probes p2, p4; the
ambient one would also reach a kernel-`\author` class, a shape pdflatex does not compile); aa.cls's declaration
is unread, inst_support owning aa's `\author` (all 100 aa census papers keyed `inst_support.sty`, the same values).
Whether aastex should take revtex's conventions is an observer decision left open. The fifteen former
rows, each in its binding (latexml_package: revtex4_support, authblk, llncs, aa, inst_support, sv_support,
ams_support, IEEEtran, jheppub, iopart_support, report, book; latexml_contrib: jcappub, jinstpub, jpconf); no binding
file name is a key in `observer/`. Offline (`ab_audit fmshadow --re-resolve`) no binding loads, so the re-resolver holds
the bindings' declarations by reference (`fmshadow/conventions.rs` `DECLARED`, `resolver::resolve_with`) and fails a
paper loudly (`stale-conventions`) when a block's recorded conventions are not the ones the list gives its binding, or
it records none: a summary column of its own (`stale_conventions`), counted by the gate as unclassified, and a non-zero
exit. A drift guard scans the bindings' sources for the declaration and checks the list is exactly theirs, each
`binding:` its own registry entry's name and extension.
A pure refactor: the observer census (1,612 papers over every family that declares, `LATEXML_FM_SHADOW=1`) gives
byte-identical shadow records on both binaries, and the same XML (one display formula's parse varied under the census
load, 2002.02531, identical on solo reruns of both), and the A/B (5,309 papers: those families plus 2,000 of
popint110u; E 7,230 → 7,230, F 12 → 12) changes no paper (its four changed rows — math-ambiguity enumeration counts
under load, 2507.14058, 2411.02167, gr-qc9505014, and a 180 s timeout, 2203.01615 — identical on solo reruns of both).
Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch87a::a_bindings_declared_conventions_are_read_and_an_undeclared_family_is_the_kernels`, engine
unit test `policy::tests::a_declaration_is_read_and_an_undeclared_family_takes_the_kernel`, ab_audit
`fmshadow::tests::{a_declared_familys_dump_re_resolves_under_its_bindings_conventions,
the_declared_list_is_every_bindings_own_declaration,
stale_conventions_have_their_own_column_count_in_the_gate_and_fail_the_run}`.

### 840. A space a name sets before its own mark is the name's; spacing-only math, `\enskip` after a mark part names

OD #52(i) rewrites a horizontal space in an author block (`\hspace`, `\hfill`) to `\quad`, which with `\quad` and
`\qquad` is a separator of the author/affiliation split (Perl's `@authoraffilsplits`, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:681-682).
A name that sets a space before its own mark then lost its co-authors: `Oleg Lychkovskiy\thanks{…}\hspace*{2mm}$^{\rm
a,b}$, Sergei Blinnikov\hspace*{2mm}$^{\rm a,c}$` (0905.3658) split into the line "Oleg Lychkovskiy" and the mark-led
line "$^{\rm a,b}$, Sergei Blinnikov", an affiliation (one creator, a contact ", Sergei Blinnikov"); Perl, which never
rewrites `\hspace`, reads two creators — but splits a written `\quad` there the same way. Ours (78m, rows.rs
`space_before_own_mark`): at the block's top level, outside math, after a name letter, a run of horizontal space that
opens with `\hspace` (its `*` and length read with it), `\hfill`, `\hfil`, `\quad` or `\qquad` (more spacing and spaces
after it in the run) is dropped when a mark or a note of the name before it follows (`leading_marks_end`: `$^{…}$`,
`\textsuperscript{…}`, `\altaffilmark{…}`, `\thanks{…}`, `\footnote{…}`) and no entry text follows that — a comma, `;`,
the word "and", a line separator, a separating run of spacing (a separating space, an `\enskip` — a separator right
after a mark, below —, or two or more spacing commands as #52(o) counts them), `\par`, a closing brace or the end come
after it; one spacing command after the marks (a tie, a control space) and the spaces around it are passed over before
that test, being the next entry's. A mark that leads an entry keeps the space a separator: `$^1$Univ A\quad$^2$Univ B`
and `$^1$~Univ A\quad$^2$~Univ B` (78m r2; r1 read the tie as "more spacing", so Ann had "Univ A² Univ B" and Bob none)
are an affiliation line's two entries, as `\textsuperscript{2}\ Univ B` is. Two more spacings part names (78m): a math
group at the block's top level holding only spacing (`\quad`, `\qquad`, the spacing commands of #52(o), spaces) is that
spacing written outside math (`spacing_math_unwrapped`; 1602.04504's `Michael J. Wilber$^{1,2}$ $\qquad$ Vitaly
Shmatikov$^{1,2}$ $\qquad$ Serge Belongie$^{1,2}$` was one creator, in Perl too, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1069), and
latex.ltx's `\enskip` (`\hskip.5em\relax`) at the top level right after a mark or note is a space #52(i) rewrites to
`\quad`, as `\hspace` (1312.1414's five names parted by `Berry\thanks{…} \enskip \normalsize Andrew M.\ Childs`);
elsewhere it is one of #52(o)'s spacing commands (`is_spacing_command`), one of which stays inside a name (`J.\enskip
Smith$^{1}$`, `A.\enskip B. Smith`, which 78m r1, reading every top-level `\enskip` as a separator, parted) and a run of
two or more of which parts names. The labels of a mark lose a `\rm` glued to them as Perl's `s/\\rm//g`
(Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:365) strips it (`clean_frontmatter_labels`): `$^{\rm a,b}$` reads "\rma,b", the tokenizer
having skipped the space after `\rm`, which OD #34's `FONT_SWITCH` (a switch before a non-letter) left, so "\rma" was
requested and no `${\rm ^a}$` line answered it. Residual: in a block marked with labels, a name whose only mark is a
footnote symbol continues the line before it (`Bob Baker$^{2}$\quad Cat Cole$^{\S}$` is one name, the base too:
1312.1414's "Richard Cleve Robin Kothari Rolando D. Somma", flagged `merged_creators`; SYNC_STATUS 78m bullet). Repros
sectioning-frontmatter/{author_space_before_own_mark_is_the_name, author_spacing_math_between_names_separates,
author_tie_after_entry_mark_is_the_entry, author_enskip_in_name_and_after_note}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78m::{author_space_before_own_mark_is_the_name, author_spacing_math_between_names_separates,
author_tie_after_entry_mark_is_the_entry, author_enskip_in_name_and_after_note}`.

### 841. jpconf.cls is read raw, then its address and e-mail blocks are the frontmatter

IOP's conference class (jpconf.cls 2004/05/04 v1.0, Journal of Physics: Conference Series; not in TeX Live, 58 census
papers ship it) copies iopart.cls's author block: `\address` (:108-110) and `\ead`/`\eads`/`\mailto` (:104-106) print
an `{indented}` list item where they stand. Perl has no binding (OmniBus: `\address` an address contact, `\ead` an empty
e-mail contact, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1068); under the raw-class lever (#444) the blocks were bullet lists after the
abstract and the authors had no contact (0705.0202, 1011.0523). Ours (78m, `latexml_contrib/src/jpconf_cls.rs`): the
paper's copy is read raw (`RawRead`, `shipped`), then iopart_support's address and e-mail definitions are made
(`iopart_support_sty::iop_address_and_email`, factored out of the iopart_support binding unchanged): each `\address` an
affiliation of the authors before it (`\lx@add@affiliation@marked`), each `\ead` an e-mail placed with its author
(#806, #808, #809). The class's other definitions stay its own; jpconf.cls is on `author_files::AUTHOR_FILES`. Repro
sectioning-frontmatter/jpconf_copy (a stand-in jpconf.cls written from scratch); guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78m::jpconf_address_and_email_are_frontmatter`.

### 842. bmcart.cls is read raw, then its title, author and address printers are the frontmatter

BioMed Central's bmcart.cls (VTeX; not in TeX Live, 20 census papers ship it) lets `\title`, `\author`, `\address` and
`{fmbox}` to its printers in `{frontmatter}` (:966-984): `\title@fmt` typesets the title in the `{fmbox}` (:1034-1053),
`\author@fmt[keys]{name}` the name and the numbers of its `addressref` addresses (:1198-1255), `\address@fmt[id=…]`
stores the address (:1287-1296) for the "Author details" that `\thebibliography` prints (:1708-1712 `\printaddresses`),
which the kernel's bibliography constructor never runs. Read raw (#444) the document had no title, no creator and no
address (1711.01177: a `titlepage` of boxes, the marks "??"); Perl, with no binding, makes one creator "[" (OmniBus's
`\author` reads the bracket as the name) and 7 Errors (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1067). Ours (78m,
`latexml_contrib/src/bmcart_cls.rs`): the copy is read raw, then `\title@fmt` is `\lx@add@title`; `\author@fmt` a
`\lx@add@creator[role=author,annotations={…}]` requesting its `addressref` and `presentaddressref` ids, its name parts
as the printed name reads them (:1247-1249: `\inits` dropped, `\fnm`, `\snm`, `\particle`, `\suffix` as written), each
address of its `email` key (`email={a@x, b@y}`) an `\lx@add@email`; `\address@fmt` an affiliation
`\lx@add@contact[role=affiliation,label={id}]` (the class's `aff<n>` without an `id`), its parts as
`\address@definitions` prints them (:1298-1304); `\@bmcartnote[id=…]{text}`, an article note (`{artnotes}`'s
`\note[id=n1]{Corresponding author}`, :1371-1395), which the class stores by its `id` for `\printartnotes` to print
under the title block's rule (:999-1002 `\auto@set@thanksbox`, :1406-1409, :1440-1447), a note
`\lx@add@contact[role=note,label={note:id}]` as elsart_support_core's `\fntext[label]` is, and the author's `noteref`
ids (and `thanksref`'s, whose alias `noteref` is, :1131-1143) requests of `note:id` among its `annotations`; `{fmbox}`
only holds them, its "Full list of author information …" line (:1002) a print flourish. (78m r1 kept `{artnotes}` to the
class, whose printer the empty `\bmc@endfmbox` never ran, so the notes were dropped silently: 1507.06515's
"Corresponding author", 2007.00437's "Second corresponding author: kcsamir@gmail.com", 2112.10068's "Equal contributor"
of two authors, which the PDF prints.) The class's `corref` key (its "Correspondence:" line, :1463-1467) keeps the
class's own printing, the e-mail it names an `email` contact already. bmcart.cls is on `author_files::AUTHOR_FILES`.
