### 852. algorithm2e's `noline` block gives its indentation back

algorithm2e.sty:1851-1860 `\algocf@Noline` sets the block's body in a box of its own (`\algocf@push{\skiprule}` around
it, `\algocf@pop` after), so the line after a block is at the block's level; `\SetAlgoNoLine` (the `noline` option,
:1438, and `\SetNoline`, :3244) and `\SetNothing` make `\algocf@group` (an `\If`'s branch, a loop's body) and the block
`\algocf@Noline` (:1901-1905, :1919-1923). Perl's `\algocf@Noline` (algorithm2e.sty.ltxml:120) pushes
`\lx@algo@advlevel` and never pops it, unlike its `\algocf@Vline`/`\algocf@Vsline`, so every line after a block went one
level deeper (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1062). Ours (78o, algorithm2e_sty.rs) pops it as `\algocf@Vline` does (1410.4452's
Algorithm 1 now reads as its PDF: "else", "end", "foreach" back at the left). Repro
listings-algorithms/algorithm2e_noline_block_pops_its_indentation; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78o::{algorithm2e_noline_block_pops_its_indentation, algorithm2e_setalgonoline_groups_pop_their_indentation}`.

### 853. A minipage holding a `\subcaption` is the sub-figure

subcaption.sty:251 makes `\subcaption` `\caption` under `\@captype` `sub<type>`: in a minipage of a figure it numbers
the minipage "1a", and a `\label` after it names that panel; caption's `\caption@subtypehook` (caption.sty:639-664)
steps the float's counter ahead of the float's own caption. Perl's `\subcaption` (subcaption.sty.ltxml:43-56, with a
TODO for exactly this) changes `\@captype` only: the sub-caption's number is made but no element carries it, and its
label falls to the figure (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1085). Ours (78o): `begin_caption_box`/`end_caption_box`
(latex_constructs/mod.rs) take a box's caption of the float's sub-type as well as of its type (`caption_box_types`), so the
minipage becomes the sub-caption's panel — its id, tags and list entry, the labels its content left, as a `{subfigure}`
has them (#447), and the float's element (`ltx:table` in a `table`, as a `{subtable}` is; blocks.rs
`adopt_box_caption`, 2502.10377); `\lx@subcaption@type` (subcaption_sty.rs) steps the float's counter ahead
once per float as `{subfigure}`'s `before_float` does (`preincrement_float_counter`, not again under `\ContinuedFloat`).
A box holding two sub-captions (2008.05644: two `\includegraphics` + `\subcaption` pairs in one minipage) is not one
sub-figure: it stays as before (`\@@add@caption@counters` counts the captions per type, `CAPTION_COUNT_PREFIX`).
Witness 2011.13897 (PDF "2a"/"2b", before "2"/"2"; fidelity3 N4). Outside a float (`\captionsetup{type=figure}` in a
`center`) nothing changes (the RED `captions-floats/subcaption_before_caption_numbers_its_figure` stays). Repros
captions-floats/subcaption_in_a_minipage_labels_its_panel (and, now green, subcaption_labels_in_scaled_panels_stay_on_their_panels,
continuedfloat_minipage_subcaption_continues_the_letters); guards `perfect_kernel_batch78o::{subcaption_in_a_minipage_labels_its_panel,
subcaption_in_a_minipage_of_a_table_is_a_subtable, subcaption_minipage_panels_in_boxes_and_continued_floats}`.

### 854. acmart makes its theorems at the end of the preamble, each only when undefined

acmart.cls:3460-3489 (TL 2025; 2510.04987's copy :3405-3430) defines `{theorem}`, `{conjecture}`, `{proposition}`,
`{lemma}`, `{corollary}` (style `acmplain`) and `{example}`, `{definition}` (`acmdefinition`) `\AtEndPreamble`, under the
`acmthm` key (default true, :86-93), each `\@ifundefined`, so an author's own `\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}` keeps its
numbering and style and an author's `\newcommand{\example}` its meaning. Perl's acmart.cls.ltxml:236-243 makes them at
class load (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1086): the author's `{theorem}` kept the class's within-section counter ("Theorem 1"
twice in 2306.01662, PDF 1, 2), the author's `\theoremstyle{definition}` theorems the class's italic heads, and
2510.04987's `\example` opened a theorem in 14 table cells. Ours (78o, acmart_cls.rs) is the class's `\AtEndPreamble`
block, with `acmthm` read from the class options. Repros class-bindings/acmart_author_theorem_name_wins,
class-bindings/acmart_author_newtheorem_numbers_as_the_author_says; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78o::{acmart_author_theorem_name_wins, acmart_author_newtheorem_numbers_as_the_author_says,
acmart_acmthm_false_makes_no_theorems}`.

### 855. tabularray's rule keys are drawn as cell borders

tabularray draws its rules apart from the cells (tabularray.sty:1957-2290 `\SetHline`/`\SetVline`, the inner keys
`hlines`/`vlines` :4011-4012 and the child keys `hline{…}`/`vline{…}`, a rowspec's `|` through
`\__tblr_parse_colrow_spec:nn`, :4003). The binding maps `tblr` to the kernel `tabular` (Perl's ar5iv stub the same,
no rules), so only a colspec's `|` and a body `\hline` showed; an all-empty table with `hlines,vlines` (the manual's
`\makeEmptyTable`, tabularray.tex:2859-2870) was pruned whole. Ours (78p, `latexml_contrib/src/tabularray_sty.rs`
`tblr_rule_keys`, `tblr_rule_borders`, `tblr_draw_rules`): each rule key is read as tabularray reads its value
(`{<index>}{<cross>}{<style>}`, `{<cross>}{<style>}`, `<style>`; `\__tblr_set_hline_aux:nn`, :2045-2055), its positions
and cross range through tabularray's child selectors (`tblr_select`: `1,Z`, `2-4`, `odd`, `-`), against the table's
shape (the body's rows and widest row, after `evaluate=`/`expand=` when given: `\lx@tblr@rules@shape`; a last
one-cell row empty but for spaces and `\par`s is no row, :3722-3731), and drawn as the table ends
(`\lx@tblr@rules` in `\lx@tblr@end`, expandable so it starts no row after a last `\\`) as the border letters the
kernel's `\hline` and `|` give: an hline above row `i` is that row's `t` (the last one the row after a final `\\`, or
the last row's `b`), a vline left of column `j` column `j-1`'s `r` (the first column 1's `l`); a second line at a place
(`index` 2) is a second letter, a double rule. A letter the template's `|` already gives is not repeated (`vlines` is
the colspec's first `|`); a body `\hline` after `hlines` is a second line, as tabularray numbers it. `text=` lines and
white ones (`hlines={white}` on coloured rows, 2308.16907) draw none; widths, dashes and colours are not rendered. The
kernel's header guess reads the borders as it does a `tabular`'s. Open: `\SetHline`/`\SetHlines`/`\SetVline`/
`\SetVlines` in the body stay no-ops. Repros alignment-bindings/{tblr_all_empty_table_keeps_its_rules,
tblr_rule_keys_become_cell_borders}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch78p::{tblr_rules_keep_an_empty_table,
tblr_rule_keys_become_cell_borders, tblr_rules_end_a_table_with_a_cmd_column}`.

### 856. A `\label` after a counter step a group has undone does not name the object that step numbered

LaTeX's `\label` names `\@currentlabel` (latex.ltx:14963-14967), which a `\refstepcounter` sets locally: when the
group of the step closes (an `equation`, a theorem, a float's caption, a list), it reverts to the step in scope. Perl's
`floatToLabel` (Document.pm:1098-1127) starts at the current node's last child, so a label right after a closed
element that can take one named that element: a `\label` after `\end{equation}`, still inside a theorem, labelled the
equation (math0107195: PDF "Theorem 5.3", ours and Perl's the equation's 16; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1092). Ours (78p):
every counter step records its serial in scope (local) and as the latest made (global, `label_stepped_counter`); a
`\label` digested where they differ (`label_follows_an_undone_step`) climbs from the current node, not its last child
(`Document::float_to_label_scoped`, `\lx@label`'s `after_undone_step`). A label in the step's own scope is
unchanged (`\caption{…}\label` in a float, `\item…\label`, a section's). A wrapper group of LaTeXML's own around a step
LaTeX makes in the current group does not undo it (`\lx@refstep@outlives@group`, `keep_latest_refstep_in_scope`):
caption's `\captionof` (caption.sty:390-391), which LaTeXML sets in a float (2402.05535
`\captionof{figure}{…}\else…\fi\label{…}`, the figure). Where no ancestor can take the label, Perl's
fallback (the last child, else the root) stays: the root taking lastpage's `\AtEndDocument{\label{lastpage}}` gave it an
id and renumbered every generated `idN`. Effects against pdflatex: a label after a closed table, figure, equation or
list names the enclosing section's (or theorem's, or item's) number, as `\ref` prints there; a label after a
`subequations` block's inner `align` names the block's number (2505.03288 `eq:GNG` "13", int52a an unnumbered inner
group); after `\subfloat{…}\label{…}` the figure when its `\caption` comes before the subfloats — when the caption comes
after them pdflatex names the section (1504.02206 `fig:2c`: pdflatex 5.1, ours 2; review rev78p). cleveref's `\label[type]` constructor
(`\lx@cleverref@labeltype`) places its type by `float_to_label_scoped` too since 78j r5 (guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78j::cleveref_label_type_after_a_closed_float_names_the_object_in_scope`). Repro
cross-references/label_after_an_inner_equation_names_the_theorem; guards `perfect_kernel_batch78p::{
label_after_an_inner_equation_names_the_theorem, label_after_a_closed_step_names_the_step_in_scope,
label_after_captionof_names_its_float}`.

### 857. mathabx's `\curvearrowbotleftright` is U+293B

mathabx.dcl:639 declares `\curvearrowbotleftright` (mathb "F5": a bottom arc with an arrowhead at each end); Perl's
binding leaves it out (mathabx.sty.ltxml:487, commented out; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1095). No Unicode character draws a
two-headed arc; ours (78p, mathabx_sty.rs) is the bottom arc ⤻ U+293B, `\curvearrowbotright`'s, with role ARROW (its
`name` attribute keeps the command; `↔` would read as `\leftrightarrow`). Its siblings `\curvearrowbotleft`,
`\curvearrowleftright`, `\curvearrowtop*` and `\looparrowdown*` stay undefined, as in Perl. Witness 2308.12945;
repro package-bindings/mathabx_curvearrowbotleftright; guard `perfect_kernel_batch78p::mathabx_curvearrowbotleftright`.

### 858. delarray delimits a `tabular` as it does an `array`

delarray.sty:43-58 redefines `\@tabarray`, which array.sty's `\tabular` enters as `\array` does (array.sty:291,
:297-310): `\begin{tabular}[t]\{{l}.` is a tabular between `\left\{` and `\right.`. Perl has no delarray binding and
its `\tabular` never reaches `\@tabarray`, so the delimiter is read as the template, each `&` an "Extra alignment tab"
(KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1096); the Rust binding covered `array` only. Ours (78p, delarray_sty.rs): the kernel tabular's
argument reader `\lx@@tabular@args` peeks as delarray does; a delimited tabular is set in a formula of its own
(`\lx@delarray@tabular@open`, array.sty's `\hbox{$…$}`, never the array's "Missing $ inserted"), `\left<l>` the
tabular `\right<r>`, closed by `\endtabular`; a plain tabular forgets an enclosing one's right delimiter. Residual:
`\left\{ … \right.` around a text tabular stays unparsed math with a Warning (the grammar parses no
OPEN-ATOM-null-CLOSE; `$\left\{ x \right.$` the same; math parked). Witnesses 1304.5109 (6 Errors → 0), 1106.2670 (4
→ 0); repro alignment-bindings/delarray_delimits_a_tabular; guards `perfect_kernel_batch78p::{delarray_delimits_a_tabular,
delarray_plain_tabular_in_a_delimited_one}`.

### 859. A glossary entry's definition raises its diagnostics only where a printed glossary holds the entry

glossaries stores an entry's fields by `\def` (glossaries.sty:2341-2346) and typesets them only where the entry is
used: at a `\gls` (the text, first or name field) and in the glossary `\printglossary` prints (name and description).
LaTeXML digests every field at the definition for `<ltx:glossarydefinition>`, which the post-processor builds the
glossary from, so an unused entry's broken field raised its error (2104.09252 `name={$J_p_p$}`: "Double subscript";
2505.18389 a description's `\gls{nr}` of an entry never defined, 18 Errors; Perl the same, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1093).
Ours (78p, glossaries_sty.rs): `\lx@glossaries@newentry` digests the definition under a `DiagnosticsHold`; its
diagnostics are deferred (logger.rs `defer_to_label`, label `glossary:<key>`) and replayed at the document's end only
for an entry the document references (`\lx@glossaries@gls@link`, `\lx@glossaries@glsadd`) when it also prints a
glossary (`\lx@printglossary`, before or after the reference); a use still typesets its field from the macros and errs
there live, as pdflatex does.
Residuals: the math parse after digestion still warns on an unused entry's unparsable formula (2104.09252's
unparsed-math Warning). glossaries-extra's `\printunsrtglossary` is read raw and typesets each field from its macros,
raising that field's diagnostics itself. Repro index-bib/unused_glossary_entry_raises_nothing; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78p::{unused_glossary_entry_raises_nothing, printed_glossary_entry_raises_its_definition_errors}`.

### 860. Class numbering follows the class: ids, and the paper's copy where versions differ

The 78q bindings number as their classes do (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1097-#1101, #1111), and the ids follow the numbers,
where Perl's follow its kernel numbering: equations numbered within the sections (JHEP, JHEP3, PoS, jheppub, jfm;
JHEP2's binding loads JHEP's, no JHEP2.cls copy in the census to check it against) are `S2.E1`, `S2.E2` (Perl `S2.E2`,
`S2.E3`, the running equation number), an equation after jfm's `\section*` (which zeroes the counter) `Sx1.E1`; the
equations, figures and tables numbered within an appendix are `A1.E1`, `A2.F1`; llncs's appendices, numbered within the
document as article's, are `A1`, `A2` (Perl `Pt0.A1`, within the chapter llncs defines); aipproc's unnumbered sections
are `Sx1`, `Sx2` (the kernel's ids for a section below `secnumdepth`); svjour's theorems under `envcountsect` are
`S1.Thmtheorem1`, under `envcountreset` too (a counter reset by each section is declared within it and printed alone,
"1", so the ids do not depend on document order), by default `Thmtheorem1`. A link into one of these papers by an old id
breaks. l-aa (Rust-only binding over aa's) keeps l-aa.sty's own `\appendix` (:208-214): equations "A1", figures and
tables in their running numbers (astro-ph9705112, astro-ph9607057). Where the versions of a class conflict the paper's
copy decides (the class-family rule, one binding serving all versions): elsarticle's `\appendix` is the class's unless
the paper ships a v1.0.1 copy (2008/05/22; 0711.2399), which has none; emulateapj's `[appendixfloats]` is the TL 2025
class's option (most copies from 10/09/06), and a copy without it numbers the appendix floats as its own appendix code does —
"A1", "B1" always where that code zeroes them (an uncommented `\setcounter{figure}{0}`: 11/26/04 to 08/13/06, three of
four 6/22/04 copies, one of 01/26/10; 17 of 98 census copies; 0704.2079, 0801.1670, 2008.05143), the letter before the
running number, "A2", "B3", with no reset where it does not (05/14/03 to 06/22/04, most 6/22/04 copies zeroing; 16 census
copies; 0803.1491, 0709.1471, astro-ph0508218; review rev78q2); jfm's `\section` zeroes the equation counter, starred calls too (v1.23-v1.28,
72 of 74 census copies; an appendix `\section*` still keeps the count, "A 2" where jfm.cls:303 prints "A 1": the locked
`\section` ignores the binding's re-wrap there, a residual, rev78q2), except in an FLM copy declaring itself `jfm` (JFM-FLM_Au.cls,
2507.06135; 2505.15463's declares `JFM-FLM_Au` and is read raw), whose
`\@addtoreset{equation}{section}` resets it at numbered sections only. Not followed: aa.cls v4.03 (1998, 5 copies)
numbers "A1" where every later release numbers "A.1"; an elsarticle copy shaped as elsart (2111.07466: elsart's
`\def\appendix{\@ifstar…}`, no `\renewcommand\appendix`) keeps the kernel's numbering. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78q::*`.

### 865. `\nonumber` removes an `{equation}`'s number only where amsmath is loaded

latex.ltx:15737-15739 `{equation}` always prints `\@eqnnum`; `\nonumber` (:15775 `\global\@eqnswfalse`) is eqnarray's
switch, which the next `\eqnarray` sets again, and amsmath's `\nonumber` (amsmath.sty:1268-1269) is what removes an
`{equation}`'s number. Perl gives every `{equation}` amsmath's behaviour on purpose (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1915-1916,
"even though stock LaTeX provides no means to override them"), so a paper without amsmath that writes `\nonumber` in an
`{equation}` lost the number pdflatex prints, and every later number was one behind (hep-ph9710521's `\nl` in a `\beq`,
45 of 56 labels matching its PDF; nucl-th0404042's `j-sum1` and `l-sum1`, PDF 20 and 23, unnumbered). Ours (78r,
sect07.rs): LaTeX's `{equation}` marks its numbering `LATEX_EQNNUM` unless amsmath is loaded (`amsmath_nonumber`:
`\@ifpackageloaded{amsmath}`'s `\ver@amsmath.sty`, or the binding's or the raw file's loaded flag; a binding's load
beyond its original, `amsmath_loaded_beyond_original`, counts as not loaded; `\ver@` because aa.cls's binding clears the
flag after today's aa.cls loads amsmath, aa_cls.rs), and `\lx@equation@nonumber` does nothing in such an equation. One
helper, `prepare_latex_equation_counter` (sect07.rs), sets that numbering for LaTeX's `{equation}` and for the class
bindings that redefine it only to let a `$` in it: mn2e/mnras/mn (mn2e_support_sty.rs) and aa (aa_support_sty.rs, the
old aa.cls without amsmath; a shipped aa.cls that loads it keeps amsmath's `\nonumber`, 1712.01010, 1812.04463,
2501.07980). `\documentclass{mnras}` with a `\nonumber` in an `{equation}`: pdflatex (1) (2), "See 1; 2."; int54a and 78r
r1 removed the first number (78r r2 review finding 2; repro class-bindings/mnras_equation_nonumber_keeps_the_number,
guard `perfect_kernel_batch78r::mnras_equation_nonumber_keeps_the_number`). REVTeX 3's aps.sty:401-450, REVTeX 4.x (which loads
amsmath only under its `amsmath` option, revtex4-2.cls:6132-6140) and iopart.cls:771-776 print the number as LaTeX does
(28 REVTeX 3 and 8 iopart papers of the 123 census papers; 19 more REVTeX 4.x papers). Equation `\ref` numbers against
pdflatex's `.aux` (int54a / 78r): hep-ph9710521 61 / 74 of 74, nucl-th0404042 15 / 17 of 17; 13 changed census papers
92 / 274 → 273 / 274 (7 more do not build under TL 2025); the 19 REVTeX 4.x papers 370 / 561 → 560 / 561. Residual: a
`\nonumber` inside an amsmath inner block of an `{equation}` (`aligned`, `split`) still removes the equation's number,
where amsmath's local `\let\print@eqnum\@empty` ends with the block (2407.10017 `eq:chainMapHam`, PDF 41; int54a the
same). Repros cross-references/equation_nonumber_without_amsmath_keeps_the_number,
equation_nonumber_with_amsmath_removes_the_number; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78r::{equation_nonumber_without_amsmath_keeps_the_number,
equation_nonumber_with_amsmath_removes_the_number}`. A `\label` in an amsmath `{equation}` with `\nonumber` names the number the equation stepped, and a `\nonumber` after a `\tag` keeps the tag (78t, #875); in the residual's `aligned`/`split` case the label so names pdflatex's number while the equation still prints none.

### 875. A `\label` in an amsmath `{equation}` with `\nonumber` names the number the equation stepped

amsmath's `{equation}` (amsmath.sty:2913-2932) steps the counter at its start (`\incr@eqnum`, `\refstepcounter`, which
sets `\@currentlabel`); its `\nonumber` (:1269-1275) steps the counter back only while `\if@eqnsw` holds, and the
display's `\label` is made at its end (`\label@in@display`, `\endmathdisplay@a` :2821-2830), so it names the stepped
number, the next equation's, which neither equation prints. A `\nonumber` after a `\tag` (or a second one) finds the
switch off and changes nothing: `\tag{X}\nonumber` prints "(X)". Perl retracts the number and the label names the
enclosing unit (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2025-2057), and a `\nonumber` after `\tag` retracted the tag too. Ours
(78t, sect07.rs): amsmath's `{equation}` marks its numbering (`AMS_EQUATION`, set by `prepare_latex_equation_counter`
where amsmath is loaded, OD #865); `\lx@equation@nonumber` there digests the stepped number's reference forms before it
retracts the number (`eqnarray_next_number_tags`, the eqnarray form of #847: refnum, typerefnum, … and no printed tag),
and does nothing once the number is gone; the `ltx:equation` drops them when it closes without a label
(`NEXT_NUMBER_EQUATION`). `{equation*}` and `\[…\]` step nothing: their labels name the enclosing unit as before, which is
pdflatex's `\@currentlabel` there (the display's group undoes an inner step). A `\nonumber` inside an `aligned`/`split`
of an `{equation}` reaches the same branch: the label now names the stepped number as pdflatex's does, while the
equation's own number is still removed (the #865 residual). Witness 1306.2116 (`eq:covariate`, PDF 17, int57a "3.1";
`.aux` equation numbers 75 → 77 of 77). A cleveref quirk stays: cleveref's `\label` writes its `@cref` entry from the
counter as it stands at the label (cleveref.sty `\cref@currentlabel`), after `\nonumber` stepped it back, so pdflatex's
`\cref{e2}` prints "eq. (1)" (`\newlabel{e2@cref}{{[equation][1][]1}…}`) where `\ref` and `\eqref` print 2; ours prints
"(2)" for both, the number the label names (probe `\begin{equation} b=2 \nonumber\label{e2}\end{equation}` after an
`{equation}` 1, amsmath + hyperref + cleveref). KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1128. Repro
cross-references/ams_equation_nonumber_label_names_the_stepped_number; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78t::ams_equation_nonumber_label_names_the_stepped_number`.

### 876. subfigure's panels are numbered whatever their arguments, with the kernel's caption; subfigure.cfg is read

subfigure.sty:208-262: `\subfigure` (and `\subtable`, its `\let`) always `\refstepcounter{sub\@captype}`; an absent
optional is `\@empty` and prints no caption, an explicit `[]` prints the "(a)" caption (`\ifx\@empty#3`), and
`[list][caption]` captions with the second. Perl captions only non-empty text (subfigure.sty.ltxml:138-171
`\ifx.#2.\ifx.#1.\else\caption{#1}\fi`), so `\subfigure[]{…\label{a}}` and `\subfigure{…\label{a}}` named the figure and
every later panel was one letter behind (1507.00722: PDF 1(a), 1(b), int57a "1", "1"). The sub-caption is built by
`\@subcaption`/`\@make<sub>caption` (:279-290; subfig's by `\sf@subcaption`, caption3's `\caption@make`,
subfig.sty:384-411), never by `\caption`, so a document's `\def\caption#1{\splitter #1@@}` does not read it (1808.10020:
int57a 48 "Paragraph ended before \splitter" Errors, its repro a Fatal; Perl 55). subfigure.sty:205-208 reads
subfigure.cfg (TeX Live's: `\ExecuteOptions{tight,TABTOPCAP}`), so a sub-table after its table's `\caption` does not
step the table counter ahead (1(a), not 2(a)) and is captioned above its tabular. Ours (78t): subfigure_sty.rs's
`\subfigure`/`\subtable` read their optionals as given (`subfloat_tokens`) — `\lx@caption[list]{caption}`,
`\lx@caption{caption}`, or the counter's step alone (`\@@add@caption@counters`, as `\phantomcaption`) — through the
kernel's `\caption` under its own name (`\lx@caption`, sect09.rs), and the binding inputs subfigure.cfg before
`\ProcessOptions`; subfig_sty.rs's `\subfloat[list][caption]` the same, for the pre-built figure and table types and a
`\newsubfloat` type's (`define_subfloat`) alike (Perl's `\caption{#1}` printed the list entry).
subcaption's `\subcaption` keeps `\caption` (subcaption.sty:240-251 `\subcaption@newabbreviation\subcaption\caption`:
the document's `\caption` is what pdflatex calls too). `.aux` figure numbers: 1507.00722 7 → 8 of 9 (the 9th, a label
before the main `\caption`, pdflatex's empty `\@currentlabel`), 1808.10020 275 → 379 of 385 (the rest labels after a
`\subfigure` group, which pdflatex gives the section's number). Reading subfigure.cfg works the other way too, as pdflatex
does: under its `TABTOPCAP` a sub-table before a bottom `\caption` (and under `FIGTOPCAP` a sub-figure before one) does
not step ahead either, so it takes the previous float's number, "0(a)" in the first table
(`\begin{table}\subtable[A]{x\label{a}}\caption{T}\end{table}\ref{a}`: pdflatex and ours "0(a)", Perl "1(a)"; a second
such table's panels 1(a); 1909.03617's `.aux` 0(a), 0(b); 1506.06418, 2012.09202, 1506.09092; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1127)
— pdflatex's numbering, not a defect to fix.

A panel's stated width is its body's, never its caption's: subfigure.sty:232-233 measures the body
(`\setbox\@tempboxa\hbox{#4}\@tempdima=\wd\@tempboxa`) and sets the sub-caption in a `\parbox` of that width, where our
caption is a paragraph of the column's `\hsize` (`\lx@@caption PBoxContents`), so a captioned panel measured whole took a
row of its own in `arrange_panels` — `\subfigure[text]` panels always (Perl the same: latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3286
measures the panel's box), and with the "(a)" captions above the `[]` panels too (78t r1: 28 of the A/B's 1,607 papers
gained breaks, 129 → 232 in the panel figures; 2006.08949 Figure 2, one row in the PDF, four; cond-mat9707225,
astro-ph0205132; 1208.0688's `\subfigure[text]` pairs). `{@subfigure}`/`{@subtable}` record their body's width less its
`\lx@@caption`/`\@@toccaption`, its `\lx@label`s and its spaces, the glue it states (`\hskip`, `\hspace`, `\quad`; an
`\hfill` is 0 wide) adding its natural width (78x r4, as the panel grid rule counts stated glue between panels, OD #885:
1307.3388 Fig 3's `\subfigure[]{⏎\hspace{-0.4cm}⏎\includegraphics…}` pairs, 2+2 in the PDF; kerns are kept) —
`panel_body_width`, `note_sub_float_body_width` (latex_constructs/mod.rs) — which `panel_width` takes when it
is above 0: the width the source states, the LaTeX-side width FIDELITY_CHARTER §2 "Float panels" keeps. A `\label` makes
no box (a `\write`), where the `\lx@label` whatsit was sized by its key's text (0907.1044's `\subfigure[…]{\label{…}
\includegraphics…}` panels 96pt too wide; since 79c it is 0 wide everywhere, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1144); with the spaces left out a `\label` between spaces counts nothing either
(2511.21020 Figs 7-8 one row of four, 1607.02761, 2211.12798, 1601.02116; 78t r2 counted both spaces and split them 3+1).
A body of no known width (0) leaves the panel its box's width, as before the body measure (78t r2 took the 0: such panels
joined every row and, starting one, left the panel list, so 1610.06413's two-panel figures had no flex row; nlin0606018);
epsfig's `\psfig` is sized by its keys and its file, Perl's `sizer => \&image_graphicx_sizer` (epsfig.sty.ltxml:37,
epsfig_sty.rs), so hep-ex0703011's `\mbox` pairs of 2.8in panels are sized, cond-mat9707225's too; an EPS's natural or
`scale=` size came out at 72.27/100 of TeX's through that sizer until 78z, which reads its BoundingBox in bp (#886;
1106.2745 Figs 1-2, 7, 8, 10), and a
`\psfig` is a `\vbox` (psfig.sty:944) that starts a paragraph, Perl's too (astro-ph0512442 Fig 2). A body holding only a
caption (a `\captionof{subfigure}` host) keeps the box's width.

The rows are Perl's greedy rule (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3287-3295, `arrange_panels`) fed by these widths. 78t r3
emulated TeX's line breaking for a justified float (`justified_row_is_overfull`: `\sloppy`'s badness with 3em of
emergency stretch and tex.web §854's overfull line, for subfigure.sty's in-paragraph panels; a `\label`'s
`\@bsphack…\@esphack` space rule); 78t r5 removed it, as the charter directs (user 2026-10-22: the panels are a logical
grid derived from what the source states; do not re-run TeX's line breaking against one page geometry, the browser's
width varies; grid design study 2026-10-22, Q5). The grid rule — explicit breaks (`\\`, a blank line or `\par`,
`\newline`, a `{center}` boundary, `\vskip`), the stated widths and the stated glue between panels against the line, the
geometry's `\Gm@tw`, the class's real line — landed with 78x (#885; RED `captions-floats/par_breaks_a_panel_row` turned
green, `a_justified_row_keeps_its_overfull_panel` an accepted residual), the markup that says rows × columns is the next
payload, on the user's ruling (SYNC_STATUS "panel grid markup" row). Before #885 the rows missed what the tree did not
hold: the glue and `\par`
between sub-figures (our sub-figures are digested in vertical mode until something starts a paragraph: 0706.4410 Figs 3,
5, an `\hspace{1in}` between two 0.45\textwidth panels, two rows in the PDF, one here; 2207.14807 Fig 9's `}%`; 1110.0084
Figs 12-16, 27, 29), TeX's overfull and underfull lines (1201.0008 Figs 1-2: the PDF's three in a row, overfull, here
2+1; hep-ex0703011's `\mbox` pairs), the geometry (1508.01788 Figs 19-22, 1411.5428 Figs 6-7, 2111.05508), a `\\` in
`{center}` (0912.4528, 1206.5015), the panels a `tabular` held (lifted out of it: 1309.3581, astro-ph0205132) and a
two-column document's `figure*`, measured against a `\columnwidth` that is our `\textwidth`, as Perl's
(latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:321: 1707.00190, nucl-ex0511052, 2502.05562, astro-ph0205132; REVTeX 3's 345pt text,
cond-mat9707225) — SYNC_STATUS rows. Rows per float against the PDF's (pdflatex box dumps) on the grid design study's
oracle set, 453 multi-panel floats in 108 papers: int61a 300, 78t r3 344, r5 354 (exact shapes 282, 330, 336); the 9
floats int61a set right and r5 does not are set so by r3 too, where int61a's full-width captions broke the rows by
accident: the unseen glue and `\par` between panels (0706.4410 Figs 3, 5; 1110.0084 Figs 27, 29), TeX's spaces round and
between near-half panels, which the stated widths leave out (1601.02116 Figs 7-8, two `0.48\textwidth` graphics with a
space on each side; 1107.3402 Fig 5; 1511.03368 Fig 3) and a panel of no stated width (1012.1425 Fig 4). Witnesses of the PDF verdicts: 1411.5428 Figs 6-7, 0706.4410 Fig 4, 1508.01788
Figs 19-22, 1304.1952 Fig 14, 2209.01559 Fig 7. Over the r5 A/B (int61a → r5, 1,888 papers) the sub-float figures' row breaks are 3,813 → 3,144: 471 floats in 192
papers lose a break, 13 floats in 6 papers gain one — 2401.07345 as its PDF, and the geometry, lifted-`tabular` and
REVTeX 3 rows above (1309.3581, astro-ph0205132, cond-mat9707225, nucl-ex0511052), and 1408.2843 Fig 1, whose captioned
panels' graphics are missing, so their bodies have no width and fall back to the captioned box (1503.04804 Fig 3 the
same against r3, which counted the body's leading space; SYNC_STATUS grid-rule row).
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1125-#1127, #1130. Repros
captions-floats/{subfigure_empty_optional_is_a_numbered_panel, subfigure_caption_is_not_the_documents_caption,
subtable_after_the_caption_is_numbered_by_it, subfig_caption_is_not_the_documents_caption,
subfigure_panel_is_as_wide_as_its_body, a_label_between_spaces_counts_one, psfig_panels_are_as_wide_as_their_keys}
(and the RED a_justified_row_keeps_its_overfull_panel, the grid rule's); guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78t::{subfigure_empty_optional_is_a_numbered_panel, subfigure_caption_is_not_the_documents_caption,
subtable_after_the_caption_is_numbered_by_it, subfig_caption_is_not_the_documents_caption,
subfigure_panel_is_as_wide_as_its_body, a_label_between_spaces_counts_one, psfig_panels_are_as_wide_as_their_keys}`.

### 877. A `\label` after an algorithm2e line's number names the line

algorithm2e.sty:1657-1667: `\nl` is `\refstepcounter{AlgoLine}\gdef\@currentlabel{\theAlgoLine}` (with hyperref
`\stepcounter{AlgoLine}` and `\algocf@nl@sethref{\theAlgoLine}`) then `\algocf@printnl`, so a `\label` after a line's
number names that line until the next number: in the line, after its `\;` (`stmt\; \label{x}`, the label then at the
next line's start), or at a block's start (`\While{c}{\label{x} …}`, the `\gdef` outliving the header's group). Perl's
line carries the printed number alone and the label names the algorithm (algorithm2e.sty.ltxml:180-221). Ours (78t):
`\algocf@printnl@i` records the line as the object of its number's raw step (`Document::note_raw_refstep_object`,
marking it `RAW_REFSTEP_MARK`; the kernel's record of a `\refstepcounter` no constructor took, #813), made global as the
`\gdef` makes `\@currentlabel` (`\lx@refstep@global`, `globalize_raw_refstep`), and forgotten in the next algorithm's
group, whose `\@algocf@init` steps `algocfline` (algorithm2e.sty:2560-2561: a label at its start names that algorithm,
2010.00626's `alg:F_cycle`, PDF 2); with hyperref, `\algocf@nl@sethref`
records that step (`\lx@refstepcounter@label{AlgoLine}`) when the number is `\theAlgoLine` (`\nlset`'s own text records
none). A label after the step goes to that line wherever it stands (`Document::float_to_label_scoped`; its id is made at
its close), and the line, which printed the number itself, takes the step's reference forms into its tags
(`Document::take_raw_refstep_number`); `renumber_algo_lines` renumbers them with the printed number (the over-stepped
`AlgoLine` counter). Witnesses 2406.05437 (`step1`, `step2`: PDF 14, 17, int57a "1"; `.aux` 37 → 39 of 40), 1602.05866
(`algline:mainloop`, PDF 8). Residuals: `\nlset{text}` lines take no reference form; a labelled line's id is made at its
close, out of its listing's order (`algorithm1.1` in `algorithm1.5`); `renumber_algo_lines` restarts each listing at 1
where a paper continues the count across algorithms (1311.7635: PDF 9-11, ours 2-4; int57a the algorithm's number);
`\enl` (algorithm2e.sty:1671-1679) steps `AlgoLine` and makes it `\@currentlabel` globally but never calls
`\algocf@printnl`, so its line is recorded as no step's object and a label after it names the algorithm, as before.

The later `\label` of a key wins. With a line able to take a label, one key labels two elements where a paper repeats it:
2001.00288's `\label{algo2}` at a block's start (its line) and after `\caption` (the algorithm). LaTeX's last `\newlabel`
wins (latex.ltx `\@newl@bel`: `\global\@namedef{r@key}`, "Label multiply defined"; pdflatex "Algorithm 2"), while the
post scan registers in document order, the outer element first, so the inner, earlier one won (Perl Scan.pm:196-203, ours
scan.rs `register_scanned`; 78t r1 "Algorithm 1", a line). Ours (78t r2): a `\label` placed on its element takes the key
from the earlier holders that contain it or that it contains (`Document::release_earlier_label_holders`, from the
`\lx@label` constructor, only for a key placed before). Holders apart from each other keep it: pdflatex's last
`\newlabel` is the last written, which is the later in the document but for a float LaTeX defers past a later label of
the key (below), and the scan takes the later already; the streaming build may have spilled the earlier
(a closed top-level element, never an ancestor of the holder nor, below the root, a descendant), so the streaming and
eager builds agree (`114_streaming_graphics`: graphrot's two tables labelled `tb:tab3`).
Perl keeps both, the inner winning (`\caption{Panel}\label{x}` in a subcaption `{subfigure}`, then `\caption{Main}
\label{x}`: Perl "1(a)", pdflatex 1; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1131). In the 1,608-paper A/B 15 earlier holders in 10 papers
gave their key up (1908.05655's `fig:rule_example` on five displays inside its figure, then after the figure's
`\caption`: the figure, as pdflatex), no key left the document, and the `.aux` labels matching pdflatex's last
`\newlabel` over 144 papers are 6,582 (int58a) → 7,094 (r1) → 7,095 (r2).
Witnesses 2001.00288 (`.aux` 13 → 14 of 19 matching, int58a's 14), 1611.06737, 1711.00112, 1804.00071, 2010.05861,
2209.06323, 2511.10625, astro-ph0512093. Residual:
algorithm2e sets a caption's text in a box it places at the style's caption position (`\global\sbox\algocf@capbox`,
algorithm2e.sty:2305-2336: the bottom for `plain`/`boxed`, the top for the ruled family), and a `\label` in it is written
there, so in 2511.10625's `plain` algorithm the caption-text `\label{alg:general_astar}` is written after the same key's
`\label` after the last line and names the algorithm (pdflatex 1, ours the line, 13, as 78t r1; int58a 1). And a float
LaTeX defers writes its `\newlabel` when it is placed, after a later label of the same key, and wins in pdflatex:
`\begin{figure}[p]\caption{Deferred}\label{k}\end{figure}\section{Two}\label{k}See \ref{k}.` — pdflatex "See 1." (the
figure, written on page 2), ours and int58a "See 2." (review rev78t2's lb2; SYNC_STATUS row).

KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1129, #1131. Repros listings-algorithms/algorithm2e_line_label_names_the_line,
cross-references/the_later_label_wins; guards `perfect_kernel_batch78t::{algorithm2e_line_label_names_the_line,
the_later_label_wins}`.

### 880. `classify_thanks` reads its funding words as words

`classify_thanks` (author_block/notes.rs, #156) names an author note's kind for its `ltx_thanks_<kind>` class, and the
author block's line readers (line_kinds.rs `weldable_line`, `reads_as_place`, `institution_beside_labelled`,
`reads_as_institution`, `labelled_institution`) and the frontmatter observer's resolver ask it whether a line is a note
rather than an institution. Its funding test matched substrings, so "erc" in "Perception", "Recherche", "Commerce",
"Merced", "supercomputing", "nsf" in "transferred" and "fund" in "Fundamental" read an institution or a copyright notice
as funding (2509.05368 "Guangdong Laboratory of Machine Perception…", 1609.09226 "Intelligent Perception" (CRIPAC); 2310.19455
"Tata Institute of Fundamental Research", the IEEE notice "Copyright may be transferred…" of 2603.29506 and 9 more). Ours (78u): the words
of the lowercased text (`funding_word`) — "support…", "grant(s)"/"granted", "fund…" but not "fundament…", and a funder's
acronym on its own or with its number glued (NSF, NSFC, NIH, ONR, DARPA, ERC, and SNSF, FNRS, NSERC, SERC, which the
in-word reading also caught: "SNSF Postdoctoral Fellow", 2507.18869; "Chercheur qualifié FNRS", cond-mat0504758).
Correspondence, contribution and address are read as before. Perl has no classifier (the note is a contact there). A/B
(`census/pops/pop78u_2.tsv`: the 1,441 census papers whose author-block text the old and the new reading class
differently; release int59a vs 78u): 1,437 converted, E 3,046 = 3,046, F 6 = 6, W and words equal, 55 papers changed,
every one a `ltx_thanks_funding` → `ltx_thanks_note` on an institution, a position or the IEEE copyright notice (60
notes, read one by one); no affiliation reading moved. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78u::thanks_institution_with_erc_in_a_word_is_no_funding`,
`author_split_tests::classify_thanks_reads_funding_words_whole`.

### 881. A note written inside an author's mark is taken out after it

latex.ltx:17215 `\thanks` (and `\footnote`, `\footnotemark`) inside a superscript prints its own mark there and its text
as a footnote, so `Nataliia Babina\textsuperscript{\rm 1,\rm 2\thanks{Work done during internship at Integral AI.}}` is
"Nataliia Babina1,2∗" with a note (2512.05464). Perl's `\lx@author@withsup` (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:729-734) lets
`\textsuperscript` and `^` be the annotation request, which reads the whole operand as its label, so the label
`2\thanks{…}` answered nothing and printed nothing: the mark `2` and the note were lost, in Perl and ours alike
(KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1136). Ours (78u): `notes_out_of_marks` (author_block/preprocess.rs, first in
`add_authors_calls_sectioned`) takes every note command a mark's braced operand holds, at any depth (`^{\mathbf{1,
\thanks{…}}}`), with its arguments, out after the mark — `\textsuperscript{\rm 1,\rm 2}\thanks{…}` — so the mark's
labels are read as labels and the note is the author's, as one written after the mark; a macro of optional arguments
only whose expansion holds a note command is taken out with its `[…]` the same way (`split_mark_notes`, `makes_a_note`:
the AAAI stub `\equalcontrib`, 2603.17529; a document's `\newcommand*\samethanks[1][\value{footnote}]{\footnotemark[#1]}`,
2309.12862), while a macro of no arguments that prints a label beside a note (`\newcommand\fnA{2\footnotemark}`) is read
with its body in its place, the "2" a label (`prints_beside_a_note`, 78v) — only when its body holds no conditional and,
its notes out, only label-safe tokens (characters, font switches, spaces, a `\protect` right before a note command,
another such macro); any other falls back to being taken out whole, so what its body does beside the note stays TeX's
(`\fnD{\thanks{D note}\unskip}` "Di Delta3" and the note, `\fnE{\ifshow\footnotemark\fi}` under `\showfalse` "Ed Eps4"
and no mark, `\fnF[1][x]{6\footnotemark}`, whose "6" stays in the name text as before: 78v r2, review rev78v finding 1;
a `\relax` or another `\protect` beside the label, `{\relax 5\footnotemark}`, `{\protect 5\footnotemark}`, a
`\DeclareRobustCommand`'s `\protect\fnS␣`, which the label would keep and no list answers, and so one written after a
`\protect`, `\textsuperscript{\protect\fnA}`, its "5"/"2" in the name text as before: 78v r3, review rev78v2 finding 1),
and a `\protect` right before a note command goes out with it (`\textsuperscript{1\protect\thanks{…}}` kept the label
`1\protect`, 78v; guard `perfect_kernel_batch78v::author_protect_thanks_and_note_macro_inside_a_mark`); a mark holding nothing else goes
(`$^{\thanks{Topical Group Conveners}}$`, 2212.00809). The mark readers (`\lx@sup@request@affiliation`,
`\lx@sup@setlabel@affiliation`) read a note left in an operand after the mark all the same
(`frontmatter_sup_operand_and_notes`), for a binding that wraps a line in `\lx@author@withsup` itself. The note mark is
printed after the mark rather than inside it (the size of the mark only). Residual (order): a label no list answers is
shown by `show_unanswered_marks` at the end of the name, so a `\footnotemark` taken out of `$^{1 \footnotemark[1]}$`
precedes it ("Ann Alpha∗1", pdflatex "Ann Alpha1∗"; 2403.04164, 2203.10085); the same holds today for
`Ann$^{1}$\footnotemark[1]` written so (the census: 223 mark-then-`\footnotemark` adjacencies in 135 papers, 23 the
other way in 15). Census (`census/pops/pop78u_1.tsv`: every census paper with a note command, or a macro making one,
inside a name block's `\textsuperscript{…}`/`^{…}`; 32 papers): A/B release int59a vs 78u, XML changed in 28, every one
a regained note or mark (notes 76 → 110, words +332), E/F/W equal; the other 4 are a false hit (2503.05186's
`\corresponding` is a symbol), a block whose note was kept already (2604.18459, authblk), one with no creator either way
(2012.01602) and 2211.09622, whose main file the harness missed (its `main.tex` by hand: "corresponding author"
regained). PDF (arXiv) checked for 16: 2512.05464, 1911.03118, 1912.00833, 2306.17472, 2309.12862, 2403.04164,
2410.12564, 2502.15412, 2503.05905, 2402.13113, 1310.0294, 2211.09622, 2402.18447, 2501.01423, 2605.17958, 2603.17529 —
notes present, marks as printed; unchanged residuals there: a symbol inside a mark (`\textsuperscript{\rm 1,2,$^{*}$}`,
1911.03118) or glued to a label (`\textsuperscript{\rm 1*}`, 1912.00833; `$^{{2*}…}$`, 2305.16614) prints nothing, the
glued one losing its affiliation too, and an inline affiliation row parted only by its marks stays one contact
(2305.16614). Repros sectioning-frontmatter/author_thanks_inside_a_mark_keeps_the_mark_and_the_note,
author_math_mark_thanks_keeps_the_mark_and_the_note, author_footnotemark_inside_a_mark_is_kept,
author_note_macro_inside_a_mark_keeps_the_note; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78u::{author_thanks_inside_a_mark_keeps_the_mark_and_the_note,
author_math_mark_thanks_keeps_the_mark_and_the_note, author_footnotemark_inside_a_mark_is_kept,
author_note_macro_inside_a_mark_keeps_the_note}`,
`author_split_tests::notes_out_of_marks_takes_the_note_after_the_mark`.

### 882. A graphic named with an extension it was not shipped under is found under its base name at digestion

graphics.sty:205-231 takes `\includegraphics{recomb.eps}` as that file, and pdftex.def's `.eps` rule converts it
(epstopdf); authors who ran epstopdf themselves often shipped only `recomb.pdf`, which arXiv's pdflatex of the time read
(TL 2025's epstopdf asks for `recomb-eps-converted-to.pdf` instead: "File not found"). Perl's `image_candidates`
(Util/Image.pm:43-56) searches `recomb.eps.*` and `recomb.eps` only, so the graphic has no candidates and
`image_graphicx_sizer` no size, and its post loses the image too (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1137). Ours (78v): when a name with
a graphics extension (`has_graphics_extension`) names no file on the search paths nor in the texmf tree, `image_candidates`
(util/image.rs) retries its base name and keeps the files of a graphics type that answer it — the rule post's
`find_graphic_file` (latexml_post graphics.rs) already applied, which kept the HTML right — so the box has the real
file's size and a sub-figure panel its width. A requested file that exists is found first and stays the only candidate
(`fig.eps` beside a `fig.pdf`); an extensionless name, or one the search finds, is untouched. The retry's hits are
listed in the order TeX tries them (`in_graphics_type_order`: by type, pdftex.def's `\Gin@extensions` order,
pdftex.def:597-600, its uppercase `.PDF,…,.JB2` after its lowercase ones as it lists them, then `.eps`, which
epstopdf-base.sty:498-505 appends, `.ps` and post's types, their other-case variants last; then by search directory, the `\graphicspath`/`\input@path` order each type is looked for along; then by name
within one directory), not the directory's, since the sizer reads the first readable one (0907.3747 had
`nuebar.pdf,nuebar.ps` beside `nuebar_limit.ps,nuebar_limit.pdf`; 78v r2, review rev78v finding 3;
`\graphicspath{{new/}{figs/}}` takes `new/plot.pdf` first, where a tie-break by full path took `figs/plot.pdf` and sized
the box from it: 78v r3, review rev78v2 findings 2-3, guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78v::includegraphics_eps_retry_keeps_the_graphicspath_order`). Witnesses 1408.2843 Fig 1-2
(`recomb.eps` → `recomb.pdf`), 1503.04804 Fig 3 (`pnt_pwpt_*.eps` → `.pdf`); 97 of the census's 26,364 graphics papers name
such a file (in the first five per paper: 261 `.eps`, 12 `.png`, 12 `.pdf`, 1 `.ps`, 1 `.jpg` names), 77 of which gain
candidates and sizes in the 78v A/B. Repro
package-bindings/includegraphics_eps_shipped_only_as_pdf_is_sized; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78v::includegraphics_eps_shipped_only_as_pdf_is_sized`.

### 883. Output that followed a hash table's layout is in key order: the dump's records, CrossRef's missing-id report, a PI's keys, held-tag roles, idcheck, the fragment index, an extensionless graphic's candidates

The det354 determinism audit (agent_reports/2026-10-22_det354_audit.md) found no hash order reaching output from one
run to the next, but these sites wrote what a hash table or the filesystem listed, so their order changed from one binary
(or host) to the next; each now sorts, by key, at the emit site (78w):

- **The format dump** (`dump_writer.rs` `write_dump`): Perl TeX_Job.pool.ltxml:150,153 walks `sort @tables` and, in each,
  `sort keys`, so its dump is in (table, key) order; ours wrote `diff_from_snapshot`'s hash order, one key set in 55
  record orders across 173 vendor dumps, and since the dump is applied in file order that also set the symbol ids of
  every conversion. Each section (early aliases, regular entries, late aliases) is now in (table name, key) order — a
  table's `Display` name sorts as Perl's lowercase names do — so a dump is a function of its content. Applying a dump
  is order-free but for one record kind (each record `assign_internal('global')` to a distinct key; a late alias names a
  definition's own cs, never another alias), as det354 measured (20 papers byte-identical XML, HTML and logs under a
  shuffled Section 1). The exception: a register's `M` row (`R(…)`) skips writing its address slot when that slot
  already holds a value (`dump_reader.rs` `should_assign`, `:979`, mirroring Perl `def_register`), so it depends on
  whether the address's `V` row came first; both orders end at the `V` row's value, and with the sort every `M` row
  (`meaning`) loads before every `V` row (`value`), so the `V` value is the one written last (review rev78w finding 7).
  Unit test `dump_writer::tests::a_shuffled_diff_writes_the_same_dump`.
- **CrossRef's report of unresolved references** (latexml_post `crossref.rs` `report_missing`): Perl CrossRef.pm:64-76
  — the severities `error, warn, info`, the types of each sorted; the ids of a type are sorted too, where Perl's hash
  `keys` order is random. Guard `perfect_kernel_batch78w::missing_targets_are_reported_in_order`.
- **A processing instruction's keys** (`document.rs` `insert_pi`, `pi_data`): `class`, `package`, `options` first, each
  only when its value is true to Perl (not empty, not `0`: `$attrib{$_} ? ($_) : ()`, Document.pm:707; an
  `options=""` used to be printed), then the rest sorted (Document.pm:708). Unit tests `document::pi_data_order`.
- **The held-tag roles** a label answers for (latex_constructs `sect11.rs` `tie_held_tags`, `held_tag_roles`), so a
  reference showing two roles replays their held diagnostics in the roles' order (logger.rs `replay_shown_deferred`).
  Unit test `sect11::held_tag_role_order`.
- **idcheck's "Cached IDs not in document"** list (latexml_post `document.rs` `idcheck`; Perl Post.pm:1006-1014 random).
- **The streaming fragment index's side file** (`sxml/fragment_index.rs` `save`). Unit test
  `fragment_index::tests::save_lists_each_kind_in_key_order`.
- **An image name's candidates** (`util/image.rs` `image_candidates`): the files a name answers — `fig.<ext>` for an
  extensionless `\includegraphics{fig}`, and the exact, case-folded and other-extension lists — are in TeX's order
  (`in_graphics_type_order`, OD #882: by type in pdftex.def's `\Gin@extensions` order, pdftex.def:597-600 — since 79a
  `\Gin@extensions` first, as TeX edits it: `\DeclareGraphicsExtensions`, grfext, epstopdf's `.eps`, OD #886 —, then by
  search directory, then by name), not `read_dir`'s, which the filesystem decides (a tmpfs lists newest first, ext4 by
  name hash) and which Perl's `pathname_findall` follows (Pathname.pm:350-371). The first candidate gives the natural
  box (`cssstyle`) and is pdflatex's choice. This also changes Perl's fixed order across search directories: Perl's
  list gives "precedence to leading directories" (Pathname.pm:375), all of one directory's hits before the next's,
  where the type now comes first, so `\graphicspath{{a/}{b/}}` lists `b/fig.pdf` before `a/fig.png` — TeX's order, as
  graphics.sty:206-224 runs `\@for\Gin@temp:=\Gin@extensions` outermost with the path search inside `\IfFileExists`
  (review rev78w finding 4; no A/B paper has the shape). Witness 2011.14197 (`fig3..6.eps,.pdf` → `.pdf,.eps`, sized by
  `width=`, no size change). Unit test `util::image::candidate_order_tests::
  extensionless_candidates_in_one_order_whatever_the_directory_lists` (`image_candidate_lists`, the names of two
  directories fed as listed, reversed and rotated; red without the sort); the conversion guard
  `perfect_kernel_batch78w::includegraphics_extensionless_candidates_in_type_order` is the whole-output check, red on
  int64a only on a tmpfs `/tmp` (on ext4, the CI runner's, int64a's order already passes; review rev78w finding 1);
  repro package-bindings/includegraphics_extensionless_candidates_in_type_order.

Not changed: the custom frontmatter blocks (`frontmatter/insert.rs` `custom_keys`) follow the source order, deterministic
(Perl's `keys %$frontmatter` is random; main-session decision); the `xmlns:*` declaration order on the root is stable
today and tracked as a SYNC row (Perl's first-use order, Document.pm:1393-1394,1874).

### 884. A class's `\@makecaption` reaches every caption it makes, as names and separators; caption replaces it

LaTeX makes a kernel float's caption with the class's `\@makecaption` whatever its type — a figure, a table, a newfloat
type (newfloat.sty:59-125 `\@float`), a listings caption (listings.sty:1675 `\lst@makecaption`) — while float.sty's own
styles (`\floatc@plain`) and longtable (longtable.sty:475-483 `\LT@makecaption`, "Table 1: text") make theirs
themselves; caption, once loaded, replaces `\@makecaption` and formats float.sty's and longtable's captions too
(caption.sty:856-868, :1167), its default separator the class's (caption3.sty:1125-1171: caption-ams-smf.sto:41's
`.\enspace` under an AMS class, else :787's colon). Perl's bindings give each type a fixed format (`\format@title@figure`
"Figure 1: ", listings' "Listing 1: ", newfloat's none, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1124), so a class's format reached figures and
tables only, and IEEEtran's and acmart's not at all (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1140). Here:

- **`\lx@makecaption{<type>}{<text>}`** (latex_constructs_rust_only.rs, the kernel's "Figure 1: text") is the class's
  `\@makecaption`: newfloat's types (newfloat_sty.rs) and listings (listings_sty.rs) take it, and a class whose
  `\@makecaption` is its own redefines it with its figure's and table's formats — the AMS classes' ". " (ams_support_sty.rs
  `ams_class_caption_format`, from ams_core_cls.rs and amsbook_cls.rs, not from ams_support, which amsaddr and the
  `\curraddr`/`\subjclass` autoloads bring to article: there the kernel's "Figure 1: " stays) and, through
  `caption_sty::class_makecaption` (installed at `\begin{document}` unless caption is loaded; caption's kernel alone,
  floatrow's, keeps it), IEEEtran's by mode ("Fig. 1. text", "TABLE I" over its text, compsoc's arabic tables and
  conferences' "Figure"), ieeeaccess's, ieeeoj's and ieeetj's one-line "FIGURE 1. text" / "TABLE 1. text" (their
  `\figurename` and arabic `\thetable`, ieeeaccess Roman under `jtehm`), jfm's, webofc's and jinstpub's
  (`class_makecaption_label`). A figure or table float.sty restyled (`\restylefloat{table}`) keeps float.sty's format
  (`\lx@class@floatsty@kept`: 2006.08364's "TABLE I: List of …").
- **Names and separators only** (user ruling 2026-10-22): the class's caption fonts — acmart's journal small sans serif,
  conference bold, siggraph italic text, sigchi small figure and table captions; IEEEtran's small-caps table text and
  compsoc `\sffamily`; jfm's small-caps label; webofc's and jinstpub's bold label — are set only under the class caption
  fonts knob (caption_sty.rs `CLASS_CAPTION_FONTS`, latexml.sty's `classcaptionfonts` option ahead of the class; off by
  default), so an HTML theme styles every caption alike. Under ar5iv the route is `--preload=[classcaptionfonts]ar5iv.sty`
  (78z, Rust-only like the knob): ar5iv.sty declares `classcaptionfonts`/`noclasscaptionfonts` and passes the one given
  to latexml.sty with its own options (ar5iv_sty.rs `pass_options`), as a LaTeX package's
  `\DeclareOption{…}{\PassOptionsToPackage{\CurrentOption}{latexml}}` would. A second preload of latexml.sty beside
  ar5iv.sty's cannot: a preload's options go to `opt@<name>.<ext>` only (core_interface.rs, the preload loop), so after
  ar5iv.sty the repeat load has no new options to apply (content.rs `apply_repeat_options` returns at its first test),
  and before it latexml.sty takes its options alone and ar5iv's are lost (`rawclasses`: TeX Live's paper.cls fell to
  OmniBus). Perl alike for a repeat load (Core.pm:333-335, Package.pm:2357, :2586-2590); the general behaviour is the SYNC_STATUS row
  "A preload's options do not reach a package another preload already loaded". Guards `perfect_kernel_batch78z::{ar5iv_classcaptionfonts_option_sets_the_knob,
  ar5iv_classcaptionfonts_option_keeps_ar5iv_options}` (review rev78y2 finding 1). Not the class's, so not behind the knob: a package's own label fonts (algorithm2e's `\fnum@font@algorithm`, as
  Perl's binding), the document's `\captionsetup` keys, and the kernel's `\normalfont` in `\lx@fnum@@`, which listings'
  labels now take as a figure's does (`<text font="serif">Listing 3</text>` in a sans context, 2409.06446).
- **caption** (caption_sty.rs) lets `\lx@makecaption` be its own at `\begin{document}`, in the class's default
  separator (`CAPTION_DEFAULT_LABELSEP`, an AMS class known by its `\@captionheadfont`), and gives a float.sty type that
  separator when nothing sets one (acmart's journal formats "Program 1. …"), its label in caption's fonts, not float.sty's
  `\@fs@cfont` (`\rmfamily`: acmart sigchi-a's "Program 1" in the sans body); listings' captions are caption's
  (`\lx@format@caption@@`), as caption formats them.
- **A package that makes its captions itself** marks its type (`lx@caption@own@<type>`), which caption then formats
  not at all: algorithm2e's `algorithm` (algorithm2e.sty:2287-2318 `\algocf@makecaption`; 1908.06049, 2205.14076), whose
  label closes with `\algocf@capseparator` (":", :2285-2289) — unless float.sty made the type (algorithm.sty's
  `\newfloat{algorithm}` beside `[algo2e]`: caption's "Algorithm 1 Leakage Removal", 2204.02306, 1812.03871, 2408.08621).
- **longtable** keeps its own "Table 1: " (`\lx@longtable@format`) without caption, unless a binding ports its class's or
  package's own `\LT@makecaption` as its table format (`\lx@longtable@classformat`: emulateapj.cls:1303-1313,
  caption2.sty:338).

Not ported: IEEEtran's `\footnotesize` and `captionsoff` (IEEEtran.cls:2800-2808 prints the label only; the captions are
kept), caption's AMS default fonts (`\@captionheadfont` labels), and float.sty's style formats on a `\restylefloat`ed
kernel float (a ruled figure's "Fig. 1 text" keeps the kernel's ": "; float_sty.rs records the style only). The Perl
golden tests/complex/acm_aria.xml (`acmsmall`) now reads `<tag close=". ">Fig. 1</tag>caption text`, and
tests/structure/algorithm2e_{frames,linenumbers}.xml "Algorithm 1" closed by ": ". Witnesses

### 885. A float's panels are set in rows from what the source states, against the class's real line

User rulings 2026-10-22 (FIDELITY_CHARTER §2 "Float panels"; grid design study `agent_reports/2026-10-22_grid_design.md`
Q3): a float's rows come from what the source states, not from TeX's line breaking against one page geometry. Perl's
`arrange_panels_and_breaks` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3229-3349) fills a row greedily with the panels' box widths
against the float's `\hsize`, and sees no more than the tree: our panels (as Perl's) are digested in vertical mode, where
TeX's are in a paragraph (subfigure.sty's `\@subfloat`, graphicx's `\leavevmode`), so a blank line, a `\vskip` or the
glue between two panels leaves nothing to set the rows by; a `\\` in a `{center}` is skipped in its capture
(`\lx@newline`, Perl the same: "skip, if in insertBlock"); and every width is measured against Perl's `\columnwidth` =
`\textwidth` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:321), so a two-column document's `figure*` of `0.74\columnwidth` pairs broke
where the PDF sets one row. Ours (78x), `arrange_panels` (latex_constructs/mod.rs) keeping Perl's greedy rule, its merges
and its standalone blocks:

- **An explicit break always breaks.** The source's row separators are recorded where they are constructed, as an
  internal `ltx:break` (`note_panel_separator`, attribute `_panelsep`) in the float's own list or the capture of a
  `{center}`-like environment directly in it (`aligning_environment`, `in_aligning_capture`, a count in the document's
  state; never a box's, whose capture would settle differently): a source `\par` (not the one leaving horizontal mode
  inserts, 2605.00347), a `{center}`/`{flushleft}`/`{flushright}` boundary, a `\\` in such a capture, a `\vskip` (not
  `\vspace`'s or `\medskip`'s: in a paragraph latex.ltx:9361-9370 `\@vspace` is a `\vadjust`, no line break), a forced
  `\linebreak`. `arrange_panels` keeps one between two panels as the row's `<ltx:break class="ltx_break"/>` and drops
  the rest; `settle_float_paragraphs` drops any no float took. A separator is a mark, not content: a capture's
  container is chosen without the separators it holds (`insert_block_as`), which reach the float where the capture
  unwraps into it and leave with a capture that stays a container (`drop_panel_separators`; 78x r6: a leading
  `\hspace*{5pt}` or `\hskip` in a `{center}` chose the inline candidate holding its `ltx:break`, the `\parbox` panels
  after it hoisted out as `logical-block`s and the caption kept in the row's `ltx:block`, 1710.06503 Fig 1, the
  ws-procs961x669 binding net; guard `an_hspace_star_opens_the_row_paragraph`). The float's begin lets `\vspace`, `\linebreak` and
  `\hspace` to the rule's `\lx@panel@vspace`/`\lx@panel@linebreak`/`\lx@panel@hspace` only while they have the kernel's
  meaning (`\lx@kernel@…`): an author's or a package's own stands.
- **The stated glue counts.** `\hskip` (so `\quad`, `\qquad`) and `\hspace` between two panels add their natural width to
  the row; plain spaces, `\label`s and `\hfill` count 0. A row that begins a paragraph (the float's first, one after a
  `\par`, a `{center}` boundary, a `\vskip`, a caption, or a centred `\\`) keeps the glue stated before its first
  panel, as TeX keeps glue at a paragraph's start — under `\centering`, `\raggedright`, `\raggedleft` and in a
  `{center}`/`{flushleft}`/`{flushright}` a `\\` is `\@centercr`, whose `\par` ends the paragraph (a direct `ltx:break`
  carrying the alignment's class, the capture's separator `cr`), and so in every float of a class that centres its
  floats (`declare_panel_floats_centred`: REVTeX's `\appdef\@xfloat@prep{\appdef\@parboxrestore{\centering}}`,
  revtex4-2.cls:6770-6772; review rev78x3 finding 3, `p7.tex` F1, `p1.tex` F10: `\\\hspace{-0.05\columnwidth}` before
  three 0.34\columnwidth panels, one line in the PDF; not AASTeX's or emulateapj's, which `\def\@xfloat@prep` again
  without `\centering`, aastex701.cls:8066, emulateapj.cls:949, `withdraw_panel_floats_centred`; a `\newline` never,
  latex.ltx:9256's `\@normalcr` in every context, its break marked `_normalcr`: review rev78x4 findings 1-2, `n3.tex`
  F4, `n7.tex` F1, `n5.tex`); after a justified `\\` or a `\linebreak` only an `\hspace*`'s (separator `glue*`: latex.ltx's
  `\vrule width\z@\nobreak\hskip`, which a line break does not discard), after a computed break none (2212.03198 Figs 6,
  10-12, 15: `\hspace*{-0.5cm}` before three sub-figures, one row in the PDF, 2+1 when it was dropped once 78z sized
  the EPS panels in bp). Directly in the float's own group (`lx@float@frame`), or in a `{center}`-like environment's
  directly in it (whose lines are the float's rows, as they are for `\hskip`; review rev78x2 finding 6), `\hspace`
  is `\lx@panel@hskip`, a constructor absorbed exactly as the kernel's `\hspace` box is (the same spaces, size and
  `isSkip`), whose absorption notes the separator: `\unskip` removes glue and separator together, and nothing joins a
  cell's, a box's, a listing's or math's material (an alignment cell's `@{\hspace{…}}`, 2602.02905; a listing line's
  indentation, 1908.05655; algorithm2e's `\hspace{1.5mm}Compute`, 1610.04467, 1712.10197, 1901.07422, 1901.07434,
  2009.06170, 2011.13396, 2405.17108, 2410.15995, 2605.09653). An uncaptioned sub-figure is its body's material too
  (`note_sub_float_body_width`, OD #876: spaces and `\lx@label`s left out, its stated glue counted; 1007.2355 Figs 1, 3;
1307.3388 Fig 3).
- **A row TeX sets in one `\hbox` stays one row** (`note_panel_hbox`): a sub-float whose body is one (subfigure.sty's
  `\subfigure`, subfigure.sty:232; cond-mat0610021 Fig 11, two `width=200pt` graphics in one sub-figure, one overfull
  `\hbox` in pdflatex), and the sub-floats begun in one `\hbox` (an adjustbox's or a `\resizebox`'s sub-figures, 2311.18531
  A7.F5/F6), as a binding's fixed row (`_gridrow`) — keyed on the group that set the box's restricted horizontal mode
  (`state::frame_of_binding`), not the group a sub-float is begun in: subcaption's `\subfloat` begins each in a
  `\begingroup` of its own (review rev78x2 finding 3).
- **The line is the class's real one, for rows only** (`install_panel_line`, at a float not inside another,
  `panel_page`): in two columns a `figure`'s line is the column, a `figure*`'s the text width. A class binding declares
  its real page (`declare_panel_page`: column and text widths as pdflatex gives them, and whether it is set in two
  columns now) — IEEEtran (IEEEtran.cls:1734-1811, its `\ProcessOptions` running the options in their declaration order,
  `last_declared_class_option`) 43pc = 516pt in two 252pt columns, compsoc's 7in + 12bp = 517.935pt in two of 252.945pt,
  compsoc `conference` the paper less 1.5in (505.89pt in two of 243.911pt 0.25in apart on letter paper), a draft option
  the paper less 2in (469.755pt on letter, 452.968pt on A4) in two columns the mode's `\columnsep` apart, one column
  under `onecolumn` or `peerreview` (whose `\if@twocolumn` the binding keeps true); REVTeX 4.x 246/510pt in two columns
  under `twocolumn` (and `reprint` from 4.1 on), one column of 510pt otherwise, and `preprint` (`manuscript`) 468pt, in
  two 229pt columns where `twocolumn` (or an earlier `reprint`) sets two — the options as given, a later `reprint`
  undoing it (review rev78x2 finding 4, values by pdflatex `\showthe`); AASTeX 6.x 242.3/513.1pt under
  `twocolumn` (its appendix in one column unless `twocolappendix`, aastex631.cls:1336-1342); mnras 244/508pt; aa
  256.1/523.5pt — and REVTeX's `\onecolumngrid`/`\twocolumngrid`/`\restorecolumngrid` and `{widetext}` regions follow
  (`set_panel_page_twocolumn`). A declared page holds only while `\textwidth` is still the binding's (an author's
  `\textwidth 7.2in` is the page: 2211.03584). A float whose binding sets its own `\hsize` after its begin (a
  wrapfigure's width, wrapfig_sty.rs) keeps it as its line (`PANEL_LINE_HSIZE`: 2609.34643 S3.SS3.fig1, a
  `0.27\textwidth` wrapfigure set against the page's line, its picture and pagination wrapped in one block). Without a declaration: `\textwidth`, or the geometry's `\Gm@tw` while
  `\textwidth` is still the class's `\Gm@doctw` (a later `\setlength{\textwidth}{15cm}` is the page: 1704.03351 Figs 16,
  35, 36), in two columns (`\if@twocolumn`) the column `(\textwidth − \columnsep)/2`, or for a binding that keeps the
  kernel's 345pt line that line as the column and twice it and `\columnsep` as the text. The registers keep Perl's
  values; this replaces the geometry's arrangement width of OD #99, which a float with no real line keeps (below).
- **Each panel's stated width is taken at that geometry.** Where a register differs from its real value, the float keeps
  the tokens its body states for widths (`parameter::KEEP_STATED_LENGTHS`, in its group): a constructor's braced or
  bracketed typed arguments (`Parameter::stated`, read once by `reparse_argument`, on the whatsit as `STATED_LENGTHS`)
  and a `KeyVals`' length values (`KeyVals::stated_entry`, the last given of a key: 2601.01508's
  `width=0.33\textwidth,width=2.3in`). A binding declares which is a construct's width (`declare_panel_width`:
  `{minipage}`'s fourth argument, `\parbox`'s (the macro hands `\lx@parbox` the tokens the source states, read outside
  the box as latex.ltx:16252 reads them, and sets the box's registers inside it, `\lx@parbox@restore`; read as a value
  first, Perl's `{Dimension}` macro, a `\parbox{\linewidth}` note stated 1.503 of a two-column article's column,
  `perfect_kernel_batch79f::a_parbox_states_its_width_against_the_page`), `\makebox`/`\framebox`'s, `\rule`'s, `\resizebox`'s, subcaption's
  `{subfigure}`s', `\includegraphics`' `width` key — never a height, never a box's body: 1703.09474 Fig 13, 2503.09651
  Fig 1; a graphic that states only its height keeps its aspect ratio, so the height scales its natural width,
  2209.01559 Fig 6); one that sizes a box of its own accord keeps none (`\lx@panel@unstated`: subcaption's `\subfloat`, whose
  `{\columnwidth}` made a `figure*`'s first sub-float 0 wide, 2602.06569 S4.F1/F2, 1902.05392 S3.F3), and its
  constructor is marked as stating none (`WITHHOLD_STATED_LENGTHS` → `STATED_LENGTHS_WITHHELD`), not an unknown width
  (review rev78x4 finding 3, `n6.tex` F1: two 4.5cm `\subfloat`s, two lines of REVTeX's 246pt column). At the float's
  end, inside its group (`after_float` → `note_stated_widths`, its body the box list being built: a width macro the
  float defines, or one a later `\renewcommand` changes, is read with the meaning it has there; review rev78x2 finding 1,
  where r2 evaluated as the element opened, after the group ended), each stated width is evaluated twice in a group and
  a mouth of its own, at the registers' values and at the real ones (`\textwidth`, `\columnwidth`, `\linewidth`,
  `\hsize`; calc's evaluator where loaded; its diagnostics, the source's when first read, not reported again), and the
  box records what the real one adds in the ratio of the two (`PANEL_WIDTH_DELTA`): the width the construct gave its box
  (a positional argument's digested value; a graphic's box, its rotation included) times `real/ours − 1`, so a width
  the body narrowed (`\setlength\linewidth{…}` before `0.9\linewidth`) scales as TeX's does; a `\scalebox` or
  `\resizebox` of no width of its own scales its content's by its `xscale`, and a rotation (`angle`) turns its content's
  width and height deltas (review rev78x2 finding 2: four `\scalebox{0.5}` of `0.6\columnwidth` graphics, four
  `angle=90` ones, four `\rotatebox{90}` boxes, 3+1 each in REVTeX's column). A length register a stated width reads
  is what its `\setlength` stated, evaluated at the same geometry while the register still holds the value it gave
  (`note_setlength`: sect12.rs's and calc's `\setlength` record the tokens in the assignment's scope); a register the
  document allocated (`\newlength`, `\newdimen`, `\newskip`: `note_length_allocated`) whose value no `\setlength`
  recorded (`\figu=0.48\columnwidth`, `\settowidth`, an `\addtolength` since) holds a value of the registers' geometry
  the real one cannot re-evaluate (`Unevaluable`); so is a stated width or height the float's end cannot read (a macro
  of a group that has ended, `{\def\w{0.48\columnwidth}…}`, read as an undefined `\w`, 0) or that does not give again
  there, within 4sp, the value the construct gave its box (`StatedSize::given`: a positional argument's digested value,
  a `width=`/`height=`'s digested value; an outer `\def\w{0.2\textwidth}` an inner one shadowed), and a length a box
  was given whose tokens were not kept (a box built before the float). Such a float is arranged exactly as before the
  rule (`after_float`): at its `\hsize`, or, under geometry, for a full-column float (`\hsize` = `\Gm@doctw` <
  `\Gm@tw`) at the geometry's text width, OD #99's arrangement width (`PANEL_FALLBACK_LINE`; review rev78x3 findings
  1-2, `p1.tex` F1-F2, `p8.tex` F1, and `p2.tex` F2-F4: four `\figw=3.8cm` panels under `[a4paper,margin=1in]{geometry}`,
  one row as in the PDF, 3+1 against the 345pt `\hsize` in r3) — never worse than that; the kernel's and the bindings' registers (`\tabcolsep`, `\columnsep`, `\p@`) stand as they are.
  Nothing is recorded while a format is built (`--init`, a dump); inside a parbox of a stated width (`declare_panel_parbox_width`: a `{minipage}`, a `\parbox`,
  subcaption's sub-figures, whose content's `\linewidth`, `\hsize`, `\textwidth`, `\columnwidth` are that width,
  latex.ltx `\@iiiminipage`) its content is evaluated against that width (a child's `\linewidth` is its parent's
  evaluated width; an `\hbox`'s content, `\makebox[w]`, `\resizebox{w}{!}`, at the enclosing line), and the box's panels are set against it (2504.07193 Fig 5, a
  `{minipage}{\textwidth}` of sub-figures); an `\hspace`'s glue the same way (`PANEL_GLUE_DELTA`; 2311.18531 Fig 1,
  `0.48 + 3×0.24\textwidth` with `−0.25\textwidth` of `\hspace` under geometry, one row of 4); a sub-float's line is its
  stated width at the real geometry (2605.03152 S3.F2), or the float's real line where it kept the float's
  (subfigure.sty's in-line panels, their content evaluated as the float's: 1902.04580 Figs 15-16). A panel's real width
  is its box's plus its own or its contents' outermost difference (`panel_width_delta`; a minipage folded into its
  lone child carries it as `_panelwidthdelta`, 2007.15568 Tables 2-3); a row with no real line of its own (a paragraph
  of floats settled into a row, `settle_float_paragraph`) is set at the registers' widths (2202.03884). No gullet, constructor-time,
  conditional or keyval geometry: 78x r1's shadow geometry (every shadowed register read while an argument was read,
  thread-local, review rev78x findings 1, 7) is gone. A plain `\hskip` (not braced) keeps its value at the registers' geometry.

### 886. An EPS graphic's box is its BoundingBox in bp; the first readable candidate sizes the box whatever its type

TeX reads an EPS's `%%BoundingBox` as bp: graphics.sty's `\Gread@eps` (`\Gread@BBox`, graphics.sty:52, read at
:365-399; `%%HiResBoundingBox` only under the `hiresbb` option, :56-57) for latex + dvips, epstopdf's page for pdflatex,
so a 40bp-wide EPS is a 40.15pt box (pdflatex 40.14989pt). Perl's `image_graphicx_sizer` (Util/Image.pm:259-272) turns
every image size into pt as device pixels at `DPI` (`$w * 72.27 / $dpi`, :271), a raster's and, through ImageMagick's
72-dpi read, a vector's alike, so an EPS is 72.27/100 of TeX's (without ImageMagick Perl reads no EPS size at all: 0pt).
Ours did the same through its raster reader (`read_image_dimensions`, the BoundingBox handed back as pixels): 28.908pt for
the 40bp figure, `scale=0.565` of an EPS 187.90pt where latex makes it 260.88pt, and since 78t's `\psfig` sizer (#876)
a natural-size `\psfig` panel row of 72.27/100 the width (1106.2745 Figs 1-2, 7, 8, 10). It also read the first
*raster-readable* candidate, so beside `fig.pdf` an extensionless `\includegraphics{fig}` was sized by a `fig.ps` further
down its candidate list, where pdflatex reads `fig.pdf`.

Ours (78z, user ruling 2026-10-22 "fix to TeX's bp"): `image_graphicx_sizer` (latexml_core util/image.rs) takes the first
candidate whose size it can read, whatever its type — the candidates are in TeX's order (`in_graphics_type_order`, #883),
Perl's own rule (Util/Image.pm:259-272 returns on the first candidate whose width it reads; the natural `cssstyle`
reads the same one since 79a, below) — and sizes it by kind: `read_image_size` tells a raster's pixels
(`ImageSize::Pixels`, PNG/JPEG) from a PostScript file's bp (`ImageSize::PostScriptBp`), and a PDF page box or an SVG is
read by `natural_size_pt` as before. A vector size (EPS/PS, PDF, SVG) is bp → pt and goes through the graphicx algebra in
pt without quantization (`graphicx_box_pt`, the PDF branch's); a raster keeps Perl's DPI rule (100 DPI, the pixel path's
`ceil`; #337 for its crop). One code path, no package names: `\includegraphics`, `\psfig`/`\epsfig` (epsfig_sty.rs) and
adjustbox's `\adjincludegraphics` share it. An EPS's size is its `%%BoundingBox` (`read_postscript_size_bp`), its
`%%HiResBoundingBox` only when it has none, as post already read it (latexml_post graphics.rs
`read_postscript_bounding_box_full`): the high-resolution box came first, rounded, so a file with a stale page-sized
HiRes box (hep-ex0703011's `eeggmet.eps`: BoundingBox 540x522, HiRes 612x792) had a natural `cssstyle` of 61.4em x 79.5em
for an image post renders at 54.2em x 52.4em. Measured (pdflatex / latex, TL 2025; ours): natural 40.14989 / 40.15 /
40.15pt; `scale=0.565` 22.68478 / 22.68483 / 22.68475pt; `width=100pt` height 50.00171 / 50.00186 / 50.0pt; the HiRes
file 200.7495 / 200.75 / 200.75pt; `fig` beside `fig.pdf` (200bp) and `fig.ps` (40bp) 200.7495 / - / 200.75pt; a
200x100 px PNG 200.7495pt / - / 144.54pt (100 DPI, unchanged). Not read (Perl alike): graphicx's `bb=`/`bbllx=`…,
`natwidth=`/`natheight=` and `hiresbb`, which set the natural size in TeX (cond-mat0610021's `bb=0in 0in 2in 2in`).

A/B (release int67a vs 78z, both on int67a's dumps; census `package:epsfig|package:psfig|cs:psfig|cs:epsfbox|cs:epsffile|cs:epsfig`
300 seed 78, 80 pre-2008 graphicx papers, 59 random controls, 14 witnesses; 452 compared): E 540 = 540, F 2 = 2, W 5,698
= 5,698, words equal, 0 worse; XML changed in 20 (0 controls): box sizes in 12 (a `\resizebox` or `\scalebox` around an
EPS now scales its true natural size — cond-mat0211312's `xscale` 1.0008 → 0.7206 of a 478.8pt figure into 345pt — and
the inline-block, rotated-figure and picture sizes around one), the natural `cssstyle` from the BoundingBox in 5
(0710.5533, cond-mat0603833, hep-th0701149, nucl-th0411072 by 0.1em; hep-ex0703011 above), panel rows in 3: 1012.3355
Fig 2 now (a)(b) | (c)(d) as latex sets it (was (a)(b)(c) | (d)); 1106.2745 Fig 2 2+2 (was 3+1; latex one per row in
aa's 255.8pt column, which int67a did not have; since 78x one per row as latex, against aa's declared column, OD #885,
and Figs 1 and 3 as latex too, 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 and 3+1); cond-mat0610021 Fig
11 a break between a sub-figure's two graphics, whose `\subfigure` body TeX sets in one overfull `\hbox` (the grid rule
broke such a body whenever its stated widths exceeded the line: int67a did so for two `width=200pt` graphics too; since
78x one row, `note_panel_hbox`, OD #885). Witnesses 1106.2745, hep-ex0703011, 1012.3355. Repros package-bindings/includegraphics_eps_box_is_its_bounding_box,
captions-floats/psfig_natural_panels_are_as_wide_as_their_bounding_box; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78z::{includegraphics_eps_box_is_its_bounding_box,
psfig_natural_panels_are_as_wide_as_their_bounding_box}`, `perfect_kernel_batch64::adjustimage_includes_the_graphic`
(its 10bp EPS 10.0pt, was 7.2pt), `util::image::sizing_characterization_tests::sizer_matrix_across_formats_and_options`
(the EPS rows now the PDF rows), `util::image::…::read_image_dimensions_returns_pixels_for_raster_and_bp_for_eps`.

The natural `cssstyle` and the box read one candidate (79a, review rev78z finding 1): `first_natural_size` (util/image.rs)
is the first candidate any reader sizes, by its content (`natural_size`: `read_image_size`, then `natural_size_pt`), and
both `image_graphicx_sizer` and `natural_display_size_pt_of_candidates` take it; when it is a raster there is no `em`

post renders (pdflatex sets the png 200.7495pt); now no `cssstyle`. A vector first (`m.pdf` before `m.png`) keeps its
`em` size. And the candidates follow `\Gin@extensions` (graphics.sty:206-224 tries it in turn):
`declared_graphics_extensions` ranks its extensions first, in their order, before the driver's order (#883). The graphics
binding seeds it as pdftex.def:597-600 sets it (79a r2, review rev79a finding 3: started `\@empty`, grfext's
`\AppendGraphicsExtensions{.eps}` left `.eps` alone and first), and TeX's edits act on it: `\DeclareGraphicsExtensions`
(graphics.sty:116-117), grfext's `\Append…`/`\Prepend…`/`\RemoveGraphicsExtensions` (read raw; 1711.06128's
`\AppendGraphicsExtensions{.gif}`), pdftex.def:695's begin-document `,.eps`, and epstopdf-base.sty:498-505's
`\AppendGraphicsExtensions{.eps}` (every `.eps` removed, one appended: `\lx@graphics@eps@last`) when `\usepackage{epstopdf}`
loads it, or at `\begin{document}` with grfext loaded — so `\DeclareGraphicsExtensions{.pdf,.eps,.png}\usepackage{epstopdf}`
tries `.png` first, and a preamble `\PrependGraphicsExtensions{.eps}` with grfext alone is undone, as pdflatex prints the
png (200.7495pt); epstopdf's `prepend` option makes its load `\PrependGraphicsExtensions{.eps}` instead, and
`\epstopdfsetup{prepend}` is one (epstopdf-base.sty:218-248, :509-515; 79a r3, review rev79a2 finding 4: pdflatex
the eps). An extension is matched as kpathsea finds the file, the name as written, then in another case (TL's
`texmf_casefold_search=1`; `declared_rank`, 79a r3, review rev79a2 finding 2): `\DeclareGraphicsExtensions{.pdf,.jpeg,.png}`
beside `img/nsfnet.PNG` and `img/nsfnet.eps` is the PNG, found by the `.png` entry before the begin-document `.eps`,
as 1608.05172's pdflatex log reads `<./img/nsfnet.PNG>` (r2 matched the case and took the eps), and
