the candidate sort key puts the case fold ahead of the `\graphicspath` directory, where TeX runs one `\IfFileExists`
per directory and kpathsea folds the case inside each, so an exact-case `dirB/q.png` wins over a folded `dirA/q.PNG`
(TeX takes `dirA/q.PNG`; only when one base name sits in two search directories in different cases). The seed is pdftex.def's list under
any driver option, where TeX loads the named driver's (`[dvips]`: dvips.def:202 `.eps,.ps,.eps.gz,.ps.gz,.eps.Z,.mps`,

beside `fig.png` and `fig.eps` is the eps, box and `cssstyle` alike (2107.02597's gnuplot epslatex figures: their
`.png` beside the `.eps`; pdflatex reads the eps, and with the png first the one-candidate rule would have dropped the
eps's `em` size; post still renders the png, by its own desirability). Repros
package-bindings/{natural_cssstyle_reads_the_box_candidate, declared_graphics_extensions_order_the_candidates,
append_graphics_extensions_keeps_the_driver_order, prepend_graphics_extensions_puts_the_type_first,
epstopdf_appends_eps_last, declared_graphics_extensions_fold_case, epstopdf_prepend_puts_eps_first}; guards

### 887. A float's panel grid is stated in the XML: its rows and columns, gallery or matrix, each panel's width, its line and fill

User rulings 2026-10-22 (FIDELITY_CHARTER §2 "Float panels"; grid design study `agent_reports/2026-10-22_grid_design.md`
Q4 option (a); SYNC_STATUS row "Panel grid markup"). Perl's `arrange_panels_and_breaks` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3229-3349)
sets a float's panels in rows with `ltx:break`s and marks them `ltx_figure_panel` (more than one), and says no more: the
rows are only the runs between breaks, a panel's stated width is lost (subcaption.sty.ltxml:60-66 stores a
`{subfigure}`'s `width` as a property its template never emits), and nothing tells a gallery of independent panels from
a matrix whose rows and columns mean something. Ours (79c), once `arrange_panels` set the rows and `collapse_float` ran
(`annotate_panel_grid`, latex_constructs/mod.rs; the three float `after_close` tags, sect09.rs):

- **On a float of two or more panels**: `panelrows` (the rows that hold a panel, as the HTML sets them: runs of
  `ltx_figure_panel`s between breaks and captions), `panelcols` (the most columns a row takes) and the class
  `ltx_panels_matrix` or `ltx_panels_gallery`. A float of one panel states none of it.
- **On each panel**: `panelwidth`, the width the row rule set it at as a fraction of its row's line (3 decimals), only
  where that width is the real geometry's — the float's line is the class's real one with every stated width evaluated
  there (`install_panel_line`, `note_stated_widths`, OD #885), or the registers are the real geometry already
  (`PANEL_REGISTERS_REAL`: a sub-float's own `\hsize`, a wrapfigure's) — and the source states it (`panel_width_is_stated`,
  `states_its_width`: a graphic's, a rule's, a picture's, a box's of a declared width, or theirs side by side in a
  sub-float or a merged block; not our measure of a paragraph of text, a tabular, a list: 1807.05122 S2.F2's text panel
  measured 9.7 lines wide; not a sub-float set at the float's whole `\hsize` with no body width, subfig's `\subfloat`).
  A float arranged at the fallback line (a width it could not evaluate, OD #885) states no `panelwidth`: never a guess.
  A graphic panel whose `\includegraphics` states only a `width=` takes that width, not its box's, where the two are
  within 1% and a point (`graphic_rounding`: a raster's box is 72/72.27 of it rounded up to a pixel, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
  #1142; 2208.08007 S0.F1.g1's `width=\linewidth` stated 0.997; review rev79c finding 4).
- **The float's line and fill** (user ruling 2026-10-23), where every panel states its `panelwidth`: `panelline`, the
  line its rows are set against as a fraction of the PDF's running-text column at the float (`PANEL_COLUMN`,
  `install_panel_line`: the class's real column in two columns, its text width in one — 1 for a `figure`, 2.073 for
  REVTeX's `figure*` (510pt of the 246pt column), 0.5 for a `{wrapfigure}{r}{0.5\textwidth}`; a float held in a `{minipage}` is set against the box's line as a
  fraction of the page outside the box (`PANEL_BOX_PAGE`, 79f: 0.5 in a half-width minipage, as the PDF;
  `captions-floats/panel_line_of_a_float_in_a_minipage`), and `panelfill`, the widest row's sum of its panels' `panelwidth` (fractions of the float's own line; 3
  decimals each). **Rendering rule**: a panel renders at `panelwidth × panelline` of the theme's column, divided by
  `max(1, panelfill × panelline)` — so a `figure*` fills the column and a narrow float stays narrow; the converter knows
  only the PDF's column and the float's line, never a theme constant (no rem/pt value is emitted).
  The column is OD #885's page model, declared by each class binding where its original sets its page (79f):
  article/report/book `[twocolumn]` as size10/11/12.clo set it for the paper and size options
  (`standard_class_twocolumn_page`: 469/229.5pt on letter, 452/221pt on A4, 410pt under `\documentstyle`; `figure*`
  2.044 as the PDF, was 2), acmart's two-column formats (506.295/241.147pt; `figure*` 2.100, was 1), elsarticle
  `3p`/`5p`, emulateapj, ieeeconf, iopart, mn2e, REVTeX, svjour/svjour3, AASTeX; `\twocolumn`/`\onecolumn` switch the
  declared page, and a style that sets its own page over the class keeps its own `\columnsep` (2008.06630's 3dv.sty).
  A class with no declaration is still read against the binding's 345pt `\textwidth`.
- **A matrix only on strong signals**: an author-built `tabular` of panels — the float's one content a `tabular` (or a
  box holding only it: `\resizebox`, `adjustbox`) two or more of whose cells hold a graphic; `panelrows`/`panelcols`
  are its rows and the most columns a row takes (`colspan` counted), its cells keep their `colspan`/`rowspan`
  (`tabular_panel_grid`; 1403.6637 S4.F6/F8, 0908.0534 Figs 1-2, 2008.05524 Tables 11-16, 1104.5469). A cell counts
  only for a graphic or picture of a panel's size, 24pt or more both wide and tall (`is_panel_graphic`,
  `PANEL_GRAPHIC_LEAST`): a data table's icons, bars and sparklines make no matrix (review rev79c finding 1: 2608.05898
  S4.T2/T5's 102pt x 6.69pt bars, 2506.23665 Ch3.T4/T5, Ch5.T4/T5's 18pt-high sparklines, 2411.16612 S7.T1/T2's 8pt
  icons, 2501.18280 S4.T3/A4.T6, 1509.07152 S10.T23, 1805.10096 Sx4.T1, 2504.02271 S2.T1: 13 of r1's 253 `tabular`
  matrices in the 1,907-paper population; the larger dimension alone would keep the bars and sparklines; 2502.08151
  S7.T3's 491pt x 29pt image strips stay one) — or two or more rows that agree
  panel for panel (the most panels a row takes, two or more; each width within 0.01 of the line of the other row's),
  every other row taking all those columns, each of its panels as wide as the columns it spans (`panelspan` when two or
  more), and whose panels' own captions are none or exactly one whole row's (`matrix_spans`; main-session decision 3,
  2026-10-23, review rev79c finding 2, checked on the PDFs): captions on one whole row label its columns (2209.01559
  Figs 3, 5; 1404.0431 Fig 1; 2212.03198 Figs 7, 10, 13, 14; 1811.02385 S4.F3-F6); captions on every panel, on more
  than one row, or on some panels of a row make the panels a gallery's, independent, their order not their place
  (2503.15158 S4.F7, 2404.12123 S3.F6, 2106.04682 A2.F4 (a)-(e) and a legend, 1808.10020 chapter5.figure11, 2602.17978
  Ch4.F2/F3). 1401.5657 Fig 2's `0.316 + 3×0.21` columns are a matrix. Every other float of two or more panels is a
  gallery.
- **Nested groups**: a sub-float holding panels of its own is a flex figure of its own in HTML and states its own grid
  (its panels' widths fractions of its line); as a panel of its float it states its width there too. `collapse_float`
  gives a lone inner float's grid to the float it becomes; an inner float beside other content leaves its grid behind and
  drops its panels' widths (fractions of the inner's line), the float's own grid made of its panels — also beside
  content of no width, where the inner was the float's only panel (review rev79c finding 3; repro
  `captions-floats/panel_grid_collapse_drops_inner_widths`).
- **Schema**: `Panel.attributes` (`panelwidth` `xsd:decimal`, `panelspan` `xsd:nonNegativeInteger`) in
  `Common.attributes` — a panel is any element a float sets in rows (`ltx:graphics`, `ltx:p`, `ltx:tabular`,
  `ltx:block`, a sub-float…) — and `PanelGrid.attributes` (`panelrows`, `panelcols` `xsd:nonNegativeInteger`,
  `panelline`, `panelfill` `xsd:decimal`) on `figure`, `table`, `float` (LaTeXML-common.rnc, LaTeXML-para.rnc, their
  `.rng`, and the runtime `LaTeXML.model`, edited to match: 154 elements, 3 floats; the model carries no types).
- **XSLT**: `base-styling` (LaTeXML-common.xsl) maps a float's `panelrows`/`panelcols`/`panelline`/`panelfill` to
  `--ltx-panel-rows`/`--ltx-panel-cols`/`--ltx-panel-line`/`--ltx-panel-fill` on its own element, inherited by the flex
  rows and cells inside (and present on a `tabular` matrix, which has none); `build_subfigure` (LaTeXML-para-xhtml.xsl)
  maps a panel's `panelwidth`/`panelspan` to `--ltx-panel-width`/`--ltx-panel-span` on the `div.ltx_flex_cell` holding
  it, the flex item they size. Each only for a numeric value, written as `number()` of it, never the attribute's text
  (review rev79c finding 5: crafted XML cannot inject into `style`). The classes pass through as every class does. No
  CSS rule reads them yet (the CSS is the goal-end item); the HTML is otherwise unchanged.

The grid study's oracle (453 multi-panel floats, the study's labels from the PDF rows, sub-captions, a `tabular` and
text between rows): study matrix 42 — ours matrix 20 (10 of 11 `tabular` grids, 10 of 15 uniform uncaptioned grids),
gallery 22 (16 matrices labelled by text rows or columns, `ltx:p` panels the rule does not read as columns; 5 uniform
grids whose panels are text or of unequal widths row to row; 1 `tabular` beside two sub-figures); study gallery 411 —
ours gallery 405, matrix 5 (two-row grids captioned on one row only, 1404.0431 Fig 1, 2212.03198 Figs 7, 10, 13, 14),
none 1. Rows and shapes unchanged (429 and 422 of 453). Round 2 (review rev79c, the
line and fill): the oracle's confusion table, rows and shapes are unchanged (its five one-row-captioned grids are the
matrices decision 3 keeps; 2411.16612 S7.T1/T2, outside its categories, lose their `tabular` matrix). In the 1,907-paper
population, r1 → r2: 13 `tabular` data tables lose `ltx_panels_matrix` (finding 1), the 6 partly captioned grids become
galleries (finding 2), 115 floats' panel widths move by KPE #1142's rounding (finding 4), 5,079 floats gain
`panelline`/`panelfill`; with the grid markup stripped every paper is byte-identical. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch79c::*`
(repros `captions-floats/panel_grid_markup`, `panel_grid_markup_of_an_unevaluable_width`, `panel_grid_matrix_signals`,
`panel_grid_line_and_fill`, `panel_grid_collapse_drops_inner_widths`),
`integration::{panel_grid_markup_reaches_the_html_as_custom_properties, panel_grid_markup_states_only_numbers}`
(latexml_post).

### 888. An eqnarray continuation row that prints a number of its own is its own equation

latex.ltx:15789-15797: `\@@eqncr` prints the number of every row it ends while `\if@eqnsw` holds (#847), whatever the
row holds. Perl's `rearrangeEqnarray` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2357-2364) joins a row with only its third column
(`&&+ 2,`, a continued right-hand side) to the equation above: its rule keeps the row separate when both are numbered
*and* the row is labelled, but that label test reads `hasAttribute('label')`, which LaTeXML never sets (#54,
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #46), so Perl always joins these rows; and `equationgroupJoinRows` keeps the last row's tags: so in
`\log &&\frac{a}{b} = … \\ &&+ 0.8184(\log c)^2,` both rows' numbers become one equation with the second's, the first's
is lost, and a `\label` on the first names the second's (1310.2253 `eqn:zg`: PDF 11, ours and Perl 12). Ours (79d): a
third-column-only row that is numbered under a numbered equation stands as its own equation, as a numbered
relation-column continuation (`&=& z`) already does in Perl's rule (:2353-2354), so each row keeps its number and a
label the row that states it. A continuation under an unnumbered row, or itself unnumbered (`\nonumber`, a `\cr` row),
still joins. The single-column relation join (:2333-2335) is unchanged (its RELOP test reads a cell's first child, the
`Math` wrapper in the repro's `p = q \\ = r` cells, and did not fire). The split costs the joined formula of each such
pair (two equations, the second its right-hand side alone), as #847's split of a labelled continuation does. Repro
cross-references/eqnarray_numbered_continuation_row_keeps_its_number; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch79d::eqnarray_numbered_continuation_row_keeps_its_number`.

### 889. A constructor's `require_math` warning names the command it reverts as

Perl's `requireMath` (Package.pm:1466) warns with the definition's own name. A constructor defined with an `alias`
stands in for another command — the Springer classes' `\vec` is `\lx@sv@vec@boldmath` reverting as `\vec`
(sv_support_sty.rs), fourier's `\math@bb` reverts as `\mathbb` (fourier_sty.rs:15) — so its text-mode warning named an
internal macro the author never wrote, where pdflatex's "Missing $ inserted" is at the author's command. Ours (79d,
dialect.rs `def_constructor`): the warning names the `alias` when it is a control sequence ("\vec should only appear in
math mode", "\mathbb …"); an empty alias (latexml_sty's `alias => ""` entries) keeps the definition's name. No robust
constructor uses `require_math`. Repro class-bindings/llncs_text_mode_vec_warns_as_vec; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch79d::llncs_text_mode_vec_warns_as_vec`.

### 890. `\subfile` loads the subfile by `\subimport`, so its own directory is searched first (Perl: `\input`)

subfiles.sty:120-131 makes `\subfile{f}` `\subimport{\filename@area}{\filename@base}` (import.sty, which it requires;
the base keeps its extension) and `\subfileinclude` the same through `\subincludefrom`: what the subfile inputs and the
figures it names are found in its own directory, as pdflatex finds them. Perl's subfiles.sty.ltxml binds `\subfile` as
`\input`, so 2209.05589's `\subfile{./sub/OPA_v2.tex}` lost all 11 figures (`\includegraphics{FigScheme.eps}`, in
`sub/`) to `ltx_missing_image`. Ours (subfiles_sty.rs): `\subfile` splits its argument at the last `/` and calls our
`\subimport`. The group `\subfiles@subfile` opens around the load is not taken, as Perl takes none: a subfile's own
definitions stay visible after it. Repro package-bindings/subfile_figure_in_its_directory; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch79g::a_subfile_finds_the_figures_in_its_directory`.

### 891. xr's `\externaldocument` imports the other document's labels: `\ref` prints its numbers (Perl: no binding)

xr.sty (v6; xr-hyper.sty alike) reads the other document's `.aux`, and every `.aux` it `\@input`s, defining
`\r@<prefix><label>` from each `\newlabel` (`\XR@test`), so `\ref{fig:s1}` prints "S1". Perl ships no binding, and the
raw package's `\r@…` never reach a `\ref` that post resolves: every such reference was an `ltx_missing_label`
(1307.3388's 40 references to its supplement, 1608.05314's 73; in the census, 21 of the 125 papers that call
`\externaldocument` ship the external `.aux` — the others print "??" in pdflatex too — and 15 of the 21 now resolve every
external reference). Ours (contrib xr_sty.rs, for xr and xr-hyper; siamart loads it as siamart220329.cls:1266
does): `\externaldocument[prefix][nocite]{file}[url]` records each imported label's reference text (sect11.rs
`record_external_label`), and `\ref`/`\eqref` print it, typeset as TeX (IEEEtran's `\mbox {IV-A.1}` prints "IV-A.1";
2510.26552, 1312.7580), in an `ltx:ref` of class `ltx_ref_external` that keeps its
`labelref` (an `href` to the URL's anchor where the URL is given; the default `file.pdf` names no page of ours). Post
does not mark such a reference missing, and where this document holds the label after all it drops the imported text
and fills the reference from the target here, as LaTeX's own `.aux`, read at `\begin{document}`, redefines the
`\r@<label>` xr made in the preamble. A missing `.aux` warns, as xr does ("No file supp.aux; labels not imported").
`\cref` and `\autoref` name the type as pdflatex does (79h): xr also records cleveref's `<label>@cref` record
(`{[<type>][<n>][<parents>]<number>}`) and hyperref's anchor, so `\cref` prints this document's `\crefname` of the type
and the number in the type's label format, or the document's `\crefformat` for it (cleveref_sty.rs
`external_cref_text`), and `\autoref` the anchor's type's `\<type>autorefname` (hyperref_sty.rs
`external_autoref_text`, hyperref.sty `\HyRef@testreftype`): "fig. S1", "Equation (S2)", "subsection II-A". A label with
no `@cref` record prints "??" under `\cref` in pdflatex and stays a missing label here. 2412.14256 19 → 0 unresolved
references, 2508.18808 88 → 0, 2402.05535 41 → 14, 2608.12136 64 → 22 (the rest name labels the shipped `.aux` lacks, or
an `\aux` round trip, `\clonelabel`, which pdflatex resolves on its second run). Not imported: the `\bibcite`s v6 also
reads. Repros package-bindings/xr_external_document_labels, package-bindings/xr_external_cref_autoref; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch79g::{xr_prints_the_other_documents_numbers, xr_yields_to_a_label_of_this_document}`,
`perfect_kernel_batch79h::xr_cref_and_autoref_name_the_other_documents_types`.

### 892. `\begin{thebibliography}` takes one token as its argument when no brace follows (Perl: a braced argument only)

LaTeX's `thebibliography` takes one undelimited argument, the widest label (revtex4.cls:5549 `[1]`, revtex4-1.cls:7308
`\thebibliography@nogroup#1`, natbib.sty:1063, latex.ltx's `\thebibliography#1`), so a bare token after
`\begin{thebibliography}` is that argument. Perl's `\thebibliography` reads the argument only when a `{` follows ("in
some perverse situations (revtex?) it seems to be allowable to omit the argument"), so 1203.4144's placeholder line —
`\bibitem` then `\bibitem{Moffatt} Dormy E., …` — gave the bare `\bibitem` the next `\bibitem` as its key: the entry and
its citation were lost (`<ltx:bibitem> isn't allowed in <ltx:tag>`), where pdflatex prints "[1] Dormy E., …" with 0
errors. Ours (sect11.rs `\thebibliography`): with no brace, a character token is the argument, and so is a `\bibitem`
that opens no entry (not followed by `{` or `[`); a `\bibitem{x}` or any other command stays, keeping Perl's leniency where
TeX would take the `\bibitem` as the width and print the entry's key as text. 32 of the census's 35,942 papers have an
unbraced `thebibliography`. Repro index-bib/thebibliography_placeholder_bibitem_is_the_width; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch79g::a_placeholder_bibitem_is_the_bibliography_width`.

### 893. `\label` is locked against the class and package files, as the kernel minipage is (Perl: not locked)

LaTeX's `\label` writes `\newlabel{key}{{\@currentlabel}{\thepage}}` to the `.aux` (latex.ltx), which the next run
reads back to define `\r@key`; LaTeXML has no next run and records the label itself (`\lx@label`, sect11.rs). A raw
class that redefines `\label` — most often as the same `.aux` write, SIAM's siamltex-derived CMSLATEX.CLS:736 and
siuro210301.cls, jasatex.cls, myajour.cls — therefore left every label of the document unrecorded and every reference
missing (1607.06796 71, 1504.01662 57, math-ph0209020 31, 1009.5642 28, 2412.10948 27 dangling references). Ours
(sect11.rs): `\label:locked@files`, the lock OD #453 gives the kernel minipage, so the class and package files'
redefinitions are refused ("Ignoring redefinition of \label") while the document's own stay its own, as in LaTeX. A raw
package's wrapper of `\label` loses its extra behaviour with it (showlabels' margin keys, refcheck's marks, smartref's
page records; 25, 15 and 2 of the census's 35,942 papers); the packages whose wrappers matter have bindings
(showkeys, lineno, titleref, threeparttable, caption, cleveref, hyperref, amsmath). A shipped copy of a bound class
was already held to the copy by OD #731 (79i). Repro package-bindings/raw_class_redefines_label; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch79j::a_raw_class_redefining_label_keeps_the_documents_labels`.

### 894. An author block's tabular juggle is the line break it prints (Perl: digested, a tabular left open)

LaTeX sets `\author` inside the title page's own tabular (article.cls `\@maketitle`, sig-alternate.cls), so a class or
template macro that closes it and opens another — the ACM SIG template's
`\def\sharedaffiliation{\end{tabular}\begin{tabular}{c}}`, set between the names and their shared affiliation; the
class's own `\alignauthor` juggles the same way — breaks the block into columns. LaTeXML digests the author outside any
tabular: the juggle closed a tabular nothing opened ("Attempt to close a group that switched to mode
restricted_horizontal") and left one open, whose lines — the affiliation — were lost, and the item's unclosed group
kept its `\label` binding for the rest of the document (every reference dangling; the group itself now closes with
the item, queue_digest.rs `digest_in_own_group`, a Rust-only fix as Perl's `egroup` runs after the item's errors).
Ours (author_block separators.rs `tabular_juggles_as_line_breaks`): a parameterless macro of the author block whose
expansion begins `\end{tabular}` is read as the `\\` it prints, so the names and the affiliation split as lines; the
author separators (`\alignauthor`) stay for the splitter. Witnesses 1704.03168, 1301.5612, 1401.6981, 0712.1016
(sig-alternate; 21 census papers write `\sharedaffiliation`). Repros sectioning-frontmatter/author_shared_affiliation_line,
sectioning-frontmatter/author_group_left_open_keeps_labels; guards `perfect_kernel_batch79l`.

### 895. autonum numbers every equation; its package code is not loaded (Perl: no binding, raw-loaded)

autonum.sty numbers only the equations a reference names: its patched `\ref`/`\eqref`/`\cref` record the labels they
name in the aux file (autonum.sty:330-345), and on the next run the display environments it renews at
`\begin{document}` (:127-140, :186-280) drop the other equations' numbers. A single pass has no earlier run to read,
and raw-loaded the renewals reach only the environments no binding locks: `{split}`'s ran inside our locked `{align}`,
whose own renewal — the one that restores `\label` globally at its end (`\autonum@restoreSubcommands`) — did not, so the
display's `\label` stayed global and every later `\label` failed ("\lx@ams@display@outer@label undefined", the label
lost; 1905.00606: 20 errors, 6 dangling). Ours (latexml_contrib autonum_sty.rs): autonum's packages and its hyperref
option load, its code does not; every equation keeps its number, as without autonum, so a reference to an equation
that follows an unreferenced one prints a later number than the PDF (31 census papers load autonum). autonum's own
`<env>+` forms — the environment as amsmath left it (autonum.sty:176-183 `\autonum@renameEnvironment`) — are aliases of
the environments, for `equation`, `gather`, `multline`, `flalign`, `align`, `alignat`, `split` (1405.2249,
1904.08614: `{align+}`, undefined without them). Its `\[`, redefined as an `{equation}` numbered only when referenced,
stays unnumbered. Its reference patchers (`\autonum@generatePatchedReference{cmd}`, `…CSL`, `…General`, autonum.sty:302-322),
which a document may call for its own reference commands (2211.09537's `{autoref}`), are no-ops: there is nothing to
mark. Repro cross-references/autonum_split_in_align_keeps_later_labels; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch80a::autonum_leaves_the_displays_their_labels`.

### 896. A `\newlabel` record names its label; a record written to the `.aux` is read back as written (Perl: stubs)

LaTeX keeps a label as `\newlabel{<name>}{{<text>}{<page>}…}` (latex.ltx `\newlabel` → `\@newl@bel r`,
`\global\@namedef{r@<name>}{…}`): `\label` writes it to the `.aux` file, the next run reads it at `\begin{document}`,
and `\ref` prints the text. Perl stubs `\newlabel` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml L5796-5800), its `\protected@write`
writes nothing, and nothing written to the `.aux` is read — LaTeXML labels through its own `\label`. A document's own
records were therefore lost: the labels of a companion paper written into the source (1608.05314's
`\newlabel{cohadj:eq:horn-1}{{1.1.2}…}`, 2608.10941's supplement table), and label macros that write their record to
the `.aux` themselves (2503.03625's `\customlabel{eq:TC-1}{TC-1}`, `\protected@write\@auxout{}{\string\newlabel…}`;
1004.2872's `\phantomequation`, `\immediate\write\@auxout`) — about 57 of the census's 35,942 papers, every reference
to them missing where pdflatex prints the text. Ours: `\newlabel` defines `\r@<name>` and records the label as xr
records another document's (sect11.rs `record_newlabel`, `ltx_ref_external`: post fills the reference from this
document's own label where it has one); a `\write` to an `.aux` file reads each `\newlabel` it holds back as it is
written (tex_file_io.rs, sect11.rs `read_back_aux_text`), and `\protected@write` writes a text holding a `\newlabel` to
the `.aux` as latex.ltx does (`\let\protect\@unexpandable@protect`), other texts still unwritten. A single run reads a
record at its write, so a reference before it stays missing (every witness refers after the record). Repro
cross-references/newlabel_records_name_their_references; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch80a::a_newlabel_record_names_its_references`.

### 897. Names parted by horizontal space alone are separate creators (Perl: one author holds them)

pdflatex sets names apart that an author line separates only by horizontal space: a wide space (`\quad`, `\qquad`, a
group of them `{\quad}`, `\hspace{…}`, `\hskip`/`\kern` a length of 4pt or more, `\enspace`, `\enskip`, `\hfill`),
marked names or not, or a name's marks or notes followed by any space (` `, `\ `, `\:`, `\,`, `\;`, `~`, a line
ending in `\`). Perl's `SplitTokens` splits at commas and "and" only, so one creator held them all — or, where the
classifier read the run as a continuation, the names after the first were lost: 2207.06953 kept 2 of its 7 authors,
2411.14257 1 of 4, 2406.12338 1 of 5 (`\thanks{…} {Carla Schenker,}` — each note leads its name), 2604.17501 lost
Ruiyao Xu and Mihir Parmar. Ours: `space_parted_names` (author_block/space_parted.rs) writes each such space as the
comma the split reads, at the line's top level, outside `$…$` and `\(…\)` math, after a name letter, and only where
every piece then reads as a name or qualifies one and two or more read as names (`name_count`): `John Smith\quad Bell
Labs` and `Mc\kern1pt Donald` stay as written, a narrow space with no mark before it parts nothing (`Florian P.\
Busch`, 2212.12575; ecai's `Ann Able \ Bob Baker`, #52(o)'s 77n r2 negative), and a run of two or more narrow spaces
stays #52(o)'s. In a line whose marks lead its names, a space parts two names before the next name's marks
(`$^{1}$Ann Able \: $^{2}$Bob Baker`) or a wide space before a name. A brace group of spacing with a `\quad` in it is
that spacing (`spacing_math_unwrapped`: `Byeongjun Park$^{1}${\quad} Byung-Hoon Kim…`, 2609.03563); a names line
continued after a wide space on its first name's printed line is more names (`space_parts_names`: `\textbf{Ruiyao
Xu}$^{\star}$ \quad \textbf{Mihir Parmar}…`, 2604.17501; 2212.12575). Witnesses 2406.07115 (`\:`), 2609.32353
(`\thanks{…} \ `), 2310.15398 (`\textsuperscript{2} \,`), 2609.03563, 2212.12575, 1909.09562 (llncs `\kern1em`),
2312.06613 (inside `\normalsize{…}`), 2207.06953, 2102.12470, 2002.09131, 2411.14257, 2308.08563 (`$^{1,2,*}$ Defu
Lian`), 0811.3255 and 1311.0077 (aastex `\altaffilmark`), 0806.3855 (A&A `\inst{1}\fnmsep\thanks{…}`), 2406.12338,
1911.02873 (jfm `\ns`: before 84a one creator and an `Error:frontmatter:merged_creators`, now three creators and no
Error). Repros `sectioning-frontmatter/author_{mark_then_space_separates_names, wide_space_after_marked_name_separates,
braced_quad_separates_names, kern_separates_names, wide_space_inside_wrapper_separates,
aastex_mark_then_space_separates, prefix_marks_then_space_separate_names, prefix_notes_then_space_separate_names,
space_inside_a_name_stays}`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch84a::*`, `perfect_kernel_batch77d::
names_parted_only_by_marks_are_split`, `perfect_kernel_batchfms2b::a_mark_in_paren_math_is_cut_whole` (a mark's space
inside `\( ^{1} \)` parts nothing). A comma set in no width before a name's marks, `\rlap,`/`\llap,`, is written as
the comma it prints where the line is cut: kept, the marks the split moves before a glued comma became `\rlap`'s
argument (hep-ph0411288's ptptex `Tatsuo~{\sc Kobayashi}\rlap,${}^{1,}$\footnote{…}`: 6 math Errors in 84a r1; int111d
had given each author the next one's mark and note) — repro `author_lapped_comma_before_marks`, guard
`perfect_kernel_batch84a::author_lapped_comma_before_marks`. A group holding only marks is the name's marks
(`Jia-Bin Huang{$^{2}$} ~ David W. Jacobs{$^{2}$}`, 2406.09417; repro and guard
`author_grouped_marks_then_space_separate_names`).

### 898. eptcs.cls: `\institute` and `\email` inside `\author` are each a line under the names (Perl: no binding)

eptcs.cls (Electronic Proceedings in Theoretical Computer Science; v1.5-v1.7, shipped with each paper, not in TeX Live)
sets `\@author` in a centred `tabular` (eptcs.cls:160-180, `\and` the article class's), and defines `\institute{#1}`
as `\\` and a one-column `tabular` of #1 and `\email{#1}` as `\\{\footnotesize\tt #1}` (:186-191), written inside
`\author` after the names. Read raw as the kernel's author line, the institute and the e-mail stayed in the name
("Ilaria De Crescenzo Università degli Studi di Salerno Dipartimento di Informatica", 1408.5969): the frontmatter
scorer found every one of its 6 sample papers wrong, and 18 of the census's 73 eptcs papers change. Ours: a contrib
binding (`latexml_contrib/src/eptcs_cls.rs`) reads the shipped class raw and reads `\author` as the class prints it —
each `\and` cell a row of names (`Tobias Grubenmann and Jens Lehmann`, 2109.08295), every institute under the row
each name's affiliation (FIDELITY_CHARTER R12), an e-mail line the author it spells, else, a list of one address per
name, the name at its place, else the row's only author, else the block's (§4; `row_email_owners`,
author_block/row_emails.rs). A cell that opens with a `tabular` of names (1407.7928) or with an environment of the
paper's own that opens one (2409.15014's `{authors}{5}`) is read by its columns: a column's names its cell, a full
row's cell a line under its column, any other line every name's. A block with no `\institute`, `\email` or leading
table is the kernel's. Open: an institute or e-mail block labelled by marks (`$^{1}$ Quantinuum … \\ $^{2}$
Informatics Institute …`, `\email{$^{a, b}$ \{…\}@quantinuum.com, $^{c}$ …}`, 2304.02524) goes whole to every
name, not by its labels. Repros `class-bindings/eptcs/eptcs_{institute_email_cells, row_of_names, author_tabular,
author_environment_columns}` (beside a stand-in `eptcs.cls` written from scratch); guards `perfect_kernel_batch84b::*`.

### 899. lmcs.cls: an author's letters request the addresses they label; `\lmcsorcid` is the author's ORCID (Perl: no binding)

lmcs.cls (Logical Methods in Computer Science; shipped with each paper, not in TeX Live; the contrib binding
`latexml_contrib/src/lmcs_cls.rs` loads amsart under it) prints `\author[short]{Name}[a,b]` with the letters raised
after the name and the addresses as one list after all names, each led by the next letter, a, b, c, … (2306.08266's
v0.92 copy, lmcs.cls:391-450); the earlier classes' papers write the letters themselves, `Name\rsuper a` and
`\address{{\lsuper a}Univ}` (1103.0510's LMCS.cls v0.8, cs0701140, 1202.6352). The binding read neither: every address
went to the last author, the letters were left as a paragraph of their own, an ORCID was "ORCID:0000-…" inside the name
(the frontmatter scorer's 2 of 2 lmcs sample papers), and `\lmcsheading` read four of its seven arguments, leaving the
submission and publication dates in the first paragraph. Ours: a name's letters (`[a,b]`, `\rsuper{a,b}`) are `\inst`
requests, llncs's; an address is labelled by the letters written before it, else, in a paper whose names carry
letters, by its place in the list, and an address with several letters (`{\lsuper{b,c}}`, 1202.6352) is each one's;
an address of spacing alone (`\address{\vskip-6 pt}`) is none; a paper whose names carry no letters keeps amsart's
reading, an address the run of authors' it follows (2108.06944, 2402.11987); each address of an `\email` list goes to
the author it spells, else the one its address's letter names, else the group's author (2402.09138's one `\email`
of three addresses); `\lmcsorcid` in a name is the author's ORCID contact; `\lmcsheading`'s fifth and sixth
arguments are the paper's submitted and published dates; `\subjclass` is named as the paper's class names it (2012
ACM CCS, the earlier classes' 1998 ACM Subject Classification). Shared change: `sequenced_contact_labels`
(frontmatter/place.rs) counts an `address` contact as it counts an `affiliation`, so an e-mail under a lettered
`\address` is placed by its letter. Repros `class-bindings/lmcs_{lettered_addresses, unlettered_addresses,
written_letters}`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch84c::*`.

### 900. An unmarked author block's next name line under the lines of the name above starts the next author (Perl: the first author holds every line)

A hand-formatted `\author{…}` in the article class often lists its authors as blocks of lines: a name line, its
address lines, then the next name line (`\author{Laura Rebollo-Neira\\ Mathematics Department\\ Aston University\\ B3
7ET, Birmingham, UK\\ \vspace{0.1cm}\\ A. Plastino\\ IFLP-CCT-Conicet\\ …}`, 1702.01413), which pdflatex prints as one
centred column of author blocks. Perl's no-marker branch reads the first `\\` piece of each `@authorsplits` part as
the names and the rest as their affiliations (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:720-725; its parts are cut at every comma and
"and" too, so the column falls into creators named by address fragments, "Birmingham", "UK"), and ours kept the
first-line rule, so every later name was an affiliation contact of the first author — silently: the frontmatter
scorer's largest missing-author shape (9 of the 18 missing authors on int114a). Ours (`opens_next_author`,
author_block/name_text.rs, a rule of `name_groups`): after the lines under a name, a line that reads as a name and
nothing else (`reads_as_name_alone`: every part a name, `name_count`, a trailing address aside, `\name … \email …`; no
word of a title-case common-noun phrase, `NON_PERSON_WORDS` — roles, titles, fields of study, facilities, documents:
`Chief Scientist`, `Associate Dean`, `Mathematical Sciences`, `James Clerk Maxwell Building`, `Technical Report`; no
note, no leading mark, no e-mail or link line), not going on with the line above (that line ending in a connective,
`School of Physical and \\ Mathematical Sciences`, or the line opening with one), starts the next author when
- a line that prints nothing stands before it (`\\ \vspace{0.1cm}\\`, `\\ \\`, `$ $\\`; the dispatch hands
  `name_groups` a gap flag per line), or a positive `\\[len]` does — pdflatex prints the same gap, so
  `strip_linebreak_options_keeping_gaps` writes it `\\ \\` at the block's top level, outside environments, but not
  after a row of names (`\\[0.2em]` rows, 2605.24414), nor in the whole-block tabular/minipage fallback, whose
  content keeps its line breaks as written (1901.06146); a gap before every line under the names line, the first line
  break's included, or before every line from the second under it on, or at every line break of the block down to the
  candidate, is the block's spacing, no gap (`Ann Able \\[2pt] University of X \\[2pt] Hong Kong`; `\\ University of X \\[2pt]
  Santa Barbara \\[2pt] California`; `\\[3pt] University of X \\[3pt] Santa Barbara \\ California`; lengths are not
  compared, so a wider gap among narrower ones parts no authors, nor does a name set as that place is: RED
  `author_block_uniform_gaps_hide_a_wider_gap`); and a gap-opened last line of the block needs a person's cue (`\\
  \\ Hong Kong`, `\\[12pt] Hong Kong` stay lines);
- it is styled as the names over it in markup of its own the line above is not (`{\bf Anne Schilling}` under `{\em
  …}`, 1509.03383; `\name Mohammad Rostami` under `\addr …`, 2408.11742), or, with a line under it, plain as they
  are under a line set in a style group of its own (`Eddie Monroe` under `{\it Institute of Noetic Sciences …}`,
  1709.07791; not a closing `\textit{University of X} \\ Costa Rica`);
- the line under it is an e-mail address its names spell, a line styled as the block's styled affiliation lines
  (`David Hanson \\ {\it Hanson Robotics}`, 1709.07791), or an institution of its own under a person's name
  (`person_over_institution`): an institution that does not go on with the line (`continues_the_line`: a connective
  opening it, every word of the line again, or its words before the first comma one generic institution noun and the
  adjectives before it, `INSTITUTION_ADJECTIVES` — `Johns Hopkins \\ University, Baltimore`, `Los Alamos \\ National
  Laboratory`, `San Diego \\ State University`), under a name carrying a person's cue, an initial or a particle
  (`Palash B. Pal \\ Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics`, gr-qc9906006; `James M. Robins \\ Department of …`,
  1908.10448). Two capitalized words alone over an institution are as often a place, an institution's name or a role
  (`Santa Barbara \\ Kavli Institute …`, `Max Planck \\ Institute for …`, `Associate Dean \\ School of Medicine`), so
  with no gap and no styling a cue-less name stays a line.
With no gap, a name styled as the line above it that itself reads as a name is a stacked run of names, whose lines
below are the run's: its last name does not take them alone by position (1702.07694's `\name Stephen N. Pallone
\email … \\ \name Peter I. Frazier \email … \\ \name Shane G. Henderson \email … \\\\ \addr …`). After a gap, no
line opens the next author when every line between the names line and it reads as names — a name, or a row of them
(each piece of `split_author_line` a name) — however styled: the gap parts rows of names from the lines they share
(`Ann A. Able \\ Bob B. Baker \\[6pt] Cat C. Cole \\ Institute of Y, Z`; `\textbf{6 names} \\ \textbf{5
names\thanks{…}} \\ \\ CUHK MMLab \\ \texttt{…}`, 2604.18394, the lab no creator); otherwise a gap parts the
authors whatever the line above reads as (`Comunidad de Palo Blanco, Salamanca Gto. México.\\ \\ V.I. Tkach`,
0801.1297). A line that opens the next author — by this rule or by #52's alternation, note or "and" rules — is a names
line: a row of names on it parted by a run of spacing is parted as the block's first names line is (#52(o), then
`space_parted_names`: `\\ \\ Bob Baker~~~~Cat Cole \\ Univ B`, two creators). A name-shaped line with none of these
stays a line (`Hanson Robotics` over a name, `Hong Kong` over `The Hong Kong University …`, a closing `Costa Rica`),
as does a name directly under names (Perl's reading). The "and"-led opening of #52's math-ph0303018 rule skips a field
of study the same way (`\\and Computer Engineering`, 2510.15190). And a block a line break opens after names only
horizontal space parts it from (the JASA template's `Name\thanks{…}\hspace{.2cm}\\`), names with no lines of their
own, is those names' lines when its first line is an institution: the names line and the block's lines are one
group's, which `name_groups` parts as any — its first group's lines are the names', its later groups the next
authors' (an "and" line opening one and dropped, a gap, the names' styling, a note, an institution under a person's
name: `Assaf P. Oron\hspace{.2cm}\\ Children's Core …\\ and \\ Nancy Flournoy \\ …`, 1701.05964; 2004.03971's Han
Lin Shang; 2503.11250's `\\[5pt]` gaps; 1504.05438's "and" line; `Lin Liu \hspace{.2cm} \\ Institute of Natural
Sciences, School of Mathematical Sciences, MOE-LSC \\ …`, 1908.10448: before, three creators named by the
institution's parts). Residuals, each a RED repro: a cue-less person's name over an institution with no gap or
styling stays a line (1908.10448's `Zach Shahn \\ IBM Research,`; `article_plain_name_line_between_affiliations`), and
so does a row of names (`author_block_row_of_names_with_no_signal`, SYNC row 121); the names of a stacked run stay
lines of its first name (1702.07694; deferred; `author_block_stacked_names_each_a_creator`); an eponym or a place with
a particle over an institution reads as a person (`L.D. Landau \\ Institute for Theoretical Physics`, `Rio de Janeiro
\\ Centro …`; `author_block_eponym_or_place_over_institution`); a cued name under a place that reads as a name, or
over an institution whose head noun leads it (`Bob B. Baker \\ Imperial College, London`), stays a line
(`author_block_next_name_under_a_place_or_whole_institution`); a wider gap among uniform ones parts no authors
(`author_block_uniform_gaps_hide_a_wider_gap`); a name line carrying a note or an address after a wide space stays a
line (`author_block_name_line_with_trailing_text`, int114a's reading); an organisation's name after a gap, with a
line under it, opens an author as a name does (`University of X \\ \\ Google DeepMind \\ London, UK`; only words

(solv-int9710025, pre-existing; `author_block_leading_spacer_line`). Witnesses 1702.01413, 0801.1297, 1608.08479,

### 901. llncs's one `\institute` is every author's, its e-mail lines by their owners (Perl: on the first author)

llncs.cls:868-886 prints a sole institute (no `\and` in `\institute`, `\c@@inst=1`) unnumbered under the whole author
row; `\inst{n}` (:894) numbers each author's when there are several. Perl numbers the sole institute `affiliation:1`
(llncs.cls.ltxml:46-49), which no author requests without `\inst{1}`, and its prefix-stripped fallback strands it on
the first author (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1195); #159 had kept it once on a nameless creator under the names, so no author
had an affiliation (20 of the frontmatter scorer's 56 llncs sample papers). Ours: the binding queues the sole
institute with `_share=authors` (`\lx@llncs@institute@sole`), and the frontmatter's flush (`share_row_contacts`,
base_utilities/frontmatter/shared_row.rs, before anything is digested) makes it every author's unless it is picked:
only the class's own request picks it, a command requesting a labelled annotation (`\inst{1}`) with a number; a
hand-typed `$^{1}$` (2607.02596), a paper's mark macro (`\affmark{1}`, `\printfnsymbol{1}`: 1804.05870, 2007.07423,
2102.12877, 2403.11865) and llncs's `\fnmsep` are answered by no one and pick nothing (`\inst{*}`, 2207.04574, and an
empty `\inst{}`, 2604.20229, neither). Not shared, as before: an institute holding marks of its own (a superscript, or
a paper macro raising its argument bare, `\textsuperscript{#1}`: 2608.21425's `\affmark{1} City University … \quad
\affmark{2} …`), a shown mark numbering another institute than the first (`Ann Able$^{1,2}$` over `{1} Univ A \\ {2}
Univ B`: several institutes numbered by hand, astro-ph0305539's shape), an empty `\institute{}` (none, 2407.13764).
Shared, each author's content requests `row:shared`, which the contact sets as its own label, so it is digested once
and placed on every author as an `\inst`-picked one is.

Its e-mail lines are lines under the row, taken out of the contact and each decided on its own (`row_email_calls`); the contact's lines are its `\\`/`\newline`/`\par` parts. With several authors, a line
holding an `@` outside the class's `\email` calls — at any depth, a note's too, or in what a command of the paper's
own on it prints (a parameterless macro's body; a `\urldef`'d command's text, which `\urldef` keeps beside it,
url_sty.rs) — is an e-mail line (`holds_raw_address`): `{\tt \{joxan,navas,andrews\}@…}` (1103.2027), `\texttt{…}`,
`\url{{farazi, pallgeuer}@…}` (1809.11127), `\href{mailto:…}{…}` (2408.03209), `\mailsa` (1307.8067; 1408.0384's
`\mailk, \mailt`). The address reader (`email_addresses`) reads it after an `Email:` label (the contact's own name)
or a label of its own (`Corresponding author:`, its first word a contact's, which keeps the line whole), each address
its owner's as a call's are;
a line of a shared institute the reader cannot read is the block's, as written, an affiliation (1708.06860's brace
list cut across two `\urldef`s; `Department of CS: {\tt able@x.edu}`, no label of its own); when that line is the
institute's own first line (`… Hamburg, Germany \mailsa`, 1706.02124; an address in the institute's `\thanks`), the
whole institute is the block's, as written (int114a's placement). Each `\email` call: each address the reader takes goes to the author it spells; else, a list of one address per author that every
spelled address agrees with — an address several names spell agreeing only when the name at its place is one of them
(`lee@` at Cid Cole's place under Ann Lee and Bob Lee is no order), a list of local parts the reader cannot part never
— to the author at its place; else, with one author, to that author; else, the one address left of several authors,
to the one marked as the corresponding author (`marked_corresponding_author`) who owns no other address of the line
(2510.12629's `kgwo0528@` stays the block's beside Jinwoo Kim's `jinwookim@`), unless it is a template's
(`{firstname.lastname}@`, `first.last@`: no one's); else, in a shared institute, to the author
block (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4, `row_address_owners`, the reading of eptcs's rows, #898). A brace list of local parts is each address apart
(`\{saad,saia\}@cs.unm.edu`, 1405.1167); split so, a list no one owns keeps its printed braces
(`{stomforde|bsick}@uni-kassel.de`, 1701.08125). One address in printed braces is that address, set as written
(`\email{\{fatima.iribu@gmail.com\}}` ×3, 2410.04091: one per author, each the author's at its place). A call the
reader cannot part (`{a,b}@x` without printed braces, 2206.10050; 1809.06205, 2607.18577), or parts into pieces no
whole address (`[a@insa-, b@insa-]rouen.fr`, 2609.24668), is the call as written, the block's (user ruling R10), one
author's when there is one; when another call or line is not read, no list is one per author and the others go by
spelling alone. A label of the call's own the rule recognises goes with it, in its piece, the call then unparted
(`call_label`): before the call, one to four words of letters and hyphens ending in a colon, read as printed
(through a font's group, a `~`, a spacing command: `\textit{Corresponding author:}`, `Corresponding~author:`,
`\hspace{1cm}Contact:`), the first a contact's (`names_a_contact`, one vocabulary with the `Email:` label reader
`split_email_label`: corresponding, correspondence, contact, author, e-mail, mail, address), from a later line's start
or after a `,` or `;`, the spacing before it aside (`Corresponding author:`, 2410.06985, 2609.00838; `Contact:`,
2509.05139; `Correspondence to:`, the r4 re-review's q03, q23); after it, a parenthetical of words
(`(Corresponding author)`, 2608.24697). Other text on the call's line stays the institute's, every author's: `… Rouen,
France. \email{…}` (2609.24668), `\hspace{0.5cm}` (2310.06847), text that only ends in a colon (`Department of
Computer Science:`, `Dept. of CS:`, `Lab of A. B. Smith:`: the r3 re-review's n09, n10, n35) — and a label of a form
the rule does not recognise, a residual (prose without a colon, `Corresponding author email \email{…}`; a label word
the rule does not know, `Reach me at: \email{…}`, kept off the block so that n09/n10's department stays the
institute's; a label after a `.` or after other text on its line, `Univ X. Corresponding author: \email{…}`). A
connective between two calls (`\email{a} and \email{b}`, `\&`, `or`: the r4 re-review's q08, q28) is no call
separator and stays the institute's, every author's — a residual. A shared contact's `\email` inside its `\thanks` (no other `@` in it) stays in the
note, given its owner's label in place; as int114a, the address leaves the note's sentence. Every address goes through
`\lx@row@email{label}{address}` (llncs's sets its `\emailname`). An e-mail digested inside a shared contact all the
same (a paper's own `\email` macro) never inherits `row:shared`: it keeps its own label, else is the block's
(`SHARED_ROW_LABEL`, `\lx@annotate@frontmatter@now`). So in a shared institute an address the rule reads, and a
label it recognises, is one author's or the block's, never every author's; a shared contact every line of which is
taken is none. An `\inst{1}`-picked institute is its picked authors' as the marks decide, and the block is the
shared path's fail-safe only: a piece leaves it only when it is an address the reader reads and an owner is found for
(the rules above), with the label the rule recognises; everything else stays in it, as written, its picked authors'
(int114a's placement): a line the reader cannot read, first or later (`\institute{Univ X, able@x.edu}`, `Univ X\\
Twitter: @univx`; the r3 re-review's n31-n33, the r4 re-review's q01, q25), the calls on it each read apart
(`\email{able@x.edu}, Twitter: @univx`, q31), a line holding a note (q02), `Department of CS: {\tt able@x.edu}` (q19),
a call or line no address of which an owner is found for (2109.05583's template, 2307.04136, 2609.24668), and the
text between — save decision 3 of 2026-10-22: of a call or line parted by owner (a group written out), an address no
one is found for is the block's, as in a shared institute (2510.12629's `\email{kgwo0528@gmail.com,
jinwookim@kw.ac.kr}`: `jinwookim@` Jinwoo Kim's, `kgwo0528@` the block's); a picked contact every line of which is
taken stays, empty, answering its authors' `\inst{1}` marks. Two residuals of the picked path (the r5 re-review):
the corresponding-author step is not limited to the picked authors, so a "Corresponding author" note on an author with
no mark takes an unspelled address out of the picked institute (s17, RED below); and one address no one spells, alone
in its call under two or more picked authors, stays every picked author's (s01, s16, s19; int114a's placement, while
the same address in a call parted by owner is the block's) — FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 sends an unspelled address to the
block, so it waits on a ruling. A shared institute's line holding a note with an `@` reads the line's own word as the
spelled author's address (`Univ X\\ Visit\footnote{able@x.edu}`: "Visit" Ann's e-mail, s23, RED below; the picked
path keeps the line, q02, v03). Left in the contact, an e-mail would
have inherited the institute's label (Perl Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:497-500): every author's, or with `\inst{1}` every
`\inst{1}` author's (2608.11332's brace list whole on both, arXiv/html_feedback#6881's witness, now each address its
owner's).

The binding also takes an `\institute` written inside `\author` out of the last name (1609.01220): it is the class's
store, run when `\@maketitle` sets the names, before `\institutename` prints it, so it wins over an outer
`\institute` before or after it (`\lx@llncs@inner@institute`; a later `\author` without one gives the store back).
Unchanged: `\inst`-numbered institutes, several institutes without marks (the block's, or Perl's numeric pairing when
as many as the authors; 2207.06953's hand-typed `$^1$` marks still read by no one), the lazy superscript block.
Witnesses 1002.2793, 1307.8067, 1405.1167, 1509.00818, 1609.01220, 1809.11127, 1910.11599, 2011.00616, 2101.06781,
2106.04289, 2205.06740, 2207.04574, 2207.11464, 2306.03360, 2405.11276, 2502.08785, 2511.12796, 2603.26486,

2207.07506, 2407.18381, 2408.03209, 2411.00887, 2504.06600 (address lines outside the calls); 2410.06985,
