### 902. imsart's `{keyword}` blocks are the VTeX classes' markup; an amsart document's own stored `\subjclass`/`\keywords` reach the frontmatter (Perl: one keyword kept; lost)

imsart.sty (shipped with each paper, not in TeX Live) writes its keywords and subject classification as
`{keyword}[class=<class>]` blocks of `\kwd[<sep>]{<entry>}` entries — `\begin{keyword}[class=MSC] \kwd[Primary ]{60J10}
\kwd[; Secondary ]{60G35}\end{keyword}` — which it sets in `\keyword@box` for the title page (imsart.sty: 1518-1567 of
1410.4462's copy, :2334-2393 of 2605.27137's) or, under the journal options' `keywordsasfootnote` (aap, aop, aos, …),
collects through its `\pseudo@keyword` (:474-490, read first by its own `\begin`) for a title footnote (:1604-1630). The
imsart binding (`latexml_contrib/src/imsart_cls.rs`) loaded OmniBus, whose `\kwd` re-added the keywords with its one
entry (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1196), and the raw blocks set the box nothing typesets: 1410.4462, 2407.13970 and 2605.27137
kept their last keyword only and lost their MSC codes (Perl the same). Ours: the binding defines the markup arxbj and
arximspdf already share (`vtex_keyword_markup`, ims_support_sty.rs) and locks it against the raw files' (`\keyword`,
`\endkeyword`, `\begin{keyword}`, `\end{keyword}`, `\kwd`, `\@kwd`, `\pseudo@keyword`) while the class loads — imsart.sty
read raw, and a shipped copy of the class under another name that declares itself imsart, read after the binding with
the imsart.sty copy it loads (1401.3408's myimsart.cls and myimsart.sty) — and unlocks it at the class's
`\AtEndOfClass`, so a document's own `\renewcommand{\kwd}` is the document's, as `\arxiv` is. Each block's entries are
one list joined by the class's `\sep`, under the class's `\keyword@<class>` heading (imsart.sty's own
`\setattribute`/`\setpkgattr` lines; the binding's defaults are those of :1521-1525); a block whose class is a subject
classification — `AMS`, `MSC`, `MSC2010`, `MSC2020` — is an `ltx:classification`, any other an `ltx:keywords`. The
classification's scheme is the printed heading, edition included, without the closing ":" or "." its name keeps
(`\lx@ims@scheme`: "MSC 2010 subject classifications", 1410.4462; "MSC2020 subject classifications", 2605.27137 and
2407.13970, through the copy's `\ims@href`), as the AMS classes' `\subjclass` gives "2000 Mathematics Subject
Classification": the HTML heads a classification with its scheme and shows the name only without one
(LaTeXML-structure-xhtml.xsl:239-240, Perl's the same), so the class key alone read "MSC". A key the class gives no
heading keeps the key (arxbj's `class=MSC`, where pdflatex prints no heading). Shared change: arxbj's and arximspdf's
`class=AMS` schemes are their headings ("AMS 2000 subject classifications", was "AMS"), and their `class=MSC…` blocks are
classifications (were keywords).

amsart.cls's `\subjclass` and `\keywords` store `\@subjclass` and `\@keywords`, which its `\maketitle` prints in a
first-page footnote (amsart.cls:553-564, :657-658); the binding's setters give the frontmatter directly and never set
them. A document carrying its own copy (`\renewcommand*\subjclass[2][2000]{\def\@subjclass{#2}…}`, 2004.06211:12,
1009.1929) lost its classification, as Perl does; so did kms-j's and kms-b's (1109.3766, 2207.08173), whose
`\@adminfootnotes` print `\@subjclass`. Ours: the AMS classes' `\maketitle` hands a non-empty stored value to
the frontmatter (`\lx@ams@stored@topmatter` at `\lx@maketitle@begin`, `amsart_class_internals`): the subject
classification under the edition's `\subjclassname` (the scheme and the name), the keywords under `\keywordsname`, then
empties the store; it does nothing once the binding's own setter ran (`\lx@ams@subjclass@given`,
`\lx@ams@keywords@given`), so a paper using the class's commands is unchanged, nor when the K11 reroute owns a raw
class's `\keywords` store (`\iflx@ams@keywords@rerouted`: a class wrapping acmart, guard
`perfect_kernel_batch58::acmart_under_a_wrapper_class_keeps_its_setters`). The hand-over reaches every class loading
the AMS binding, also one whose title page never prints `\@subjclass`: CSML.cls's `\@maketitle` (:292-299) prints only
`\@ACMCCS`, `\@amsclass` and `\@keywords`, so its papers' unprinted `\subjclass` codes (1504.03919, 1510.01752,
1602.00476, 1608.04592) are a classification, kept by FIDELITY_CHARTER §2 (authored text is kept, even where the class
discards it). Residual (RED, no guard): a document's `\subjclass` copy that stores `\@subjclass` but sets no
`\subjclassname` takes the binding's default edition, 1991 (Perl's `\@subjclassyear`), where amsart.cls prints 2020
(:789); no corpus paper (`sectioning-frontmatter/amsart_document_subjclass_copy_default_edition`). Residuals of
the 86a r2 re-review: an imsart block on a supplement's own title page, the frontmatter sealed, is kept in place as
bare text run into the next paragraph, its heading lost (RED `sectioning-frontmatter/imsart_supplement_keyword_block_keeps_its_heading`;
85a lost the words; OmniBus's sealed `{keyword}` after a `\section*` is still dropped; no corpus paper); arxbj's
`class=MSC` block, which prints no heading, shows the class key "MSC" as its `<h6>`; and, pre-existing, other bindings'
classifications show a scheme the paper does not print — the AMS binding's default edition beside a class's own
heading (`scheme="1991 Mathematics Subject Classification"`, `name="Mathematical subject classification (2010)"`:
1310.5294, cedram-alco; m2an's 0811.1789, 1512.06935, 2407.04312, 2411.09498), and a bare "AMS"/"keywords" in
tac_cls.rs:30 (2312.12356), sigma_cls.rs:98 (0705.3628), ejpecp_cls.rs:45-55 (2312.17406, its "Primary"/"Secondary"
lost too) and siamart_cls.rs:93-171 (1707.06953) — a later batch, each binding's printed heading. Repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/{imsart_keyword_blocks_footnote_option, imsart_keyword_blocks_in_the_box,
imsart_document_kwd_is_the_documents, imsart_renamed_copy_keyword_blocks, arxbj_keyword_classification_headings,
omnibus_kwd_entries_add_up, omnibus_kwd_blocks_each_entry_once, amsart_document_subjclass_store}`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch86a::*`.

### 903. An abstract placed ahead of title-page text pdflatex prints before it follows that text, wrapped as a continued `<titlepage>` (Perl: the text after the abstract, or lost)

Perl's `\lx@frontmatterhere` constructor inserts every queued frontmatter element at once
(`Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:824-844`, `:918`); construction runs after digestion, so an abstract given after
`\maketitle` is already queued and lands in the block at the head, and whatever the document typesets between
`\maketitle` and `\begin{abstract}` follows it as body (`latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1099`). Rust did the same and
adds the class's own title page (the `\@maketitle` deposit and class `\maketitle` replay, #265), which runs after
`\lx@frontmatterhere` (`sect05.rs` `\lx@maketitle@body`) — so AAAI's `\affiliations` (aaai21.sty:58, a store delimited
by `_` that `\@maketitle` reads at :75; aaai24/2026 and aaai2027 alike), dmtcs's addresses, pnastwo's affiliations and
`\@contributor` line all came after the abstract, though pdflatex prints them above it. The same held for lines
hand-typeset between `\maketitle` and the abstract, and, without `\maketitle`, for setters that print in place before
it (the fallback places the frontmatter at the top, #246's wrap running only for an abstract-only queue). The
frontmatter scorer's readability tier counts each as a piece out of print order; it was the largest class on the
3,000-paper sample (`agent_reports/2026-10-28_rc_order.md` groups G-A and G-C).

Ours (`base_utilities/frontmatter/cover_order.rs` `place_abstract_after_cover`; user ruling 2026-09-20, titlepage layout
is not semantic, the frontmatter schema is; main-session decision 2026-10-28 under the readability bar): a frontmatter
entry set after `\lx@frontmatterhere`'s `after_digest` (`lx_frontmatter_here_digested`) — queued after it (the stamp
taken by `queue_front_matter` and handed to the later flush that digests it) or digested in place after it
(`{abstract}`) — is LATE: its element carries `_late` (`frontmatter_push`, stripped at finalize). A late abstract's
`\lx@frontmatter@mark` builds a marker of its own (`ltx:_LateAbstract_Capture_`, which the flush's marker sweep leaves
alone). Where the abstract is already placed (the eager build) the marker is settled at once; in a streamed build
`insert_late_frontmatter` settles it after placing the abstract, so both builds give one tree. The root children between
the placed run of frontmatter that begins with the first late abstract and the marker are read as #246 reads a cover:
title-page layout (`is_titlepage_layout`) that the class's title page printed — every root child built between
`\lx@deposit@begin` and `\lx@deposit@end`, which `\lx@deposit@maketitle` puts around a kept deposit (`_deposit`) — or
that is no running body prose (`is_body_prose`: an indented paragraph with text outside its boxes, or a list whose items
hold one; a `\noindent`ed, centred or flushed line, a box alone, a list of such lines are cover) is wrapped as
`<ltx:titlepage class="ltx_titlepage_continued">` in its order; pagebreaks, preamble residue, root footnote texts and
what an `\insert` inside the deposit sets (`_inserted`: page-foot material — AAAI's copyright slug, aaai21.sty:53
`\insert\footins{…}`, printed at the foot of the first column; a title page whose only ink it is, the AAAI-19 papers
1909.05089 and 1904.09412, keeps the abstract where it was) are passed over and follow the abstract; anything else — a
sectional unit, a TOC, a float, body prose, a body list — keeps the abstract where it was. While a deposit runs,
`\insert` (`tex_inserts.rs`) digests its material as the internal vertical list TeX makes it (tex.web §1099-1100:
vertical mode, its `}` ends its paragraph), ended by a `\par` and set after the title page (`lx_deposit_inserts`, handed
on by `\lx@deposit@maketitle`), so an `\insert` inside a centred line leaves the line whole and one before a `\noindent`
line does not run into it (nor does what the body sets right after `\maketitle`: 2501.04820's `\footnotetext`,
2110.04708's and 2312.05616's teaser figure were set inside AAAI's slug paragraph); material opened by an implicit
`\bgroup` (§403 `scan_left_brace` takes it: revtex4*, aastex701, memoir, bxjs*) is read live to its group's end as
`\vadjust`'s is (`predigest_insert_group_contents`) and set after the title page the same way, after the braced ones
before it; outside a deposit `\insert` stays Perl's no-op, its material set in place. The speculative runs of the
title page (`speculative_title_page_run`, #767) read the material an `\insert` stashes as printed, after the run's own
text, and a deposit or replay whose only ink is that material counts as kept (`lx_title_page_deposit_kept`), so a
store printed in an `\insert` is the title page's and its label is the entry's name, taken out of the deposit with it
(as when the material was set inline; the label reader `line_label_before` reads `\bgroup`/`\egroup` as braces, so
`\insert\footins\bgroup … Keywords: \@keywords\par\egroup` no longer leaves an orphan "Keywords:" paragraph, which
int116a left too). With a cover, the run of the first late abstract is placed by one rule:
- **The fail-safe.** A late run holding an entry with title-page provenance is not moved at all: the abstract and
  everything after it keep today's slot (int116a's order). Title-page provenance is `_titlepage` on the element
  (stripped at finalize), naming the raw class's store the entry was handed on from (`\lx@store@from` around the call:
  `harvest_stores` at `\maketitle`, creators and their annotations aside; `\lx@store@hand` as it is set;
  `hand_untypeset_stores`' notes; `queue_front_matter` and `frontmatter_push` stamp it as they stamp `_late`; the
  provenance is cleared after each call list however its digestion ends), from a store the class's title page may print
  (`title_page_may_print`: unless the speculative run of the whole title page was made and the store's sentinel did not
  reach it). The class's title page prints such a store where the frontmatter cannot tell — above the cover, below it,
  at the page foot (`\footnotetext{Keywords: \@keywords}`, an `\insert`) — so no move is made.
- **Otherwise**, an abstract queued before `\maketitle`'s flush (not `_late`: smfart's `{abstract}`, the late
  `{altabstract}` after the cover; an rcresumen-style `\resumen` store `\maketitle` hands on) keeps its place ahead of
  the titlepage, and everything else in the run moves behind it: keywords printed after the abstract — a binding's,
  which carry no provenance (amsart's, set at the page foot; aaspp4's, astro-ph9911463), a raw class's store its title
  page does not print (dmtcs's preamble `\keywords`, printed after its abstract: 0905.1102) — and a title `\thanks`
  pubnote (2102.01904).

A date never follows the abstract in the frontmatter's order, so none is in the run. Once per document
(`lx_late_abstract_placed`): each later late abstract's marker (linked to the abstract its command added by an
ordinal both carry, `LATE_MARK_ORDINAL`, the eager build's and the streamed build's alike; the marker of a command that
added none — a repeat `frontmatter_drop_repeats` dropped, an empty `{abstract}` — places nothing; the ordinal is taken
by the first abstract added after its marker, kept or not, `take_late_mark`, so an abstract a binding adds later with
`\lx@add@frontmatter{ltx:abstract}` and no marker of its own carries none, and no marker places it, DEFERRED_FAMILIES
"Abstracts a class stores or queues") places its own abstract and its run behind the cover lines printed between the
abstract before it and it (86i `place_later_abstract`: they stay paragraphs, not a second titlepage) — the second of two
`{abstract}`s after `\maketitle`, both kept since 86i (OD #154; 1006.5288's centred French title between them). Late
abstracts keep their source order: the run carries every later late abstract still waiting right after it, marked or
markerless, with theirs, and each carried one then scans from its new place, right after the one before it — so three
or more late abstracts each follow their own cover lines (review probe o2d), and no late abstract stands in the region
a scan crosses (one that did would refuse the move). With anything in the region that is no cover — body prose, a
float, a list, a TOC, a sectional unit — or no cover at all, the move is refused and the run stays right after the
abstract before it (86i r3 review probes q1–q4, q10); a markerless abstract stays right after the one before it, carried
along (q9). After each move the late abstracts' marker ordinals are checked to ascend
(`keep_late_abstracts_in_source_order`): a violation is a placement bug, a `debug_assert!` failure in a debug build;
a release build reports it (`Warning:unexpected:late_abstract_order`, counted) and sets every late abstract with its
run (its keywords, its classification) in source order where the first of them stands — at the root's head if nothing
precedes it — each markerless one after the marked one it followed. A marker inside an open paragraph (a `\noindent` line running into `\begin{abstract}`)
ends the region with that paragraph, closed first, when nothing follows the marker in it. Without `\maketitle` nothing
is late: the fallback's non-abstract-only branch reads the first abstract's marker (`abstract_mark_bound`), the earliest
in source and so before every abstract in print, before the flush removes it, and applies the same rule to the first
root abstract's run after the title-ink dedup — no abstract moves behind text printed after it (nothing there is
late, so the fail-safe, a late run's, does not apply: no `\maketitle` placed a store). Residual (as before 86g): on
the fallback path, and where the first abstract is not late, a second abstract kept beside the first (smfart
`{abstract}` before `\maketitle`, a centred line, `{altabstract}`) stays ahead of the lines printed between the two;
late ones are each placed (86i, above). Residual of the fail-safe (int116a's order, out of print order): a raw
class whose title page prints frontmatter above or below the cover — `\def\@maketitle{…\noindent Keywords:
\@keywords\par}` (or `\@pacs`, a `\footnotetext{Keywords: \@keywords}`, an `\insert\footins{…}` of it, an off-table
store `\maketitle` hands on as a note) before `\maketitle` `\begin{center}Department\end{center}`
`\begin{abstract}…` — gives `abstract, keywords, para(Department)` where pdflatex prints the department before the
abstract (86g r2/r3 review probes b01, b03, b03b, b04, f1, f2, f3; no case in the 3,990-paper A/B population).
In a streamed build a root child spilled out of the tree (`_spilled_`) in the region keeps the slot, fail-safe (the smfart repro at fragment budget 3: its pagebreaks). The titlepage continues
the title block rather than standing for it, so LaTeXML-structure-xhtml.xsl's `ltx:title` template displays the title
beside an `ltx_titlepage_continued` one (it hides it beside any other titlepage with ink, #761), and
`settle_cover_title_ink` counts no such titlepage as a cover. An abstract the class's title page prints itself (a
`\begin{abstract}` inside `\@maketitle`) is late as well: the deposit's lines before it are its cover, those after it
stay after it.

Witnesses (order before → after, no word lost, nothing else moved): aaai 2011.04405, 2102.01904, 2109.06762,
2203.09121, 2208.05119, 2309.13734, 2412.11664; 2304.00893 (nature `{affiliations}`), 0905.1102 (dmtcs), 1404.2263
(pnastwo), 1609.06335 (bmc_article), 1908.08044 (INTERSPEECH2019); hand-typeset 1302.5352, 1702.07128, 2309.14687;
no `\maketitle` 1207.1161 (arxiv.cls:241 `\affiliation`), 1303.3004 (ae100prg.cls:188 `\address`), astro-ph0210637
(newpasp_crete.sty:74 `\affil`). Not covered: 2403.15998 (ifacconf), whose `{frontmatter}` sets the deposit, the
abstract's marker and the keywords in one box (`ifacconf.cls:984-1070` `\open@fm`, one `logical-block`): the marker
does not end its root child, so the abstract keeps its place — splitting the box at the marker is the ifacconf
binding's work, tracked in DEFERRED_FAMILIES.md ("Deferred by the difficulty rule", the abstract-before-`\maketitle`
entry) with ifacconf's 1309.1610 and 2104.15006. Reach (the int117a bundle A/B, 23,231 papers): about 1,130 gain a continued titlepage — 505 of 3,352 raw-class papers, AMS, w68, the AAAI/nature families — with no word lost or duplicated in any of them, and a stratified 40-paper print-order check against pdflatex 39/40 (97.5 %, Wilson 0.871-0.996; `agent_reports/2026-10-28_check_86g_reach.md`). Residuals it found: a page-foot stamp placed by absolute positioning (an IEEE copyright `tikz` overlay at `current page.south`, EPTCS's footer) is cover, though pdflatex prints it at the foot, after the abstract — only `\insert` material is recognised as page-foot (1904.01081, 1807.02323, 2305.08722, 2606.03568; about 13-16 of the 1,130; fix: treat a page-anchored overlay as `_inserted` is); non-cover prose printed before the abstract is labelled titlepage — acknowledgements (2507.17794), a Turkish abstract (2511.07595), an epigraph (2606.03158), teaser figures (1905.09264, 2403.01323, 2602.21203, 2011.06048), and in 2105.08612 and 2405.19307 a minipage figure is no longer lifted to a root `figure` (about 8-10; order and content right, the label wrong); the audit's `\noindent` tightening is not taken, since it would send genuine pre-abstract notices (1806.06803, 1211.5804, 2308.09464, 2202.00765) back out of print order. Detector residuals (the 86g r4 re-review; no corpus witness, 0 of
3,990 rows differ): a store the class prints through a field the kernel refuses (a raw `\renewcommand\author` whose
`\@author` appends `\@keywords`; any refused or nulled creator field extended with a store) is not seen by the
speculative title-page run, so `title_page_may_print` says no and the run moves — the keywords behind the cover though
pdflatex prints them above it, as many out-of-order pairs as int116a (RED
`sectioning-frontmatter/late_abstract_after_a_refused_author_store`); and a speculative run that aborts is read as made
and printing nothing (`aborted_printed_nothing`, the safe answer for `hand_untypeset_stores`), not as unknown —
suspected only, no title page that pdflatex compiles was found to abort it. Repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/{late_abstract_after_hand_typeset_cover, late_abstract_after_the_class_title_page,
abstract_inside_the_class_title_page, abstract_after_in_place_setters_without_maketitle,
late_abstract_after_body_content_keeps_its_slot, late_abstract_after_an_earlier_abstract,
late_abstract_after_a_class_store_abstract, late_abstract_after_class_printed_frontmatter,
late_abstract_after_a_class_note_store}`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch86g::*`,
`114_streaming_structure::streaming_late_abstract_follows_its_cover`, and
`perfect_kernel_batch56::late_abstract_after_maketitle_leaves_no_marker_and_wraps_nothing` (body prose stays body).

### 904. pos.sty and rmaa.cls have bindings: their title-page stores are the frontmatter (Perl: no binding; pos.sty unread, an empty name; rmaa through OmniBus)

pos.sty (SISSA's PoS template v2.1 2018/11/13 and v2.2 2021/09/21, under `article`; not in TeX Live, every paper ships
it) and rmaa.cls (RevMexAA, v1.9 to v3.26; shipped too) were read raw, and their title pages live in stores only their
own `\maketitle` prints, which the kernel's locked `\maketitle` refuses. pos.sty:88 `\RenewDocumentCommand\author{som}`
is refused by the kernel's locked `\author`, so `\author*{Javier M. Duarte}` read `*` as the name and the name as an
affiliation; `\affiliation` and `\emailAdd` (:411-430) fill token registers, `\FullConference` (:364-369) a box,
`\onbehalf` (:249-260) an expl3 token list — all lost. rmaa.cls:500-503 `\altaffiltext` appends
`\protect\footnotetext[#1]{#2}` to `\@thanks`, which the kernel's `\maketitle` empties (sect05.rs, TITLE_PAGE_FIELDS and
the `\maketitle` tail); `\resumen` (:450-453) and `\addkeyword`/`\keywords` (:509-546) store the Spanish abstract and
the "Key Words:" line; `\affil{…}` inside an `\author` (:491-494, `\\[1.5ex]…\\[1.5ex]`) stayed in the name.

Ours: `pos_sty.rs` and `rmaa_cls.rs` define the title-page commands before the copy is read raw (the copy's `\newcommand`
of a name LaTeXML defines is ignored with an `Info:ignore`, as any; its `\NewDocumentCommand\onbehalf` too). pos.sty:
`\author*[marks]{name}` is `\lx@add@authors@append[annotations={marks}]` (jheppub's), the star the speaker's note — the
text of the copy's own speaker footnote (`\footnotetext{\speakerText}`, "Speaker"; a v2.1 copy's written-out "Presenter",
2107.12913; read from the copy, `speaker_text`), given once, labelled `lx@pos@speaker` and requested by every starred
author beside its marks (the footnote under every star). The label keeps it off the kernel's dealing of unlabelled notes
one per labelled author, in order, when they are as many: `\author[a]{Ann Lee}\author*[b]{Bob Kim}\onbehalf{…}` (or
`\note{…}`) had given Ann Lee the "Speaker" note and Bob Kim the other; `\affiliation[label]`, `\emailAdd`, `\note`, `\dedicated` are
jheppub.sty's (shared, `jheppub_sty::jhep_contact_markup`; the e-mails placed by FIDELITY_CHARTER §4, an address no name
spells the block's, as the template's unattributed "E-mail:" line); `\ShortTitle`/`\FullConference` PoS.cls's
(`pos_cls::pos_title_page_fields`); `\onbehalf[*]{…}` a note of the author given last before it, after whose name it is
printed; `\notes{…}` a note; the abstract one argument (`\abstract:redefined@nargs`). Without a copy the binding loads
pos.sty's packages. rmaa.cls: `\altaffilmark`/`\altaffiltext` are the AAS markup (shared with OmniBus, aas_support and
aguplus, `aas_support_sty::altaffil_markup`): each label the affiliation of every author whose mark lists it, an
unmarked one the block's (1301.7157); `\affil` an affiliation of the authors before it (`annotate=new`); `\resumen` and
`\abstract` two abstracts handed on in the title page's order, "Resumen" before "Abstract", whichever is given first, at
`\maketitle` (else at the first section, else at the end, as aguplus's addresses); the keywords one accumulating list
(`\@kwdsep` " --- "); `\shorttitle` (:550, the running head) the toc title, as OmniBus's (Perl keeps it, 0903.4819), only until the title
page is made — the class's own `abstracts` environment re-sets the running head with `\shorttitle{Abstracts}` (:1366),
no toc title of the paper's (the 86b r2 re-review's r2 probe).
The class's `\newcommand`s of these names are ignored, so no lock is needed; its document-time
`\renewcommand{\altaffilmark}[1]{\relax}` in the index and contents environments stays the class's.

Residuals: an `\emailAdd` inside an `\author` is kept as that author's e-mail, which pdflatex prints nowhere (the address
list is extended locally inside the title page's author group, pos.sty:468-476); the `\onbehalf` line of a
multi-author list rides on its last author (2308.05475, 2507.06616), placing it on the block needs the block to exist
for a non-address contact (`\lx@add@contact@placed` warned "Orphaned frontmatter annotation … addresses:block"); a
paper's `\author{, on behalf of the FASER Collaboration}` (2211.04319) is a creator, as before; rmaa's Spanish abstract
is kept where the class prints it only beside an `\abstract` (`\if@abstractpresent`, :970; astro-ph0208329 gives
`\boldabstract`), and its keywords likewise; an unlabelled `\affiliation` after several authors is the last author's
only (jheppub's shared markup), where pos.sty prints it under every name (`\author{Ann Lee}\author*{Bob Kim}
\affiliation{Inst A}`; no corpus pos.sty paper has two unlabelled authors; RED
`sectioning-frontmatter/pos_sty_unlabelled_affiliation_several_authors`, a fix of the shared markup needs a jheppub
A/B); and, pre-existing, the kernel's dealing of unlabelled notes reaches jheppub's and pos.sty's `\note` given inside an
`\author` (`\author[a]{Ann Lee}\author[b]{Bob Kim\note{Deceased.}}\note{Also at CERN.}` gives Ann Lee "Deceased.",
int116a alike; pos.sty's `\author[b]{Bob Kim\note{Speaker}}\onbehalf{…}` the same). Witnesses 2409.20413, 2512.14592, 2602.22379 (pos.sty), 0903.4819,
astro-ph0208329, 1301.7157, astro-ph0105072 (rmaa). Census A/B against int116a: all 31 pos.sty and 8 rmaa papers (38
changed, all better, every creator compared: E 52 → 52, F 1 → 1 — 2504.21590's expansion-loop Fatal on both — W 93 →
93) and 345 OmniBus/aguplus/AASTeX `\altaffiltext` papers (byte-identical). Repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/{pos_sty_speaker_author_contacts, pos_sty_marked_authors, pos_sty_marked_speaker_second,
pos_sty_report_unstarred_author, rmaa_altaffiltext_marks, rmaa_altaffiltext_unmarked}`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch86b::*`.

### 905. fcs's and dgruyter's `\author*[labels]` mark the corresponding author and request its labelled affiliations (Perl: no fcs or dgruyter author binding, the authors mangled)

fcs.cls:268-290 `\DeclareDocumentCommand \author { s o m }` and dgruyter.sty:2392-2475 (authblk's
`\author[labels]{name}` under `\@ifstar`, `article` only) mark the corresponding author with the star — fcs an envelope
(:720-723), dgruyter a `*` and "*Corresponding author:" on the affiliation note — and the option lists the labels of
the `\address[n]` (fcs, :293-307) or `\affil[n]` (dgruyter) lines the name requests. The fcs binding left the kernel's
`\author[]{}` and OmniBus's label-blind `\address`; dgruyter's raw copy's redefinitions are refused (the `\author`
lock), leaving authblk's binding: either way `\author*[1]{Name}` was a creator "*" and "[1]Name" a paragraph after the
abstract (2410.08723, 1910.07269). Ours: fcs_cls.rs `\author OptionalMatch:* []{}` is
`\lx@add@authors@append[annotations={#2}]{#3}` (sn-jnl's) and, starred, a `corresponding` contact "✉" (acmart's
`\correspondingauthor`); `\address[n]{…}` an address labelled `n`. dgruyter_sty.rs loads authblk (`noblocks`) before the
copy and, under `article`, wraps its `\author` with the star: the `corresponding` contact "Corresponding author" (the
copy's `\CorrAuth`). Perl has neither binding (0 errors on the fcs repro, 5 on 2410.08723, every name mangled).

The same batch makes revtex4_support's `\affil` a guess a document's definition replaces (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1199,
1104.4073, 1907.12838, 1908.05079; aastex_cls.rs keeps it the class's under AASTeX).

Census A/B against int116a (`ab_66bundle/pop86c.tsv`, 1,249 papers: 880 AMS-derived-class or setter-redefining papers,
a 292-paper amsart sample, 53 REVTeX/AASTeX papers defining `\affil`, all 24 fcs and dgruyter papers): 23 changed, none
worse, every creator compared: the 20 fcs/dgruyter papers with the starred name, its corresponding contact and its
labelled affiliations, and the 3 REVTeX papers with the document's `\affil`; the AMS papers and the amsart sample
byte-identical; E 2,273 → 2,273, F 3 → 3.
Repros `sectioning-frontmatter/{fcs_author_star_and_address_labels, dgruyter_author_star_and_affil_labels}`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch86c::{fcs_author_star_and_address_labels, dgruyter_author_star_and_affiliation_labels}`.

### 906. The `\maketitle` replay gate does not run what `\ifx` and its kin only compare or show; the full stop closing an IEEE author block after a grade is no part of its names, and the notes after it stay the block's (Perl: the class body is never run; IEEE grades dropped)

`body_vocabulary_is_defined` (#756) refused a class title page that tests a control sequence TeX never defines:
zaa.cls:166 `\ifx\@dedication\undefined` gave "The \maketitle body was not replayed: it uses \undefined", and the
addresses only its `\maketitle` prints (`\@addresses`, :115-127, in its `\afootnote`, :190; numbered stores K11 does not
take) were lost (1902.07328: "University of Calgary" and the MSC line "Primary 34K20, secondary 34N05", which pdflatex
prints). A token TeX reads unexpanded and never runs is now not checked (`unrun_operands`, sect05.rs): `\ifx`'s two
comparands (tex.web §507, `get_next`), e-TeX's `\ifdefined`'s one (etex.ch `if_def_code`), `\string`'s and
`\meaning`'s (§470-471, `get_token`). A parameter (`#1`) is one comparand; after `\expandafter\ifx` a
`\csname…\endcsname` first comparand's name tokens are checked as any others and the token after `\endcsname` is the
second. Any other first comparand after `\expandafter\ifx` is expanded once (§367), so nothing there is skipped
(`\expandafter\ifx\Hy@pdfversion\relax`). `\noexpand`'s operand is checked as well: in an `\edef`/`\xdef` replacement
text, its main use, the operand is stored and runs when the macro is called (`\edef\x{\noexpand\Hy@SectionAnchorHref{a}}\x`).
Both bodies are refused by the gate, which names the control sequence; 86d's first round admitted them, and the
replay's error net then discarded each body after 1 error. A `\newif` switch in a skipped place is no conditional for
the dead-branch reading (`switch_is_operand`: `\ifx\if@x\undefined` keeps its branches; not after `\expandafter\ifx`),
so the skipped positions stay the body's.
`\@ifundefined{name}` and `\ifcsname` take characters and needed nothing. Both branches of an `\ifx` are still
checked: `\ifx\@foo\undefined\else…\@foo…\fi` with `\@foo` undefined stays refused (the dead-branch reading of
`\@ifundefined` admitted apa7's man-mode title page, the #265/68u dead end). A replayed body that calls the kernel's
`\maketitle` (`\let\@origmaketitle\maketitle` … `\def\maketitle{\ifx\@institute\undefined…\fi\@origmaketitle}`, the
77i probe `relax`, replayed now) runs it with `\lx@maketitle@body` empty (`title_page_replay_tokens`), as it already ran
`\@maketitle` relaxed: that nested `\maketitle` superseded the first and handed the class's keywords store on as a
`<pubnote>` beside the deposit's "Key words: lensing" — pre-existing for any such wrapper the gate admitted
(`\def\maketitle{\@origmaketitle}` gave it on the base, 501e8ba4f1).

The full stop or semicolon closing an IEEE author block right after a grade is no part of its names: IEEEtran's binding
takes it out before the block is read (`without_stop_after_grade`, ieeetran_cls.rs; only what prints no text after it,
and only such material between it and an `\IEEEmembership{…}`: spaces, `\par`, `\\`, `\vspace{…}`, `\thanks{…}`,
`\footnote{…}` and `\IEEEcompsocitemizethanks{…}` notes). `…,\\ and Farshid Alambeigi$^{1}$
\IEEEmembership{Member, IEEE}\thanks{…}.}` (2405.17600): the lone "." left once the grade and the note are set apart
made the last line no names, so its grade was dropped (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #534); in an `\IEEEauthorblockN` the line's
authors became every author's affiliation ("Charlie Zhang, , Xianbin Wang, , Jiangchuan Liu, .", 2405.10825;
2112.14209, 2409.11755, 2510.15773). Every reading of the names after it — the line test (`names_continue`), the block's
cautious split, a grade rejoining its name (`is_name_qualifier`) — took the "." for a word, so the stop is removed once
at the binding, not taught to each test: a rule in the shared `name_count` alone kept 2405.10825's names one author (an
Error), and 1810.08035's `{\em Senior Member, IEEE}.` became a creator of its own. A stop after any other text (an
affiliation's, a grade written `{\em …}`: 1810.08035, whose last line stays every author's affiliation, as before) stays.
The notes between the grade and the end of the block keep the reading the stop gave them. Where the names carry no
marks, the stop had made the last line no names and the notes the document's `<pubnote>`s. The binding now sets them on
a line of their own after a `\\`: a line of notes alone reads as no names and yields the document's notes, as
2510.15773's own `\\`-lines did. So they stay the document's: all six of 2112.14209's (with "L. Qiao, J. Zhang, Z. Gao,
and D. Zheng are with…" and the ICCC presented-in-part note), 2409.11755's one, which covers all five authors ("H. Fukada
and N. Ishikawa are with … H. Iimori, C. Pradhan, and S. Malomsoky are with Ericsson…"; pdflatex prints it as an
unmarked page-1 footnote), and 2510.15773's four (the first had followed the grade; the other three were on `\\`-lines).
Left after the grade, they went to the last author by position alone in 86d's first round: Marco Di Renzo held
2112.14209's six, Naoki Ishikawa 2409.11755's one (the HTML put a † on his name), Chau Yuen 2510.15773's first. Charter
§4 rules that out: IEEEtran journal `\thanks` print unmarked, and nothing ties them to an owner. The stop is removed only where no note changes hands by it, decided by the shared reader's own tests of a mark, three
of them: any mark on the names (`names_any`: `author_mark_position` on the block with its notes taken out, as
`llncs_cls.rs` reads its list; it sees a `\let` alias of `\textsuperscript`, a mark in a group or an `\mbox`); a mark on
the names that reads as a label (`names_labelled`: `leads_with_mark` on the names from one of those marks, the test the
notes are read by — `$^{1}$`, `\IEEEauthorrefmark{2}`, `$^{1,*}$`, not `$^{*}$`, `$^{\dag}$`, `\textsuperscript{*}`);
and a note after the grade leading with a label (`notes_marked`: `leads_with_mark` on each, `$^{1}$…`, `\up{1}…`; a
symbol such as `$^{*}$` is a note's own mark, no affiliation's). Three branches: with neither the names nor a note
marked (`!names_any && !notes_marked`), the stop goes and the notes move to their own line (above); with a label on the
names and a note marked (`names_labelled && notes_marked`), the stop goes and the notes stay in place, read by their
marks as the base reads them with the stop; only the grade is added (2405.17600, whose first marks, `$^{*1}$`, lead with a
symbol; Sarah Go's `$^{1}$` is the label; the guard's `$^{1}$` and `\let\up\textsuperscript` variants; the 86d r2 re-review's m0-m3, m5, m9, m13, the r3 re-review's
a7, a17: the same notes and affiliations as on the base). Every other block is left exactly as the base reads it, stop
and all: marks on the names alone (`Ann Able$^{*}$,… Cat Cole,~\IEEEmembership{Fellow,~IEEE}.\thanks{$^{*}$Corresponding
author.}\thanks{Manuscript received May 1.}`, the r2 re-review's m4 and n4b; the base's notes the document's, where
without the stop both went to Cat Cole), on the notes alone, and names marked only by symbols over a note led by a
number or letter (`Ann Able$^{*}$,… Cat Cole,~\IEEEmembership{Fellow,~IEEE}.\thanks{$^{*}$Corresponding
author.}\thanks{$^{1}$All authors are with X.}`, the r3 re-review's a9, a12: read as both-marked, the correspondence
note went to Cat Cole and the numbered note became a creator with no name; a test that took a symbol for a mark on the

as no mark and moved marked notes to a line of their own, so they lost their authors (the re-review's B1). Two

`author_ieee_correspondence_note_of_a_non_last_author`, the observer's S2c item, a reader change for its single home).
A note after a `\\` that already
follows the grade is on such a line already. `[journal,compsoc]`'s
`…Fellow,~IEEE}.\IEEEcompsocitemizethanks{\IEEEcompsocthanksitem A. Able is with X.}` keeps Cat Cole (the 86d review's
probe; it had lost her, base alike), the note the document's. Notes after a grade with no stop keep the pre-existing
reading: they go to the last author by position (`…Cat Cole,~\IEEEmembership{Fellow,~IEEE}\thanks{A. Able is with
X.}\thanks{Manuscript received May 1.}}`, both Cat Cole's). Perl does the same: on
`author_ieee_membership_after_closing_stop` it puts the `\thanks` inside Alambeigi's creator. That reading waits for a
ruling; an upper bound of 322 of the 1,801 `ieee86d` papers have a `\thanks` right after an `\IEEEmembership`.
Residual (RED `sectioning-frontmatter/author_ieee_membership_mark_before_closing_stop`, 0 of 1,801 by regex): a mark
between the grade and the stop (`…Fellow,~IEEE}$^{*}$.\thanks{…}`) is not looked past, so the last line stays every
author's affiliation.

### 908. ijcai's `\emails` section is a class's address list, placed by spelling, else author order, else the block; cas's `\address[label]` keeps its label (Perl: the n-th piece of a comma split on the n-th author; the label dropped)

ijcai19.sty:127-130 (every year's style, and ijcai97.sty's derivatives: ttm.sty) prints the `\emails` section of the one
`\author{…}` under the affiliations, attributing none: `{faraztrb, pstone}@cs.utexas.edu, garrett.a.warnell.civ@mail.mil`.
Perl's ijcai.sty.ltxml:50-53 splits it at every comma and gives the n-th piece to the n-th author (`\lx@ijcai@email` =
`\lx@add@email[labelseq=author]`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1200): a grouped address was cut into `{faraztrb` and
`pstone}@cs.utexas.edu`, and every piece after it went one author on (1905.13566: Warnell's address on Peter Stone;
2308.08563: `zhangmengdi02@` on Enhong Chen; 2105.02711: `$^3$fenglong@` on Jimeng Sun; 2401.03955's ttm.sty
`\{creddy,wmgifford,jayant\}@us.ibm.com`) — ownership by bare position, which FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 forbids. The section is
now a class's address list, as jheppub's `\emailAdd` is (#805), fixed once in the engine's `\lx@ijcai@*` machinery
(author_macros.rs), so the ijcai binding's `\author` and a raw derivative's `\lx@add@authors` marker branch (dispatch.rs)
share it: one call of the list (`\lx@sequence@call`), each address `\lx@add@contact@placed[role=email,owner=sequence]`
through `\lx@split@addresses`. Each address goes to the author it spells, else to the n-th author while the list is one
address per author in their order (Perl's answer where it is evidence), else stays on the author block, or — the one
address left there — goes to the one author a note marks as the corresponding author (`sequenced_contact_labels`; the
observer's `owner=sequence` path reads the same). A grouped address of plain text is written out, one address each, as an
author block's line gives it (`email_addresses`): `faraztrb@cs.utexas.edu` on Faraz Torabi, `pstone@cs.utexas.edu` on
Peter Stone; its underscore is `\_`, as `address_tokens` writes it (a bare `_` printed the OT1 dot accent: `scs˙lzg@` for
2304.11989's `\{scs$\_$lzg, …\}@tju.edu.cn`, in every binding's list). The section is read line by line
(`ijcai_email_lines`): a `\\` (with its `*` and `[skip]`), a `\newline` and a further `\emails` start a line of the
class's title block, so an address after one is an address of its own (2002.11711's
`1871161@stu.neu.edu.cn\\zelei.liu@ntu.edu.sg`, now Shuangfeng Zhang's and Zelei Liu's by their places); a break inside a
group, TeX's or a printed one (`\{aable, bbaker,\\ ccole\}@x.edu`, `\lbrace … \rbrace`, `\textbraceleft …
\textbraceright`), parts no line, and the group's three addresses are written out (`\lx@split@addresses` writes out a
group in any of the three). A line with no address (2609.15094's second `\emails`, `{$^{*}$Corresponding author}`,
under the two starred names of Qiang Xie and Tao Li) is no place of the list and no e-mail: a note (`role=note`, as
jheppub's `\note` files its "Corresponding author."), placed by its own evidence, else the block's — where it lost no
person, so it is no orphan warned about (relocate.rs `shared_orphan`: a note labelled `addresses:block`); filed as an
e-mail it rendered "Email: mailto:Corresponding%20author". The ijcai binding
declares its conventions (`ijcai_sty::FRONTMATTER_CONVENTIONS`, `email_owner: SpelledElseOrder`, #837). Perl's
`\lx@clear@frontmatter` of the queued e-mails before the list is kept.

Residuals, each the existing helpers' reading: a list whose groups carry the affiliation marks
(`$^1$\{chaoqiy2, jimeng\}@illinois.edu, $^2$…`, 2105.02711) is no plain list of addresses and stays whole on the author
block, the printed line — deferred: `email_addresses` reading a leading `$^n$`/`\textsuperscript{n}` as a mark would
place all five addresses by their spelling, but drops the printed mark from the contact, which needs a charter ruling; 2308.08563's
`wulk@` (Likang Wu: "Wu" and his initials) spells no one, and its list, the group written out, lists Enhong Chen before
Mengdi Zhang, so it is in no author order and the address stays on the block (Likang Wu's before by its place only); a
group in markup the split does not write out (`\texttt{\{aable, ccole\}@x.edu}`; 2501.02356's TeX-braced
`{pablo.barcelo, roberto.cominetti, mat.mw} @uc.cl`) is one contact, which the spelling gives to the one author it
scores highest — routed to the e-mail spelling code (email_owners.rs, 88a's area): a contact holding two or more local
parts spells no single author; 2304.11989's `scs_lzg@` (Zhigang Li's initials) and 2505.12894's `ericcan@` are each the
one address left on the block and go to the author the corresponding-author step finds (`marked_corresponding_author`:
Jianye Hao's `\thanks{Corresponding author}`, Peican Zhu's `\thanks{Corresponding authors.}`), not to their owners — the
step is a user ruling (jheppub and iopart use it too), kept; two narrower refinements are the user's to choose: skip a
marked author who already owns an address of the same list (Jianye Hao has `sjianye.hao@`, so `scs_lzg@` stays on the
block), and let no plural legend ("Corresponding authors.") mark one author (2505.12894, where Tang and Wang carry the
`*`). The single unmarked `\affiliations` line still goes to the first author only (Perl's
`\lx@add@affiliations[labelseq=author]`), where ijcai prints it under every name — a follow-up batch reusing
`\lx@add@affiliation@shared` (author_macros.rs, aistats's line under a row of names).

cas-common.sty:1216 `\NewDocumentCommand \address { O{} m O{} }` files the address in the list `\affiliation` files into
(`g_stm_aff<n>_seq`), labelled as it labels (`\textsuperscript{\itshape\@currentlabel}` from `#1`, a letter label
`\stmLabel`led, :1222-1242); its text is printed as written. The cas binding (cas_dc_cls.rs, Rust-only; Perl has none)
left `\address` to OmniBus's `\address[]{}` (Perl OmniBus.cls.ltxml:91, `\lx@add@address{#2}`), which dropped the label:
`\author[1]{O. U. Salman}[orcid=…]\author[2]{L. Truskinovsky}[]\address[1]{LSPM…}\address[2]{PMMH…}` gave both
addresses to Truskinovsky (2011.00505; without the ORCID the positional reading hid it). `\address[]{}[]` is now
`\lx@add@contact[label=…,role=affiliation]{#2}`, the path of `\affiliation`: the role moves from OmniBus's
`role=address` to `role=affiliation`, as cas files both commands in one list (the HTML is unchanged, no CSS rule reads
either role and the schema takes both; the TEI output changes, LaTeXML-tei.xsl:189 `address` vs :193 `affiliation`).
The trailing optional of both commands — the `stm/address` keys `foot`, `type`, `name` (:1178-1190) — is typeset
nowhere, where it was text ("[foot=true]"). Every entry is labelled by the letter cas prints for it, by the class's own
entry counter (`\g_stm_aff_int`, :1175, global, never reset, shared by both commands; `cas_labelled_entry`): a label
opening with a letter steps the counter and prints its letter, which the label then stands for (`\int_gincr:N`,
`\stmLabel`, :1230-1236); a number N sets the counter and prints the N-th letter (`\int_gset:Nn`, :1238-1242); an entry
the `foot` key sets as a footnote (`__foot_address`/`__foot_affiliation`, :1294-1373) leaves the counter and labels
nothing, printed under the N-th letter or, lettered, under the letter the last main entry printed (`\@currentlabel`,
read at the flush, `\lx@label@ref{cas@current}`). An author's marks are read as cas reads them (`cas_mark_labels`,
:907-914): a list opening with a letter as labels, each the letter its entry prints (`\processAffRef`/`\stmRef`,
:197-201, :278-286, which cas reads from the run before's `.aux`: the letter, when the entry came first, else a
deferred reference; nothing for a label no entry has, where cas prints "0"), any other as numbers, N the N-th
letter (`\processAffNum`, :288-296). So `\author[1,2]{…}` under `\address[a]{…}\address[b]{…}` requests both, as it
prints "a,b" (2207.12381, where the addresses went to the last author on the base); `\address[b]{Univ X}
\address[a]{Univ Y}` prints "a Univ X", "b Univ Y", Univ X `\author[1]`'s; word labels `\address[aff2]{X}
\address[aff1]{Y}` print "a", "b", so `\author[1]` and `\author[aff2]` both have X; and `\address[1]{X}
\affiliation[a]{…}` prints "a X", "b …", which `\author[a]` and `\author[2]` request. An item cas cannot read so (a `*`
among letters, a template's `<num>` among numbers) is kept as written, and a label that is no number and opens with no
letter (`*`, `1a`, an `\int_gset:Nn` error in cas) keeps its text and leaves the counter.

A deferred label is a generalized mechanism, not a cas one: `\lx@label@ref{<key>}` (frontmatter_api.rs) stands for the
label a binding records for `key` once later input is read (`set_label_ref`, one state table any binding fills; cas
fills `cas:<label>` and `cas@current` from its entry counter), and expands to it where the queued entry is digested, at
the flush. The flush's readers of the queued keyvals before the digestion read the same text (`resolve_label_refs`,
label_refs.rs): `digest_front_matter` resolves the queue's attribute maps (`place.rs`'s `author_labels`, legends and
`sequenced_contact_labels`), and the observer's flush (`shadow_flush`) the ledger's block keyvals and API attributes
(`blocks.rs`'s requests, the resolver's labelled-author test, `api.rs`), so the dump holds the letters and an offline
re-resolve reads them too. On r2 the readers saw the raw reference as single-character requests and the shadow
misread every letter-labelled author whose entry came after it (2303.00352, 2603.22658: every affiliation gone;
2504.19452, 2509.10496: every author every one); the written XML, which expands the macro, was right. A binding
filling the table from an `.aux` round trip copies its own redefinition rule: cas's `\NewLabel` (cas-common.sty:191-195)
defines `X@<label>:` globally only when it is free and locally otherwise, and LaTeX reads the `.aux` inside a group
(latex.ltx:9486-9490), so the first entry under a label keeps it (`set_label_ref_once` for `cas:<label>`;
`cas@current`, `\@currentlabel`, stays last-wins, `set_label_ref`). `\affiliation[a]{X}\author[a]{Ann}
\affiliation[a]{Y}\author[a]{Bob}` and the same with both entries after the authors print "Ann^a, Bob^a" with X under
"a" and Y under "b": both authors have X, Y is the block's, whether the letter was written when Bob's `\author` was
read or deferred; r3 took the last entry (Bob Y in the first shape, both Y in the second). In cas,
`place.rs`'s corresponding-author step is reached by no shape: the binding queues no `owner=sequence` contact, and its
`\cormark` marks no one, so `\cortext` stays a note of the title block. `\corref{label}` (cas-common.sty:224, a
mandatory argument) prints nothing; the binding's `\corref[]` took none and left the label typeset after the name or
as a paragraph (2303.00352 "Enrique García-Macíascor1", 2104.06505, 2308.04522, 2412.03617, 2206.03104 `<p>c</p>`:
every cas paper of the census writing `\corref{`). The `\corref`/`\cormark`/`\cortext` and `\fnmark`/`\fntext` links
(cas-common.sty:204-238, :556-623) are not built.

Repros `class-bindings/{ijcai_emails_grouped_address_by_spelling, ijcai_binding_emails_in_author_order,
ijcai_emails_out_of_order_stay_on_the_block, ijcai_emails_lines_and_sections, ijcai_emails_group_broken_over_lines,
cas_address_label_keeps_its_author, cas_dc_address_letter_labels_and_keys, cas_numeric_marks_name_letter_entries,
cas_letter_entries_print_by_the_counter, cas_word_labels_out_of_order, cas_mixed_number_and_letter_entries,
cas_dc_letter_marks_before_their_entries, cas_corresponding_mark_on_a_deferred_label,
cas_first_entry_under_a_label_keeps_it, cas_first_entry_under_a_deferred_label_keeps_it, cas_corref_label_is_no_text}`;
guards
`perfect_kernel_batch88b::*` (eager, the binary's eager and `--streaming` builds the same;
`cas_deferred_labels_are_read_before_digestion` the shadow's reading as well;
`ijcai_binding_email_list_in_author_order_keeps_perl_order` a no-regression check, the base gives the same),
`06_cluster_frontmatter::frontmatter_ijcai_affiliations_emails` (the ttm.sty group on its three authors).

### 910. A symbol-font argument is read expanded, and a symbol its font cannot decode, declared at its fontmath.ltx or amssymb slot, is the token LaTeXML's own binding makes of the name (Perl: the name read as written, the symbols dropped)

latex.ltx reads the symbol-font name through `\csname sym#3\endcsname` (`\DeclareMathSymbol` :13480,
`\DeclareMathAccent` :13430, `\DeclareSymbolFontAlphabet@` :13725) and `\DeclareSymbolFont` builds
`\csname sym#1\endcsname` and `\csname#2/#3/#4/#5\endcsname` (:13138): each argument is expanded. Perl reads them as
written (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2645, :2664, :2671, :2697-2699 `ToString($fontkind)`; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1201).
mathdesign declares `\DeclareSymbolFont{\MD@greek@family upright}{OML}{\MD@greek@family}{m}{n}` (mdbch.sty:157) and
its Greek in `{\MD@greek@family}`/`{\MD@greek@family upright}` (:261, :291, :330; `\MD@greek@family` is `letters`,
mathdesign.sty:135): the name found no declaration and was taken for the encoding, which has no map, so every Greek
letter came out U+FFFD or an ASCII stand-in (Ω a newline, ω `!`; OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #27) — 703 tokens on
1808.08390, 1910.04228 and 1108.1913. Ours (sect08.rs): `\DeclareMathSymbol`'s font, `\DeclareMathAccent`'s font,
`\DeclareSymbolFont`'s name, family, series and shape (the encoding stays `ExpandedPartially`, as Perl) and
`\DeclareSymbolFontAlphabet`'s name are read `Expanded`, each space token a space (`nfss_name`): a space token keeps
the line end it came from as its text, so 1501.05180's `\DeclareSymbolFont{latex-font⏎msa}` was another font than its
`\DeclareMathSymbol\onto\mathrel{latex-font msa}{"10}` (U+FFFD, now ↠). A series or shape given by a macro is the one
latex.ltx selects (`\mddefault`, `\updefault`: mathtext.sty:103, euler.sty:225): an OML font declared with shape
`{\itdefault}` records `it` and is a math italic font (`math_italic`, its letters italic as their class says;
`Font::specialize_letters`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1147).
(`\DeclareSymbolFontAlphabet` looks up `fontdeclarations@`, plural, as Perl's pool:2673 does, so it finds no font
either way; left as it is.)

A math-font package that redeclares a symbol font as `U` (or `LMS`, `MDA`…) has no map for it (#645): its symbols stayed
undecoded. When the declared font decodes nothing, `\DeclareMathSymbol` now looks the symbol up in the reference slots —
every `\DeclareMathSymbol` of fontmath.ltx (254) and the small variant of its control-sequence `\DeclareMathDelimiter`s
(26, `\|` among them), and those of amsfonts.sty and amssymb.sty (219), with the encoding of the font they name
(`operators` OT1, `letters` OML, `symbols` OMS, `largesymbols` OMX, `AMSa`/`AMSb` msam/msbm). Declared at its reference
slot, the symbol is the token LaTeXML's own kernel/amssymb binding makes of the name: its glyph, and the role, meaning,
`name` and stretchiness the binding gives (a binding's `UNKNOWN`, no role at all, leaves the class's role) — so a paper
using kpfonts gets the symbols a paper without it gets (`reference_symbol`/`reference_glyph`, sect08.rs). `\Cap` is ⋒
ADDOP `double-intersection`, `\mid` ∣ VERTBAR, `\lgroup` ⟮ OPEN `stretchy="false"`, `\jmath` ȷ, `\uplus` ⊎, `\perp` ⟂,
`\setminus` ∖ — where the reference fonts' fontmap entries give a slot glyph (`|`, the OMX extensible piece ⎩, the plain
⊥ ◁ ⊔ `\`) or a Perl-origin slot error (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1202). The table `reference_math_slots.rs` is static and
generated by `tools/perfect_kernel/gen_reference_math_slots.py`: the slots from TL 2025's fontmath.ltx 2025/06/05 v3.0l
and amsfonts/amssymb 2013/01/14 v3.01 (the Computer Modern and AMS layouts, unchanged since LaTeX2e; a conversion should
not parse kernel files to look up fixed layouts), each binding's token captured by converting the generator's own
document (every name typeset, amssymb loaded) with `--nomathparse`; the header names the binary. A name no binding
defines — fontmath.ltx's `\varbigtriangleup`/`\varbigtriangledown`, whose `\mathchardef` LaTeXML keeps raw — falls back
to the reference font's map, as do `,` `.` `;` (set as text by the capture).

A package that puts a kernel or AMS name at the reference slot of its own font draws the reference glyph there:
kpfonts' `\Delta`/`\Omega` in `U/jkpmia` at 1 and 10 (fontmath.ltx:205/214 `operators`; kpfonts.sty:679-681 `\let`s
the name away before redeclaring it, so its old meaning is gone), `\leqslant`, `\Cap`/`\Cup` in an `AMSa` redeclared as
`U/jkpsya` (kpfonts.sty:498, :831/:833; amssymb.sty:101, :144/:146; txfonts and pxfonts likewise), eulerpx's `\jmath`
in `U/zeur` at 124 (eulerpx.sty:276), raw newtxsf's `\lfloor`, `\mid` and `\lgroup` in `LMS/ntxsy`/`LMX/ntxexx`
(newtxsf.sty:95/:150, :242/:261; fontmath.ltx:499 — newtxmath and newpxmath are bound and run none of this). Witnesses
1604.04618, 2008.13643 (kpfonts), 2506.22450 (newtxsf through wiley-article.cls:130), 2501.18458 (eulerpx). The
exception is arev: its bold `mathdesignA` (`mdbchbma`) draws ∟ at `\nless`'s slot 04 and lacks 0x24, 0x26 and 0x36
(pdflatex logs "Missing character"); we print what the author named (≮). Another slot is another glyph and stays
undecoded: a variant swap (`\epsilon` at "22, where fontmath.ltx has `\varepsilon`), and jkpsyb's and txsyb's
`\precapprox`/`\succapprox` at 118/119 (kpfonts.sty, txfonts.sty), where msbm has them the other way round (checked by
rendering) — so the symbol-font name alone (`AMSa`) is no slot contract, and a name no reference declares in an
`AMSa`/`AMSb` font stays undecoded too. A name no reference declares (shuffle's `\shuffle`, stmaryrd's `\boxslash`,
#645; kpfonts' `\neq` in `U/jkpsyc` at 44) stays undecoded too: U+FFFD, with its font's one Warning (#27). A font with a map decodes through it, not the binding (oz.sty's
`U/msa` `\Cap` ⋒ BINOP through `U_msa`), and at a slot its map records as a gap of the font (`U/eur`'s 17, `U/msb`'s
5, generated by tftopl; pdflatex "Missing character") a kernel or AMS name is U+FFFD with the font's Warning too
(`\star` at eur "3F, `\Cap` at `AMSb` "65; 89c, #27); the maps' other empty slots are glyphs with no single
character, which the reference still decodes (msbm's negated pairs, msam's `\dabar@`). The match is slot-matched in
the name and the slot, not the font (`\Cap` at `AMSb` "65 matches amssymb's `AMSa` "65), so the match alone cannot
see a font's gap: the gap record defeats the match at that slot. `\DeclareMathAccent`, undecoded in a declared font with no font map, takes the
binding's token by the name alone, at any slot (89c, #27: an accent's name is its meaning; newtxsf uses other slots,
and mdsymbol's `largesymbols` would — rendered; not reached while `\SetSymbolFont{…}{normal}` is unmodelled). The two
triggers differ because the evidence differs: an equal slot is layout evidence, which holds in a mapped font and is
defeated only at a recorded gap; a name at any slot is not, so the accent rule is confined to fonts with no map, where
an empty slot of a mapped font names nothing the map vouches for. Perl drops all these symbols. The
binding's limits placement (its `scriptpos`/`mathstyle` closures) is not carried: a kernel `\mathop` redeclared this
way (`\sum`, `\bigcup` at their largesymbols slots) sets its display limits as scripts, where the kernel's token sets
them under and over (repro fonts-nfss/redeclared_mathop_takes_display_limits, RED; no corpus witness, the packages use
their own `\sumop`), and carrying it needs a display capture or a role-based rule.

Repros fonts-nfss/{symbol_font_name_expands, u_font_kernel_slot_and_ams_names, font_package_symbols_are_the_bindings,
ams_font_slots_decode_as_msam_msbm_draw, kernel_name_at_another_slot_stays_undecoded}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch89a::{symbol_font_name_expands, kernel_and_ams_names_at_their_reference_slots,
font_packages_get_the_bindings_symbols, ams_font_slots_decode_as_the_fonts_draw,
kernel_name_at_another_slot_stays_undecoded}` (the first two also on the binary, eager and `--streaming`),
`perfect_kernel_batch68v::batch68v_u_symbol_font_without_a_map_stays_undecoded`.
### 911. Whether a formula in a name or an affiliation is a mark is read from its digested XMath, one reader for the observer's writer, the comparator, the marks a name shows and the merged-name check (Perl: no such reading; its frontmatter labels are the operand's ToString)

Frontmatter refactor stage 1 (`FRONTMATTER_DIGESTED_REFACTOR.md`; user directive 2026-10-29: decisions on the digested
representation, never TeX spelling). Four readers decided a formula's mark-ness by re-parsing its `tex` attribute: the
observer writer's view of today's frontmatter (`writer/dom.rs` `math_mark_text`, `spacing_group`, `math_base`), its
diverged copy in `ab_audit fmshadow` (`fmshadow/mod.rs`), the marks a name shows (`relocate.rs` `shown_marks`:
`past_mark_spacing` over MARK_SPACING, `{}`, then `^`), and the merged-name check (`name_text.rs` `is_name_mark`: `tex`
opening `{}^`/`^`). A spelling the prefix tests did not list was no mark: `$\rm ^a$` (tex `\rm{}^{a}`, 2105.07958's
`\address{$\rm ^a$Email: …}`), `${^2}$` on a name (2002.12524's `Po-Hao Chou${^2}$`, 2006.00536's `Radoslaw
Ryblewski${^1}$`), `${\rm ^a}$`; and a spelling that printed more was one (`{}^{3}He` started with a mark).

One reader, `observer::marks::read_formula` (re-exported `fm_read_formula`, `FmFormulaMarks`, generic over
`FmMathNode`: the engine's libxml node, and a roxmltree newtype in `ab_audit`), reads the XMath in both vocabularies:
as digested (the writer, `shown_marks` and `is_name_mark` all run before `finish_document`'s rewrite and math parse,
`core_interface.rs:632,654`) — `XMApp[@role]` `FLOATSUPERSCRIPT`/`POSTSUPERSCRIPT` (and the subscripts) holding
`XMArg[@rule]`, flat `XMTok`/`XMText`/`XMHint` siblings, chosen at digestion (`tex_math.rs` `script_handler`) — and as
parsed (the comparator reads the final XML) — `XMApp(XMTok[@role='SUPERSCRIPTOP'][@scriptpos], base, script)`, `preN`
printing the script before its base, `postN` after it; a surviving `FLOATSUPERSCRIPT` with its script unwrapped;
`XMDual` by its presentation (the last child) and `XMWrap` flattened. An application is read through only when
LaTeXML lays it out as a row (`marks::row_layout`, by the operator's role and meaning as Perl `Post/MathML.pm`'s
`lookupPresenter`, L205, picks the presenter; in both vocabularies): an infix role (`pmml_infix`, L1540, L1600-1622,
L1699-1700, L1739: the operator between its arguments), `POSTFIX` (L1632, after), any operator without a layout of
its own (`Apply:?:?`, L1523, before; `formulae`, `multirelation` alike), a script before or after its base (`pmml_script`); and then only when it holds a
script, in print order (`marks::printed_children`), an operator that prints nothing (U+2061–U+2064) none: the parser
nests a script on a word's last letter under the word's invisible times (`$Ann^{1}$` as `⁢(A, n, n¹)`,
`$\mathrm{Ann~Able}^{1}$`, `$Smith-Jones^1$` under its minus), and read so it is the digested shape's `OnBase "Ann"`
(review 90a r2 F1). Any other application is one printed item, its text in document order: one holding no script
(an accented letter, `$^{1}\mathrm{\acute{e}}$`, a letter), and every two-dimensional layout (review 90a r3 F1) — a
fraction (`Apply:FRACOP:?` → `mfrac`, L1609; `\frac`, `\tfrac`, `\binom`), a root by its meaning
(`square-root`/`nth-root` → `msqrt`/`mroot`, L1636-1645), a continued fraction (L1954's display `mfrac`), an accent
(`Apply:OVERACCENT:?`/`UNDERACCENT:?` → `mover`/`munder`, L1489-1505; `\hat`, `\overline`, `\overset`), an
enclosure (`Apply:ENCLOSE:?`, L1507, and any node carrying `enclose`, L338-342: `\boxed`, digested an
`XMArg[@enclose]`, amsmath.sty.ltxml:893-895), a big operator with its body (which Perl rows, `pmml_summation`'s `mrow`, L1796-1798, as it rows an inline `cfrac-inline` — read as one item here on the safe side, with no output change on any probe), and a script
set over or under its base (`scriptpos` `mid`, `munder`/`mover`: limits, `\stackrel`; a digested `mid` script is
ink). So a script under a fraction's bar or a root's sign is no script a formula ends on: `$\frac{a}{b^{1}}$` ending
an address line is the line's text, not `OnBase "ab"` (a reading through every application holding a script made it
one, the writer dropped the "1" from the line's key and declined it). A formula is a **mark** (`Marks`, each
superscript's printed text before the first letter or digit) when it opens with scripts nothing visible precedes
(floating, or after a box that prints nothing: `$\mbox{ }^1$`, cond-mat0206265, digested `POSTSUPERSCRIPT`), at least
one a superscript, and the first item printed after them is no letter or digit (our criterion, not the parser's:
the parser attaches a prescript, `scriptpos="pre"`, to whatever follows, a `)` as readily as a word): font switches are a token's font, spacing an `XMHint`
(`$^{1}\hspace{1mm}$`, review 88c r4 h2; a name's `{}^{1}\quad`, `author_block/rows.rs:685`), punctuation and symbols
no base (`$^{a})$`, cond-mat9808038; `$^{1}{}^{,}$`; `$^{1,2}\dagger$`, 2501.04244; `$^1,2$`, 1912.02075's
`A.P.~Orlov$^1,2$`, its marks the 1). Only the item right after the scripts counts: a reading that took any letter or
digit anywhere after the script as ink (88c's) made `^1,2` no mark, Orlov showed no mark and lost both affiliations. Scripts after printed ink are **on a base** (`OnBase`: `$97403^{1}$`, 2203.01892; `Ul. Ainy $299^A$`,
0707.4047; `$\text{Leon Bello}^{1,3}$`, 2011.08099), the base with its subscripts the item's text when it is a text box or a word or a
number (`$G_2'$`, 2208.14409's keyword "G₂′", keeps its 2), in a name and an affiliation alike (the writer's affiliation-only `math_base` and the comparator's
`affiliation_text` are one reading now). Scripts right before a letter or digit (an isotope, `{\rm ^{3}He}`, 88c r1 q24;
`${}^{\dagger}X$`) are a prescript on a printed word, **neither**: the formula's text kept as printed — the structural fail-safe for what
digestion cannot settle; the writer's and the comparator's text of it both in print order ("3He", not the parsed
document order "He3": both walks take `printed_children`). A mark formula of one or two lowercase letters glued to letters on both sides is the word's,
as an `ltx:sup` of it is (`glued_in_a_word`; `I. M. M$^{\rm c}$Hardy`, 2003.01448; `M\textsuperscript{c}Kernan`,
math0610203): the writer had dropped it as a mark while the comparator, seeing the rewritten `ltx:sup`, kept it.
`shown_marks` splits a mark's printed text into its letter or number marks (`relocate::printed_marks`, the item rule
of `script_marks` without the spelling's switches). Deleted: both `math_mark_text` copies, `spacing_group`, both
`math_base` copies, `past_mark_spacing`, `is_name_mark`'s prefix test. Kept for the callers that have only tokens
(stages 3–5): MARK_SWITCHES[32] and MARK_SPACING[4] through `script_marks`/`past_mark_switches` (the
`\lx@frontmatter@sup` label keys, `author_macros.rs`; revtex's group rule, `content_marks`/`group_shares_the_mark`),
and `notes::leads_with_mark`.

Measured on the committed code (pop90a: pop88c5's 10,389 written-family rows plus 3,000 random popint118a rows, seed
90; 13,352 papers). A/B `results_r90a4.tsv` (int118a → 90a): 14 changed, none worse, E 14,975 → 14,972, F 29 → 28
(2006.14721's B side killed at 210 s with no Fatal line; alone both give F 1), words 193,938,335 → 193,938,172; 12
better — 2105.07958 (the e-mail address Sorée's alone), 1410.8534, 1804.10344, 1810.00507, astro-ph9807043 (declined →
written, each author the affiliations of their own marks), 2002.12524, 2006.00536 (a name's `${^2}$`/`${^1}$` now
shows its mark, the author gains the affiliation), 1703.09552, 1808.04425, 2111.06000 (`$^{\hspace{0.3mm}1,2}$`),
1904.05642 (`$^{\left(1,2\right)}$`), 1002.3515 (an author's affiliations in mark order) — and 2 noise (1111.1264's
known memory abort, 2006.14721). Shadow census (`LATEXML_FM_SHADOW=1`, pop90a, int118a → 90a): same 9,049 → 9,059,
written 341 → 343, declined 141 → 131 ("the creators' names" 71 → 64, Affiliation 31 → 29), no writer 3,817 → 3,816;
19 outcomes changed, all better or neutral (the witnesses above; 0807.4407, 1309.7542, cond-mat0206329,
cond-mat0407580 names now agree; 1904.02582 `same` → `written`, its XML unchanged; cond-mat0206265 keeps int118a's
reason) bar 4 load-noise rows (1901.00143, 2101.04154, 2203.01615, 2211.11776: a timeout or no dump on one side).
`ab_audit fmshadow` on the census trees: the new comparator on int118a's tree classifies every paper as the old one
but hep-ph9805510 (`$^(c)$`, only the "(" raised: 3 of its 6 unclassified disagreements now classified); on the new
tree 7 papers go disagree → agree (the written witnesses); TOTAL unclassified 281 → 281. The print order through
rows and the two-dimensional layouts as one item (reviews 90a r2 F1, r3 F1), measured on the final code: A/B
`results_r90a6.tsv` (int118a → 90a, same population) changes the same 12 papers, better, none worse, E 14,971 →

as on int118a; AFs11, AFs14, AFs20, x05, x25, prescripts on `\alpha`, `\ell`, an accented letter and `He` read in
print order) and AFf19/RFf19 agree; 7 `\frac`/`\tfrac`/`\sqrt`/`\sqrt[3]`/`\boxed` address lines (AFg10, AFf07,
AFf08, AFg01, AFg02, AFg06, AFg09) are cut at their marks as on int118a; and the two names that end on a root over
a script (ANh01 `Ann Able$\sqrt{x^1}$`, RSh01 `Ann $\sqrt{Able^1}$`) are read, as on int118a, as names with no mark
(the reading through the root had made the root's script a name mark). The 44 reach and witness papers convert as

Residuals, each another stage's: the writer's cut reads tokens (`writer::plan`; stage 3): `${^{3}He}$` and

### 912. just.cls (Chinese Physics C's cpc-hepnp.cls under the PhiPsi15 name) has a binding: its `\email` is the author's e-mail and its `\address` after `\maketitle` the names' affiliations; cpc-hepnp itself waits for 91c (Perl: no binding; through OmniBus the list is one address of the last author)

cpc-hepnp.cls, the Chinese Physics C template (`\ProvidesClass{cpc-hepnp}`, :11; not in TeX Live), is shipped by
every paper that uses it, under its own name (`\documentclass{cpc-hepnp}`, 611 papers 2008-2026: 1101.0224,
0904.1329, 1002.4139, 0908.0848, 1401.5029) or as just.cls (the 12 PhiPsi15 proceedings papers, each a byte-identical
copy). Both are read raw. Its `\author` is the article kernel's, and its frontmatter commands print outside the
kernel's frontmatter. `\email{x}` (:100-105) appends "n) E-mail: x" to `\@thanks`, an unnumbered footnote set after
the names by the class's `\maketitle` (:124-155), which the kernel's locked `\maketitle` never sets: the e-mail is
lost with 0 errors. `\address{…}` (:173-181) prints its argument centred where it is called, after `\maketitle` in the
template, below the whole name block: a list of lines led by the marks the names carry (`$^1$ Budker Institute …\\ $^2$
Novosibirsk State University …`), or one address with no mark. It becomes a body paragraph after the names, so no
creator holds an affiliation (1603.03230: 0 of 55 right in the frontmatter scorer's archival tier).

Ours: `cpc_hepnp_cls.rs`, registered as `just` only (lib.rs), reads the paper's copy raw (`RawRead`, `shipped: true`;
the copy's name chosen as it loads, `just` or the class's own; without a copy, OmniBus and the missing-file Warning, as
before; `just.cls` listed among the author-file stand-ins, `binding/author_files.rs`, so `\IfFileExists{just.cls}`
finds it only when shipped) and redefines the class's own setters after the read, each into the frontmatter API with
no new reading of tokens, and each only where the copy defines it (the 23 variants of the census copies share
one-argument `\email` and `\address`; the 2009-13 copies have no `\emails`). `\email` and `\emails` (:107-109, the
same footnote set where it is called) become `\lx@add@email[name={E-mail:~}]`, the e-mail of the author whose line
holds it, under the class's label. `\address` becomes `\lx@add@affiliation@marked[annotate=all]`, the marked list
iopart's `\address` and informs4's `\AFF` read: each mark-led line is an affiliation of the names that request its
mark, and an address with no mark is one affiliation of every name above it (`annotate=all`, as llncs's sole
`\institute` is every author's: 1511.03783's one name; 1101.0224's six and 0904.1329's two under the cpc-hepnp name).
The address arriving after the frontmatter was placed takes the late path under `--streaming`, and the result is
identical to the eager build. 1603.03230: 54 of 55 creators exactly right in the scorer's archival tier (0 before),
and its e-mail is no longer a lost piece. Witnesses 1603.03230, 1510.03577, 1510.07251, 1511.03783, 1511.03934,
1511.05708, 1511.08514, 1511.09253, 1511.09434, 1512.00162. The `{keyword}` and `{pacs}` lists stay the class's (body
lists with their "Key words:"/"PACS:" labels, as before).

`\emails` inside `\author` is kept as that author's e-mail, though pdflatex loses it there (a `\footnotetext` in the
title tabular is an insert in an inner box, never set); after `\maketitle`, where it prints at the page foot, it is the
e-mail of the name above it. No census paper calls `\emails`.

**Why `cpc-hepnp` is not registered.** Routed through the same setters, the 611 cpc-hepnp papers gained e-mails (562
of the 623) and affiliations (585), but about 90 of them gained affiliations on names that do not request them, where
the base had none, which the user's condition for routing (nothing worse) excludes:
- **An e-mail mark after a comma is read as a label** (`$^{1,4,3)}$`, the `n)` mark of the name's e-mail footnote,
  :104 `\arabic{email})`): 41 papers. The `n)` names line n — 2105.14997's Shudong Wang (`1,4,3)`) holds College of
  Physics, Jilin University, where pdflatex shows `3)` is his e-mail mark; 1410.4949's `3,4)` (a typo for 3,4) comes
  out right by chance.
- **A typed-number list** (`1~(Institute …)\\ 2~(…)`, the 2009-13 template: 50 papers; 21 more unmarked multi-line
  lists) has no mark the marked list reads, so it is one address with no mark, every name's: each name holds the whole
  list (0906.3801: 11 names, 8 lines; 1001.2445: 80 names).
- **A marked list inside a font group** (`\address{(BESIII Collaboration)\\ \it{$^{1}$ …\\ $^{2}$ …}}`, 6 papers) is
  read as one entry, labelled by its first mark: 1709.03653's 156 names marked 1 each hold the whole list, the others
  none (XML 0.43 → 1.78 MB). The marked-list reader does not enter a group.
A `\documentclass{cpc-hepnp}` paper converts as before (byte-identical to int119a); the no-change guard pins it.

A/B of the 623 papers whose main file asks for `cpc-hepnp` (611) or `just` (12), against int119a, with
`--preload=ar5iv.sty` as the guards: the 611 cpc-hepnp papers unchanged; the 12 just papers as with cpc-hepnp routed
(all frontmatter: e-mails and affiliations gained, the only words lost marks, now links). Without the preload the base
loads OmniBus for the missing binding with a `missing_file` Warning: on 1603.03230 2 Errors (`\figcaption`,
`\tabcaption` undefined), the e-mail kept as "Email: ", the keywords an `ltx:classification` split wrongly ("1",
"3.40.Gp"). The binding reads the class raw either way: 0 errors there, the keywords as body lists, and the class's own
`\@obsoletefile{article.cls}{article.sty}` Warning, as pdflatex prints.

Residuals:
- **CPC's e-mail mark `affiliations;n)`** (`E.A.Kozyrev$^{1,2;1)}$`; under cpc-hepnp 341 papers). A mark is parted at
  commas only (`clean_frontmatter_labels`; Perl's cleanFrontmatterLabels, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:366, the same), so
  `2;1)` requests no line. Kozyrev lacks Novosibirsk State University (1603.03230); 1510.07251's Achasov (`$^{1;1)}$`),
  1510.07985's three authors (`$^{1;1)}$`, `$^{2,3;2)}$`, `$^{2;3);\dagger}$`), 1511.03934's Berger and 1511.09245's
  Kardapoltsev (`$^{1,2;1)}$`) lack lines. A line that no name requests goes to a creator with no name (1510.07251,
  1510.07985, 1511.09245), as the marked list places any unrequested entry. RED repro
  `class-bindings/just_semicolon_email_marks`.
- **A name's own mark stays in its name** (`Longke Li$^{1)}$`, 1510.03577: `<sup>1</sup>` in the `personname`, the ")"
  gone), as before the binding.
- **91c, the plan that registers `cpc-hepnp`** (proposed, main session 2026-10-29): (1) the cpc-hepnp binding declares
  its house mark convention — an item ending in `)` is a footnote mark, not a label, and `;` separates items like `,`.
  This is binding-declared data the marked-list reader consults, not a global scanner; it resolves both the `,n)`
  residual (41 papers) and the `;n)` one (341), without r1's objection that parting at `;` turns `3)` into label 3.
  (2) A structural fail-safe: an unmarked multi-line address under names that carry marks goes to the author block,
  once, not to every name (the typed-number and other unmarked lists, 71 papers; 0906.3801, 1001.2445). The grouped
  list (1709.03653, 6 papers) is to be re-measured under both. Then the 611-paper A/B again, nothing worse.

Repros class-bindings/{just_marked_address_after_maketitle, just_unmarked_address,
just_unmarked_address_under_several_names, just_emails_after_maketitle} (GREEN),
cpc_hepnp_unmarked_address_under_several_names (NO-CHANGE, GREEN for 91c) and just_semicolon_email_marks (RED); guards
`perfect_kernel_batch91a::{just_marked_address_after_maketitle_affiliates_every_name,
just_unmarked_address_is_its_author_s_affiliation, just_unmarked_address_under_several_names_is_every_name_s,
just_emails_after_maketitle_is_the_author_s_e_mail, cpc_hepnp_is_not_routed_until_91c}` (the first and third also
check the binary, eager and `--streaming`).

### 914. bbold's blackboard map is its own family's (`blackboard`, a name bbm and bbmss share), not the `U` encoding's, and a family's map is read without an encoding map (Perl: bbold's map decodes every `U` font)

bbold.sty.ltxml:30 registers its map as `U_fontmap`, the encoding's (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1203), so beside
`\usepackage{bbold}` every `U` symbol font without a map of its own decoded as blackboard letters, silently: a paper's
copy of mathabx.dcl:944 `\widehat` in `U/mathx` printed 𝕡 (and 89c's name rule never fired, the font now having a
map), stmaryrd's `\boxslash` in `U/stmry` σ, a raw `U/msa` `\Cap` 𝕖 — loaded first, the encoding map also stopped
u_fontmap.rs, which holds `U_msa`/`U_msb`/`U_eur`, from ever loading — and program.sty's `U/eur` `\powersetsymbol` –.
OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #27's "`U` with a family other than `msa`/`msb`/`eur` has no map" was false under bbold.

Ours: bbold_sty.rs registers the map for bbold's own font, by both names it goes by — `U_blackboard`, the family its
`\mathbb`/`\textbb`/`\bbfamily` constructors name (and `\fontfamily{bbold}` selects, font.rs's family table), and
`U_bbold`, Ubbold.fd's and bbold.sty's NFSS family (`\DeclareSymbolFont{…}{U}{bbold}{m}{n}`) — with its multichar
entry (`DeclareFontMapMultichar!("U", family, …)`, `U_<family>_fontmap_multichar`). `U` keeps no map of its own. Three
readers had reached a family map only through its encoding's, as Perl's `FontDecode`/`FontDecodeString` do
(Package.pm:2878-2882, :2907-2910), and are now its own: font.rs `decoding_map`, shared by `decode`, `decode_string`
and the `\char` multichar lookup, reads the family's map (and its multichar table, which a slot of Perl's map holds)
whether or not the encoding has one, as content.rs `font_decode` already did; math characters decode in the font's
family (`decode_in_font`, mathchar.rs), as Perl's `decodeMathChar` passes `$font` to `FontDecode` (Package.pm:2990),
where Rust had passed the encoding alone, so `\mathbb{R1}` under bbold is ℝ𝟙; and `\selectfont` gives back the encoding
`\fontencoding` named, which decodes through OT1 for want of a map (`\lx@fontencoding`, #645), when the selected family
has a map under it (sect13.rs `nfss_selected_font`), so `\usefont{U}{bbold}{m}{n}R1` is ℝ𝟙 as `\textbb{R1}` is. Every
`*_fontmap.rs` is its own encoding's map, and no other binding registers an encoding map under a shared encoding.
